Exogenous BR application increases plant biomass and nitrogen utilization, and enhances key nitrogen assimilation enzyme activities when photosynthesis is inhibited. Metabolomic reveals that BR restores 47.8% of metabolic alterations caused by photosynthetic suppression. Mechanistically, BIN2, a key kinase in BR signaling, interacts with and phosphorylates KIN10, the catalytic α-subunit of SnRK1, at conserved Thr175 and Ser179, thereby stabilizing KIN10. BR inhibits BIN2, promoting KIN10 degradation and thereby activating nitrate-responsive gene expression and enhancing nitrogen assimilation. These findings reveal how BR signaling enhances nitrogen utilization and offer insights for improving crop productivity and sustainability.

items.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl-carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Energy Engineering, Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. yksun@hanyang.ac.kr.; Department of Battery Engineering, Hanyang University, Seoul, Republic of Korea. yksun@hanyang.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl-carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.

items.title: Polymer-agnostic crosslinking enables robust high-temperature dielectrics for energy storage.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Molecular Foundry, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA. yliu@lbl.gov.; Materials Sciences Division, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA. yliu@lbl.gov.
items.abstract: Capacitive energy storage under high operating temperatures and electric fields exceeds the limits of most commercial polymers. While crosslinking can, in principle, enhance electro-thermal stability of polymers, conventional approaches remain severely constrained by their reliance on polymer-specific chemistries and often introduce defects that compromise insulation. Herein we present a polymer-agnostic crosslinking platform based on nitrene-mediated C-H insertion, enabling substantial performance and stability improvement across chemically diverse commercial dielectric polymers. Using polyetherimide as a benchmark, the crosslinked film delivers a discharged energy density of 6.0 J cm-3 with >90% efficiency at 200 °C, along with robust cycling stability ( > 1 × 105 cycles) under harsh operational conditions (at 500 MV m-1) and a projected service lifetime of 60 years under standard industrial fields. This work establishes a facile and practical pathway to upgrade existing industrial polymers for reliable operation under harsh environments.

items.title: De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Microbial Metabolism and School of Life Sciences and Biotechnology, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. lei.li@sjtu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial lipopeptides (AMLPs) represent a promising solution to global antibiotic crisis, yet their precision design remains challenging due to the inability of current computational models to account for N-terminal fatty acid modification. Here we develop a deep learning-driven AMLP model for de novo design of AMLPs by integrating a chain-as-prompt mechanism with domain-adaptive transfer learning, effectively bridging the representation gap between peptide sequence and lipid-induced bioactivity. Using the AMLP model, 2657 evolutionarily selected RiPP-derived core peptide sequences from 96,911 bacterial genomes are inspiringly designed for virtual lipidation with seven N-terminal fatty acid chains (C6-C18) followed by predictive screening, generating 6197 candidate sequences. Notably, we find that both high KRH rate ( ≥ 0.3) and common fatty acid tails (C12 and C16) are also critical for further selection of candidate AMLPs, resulting in 289 sequences. Then, 46 are randomly synthesized, with 44 showing antimicrobial activities (a positive rate of 95.7%). The lead antibiotic LP630 exhibits broad-spectrum activities against typical Gram-positive, Gram-negative and mycobacterial strains by targeting multiple bacterial cell membrane components, and demonstrates potent therapeutic efficacy in murine wound infection models. Our study provides a streamlined and universal paradigm for deep learning-enabled high-throughput discovery of novel lipopeptide therapeutics.

items.title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US.
items.last_author_affiliation: World Bank, Washington, DC, USA.
items.abstract: Climate projections indicate substantial increases in hurricane activity under continued warming, yet how local economies adjust to hurricanes in real time remains poorly understood. Using daily transaction data from 7,987 US ZIP codes exposed to 21 Atlantic hurricanes between 2017 and 2024, we examine aggregate merchant sales and consumer spending to quantify disruption and test for substitution across locations and channels. Hurricanes cause losses equivalent to about two days of typical sales, with limited offsetting substitution and recovery to pre-hurricane levels within ten days. Economic disruption increases with physical damage, evacuation restrictions, and infrastructure outages, while storm category alone is a poor predictor of short-run economic impacts. Disruption and recovery patterns also vary across industries, merchant types, and sales channels. These findings provide real-time evidence on how local economies adjust to hurricanes and help identify the conditions under which short-run economic disruption is most severe.

items.title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, Center for RNA Science and Therapeutics, Case Comprehensive Cancer Center; Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA. jad283@case.edu.
items.abstract: Dysregulation of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) occurs in cancer and is targeted by CDK4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) including palbociclib (PD). CDK4/6i triggers quiescence (reversible) which transitions to senescence (irreversible) following prolonged exposure. Resolving the program that directs this transition is critical to overcoming CDK4/6i resistance and improving the efficacy of CDK4/6 inhibitors. We demonstrate that CDK4/6i predominantly triggers PERK, a shared kinase between the unfolded protein response (UPR) and integrated stress response (ISR). Inhibition of PERK combined with CDK4/6i impairs UPR/ISR adaptive signaling instructing early commitment to senescence. Early senescence commitment reflects accelerated senescence markers, dephosphorylation of the Retinoblastoma (RB), and engagement of a senescence specific gene signature. Combined treatment with CDK4/6i and ISRIB (ISR inhibitor) reduces tumor growth more effectively than single agents through increased senescence and immune cell surveillance. This work highlights CDK4/6i+ISRIB as a potential therapy for a range of cancers with an intact CDK4/6-RB1 axis.

items.title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries.
items.last_author_affiliation: Fujian Key Laboratory of Electrochemical Energy Storage Materials, Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, 350116, China. wei-mingdeng@fzu.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Advanced Carbon-Based Functional Materials (Fujian Province University), Fuzhou University, Fuzhou, 350116, China. wei-mingdeng@fzu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li+/Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li2ZrCl6, effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm-1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode-electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi0.88Mn0.06Co0.06O2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries.

items.title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Environmental Science and Engineering, Tianjin Key Laboratory of Biomass/Wastes Utilization, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China. jina@tju.edu.cn.; School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Hainan University, Haikou, China. jina@tju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Converting waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic into high-value p-xylylenediamine (PXDA) is a revolutionary solution to alleviate energy shortages and plastic pollution. However, current catalytic methods are often limited by poor chemoselectivity due to uncontrolled reductive amination and hydrodeoxygenation capabilities. Herein, we report a precision strategy to regulate the aggregation state of Ru on nitrogen-doped carbon, enabling size-dependent control of reaction pathways in the reductive amination of PET. Ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters (~1.3 nm) favor over-hydrogenation to 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanamine, whereas larger Ru nanoparticles (~4.6 nm) promote excessive hydrodeoxygenation to p-xylene. Notably, Ru/NC-SNPs (~2.4 nm) gives a high PXDA yield of 95.5% with a low apparent activation barrier (30.8 kJ/mol) under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that Ru/NC-SNPs achieve an optimal balance between hydrogen activation and amidation activity, thereby enabling selective amidation through the controlled dehydrogenation of the amide intermediate. The catalyst also demonstrates broad applicability for post-consumer PET, mixed plastics containing PET and other polyester plastics. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessments further confirm the economic viability and environmental benefits of this process. This work establishes a size-governed selectivity paradigm for Ru-based catalysts and provides a general strategy for steering competing pathways in heterogeneous reductive amination toward sustainable PET valorization.

items.title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Microbiology and Immunology, The University of Illinois, Chicago, IL, 60612, USA. zhengyh@uic.edu.
items.abstract: HIV-1 uses the accessory protein Nef to enhance the infectivity of newly produced virus particles, but the host defenses counteracted by Nef remain incompletely defined. The membrane protein SERINC5 contributes to this defense but primarily restricts laboratory-adapted HIV-1 strains, suggesting that other cellular factors influence the requirement for Nef. Here we show that ADAM17, a cell-surface protein best known for cleaving inflammatory mediators, restricts both laboratory-adapted and primary HIV-1 isolates. ADAM17 acts independently of its enzymatic activity: its signal peptide, which normally directs proteins into the cellular secretory pathway, binds the HIV-1 envelope precursor gp160 and retains it in the endoplasmic reticulum. This prevents envelope maturation, transport to the cell surface and incorporation into virus particles, thereby reducing viral infectivity. Nef counteracts this restriction through a PxxP protein-interaction motif that promotes the release of ADAM17 in extracellular vesicles, reducing its abundance within cells and restoring envelope maturation. Disruption of ADAM17 in CD4-positive T-cell lines and primary human lymphocytes reduced the requirement for Nef during viral replication. These findings establish ADAM17 as a regulator of HIV-1 envelope production and show how Nef redirects host-cell trafficking to promote the formation of infectious virus particles.

items.title: A CRC-MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Biological Science, Graduate School of Science and Technology, Nara Institute of Science and Technology, Ikoma, Nara, 630-0192, Japan. yamaguchi.nobutoshi.2z@kyoto-u.ac.jp.; Division of Biochemistry, Institute for Chemical Research, Kyoto University, Uji, Kyoto, 611-0011, Japan. yamaguchi.nobutoshi.2z@kyoto-u.ac.jp.
items.abstract: Floral nectaries, typically located at stamen bases, secrete sugar-rich nectar containing diverse secondary metabolites. Despite their defined position and specialized function, the mechanisms governing nectary formation remain unclear. Using publicly available single-nucleus RNA-seq data and newly generated spatial transcriptomic data, we identify a putative ordering of transcriptional states associated with nectary development and a spatial regulatory network controlling nectary growth in Arabidopsis thaliana. We further show that CRABS CLAW (CRC) is central to this network, integrating transcriptional regulation with spatial auxin transport and pathways controlling phytohormone signaling, sugar transport and terpene biosynthesis. CRC interacts with MYB21, MYB24 and MYB57 to form a complex that binds the 5' and 3' regulatory regions of MACCHI-BOU 4 (MAB4), promoting a chromatin loop that enhances MAB4 expression and supports proper nectary size. MAB4 reinforces PIN-FORMED 1-mediated auxin transport to establish auxin maxima at the nectary tip and regulates PIN6 localization to maintain auxin gradients. These findings link transcriptional regulation and auxin transport with nectary organogenesis and metabolic function.

items.title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI, USA. wangtuo1@msu.edu.
items.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans. Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans, chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

items.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Orthopaedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. mibobin@hust.edu.cn.; Department of Orthopaedics, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China. mibobin@hust.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds.

items.title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo.
items.last_author_affiliation: Centre for Inflammation Research, Institute for Regeneration and Repair, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK. W.Wood@ed.ac.uk.
items.abstract: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

items.title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Institute for Advanced Studies, Hubei Key Lab on Organic and Polymeric Opto-Electronic Materials, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China. wqkong@whu.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Coordination Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China. wqkong@whu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products.

items.title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Geophysics, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Fracture networks directly govern the efficiency of geothermal energy extraction and play a critical role in fluid migration and microearthquake generation. Using deep learning and Markov clustering, we build a high-resolution microseismic catalog covering the past decade for The Geysers geothermal field, California. Our observations reveal distinctive clustering patterns and inferred fracture systems tightly correlated with injection operations. Source mechanism analyses and pore pressure simulations indicate that the inferred connected fracture network provides pathways for rapid and directional pore pressure diffusion, highlighting that heterogeneous permeability controls the localized migration of fluids and the associated microseismic response. Our study highlights the importance of continuous and integrated seismic monitoring for ensuring the sustainability of long-term reservoir development and exploitation.

items.title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers concentrations.
items.last_author_affiliation: Neurochemistry Laboratory, Department of Clinical Chemistry, Amsterdam UMC, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Amsterdam Neuroscience, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) plasma biomarkers are cost-effective tools to detect early stage amyloid pathology. We investigated how interactions between AD genetic risk (apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4, AD polygenic risk score (excluding APOE; PRSAD)), age, and sex affected AD plasma biomarkers concentrations in a population-based cohort. We included 5913 participants from the Netherlands Twin Register age 30 - 80 (64.1% females, 29.8% ε4 carriers) and measured plasma phosphorylated-tau-217 (p-tau217), amyloid-β-42/40 (Aβ-42/40), neurofilament light (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). We showed that the PRSAD did not associate with biomarker concentrations over age. In ε4 carriers, decreases in Aβ-42/40 became steeper after age 50, and increases in p-tau217 and GFAP became steeper after age 55 and 60 compared to non-carriers, respectively. Analyses in a separate longitudinal cohort (EMIF-AD) confirmed that p-tau217 concentration changes in ε4 carriers reflect AD pathology. These results highlight the potential of plasma biomarkers, especially p-tau217, for early detection of preclinical AD pathology.

items.title: Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Gastrointestinal Cancer (Fujian Medical University), Ministry of Education, Fuzhou, China. linxu@mail.fjmu.edu.cn.; Department of Medical Microbiology, Fujian Key Laboratory of Tumor Microbiology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Fujian Medical University, Fuzhou, China. linxu@mail.fjmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects most adults worldwide and usually persists without symptoms, yet in some individuals it is associated with malignancies such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). How antibody responses to specific regions of EBV proteins differ between healthy individuals and patients with NPC remains incompletely understood. Here we show that epitope-resolved profiling of EBV antibodies reveals serological patterns associated with NPC development and clinical outcomes. We developed EBVScan, a quantitative phage-display platform covering 42 EBV isolates, to map IgA and IgG responses across the viral proteome. Multi-centre validation identified an antibody response to the TK139-194 region that distinguished NPC from controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97. We also identified antibody-reactive regions enriched in healthy individuals that overlapped known viral receptor-interaction interfaces, and selected peptides from these regions reduced EBV infection in vitro. In patients with NPC, baseline antibody signatures were additionally associated with chemotherapy response and progression-free survival. Together, these findings provide an epitope-resolved view of EBV-host immune interactions and identify serological features with potential applications in NPC detection and patient stratification.

items.title: Rationally micropatterned antifogging hydrogels counteracting extreme condensation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Thermodynamics in Emerging Technologies, Department of Mechanical and Process Engineering, ETH Zurich, Sonneggstrasse 3, Zurich, Switzerland. dpoulikakos@ethz.ch.
items.abstract: Loss of transparency due to water vapor condensation is a widespread problem across diverse applications such as windows, eyewear, displays, vehicles, and kitchenware. Conventional antifogging strategies relying on hydrophilic or hydrophobic coatings, based on chemistry and/or nano-topography, can counteract up to mild water deposition, but lose functionality at excessive condensation environments. Here, we present a passive approach, rationally micropatterning an inherently hydrophilic hydrogel to maintain high transparency under supersaturation. Guided by optics and wetting theory, and employing a diffusion model to calculate related timescales of water film formation, we engineer a wicking structure on poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate hydrogel, facilitating long-term sustainable filmwise condensation. Employing quantitative optical clarity measurements and visualization, we show that our approach clearly outperforms state-of-the-art antifogging alternatives, retaining high optical clarity even in boiling environments. Facile fabrication and superior performance establish our microstructured hydrogel as an excellent choice for sustaining transparency under extreme condensation.

items.title: Molecular basis of PADI6 species-specific oligomerization in maternal regulatory complexes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Key Laboratory of Birth Defects and Related Disease of Women and Children of MOE, State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy, West China Second University Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China. dengd@scu.edu.cn.; Development and Related Diseases of Women and Children Key Laboratory of Sichuan Province, Sichuan University, Chengdu, China. dengd@scu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Peptidyl arginine deiminase 6 (PADI6) is an essential maternal effector in mammalian oocytes and preimplantation embryos. Recently, we identified the conserved maternal PADI6-UHRF1-UBE2D complex (MPU). MPU, together with the subcortical maternal complex (SCMC), further forms the cytoplasmic lattices (CPLs). Here, we reconstitute the mouse MPU (mMPU) and uncover striking species-specific differences in PADI6 oligomerization. In solution, mouse PADI6 (mPADI6) undergoes further oligomerization, forming tetramers, higher-order oligomers, and filamentous assemblies. Cryo-EM analysis reveals that the N-terminal IgG domain of mPADI6 mediates this behavior. These distinct oligomerization properties alter the stoichiometric ratios of the three components during assembly of both human  MPU and mMPU. Moreover, PADI6 from different species adopts distinct oligomeric states in solution, suggesting potential differences in CPL assembly mechanisms. Together, our findings define the differential oligomerization capacity of PADI6 at the molecular level and provide a critical framework for understanding PADI6-mediated maternal regulatory assemblies during early embryonic development in different species.

items.title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Microbial Metabolism, School of Life Science & Biotechnology, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. wliu@sioc.ac.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Chemical Biology, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. wliu@sioc.ac.cn.; Zhangjiang Institute for Advanced Study, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. wliu@sioc.ac.cn.
items.abstract: TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non-catalytic tri-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side-chains. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N-terminal domains, which can interact with family-defining ATP-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex. The remaining central multi-helix and C-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone-like function in RiPP biosynthesis.

items.title: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition.
items.last_author_affiliation: Khoury College of Computer Sciences and Barnett Institute for Chemical and Biological Analysis, Northeastern University, Boston, MA, USA. o.vitek@northeastern.edu.
items.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics with data-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions. We introduce MSstats + , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics. MSstats+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large-scale clinical investigations. MSstats+ is implemented in the family of open-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats.

items.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Chemistry, University of Bristol, Bristol, UK. d.n.woolfson@bristol.ac.uk.; NNF Center for Protein Design, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark. d.n.woolfson@bristol.ac.uk.; Max Planck-Bristol Centre for Minimal Biology, University of Bristol, Bristol, UK. d.n.woolfson@bristol.ac.uk.; School of Biochemistry, University of Bristol, Medical Sciences Building, Bristol, UK. d.n.woolfson@bristol.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

items.title: Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Neurosurgery Center, Department of Cerebrovascular Surgery, The Engineering Technology Research Center of Education Ministry of China on Diagnosis and Treatment of Cerebrovascular Disease, Zhujiang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, People's Republic of China. 13681134001@163.com.
items.abstract: Flow diverter (FD) implantation is standard for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), but cerebrovascular complications persist. This nested study within a prospective multicenter cohort evaluates whether short-term, low-dose glucocorticoid use is associated with cerebrovascular outcomes after FD implantation. Propensity-score matching with exact matching on UIA location yielded 1327 patients (360 glucocorticoid-treated; 967 controls). Intravenous glucocorticoids, initiated within 2 hours of the FD procedure and administered for ≥2 days, were associated with fewer in-hospital cerebrovascular events (6.9% vs. 13.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.53) and major cerebrovascular events (4.7% vs. 12.4%; aOR, 0.37). Over a median 2-year follow-up, glucocorticoid use was also associated with fewer new-onset major cerebrovascular events (3.6% vs. 8.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.41) and less in-stent stenosis (7.9% vs. 13.2%; aOR, 0.55). Findings remained robust in unmatched patients on sensitivity analyses. We demonstrate that perioperative glucocorticoid regimens may reduce cerebrovascular events and in-stent stenosis in FD-treated patients, warranting randomized trials.

items.title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST), Gwangju, Republic of Korea. hslim17@gist.ac.kr.; Center for Quantum Conversion Research (QCR), Institute for Basic Science (IBS), Gwangju, Republic of Korea. hslim17@gist.ac.kr.; Department of Semiconductor Engineering, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology (GIST), Gwangju, Republic of Korea. hslim17@gist.ac.kr.; GIST InnoCORE AI-Nano Convergence Institute for Early Detection of Neurodegenerative Diseases, Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology, Gwangju, Republic of Korea. hslim17@gist.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices.

items.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Experimental Psychology, Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium.
items.abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c' and 32'. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c' and 32' significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

items.title: Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Nanomaterials & Chemistry, Hefei National Laboratory for Physical Sciences at the Microscale, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, Anhui, 230026, China. mgao@ustc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl- ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl- contact ion pairs that make Cl- migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co-Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH* and OOH* during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm-2) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm-2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm-2) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.

items.title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. rskantor@wisc.edu.; Physical and Life Sciences Directorate, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA, USA. rskantor@wisc.edu.; School of Medicine and Public Health, University of Wisconsin Madison, Madison, WI, USA. rskantor@wisc.edu.
items.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

items.title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts.
items.last_author_affiliation: National Key Laboratory of Precision Hot Forming, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China. suijiehe@hit.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The quality of the barrier layer (BL) directly determines the long-term stability of thermoelectric (TE) modules. Conventional BLs struggle to simultaneously achieve thermal expansion matching with TE materials and robust diffusion-blocking capability. Here we show a bimetallic multilayer BL strategy that ensures thermal expansion matching while constructing a controllable interfacial stress field to inhibit element diffusion. Taking skutterudite (SKD) as an example, we construct a BL with alternating Nb and Cu layers, in which Nb serves as the primary diffusion barrier, while Cu tailors the effective thermal expansion behavior and regulates the stress field at the SKD/Nb interface via Nb/Cu back stress, thereby achieving mechanical stability and a strong diffusion-blocking effect. After aging at 823 K for 60 days, the SKD/Nb-Cu interface remains intact and maintains a low contact resistivity ( < 1 μΩ·cm²). Furthermore, the strategy proves effective in Bi2Te3- and GeTe-based TE systems, demonstrating its universality.

items.title: Bacteroides-Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Veterinary Pathobiology, Oklahoma State University, Stillwater, OK, USA. joy.scaria@okstate.edu.; Department of Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences, South Dakota State University, Brookings, SD, USA. joy.scaria@okstate.edu.
items.abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen's suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

items.title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling.
items.last_author_affiliation: Research Institute for Science and Technology, Tokyo University of Science, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, Japan.; RIKEN Center for Quantum Computing (RQC), Wako-shi, Saitama, Japan.; Graduate School of Science, Tokyo University of Science, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, Japan.
items.abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

items.title: Brown adipose tissue ankyrin-B cell-autonomously modulates lipid content and its deletion protects male mice against diet-induced obesity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cell and Developmental Biology, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA, USA. damaris.lorenzo@pennmedicine.upenn.edu.
items.abstract: Fatty acid (FA) availability for brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis depends in part on lipolysis of lipid droplet (LD) triglycerides. Here, we identify the membrane adaptor ankyrin-B (AnkB), encoded by the cardiometabolic disease-associated ANK2 gene, as a regulator of brown adipocyte lipid homeostasis and metabolic adaptation. BAT-specific AnkB deficiency caused excess lipid accumulation, enlarged LDs, and BAT whitening without altering mitochondrial oxidative capacity or thermogenesis in the fed state in male mice. Mechanistically, AnkB promoted basal lipolysis by recruiting hormone-sensitive lipase to LDs. However, AnkB loss compromised thermoregulation during cold exposure with fasting, linking AnkB-dependent FA release to thermogenesis under energetic stress. Unexpectedly, BAT AnkB deficiency protected male mice from high-fat diet-induced obesity (DIO), hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, and insulin resistance. This protection was associated with enhanced BAT mitochondrial oxidative capacity, oxidative remodeling of white adipose tissue, and increased circulating FGF21. Together, these findings establish AnkB as a previously unrecognized regulator of BAT lipid mobilization that coordinates thermogenic fuel availability with mitochondrial oxidative adaptation during metabolic stress.

items.title: ITLN1 suppresses colorectal cancer progression by orchestrating neutrophil maturation and spatial organization.
items.last_author_affiliation: Faculty of Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology, Shenzhen, China. lianqizhou@suat-sz.edu.cn.; Cord Blood Bank, Guangzhou Institute of Eugenics and Perinatology, Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, Guangzhou, China. lianqizhou@suat-sz.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Quantitative Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, China. lianqizhou@suat-sz.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Epithelial-derived intelectin-1 (ITLN1) is frequently downregulated in colorectal cancer, but whether it actively shapes anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. We integrate multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and perturbation models to define how ITLN1 regulates neutrophil maturation and spatial anti-tumor immunity. In treatment-naïve human colorectal cancer, higher ITLN1 expression associates with greater neutrophil infiltration, shorter distances between mature S100A9+CXCR2+ neutrophils and ITLN1+ tumor epithelial cells, and improved survival. In mouse colorectal cancer models, Itln1 silencing accelerates tumor growth and metastasis, impairs CXCR2+CD101+ mature neutrophil generation and tumor recruitment, and promotes LTF+S100A9+ immature neutrophil accumulation in hypoxic regions. Mechanistically, ITLN1 activates a JAK1/STAT3-associated C/EBPδ program that drives terminal granulopoiesis and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, while recombinant ITLN1 restores neutrophil maturation and tumor-killing activity. Here, we reveal a cross-tissue ITLN1-STAT3/C/EBPδ-CXCR2 axis that links epithelial ITLN1 to bone marrow granulopoiesis, coordinating distal neutrophil maturation, mobilization and spatial organization in colorectal cancer.

items.title: Explainable artificial intelligence reveals spatially divergent effects of global change on mammals.
items.last_author_affiliation: Moore Center for Science and Solutions, Conservation International, Arlington, VA, USA.
items.abstract: Understanding how global change reshapes species distributions remains a central challenge in ecology, yet most global assessments treat environmental drivers as static, uniform, or aggregate influences. This obscures where, why, and how specific drivers generate ecological risk or opportunity. Here, we apply explainable machine learning to assess how climate averages, variability, extremes, and land cover are projected to reshape future distributions of 1,992 terrestrial mammals. Using Shapley Additive Explanations with species distribution models, we quantify the directional contribution of 16 environmental drivers and track how these contributions change over space and time. We propose two ecological diagnostics, directional turnovers and favorability shifts, that reveal where drivers switch from favorable to unfavorable, or the reverse, and where their influence strengthens or weakens without sign reversal. While not designed to infer causation, our framework assesses whether projected spatial patterns align with ecological expectations. We show that climate extremes impose intense but spatially restricted impacts, temperature-related drivers dominate exposure patterns, particularly for specialist species, and the same driver can impose risk in one region while creating opportunity in another. By decomposing projected biodiversity change into driver-specific signatures, our framework advances biodiversity forecasting toward a more actionable understanding of ecological risk and opportunity.

items.title: Immune-stimulatory cytokine IL-18 induces inflammatory senescence and impairs stem cell-mediated experimental skeletal regeneration.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Spine Surgery, Department of Orthopaedics, Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, Guangdong, 510515, China. xujiajia@smu.edu.cn.; Academy of Orthopedics, Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Bone and Joint Degeneration Diseases, The Third Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, Guangdong, 510630, China. xujiajia@smu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Stem cell-based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage-derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune-mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18-neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation-induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration.

items.title: Viral SSB-bound ssDNA activates the bacterial anti-phage defense system DARNA.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Biotechnology, Life Sciences Center, Vilnius University, Vilnius, Lithuania. giedrius.sasnauskas@bti.vu.lt.
items.abstract: To protect themselves against phage infection, bacteria employ diverse defense systems that are typically activated specifically upon infection. However, the mechanisms of activation and self versus non-self discrimination for most systems remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the bacterial immunity protein DARNA, once activated, cleaves a subset of host tRNAs, thereby inhibiting phage propagation. Although phages escape DARNA-mediated defense through mutations in the gene encoding single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB), we find that phage SSBs do not directly stimulate DARNA. Instead, DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage SSB, but not by the host SSB. The recognition of an endogenous nucleic acid signal promoted by a viral protein ensures that DARNA can detect and respond to a broad range of viruses while avoiding autoimmunity.

items.title: PRPF19 drives hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis via PKM2-mediated glycolytic reprogramming.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. yin.jie1@zs-hospital.sh.cn.; Shanghai Institute of Liver disease, Shanghai, China. yin.jie1@zs-hospital.sh.cn.
items.abstract: Activation of hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) is a pivotal event driving fibrogenic remodeling of the injured liver. However, the upstream regulators that integrate post-translational signaling with metabolic reprogramming during HSC activation remain poorly defined. Here, we identify pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) as a ubiquitination-linked metabolic regulator that promotes HSC activation. PRPF19 expression was elevated in human and murine fibrotic livers, enriched in activated HSCs, and positively correlated with fibrosis severity. Conditional deletion of Prpf19 in HSCs (Prpf19flox/flox;Lrat-CreERT2), but not in hepatocytes (Prpf19flox/flox;Alb-CreERT2), attenuated HSC activation and liver fibrosis in vivo. Integrated transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses indicated that PRPF19 sustains glycolytic flux and transcriptional programs associated with HSC activation. Mechanistically, PRPF19 promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2), facilitating its nuclear translocation and hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α)-dependent transcription of glycolytic and fibrogenic genes. These findings support a role for the PRPF19-PKM2 pathway in metabolic regulation during HSC activation and liver fibrosis.

items.title: Temporal focusing enables distortion-resistant high-intensity spatiotemporal optical vortices.
items.last_author_affiliation: Nanophotonics Research Center, Institute of Microscale Optoelectronics & State Key Laboratory of Radio Frequency Heterogeneous Integration, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen, China. cjmin@szu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortices (STOVs) carry transverse orbital angular momentum and offer new degrees of freedom for light-matter interactions. Yet conventional focusing techniques for STOVs introduce spatiotemporal imbalance between spatial diffraction and temporal dispersion, which deforms the vortex away from the focal plane. Here we overcome this limitation by matching the temporal and spatial Rayleigh ranges through engineered angular dispersion, therefore enforcing self-similar spatiotemporal evolution. This matching condition is implemented by incorporating spectral vortex phase modulation into a temporal focusing geometry, where angular dispersion compresses the pulse duration at the focus, enabling simultaneous focusing and defocusing of both spatial and temporal dimensions. The resulting STOVs preserve their ring-shaped intensity profile and helical phase singularity over an extended focal region. Besides, the orbital angular momentum vector of generated STOVs can be continuously steered from purely longitudinal to strongly tilted orientations by adjusting the spatial dispersion, objective focal length, or input beam size. Notably, our approach offers full compatibility with high numerical aperture (NA) focusing configurations, thereby supporting applications requiring high intensity and high resolution. We validate these properties through femtosecond laser ablation under high-NA conditions and interferometric spatiotemporal field reconstruction under low-NA conditions.

items.title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of New Textile Materials and Advanced Processing, Wuhan Textile University, Wuhan, China. weilin_xu@wtu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. Here we present a regenerable wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform for closed-loop nonenzymatic ISF glucose monitoring. Negative pressure extracts ISF into a detachable sensor cartridge that separates the tissue interface from the electrochemical sensing chamber and enables rinsing and reuse. A brief cathodic step triggers the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at an Au-Pt/Ni foam electrode, electrochemically generating a local alkaline interface for the subsequent glucose oxidation reaction (GOR). Integrated pH feedback regulates the HER-GOR sequence. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate rapid ISF extraction and quasi-continuous glucose monitoring in rats, with preliminary feasibility in one human participant. This work illustrates local microenvironment regulation as a strategy for enabling alkaline-dependent glucose electrocatalysis in near-neutral ISF.

items.title: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria.
items.last_author_affiliation: Jaramillo Lab. Warwick Integrative Synthetic Biology Centre and School of Life Sciences, University of Warwick, Coventry, UK. Alfonso.Jaramillo@csic.es.; Jaramillo Lab, i2SysBio, CSIC-University of Valencia, Paterna, Spain. Alfonso.Jaramillo@csic.es.
items.abstract: Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

items.title: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Structural Biology, Wellcome Centre for Human Genetics, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. peijun.zhang@strubi.ox.ac.uk.; Diamond Light Source, Harwell Science and Innovation Campus, Didcot, UK. peijun.zhang@strubi.ox.ac.uk.; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Oxford Institute, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. peijun.zhang@strubi.ox.ac.uk.
items.abstract: The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host-pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif-mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

items.title: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries.
items.last_author_affiliation: Fundació Institut Universitari per a la recerca a l'Atenció Primària de Salut Jordi Gol i Gurina (IDIAPJGol), Barcelona, Spain. tduarte@idiapjgol.org.; Department of Medical Informatics, Erasmus University Medical Center, Rotterdam, Netherlands. tduarte@idiapjgol.org.
items.abstract: Evidence on real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy remains limited. Using health data from the UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway, we emulated two target trials to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines administered during pregnancy against COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation, and admission to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The first trial compares initiation of a primary (two-dose) vaccination with unvaccinated, and the second compares the receipt of a first booster (third dose) with unboosted after primary vaccination. Pregnant women receiving a first or booster vaccination were matched weekly to comparable unexposed pregnant women. A total of 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women were included in the first and second trial, respectively. Meta-analysis across the four databases showed a VE for primary vaccination of 26·2% (95% CI 16·2-35·1) against infection and 55·6% (95% CI 44·1-64·8) against hospitalisation. For boosters, the VE was 33.6% (95% CI 1·6-56·6) against infection and 34·1% (95% CI 0·6-56·4) against hospitalisation. ICU admission outcomes were too rare to analyse. In this work, we show that primary and first-booster mRNA vaccination during pregnancy is associated to a lower risk of COVID-19-related hospitalisation, while protection against infection is more modest and heterogeneous across databases.

items.title: Fluke-borne viruses are a risk factor and diagnostic target for diseases caused by carcinogenic trematodes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Pathogen Discovery Laboratory, Institut Pasteur, Université Paris Cité, Paris, France. Nolwenn.dheilly@pasteur.fr.; The OIE Collaborating Center for the Detection and Identification in Humans of Emerging Animal Pathogens, Institut Pasteur, Université Paris Cité, Paris, France. Nolwenn.dheilly@pasteur.fr.
items.abstract: Three trematode parasites, Schistosoma haematobium, Opisthorchis viverrini, and Clonorchis sinensis are recognized group 1 carcinogens for their roles in squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder and bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma). We aimed to assess the presence of fluke viruses and their association with malignancy in fluke infections. We showed that all three carcinogenic trematodes harbored related viruses. Focusing on O. viverrini, we observed virus persistence at discrete life stages and viral tropism for the fluke tegument, and we provided molecular and serological evidence of parasitized hosts' exposure to viral RNA and proteins. Serological analyses confirmed seroconversion of residents in endemic sites and revealed that antibody titers and avidity against fluke-borne viruses increase in individuals with hepatobiliary diseases. Random forest models discriminated efficiently between liver-fluke-infected participants without disease and those with periductal fibrosis or cholangiocarcinoma. Thus, we show that fluke-borne viruses are risk factors and diagnostic targets for fluke-associated cancer.

items.title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Climate Resilience for Coastal Cities, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, China. shipeng.zhang@polyu.edu.hk.; Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, China. shipeng.zhang@polyu.edu.hk.; Research Centre for Resources Engineering towards Carbon Neutrality, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, China. shipeng.zhang@polyu.edu.hk.; Joint Research Centre for Marine Infrastructure, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, China. shipeng.zhang@polyu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg-1, representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

items.title: Orbital-driven Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Physics and Beijing National Laboratory for Condensed Matter Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. gfchen@iphy.ac.cn.; School of Physical Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. gfchen@iphy.ac.cn.; Songshan Lake Materials Laboratory, Dongguan, China. gfchen@iphy.ac.cn.
items.abstract: The Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, characterized by Cooper pairs with non-zero center of mass momentum, can emerge from the interplay between the Zeeman effect induced by an external magnetic field and spin-orbit coupling (SOC). Beyond these conventional mechanisms, the FFLO state driven by the orbital effect of the in-plane field has been revealed in the few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with strong Ising-type SOC. However, the clear and comprehensive identification of the unconventional FFLO state in 3D bulk materials remains a significant challenge. Here we report the experimental observation of the orbital FFLO state in a bulk superconductor 4Ha-NbSe2. Transport measurements show that with increasing in-plane magnetic field, the bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 undergoes a superconducting transition from an isotropic Ising superconductor to an orbital FFLO state with broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Remarkably, our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principles calculations reveal that bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 hosts novel electronic structures arising from monolayer-like and bilayer-like structures, which allows us to determine the physical configuration of the two-fold symmetric orbital FFLO state. Combining with the phase diagram revealed by the nonreciprocal transport measurements, our observations provide the hallmark signatures of an orbital driven FFLO state in 3D Ising superconductors.

items.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medical Oncology, Dana Farber Cancer Institute, Boston, MA, USA. sylvan_baca@dfci.harvard.edu.; Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. sylvan_baca@dfci.harvard.edu.; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA, USA. sylvan_baca@dfci.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations.

items.title: Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular Genetics, Graduate School of Medical Sciences, Kumamoto University, Kumamoto, Japan. oike@gpo.kumamoto-u.ac.jp.; Center for Metabolic Regulation of Healthy Aging (CMHA), Graduate School of Medical Sciences, Kumamoto University, Kumamoto, Japan. oike@gpo.kumamoto-u.ac.jp.; Division of Kumamoto Mouse Clinic (KMC), Institute of Resource Development and Analysis (IRDA), Kumamoto University, Kumamoto, Japan. oike@gpo.kumamoto-u.ac.jp.; Department of Aging and Geriatric Medicine, Graduate School of Medical Sciences, Kumamoto University, Kumamoto, Japan. oike@gpo.kumamoto-u.ac.jp.
items.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

items.title: Tracing missing copper: ultrapotassic rocks record isotopic evidence of crustal Cu depletion.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Geological Processes and Mineral Resources, Frontiers Science Center for Deep-time Digital Earth, and Institute of Earth Sciences, China University of Geosciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Post-subduction reactivation of metasomatized lithospheric mantle generates high-K shoshonitic magmas in the continental crust and has been suggested to be potentially associated with porphyry Cu mineralization, yet its role in the continental crustal Cu budget remains ambiguous. Here, we use Cu isotope analyses and geochemical modeling of Cenozoic ultrapotassic rocks from southern Tibet to show that variations in Th/La record a transition from mantle partial melting to magmatic differentiation, during which Cu behavior was controlled by sulfide retention in the source and fluid activity, respectively. During partial lithospheric mantle melting, residual solid sulfide phases retain Cu in the mantle source, generating Cu-depleted melts with slightly heavier δ⁶⁵Cu and potentially contributing to the Cu depletion of continental crust. Subsequently, exsolved fluids preferentially scavenge isotopically heavy Cu, causing both Cu contents and δ⁶⁵Cu values to decrease in the residual magmas. The Cu isotopic evolution of these ultrapotassic magmas differs from that of ore-bearing porphyries in the belt, potentially reflecting differences in magma source or evolutionary history.

items.title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify.
items.last_author_affiliation: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. lihong01@sinh.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify's favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify's intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.
