items.title: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study.
items.last_author_affiliation: University Hospital Basel, Endocrinology, Diabetology and Metabolism, Basel, Switzerland. mirjam.christ-crain@usb.ch.; University of Basel, Department of Clinical Research, Basel, Switzerland. mirjam.christ-crain@usb.ch.
items.abstract: Apelin, a hormone secreted by the posterior pituitary, antagonises arginine vasopressin in salt and water homoeostasis. Administration of apelin analogues increased urine output in hyponatremic rodent models, but corresponding human data are lacking. We therefore investigated intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in healthy participants with artificially induced syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis. In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study, 15 healthy adults (7 female; mean age, 28 years [SD, 8]) attended three study visits. Hyponatremia was induced using desmopressin, water loading, and hypotonic saline. Participants subsequently received high-dose [Pyr¹]apelin-13 (1800 nmol), low-dose [Pyr¹]apelin-13 (180 nmol), or placebo as a 3-hour infusion. The primary endpoint was cumulative urine output from infusion initiation until 1 hour after its completion. Neither apelin dose produced a clinically relevant difference in urine output compared with placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06277336. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation.Registration number: NCT06277336 .

items.title: Entropy-driven graded molecular selectivity in stacking-fault-programmed crystalline metallacycle membranes.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials, School of Chemistry, Tiangong University, Tianjin, PR China. sunyue@tiangong.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Membrane-based molecular separations are fundamentally constrained by the lack of precisely defined transport pathways, limiting high-flux fractionation of species with subtle size differences. Here, we report a class of stacking-fault-programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle (CCM) membranes featuring programmable nanoarchitectures constructed via interfacial coordination self-assembly. By rationally tuning the angular geometry of metallacyclic precursors, we fabricate two structurally distinct membranes (CCM-1 and CCM-2) possessing ordered microporous frameworks with well-defined transport channels. Both membranes exhibit simultaneously high solvent permeance and sharp molecular sieving, surpassing the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. Molecular simulations coupled with thermodynamic analysis reveal that the high selectivity arises from an entropy-dominated transport mechanism, governed by stacking-fault-induced misalignment of metallacycles. This misaligned stacking generates graded steric confinement, enabling precise discrimination between molecules with minimal size differences. Furthermore, we construct a cascade separation system integrating CCM-1 and CCM-2, achieving stepwise fractionation of complex ternary mixtures, including high-value pharmaceutical compounds. The CCM membrane process demonstrates significantly lower costs, carbon emissions, and energy consumption (89% reduction) compared to traditional chromatography and distillation methods. This work establishes stacking-fault programming as a powerful design principle for crystalline membranes, providing a general strategy to engineer entropy-governed transport pathways for energy-efficient and precision separations in chemical and pharmaceutical processes.

items.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Fiber Materials, Center for Advanced Low-dimension Materials, and College of Materials Science and Engineering, Donghua University, Shanghai, China. xunda.feng@dhu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water-hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

items.title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Stomatology, Tangdu Hospital & State Key Laboratory of Oral and Maxillofacial Reconstruction and Regeneration & School of Stomatology, The Fourth Military Medical University, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China. kjiao1@163.com.
items.abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA.

items.title: A mouse neuroimmune circuit that regulates allergic inflammation in the esophagus.
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Allergy and Immunology, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, Cincinnati, OH, USA. marc.rothenberg@cchmc.org.; Department of Pediatrics, University of Cincinnati College of Medicine, Cincinnati, OH, USA. marc.rothenberg@cchmc.org.
items.abstract: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, allergic disease associated with refractory pain in patients, yet the function of the nervous system in EoE pathogenesis remains ill-defined. Here we elucidate a mouse neuroimmune circuit that is linked to type 2-associated allergic inflammation and clinical responses in the esophagus, including pain. In a mouse allergy model, allergen exposure evokes pain-like behavior, increases esophageal Nav1.8+ sensory innervation density, and alters nociceptor sensitization. Thoracic dorsal root ganglia (DRG) show expression of type 2 cytokine receptors Il4ra and Il13ra1, and IL-4 and IL-13 sensitize DRG neurons to noxious agents. Mechanistically, conditional deletion of Il4ra in mouse NaV1.8+ neurons attenuate the above allergen-induced phenotypes as well as the levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); in parallel, IGF-1 receptor inhibition also dampens these disease features. Finally, EoE patient samples show increased esophageal neuronal density when compared with controls. Our findings thus describe a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that potentially contributes to EoE pathogenesis, including pain.

items.title: Polymer Brush-Mediated Surface-Initiated Polycondensation Enables sp2C-COF Thin Films with Controlled Crystallinity and High Photocatalytic Performance.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Marine Materials, Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Ningbo, 315201, China. tzhang@nimte.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Sp2-carbon-conjugated covalent organic frameworks (sp2C-COFs) hold exceptional potential as π-conjugated semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, yet their thin-film fabrication suffers from irreversible C = C linkages that impede crystallinity and morphology control. Herein, we report a polymer brush-mediated surface-initiated polycondensation (PB-SIP) strategy to synthesize the sp2C-COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology. The polymer brush layer acts as both a surface-tethered initiator and a soft interfacial regulator, enabling precise control over nucleation and crystallization kinetics. By modulating the polymer brush thickness, we achieve sp2C-COF films with enhanced crystallinity and reduced surface roughness. Notably, this method allows the growth of highly crystalline, homogeneous sp2C-COF coatings on 3D porous sponges, which exhibit near-complete photocatalytic antibacterial efficiency (99.4%) in natural sewage under visible light. This interfacial engineering paradigm advances the rational design of crystalline sp2C-COF films for energy-environment applications.

items.title: Metabolite-mediated reversal of motor hyperactivity restores ciliary function.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Membrane Biology, Beijing, China.; Tsinghua-Peking Center for Life Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China.; Beijing Frontier Research Center for Biological Structure, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China.; McGovern Institute for Brain Research, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China.; MOE Key Laboratory for Protein Science, Beijing, China.; School of Life Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: Hyperactive missense mutations can produce phenotypes that are difficult to predict from sequence alone. Here, we dissect such a discrepancy in Caenorhabditis elegans, where the kinesin mutant osm-3(A340V) shortens sensory cilia despite exhibiting elevated in vitro motility. A forward genetic screen identified osm-7, a hypodermal secreted protein, whose loss restored ciliary architecture by elevating intracellular glycerol over 100-fold. Glycerol supplementation alone recapitulated this rescue, re-establishing intraflagellar transport in neurons and modulating OSM-3(A340V) motility in vitro. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that A340V restricts neck-helix relaxation, a defect reversed by glycerol-induced conformational tuning. Our study indicates that impairment of neck-helix flexibility leads to kinesin hyperactivity in vitro and motility defects in vivo, and that metabolite-mediated conformational tuning represents a mechanism for reversing such motor defects.

items.title: Precision synthesis and mechanochemical structure-reactivity relationships of mechanophore-bearing polymers with diverse conformations.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Polymer Science and Polymer Engineering, The University of Akron, Akron, OH, USA. juw625@lehigh.edu.; Department of Chemistry, Lehigh University, Bethlehem, PA, USA. juw625@lehigh.edu.
items.abstract: While polymer conformation is known to influence mechanochemical reactivity, a platform that enables systematic evaluation of the conformational effects on mechanochemical transduction, including both chain scission and nonscissile mechanophore activation, has been lacking. Here, we synthesize a series of polymers bearing multiple nonscissile mechanophores, with controlled degrees of polymerization and systematic sidechain variation, yielding conformations spanning globule-like, coil, and rod-like structures. Ultrasound-induced chain scission reveals that the chain scission rate increases with sidechain mass across all conformations. Mechanophore activation further indicates that backbone flexibility strongly influences the extent of polymer uncoiling and the efficiency of force transduction. Molecular dynamics simulations show that steric hindrance from the sidechains influences backbone flexibility, thereby controlling polymer uncoiling and force transduction. These findings provide insights into the fundamental factors governing polymer mechanochemistry and open the door to developing stress-responsive materials with tunable responses.

items.title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pathology, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA. yir@northwestern.edu.; Driskill Graduate Program in Life Sciences, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA. yir@northwestern.edu.; Robert H. Lurie Comprehensive Cancer Center, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA. yir@northwestern.edu.; Department of Dermatology, Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine, Chicago, IL, USA. yir@northwestern.edu.
items.abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

items.title: Cell-free reconstitution reveals synergistic stabilization of microtubule doublets by PACRG and FAP20.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Biotechnology, Czech Academy of Sciences, BIOCEV, Prague, Czechia. zdenek.lansky@ibt.cas.cz.
items.abstract: Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

items.title: LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning.
items.last_author_affiliation: Comprehensive Cancer Center, The University of New Mexico, Albuquerque, NM, USA. asahu@salud.unm.edu.; Department of Computer Science, The University of New Mexico, Albuquerque, NM, USA. asahu@salud.unm.edu.
items.abstract: Representation learning in genomics often relies on sequence, expression, and network data, thereby overlooking a wealth of insights in the scientific literature. Here, we present LitGene, an interpretable transformer-based model that refines gene representations by integrating unstructured textual information with Gene Ontology annotations through contrastive learning. In evaluations across eight benchmark tasks for protein properties, LitGene achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits zero-shot prediction of GO terms, KEGG pathways, and gene-disease associations. LitGene identified ANGPTL6 as a potential candidate gene for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), supported by its differential expression in independent IPF samples, illustrating LitGene's utility for hypothesis generation. A SHAP-based interpretability tool highlights text features influencing predictions, while an automated literature-grounding framework provides corroborating support where available. Our results suggest that integrating textual and genetic information may help reduce biases associated with under-studied genes. The model is released as open-source code, along with a publicly accessible web interface at https://litgene.cs.unm.edu/ , which allows users to submit gene names, disease names, drug names, or custom text (e.g., publication abstracts) to obtain evidence-based predictions of related biomedical entities.

items.title: ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 amplifies ILC2 activation and allergic lung inflammation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Multi-Cell Systems, CAS Center for Excellence in Molecular Cell Science, Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry and Cell Biology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. bsun@sibs.ac.cn.; School of Life Science and Technology, ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China. bsun@sibs.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) from lung epithelial cells serves as a crucial alarmin to activate the lung-resident group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) and then to initiate type 2 inflammation. However, whether IL-33 has an intrinsic role in the ILC2-driven lung inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we characterize the proteomic features of mouse lung ILC2s during activation and observe an increased expression of intrinsic IL-33 in activated ILC2s. The expression of intrinsic IL-33 in lung ILC2s can be induced by the co-stimulation of cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) and exogenous IL-33. Deletion of ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 attenuates lung inflammation by restraining ILC2 proliferation and cytokine production. Mechanistically, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 promotes transcriptional activation of both inflammatory and proliferative signaling cascades. Additionally, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 localizes in the nucleus and promotes the expression of Fosl2 and Nfatc1 through promoting their chromatin accessibility, leading to increased ILC2 proliferation and type 2 cytokine production. Further, we confirm that intrinsic IL-33 can be induced by co-stimulation of CysLTs and exogenous IL-33 in human ILC2s (hILC2s), which is positively related to enhanced hILC2 responses. Collectively, our findings implicate IL-33 as a nuclear factor and intrinsic amplifier of lung-resident ILC2s, operating in a positive feedback loop downstream of exogenous IL-33 and CysLTs co-stimulation to promote allergic lung inflammation.

items.title: Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Protein Science, SciLifeLab, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Solna, Sweden. jochen.schwenk@scilifelab.se.; Sachs' Children and Youth Hospital, Södersjukhuset, Stockholm, Sweden. jochen.schwenk@scilifelab.se.
items.abstract: Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24-27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis-pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability. Paired pre- and post-exposure samples indicate temporal changes in protein levels after infection (LAP3) and vaccination (TIMP3). This multi-molecular epidemiological profiling of self-sampled blood captures dynamic immune trajectories and shorter-term variability in a population of young adults.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Functional diversity of GPCR-Gustducin complexes controls signaling output and suppresses alternative pathways.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Pharmacy, Institute of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Marburg University, Marburg, Germany. hannes.schihada@uni-marburg.de.
items.abstract: Gustducin (Ggust), the G protein mediating taste receptor signaling, is expressed not only in sensory taste cells but throughout the human body alongside numerous non-taste G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). Whether and how these receptors engage Ggust, and the functional consequences of such interactions, remain poorly understood. Here, we develop two complementary biosensors that enable direct monitoring of GPCR-Ggust interaction and downstream signaling in living cells, allowing pharmacological characterization of Ggust activity induced by non-taste GPCRs. We find that several non-taste GPCRs do not activate Ggust but instead stabilize the G protein heterotrimer and suppress basal signaling by forming unproductive GPCR-G protein complexes, whereas others induce conventional Ggust activation and signal transduction. We further show that these unproductive GPCR-Ggust complexes suppress the activation of alternative signaling pathways by sequestering receptors from other G proteins. This mode of interaction functionally partitions GPCRs into activators and inactivators of Ggust and represents a mechanism for balancing concurrent signaling pathways within a cell.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Molecular and Cellular Neuroscience, Cajal Neurosciences Center, Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas; Alcalá de Henares, Spain.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery. These findings demonstrate that E2F4 gene therapy can reverse established synaptic and cognitive deficits while preserving neuronal integrity and reshaping molecular responses to learning, identifying E2F4 phosphorylation as a potential therapeutic target for advanced AD states.

items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5. Against the best of these, TabPFN-3.5 was significantly behind on only one trait, spruce wood density, and ahead on 12 of 18, with significant gains on all three soybean traits and rice flowering time. In the soybean panel, which had the largest number of lines, its advantage was clearest. In leave-families-out cross-validation, where models were trained on some soybean families and used to predict lines from other families withheld from training, every model lost accuracy and TabPFN-3.5 performed on par with GBLUP and RKHS. That a general-purpose learner matches or exceeds decades of specialized GP models is consistent with Sutton's Bitter Lesson, which holds that methods that scale with computation eventually overtake those built on human knowledge of the domain.

items.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
items.corresponding_institution: Institut de recherches cliniques de Montreal (IRCM), Montreal, QC, Canada
items.abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo. We further show that EphB2 has a cell-autonomous, ligand-independent function in promoting CPN axon outgrowth by spatially organising actomyosin at axonal growth cones. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for EphB2 in promoting long-range axon extension and provide the first evidence that EPHB2 variants cause CC dysgenesis in humans. More broadly, our study links molecular variation in EPHB2 to individualised abnormalities in brain connectivity and provides a framework for understanding how heterogeneous circuit-level phenotypes arise in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
items.corresponding_institution: National Institute of Technology (NIT) Numazu College
items.abstract: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR). TrkB receptors are dephosphorylated by chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (CSPGs) mediated by protein-tyrosine phosphatase {sigma} (PTP{sigma} in an age-dependent manner. The model describes the generation or elimination of dendritic spines of visual cortical neurons under actin polymerization and depolymerization to establish appropriate synaptic contacts on afferent fibers of cells in the lateral geniculate nucleus. The simulations based on the model reproduced not only simple-cell-like receptive fields and orientation-direction maps but also a characteristic profile of the total number of synapses, which shows an early increase and a delayed decrease during the critical period. It is also demonstrated that the formation of direction selectivity is delayed behind the formation of orientation selectivity, which is likely promoted by the pruning of inappropriate synapses.

items.title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
items.corresponding_institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ)
items.abstract: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L. gastrophysus individuals collected from Northern and Southern American populations. We also used a subset of 13 specimens for geometric morphometrics. Phylogenetic analyses and automatic species delimitation methods consistently distinguished Northern and Southern Atlantic L. gastrophysus as separate clades, and geometric morphometrics supported the same split. The congruence among geographic, molecular, and morphometric data indicates that L. gastrophysus harbours two distinct lineages, highlighting the need for a formal taxonomic revision and separate fisheries management of northern and southern Atlantic populations.

items.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints. The detected instances are then used by a set of regressors trained under a multiple-instance, multiple-target regression setting to predict precise single-cell gene expression counts. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic and Visium-like datasets demonstrate that st2sc significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accurately segmenting cellular instances and predicting gene counts. The method can further resolve contested 2um bin in Visium HD. Application to human IPF lung showed the model can recover the subtype marker level analysis. This advancement further improves single-cell resolution analysis in spatial transcriptomics, facilitating more accurate downstream biological analyses.

items.title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
items.abstract: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate. Our method, Epilect, assigns single nanopore reads to strains from the basecaller's methylation calls, given a methylation profile for each strain, and declines to call when the evidence is weak. In the pairs above 99% ANI it correctly assigned 21.8% of the read placements that sequence could not place, at a precision of 0.959. In computational mixtures of 65 pairs of distinct strains at or above 99.5% ANI that were predicted to differ in methylation, its per-read F1 score exceeded that of the best of three sequence-based read-phasing tools by 0.25 (95% CI 0.08 to 0.37); where equally related strains were predicted to share a methylome, the comparison reversed. DNA methylation therefore supplies strain evidence on reads whose sequence carries none, and whether it will do so for a given pair of strains can be estimated before sequencing.

items.title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
items.abstract: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results. FoldX and ERIS-2 ranked the variants consistently, R60P most destabilising and Q133K neutral; the Rosetta value for Q133K was anomalously high. All systems stayed folded. R60P gave the only reproduced local change, loss of beta-strand structure at residues 60-61 and of three local hydrogen bonds. Y137A did not bring Thr158 into the pocket, and the Q133K Gln133-Asp54 polar contact became a Lys133-Asp54 salt bridge. In the principal-component landscape, departures from the WT region came from individual replicates (Y137A replicate 1; Q133K replicates 2-3), not a systematic shift. Conclusions. A substitution perturbs local structure most clearly when it breaks a beta-strand (R60P), and the stability predictions and dynamics together give a consistent ranking of the variants, including the first dynamic characterisation of Q133K. The results characterise the apo lectin domain and give a reproducible basis for interpreting FimH mutations, not for inferring affinity. Keywords: FimH; lectin domain; point mutations; molecular dynamics; folding stability ({Delta}{Delta}G); protein stability prediction; principal component analysis; urinary tract infection.

items.title: Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
items.abstract: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS). In an in vivo CRISPR screen, we nominate the MiS as the strongest dependency, and U6atac correlates strongest with E2F transcriptional programs in a clinical CRPC cohort. U6atac depletion led to mis-splicing of typical E2Fs, cell cycle arrest, and translation of a minor intron-containing E2F1 isoform (E2F1-MIRI) as a pharmacodynamic biomarker. Combined E2F activator depletion, induced further neuroendocrine (NE) specification. U6atac depletion shifted NE identity along the ASCL1 axis without the secretory granule program, and induced cell-surface antigens including DLL3, nominating MiS inhibition as a combination partner for antigen-directed agents.

items.title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
items.abstract: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis. Specifically, we use sinusoidal input describing functions to approximate the transfer characteristics of the ultrasensitive regulators and then obtain the frequency response of the closed-loop feedback system. The study suggests that the tryptophan system of E. coli has evolved to simultaneously satisfy the two properties of rapid response and noise mitigation. Particularly, the multiple feedback loop is responsible for the rapid response, while the nonlinear regulation provides effective noise mitigation.

items.title: Engineered Miniature ParTasR Enables Efficient PAMless Genome Editing
items.corresponding_institution: State Key Laboratory of Common Mechanisms Research for Major Diseases, Suzhou Institute of Systems Medicine, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union
items.abstract: TIGR-Tas system holds great promise for genome-engineering applications owing to its compact size and PAMless targeting capability. However, its low editing efficiency in mammalian cells severely limits its broader utility. Here, we engineered a highly active variant of ParTasR, termed eTasR, through structure-guided rational design of ParTasR combined with co-expression of the 3'[->]5' exonuclease TREX2. eTasR increased editing efficiency in mammalian cells from the original average 4.29% to 48.94% with an average 26.52-fold improvement, substantially outperforming the popular PAM-free version of nuclease-SpRY. Moreover, a single AAV delivery of eTasR in vivo effectively alleviates the disease phenotype of hereditary tyrosinemia type I (HT1) mouse model through targeted Hpd editing. Together, these findings establish eTasR as a compact, PAMless, and highly efficient genome editing tool with broad therapeutic and research applications.

items.title: Expanding Therapeutic Target Space from Genes to Disease-Relevant Molecular Forms with 3DisoTarget
items.corresponding_institution: The Chinese University Of Hong Kong
items.abstract: Therapeutic targets are commonly defined at the gene or canonical protein level, yet therapeutic effects are ultimately exerted through specific molecular states operating in specific biological contexts. Alternative splicing generates diverse RNA and translated protein forms whose functional consequences, disease relevance, and therapeutic vulnerabilities can differ substantially within the same gene. Resolving these disease-relevant molecular forms creates opportunities for selective intervention across complementary RNA- and protein-directed modalities, but requires reasoning across tightly coupled molecular layers, heterogeneous evidence, explicit biological constraints, and modality-specific therapeutic requirements. Here, we present Agent3Diso, a hybrid deterministic--agent multimodal framework for molecular-form-resolved therapeutic discovery. Agent3Diso establishes cross-layer molecular coherence from transcript identity and translation to structure, function, and disease context; enforces explicit molecular and therapeutic constraints through deterministic computation; and applies specialized agentic reasoning to evidence synthesis, mechanistic interpretation, conflict resolution, hypothesis critique, and experimental design. The framework evaluates therapeutic opportunities across multiple intervention modalities and translates prioritized disease-relevant molecular states into traceable hypotheses linking molecular identity, therapeutic rationale, modality, concrete intervention, uncertainty, and experimental validation. By integrating molecular resolution with constraint-aware and modality-conditioned agentic reasoning, Agent3Diso provides a framework for extending therapeutic discovery beyond gene-level targets toward disease-relevant molecular forms.

items.title: 2'-O-Methylated ncRNA condensates form a recombination center for IgH synapsis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Immunology and Genomic Medicine, Center for Cancer Immunotherapy and Immunobiology, Graduate School of Medicine, Kyoto University
items.abstract: While FBL-mediated RNA 2'-O-methylation has been linked to class switch recombination (CSR), how this epitranscriptomic mark orchestrates higher-order genomic architecture remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that FBL selectively promotes switch (S)-S DNA synapsis at the IgH locus during CSR, without affecting DNA cleavage. Both RNA-binding and catalytic activities of FBL were essential for CSR. Moreover, MED19 supported DNA cleavage and synapsis by regulating snoRNAs that guide 2'-O-methylation. Mechanistically, FBL methylated -germline transcripts (-GLTs), cis-acting noncoding RNAs forming nuclear condensates harboring machinery for RNA processing, RNP remodeling, and chromatin dynamics. FBL-mediated 2'-O-methylation governed condensate protein composition. FBL suppression aberrantly enriched nucleolar proteins, including WDR74. Crucially, low WDR74 expression in B cells promoted - and -GLT condensate fusion, thereby enhancing S-S synapsis, CSR, and IgH/c-Myc translocation, potentially contributing to poor myeloma prognosis. Altogether, our findings revealed that RNA 2'-O-methylation dictates GLT condensate composition and fusion dynamics to establish a recombination center, driving genomic DNA synapsis in B cells.

items.title: spearfish: ultrafast Δ-mapping of long reads to redundant transcriptomes
items.abstract: In a transcriptome, isoforms share most of their sequence, and gene families add further near-copies. Yet most long-read mappers treat each isoform as a separate target and repeat seeding, chaining and alignment for each. We introduce spearfish, a long-read mapper built for this redundancy. Its delta mapping ({Delta}-mapping) computes each target's alignment-score difference from the best candidate. It skips sequence that all candidates share, which cannot change the difference, and aligns where they differ once per distinct sequence rather than once per target. Seeds come from locally consistent parsing (LCP), so every isoform that contains an exon receives the same seeds in its interior. Collapsing them gives a core graph, a de Bruijn-like graph whose size is bounded by the distinct exonic sequence plus a small term per splice junction, independent of the number of isoforms. Over this graph, spearfish computes the exact colinear chaining score of every candidate transcript, sharing dynamic-programming state among transcripts via a procedure which we prove is equivalent to chaining on each transcript separately. Across RNA-seq experiments, using 32 threads, spearfish maps reads 24-102x faster than minimap2 in under a quarter of the memory, and 2.5-11.5x faster than lr-kallisto's pseudoalignment. On simulated reads it ranks the true transcript first more often than minimap2 on HiFi reads and at least as often on ONT reads. When using spearfish's {Delta}-mapping with oarfish for abundance estimation, the abundance estimates match or improve on those that make use of minimap2's alignments on both simulated reads (with or without primers and poly(A) tails) and on seven SG-NEx runs with spike-ins, and quantification is 4.1-8.8x faster than lr-kallisto in going from reads to abundances.

items.title: Pallatom2: Navigating the De Novo Protein Universe with Atom-to-Atom Modeling
items.abstract: Protein binder design requires precise coordination of molecular structure, binding geometry, and experimentally measurable performance. We introduce Pallatom2, an efficient, precise Atom-to-Atom generative model that jointly models protein sequence, backbone conformation, side-chain geometry, and target-interface contacts. A unified Atom14 representation and residue-guided sparse all-atom attention enable bidirectional information exchange between residue-level and atom-level representations, coordinating global structure with local atomic detail in a compact model of just 65.9 million parameters. Its conditioning system provides fine-grained control over binder-target engagement and global and local protein conformations, supporting diverse target-specific design requirements. In silico evaluation demonstrates broad generative capability across long-chain monomers, multi-domain proteins, and homomultimers, with monomer sampling extending to 1,600 residues. In binder design, Pallatom2 achieves state-of-the-art in silico screening performance across all nine targets with cross-method benchmark data under the reported protocols. These in silico results translate into substantial experimental success: biolayer interferometry identifies 112 active designs among 210 tested candidates (53.3%), with binders obtained for all ten experimentally evaluated targets. Six targets yield picomolar-scale apparent affinities, including K_D values of 3.96 pM for SC2RBD and 33.8 pM for PD-L1, while TNF reaches 1.166 nM. Beyond de novo discovery, starting-interface-guided BCMA design preserves association kinetics despite substantial sequence divergence; partial diffusion improves TNF affinity by up to 7.57-fold; and CDR-associated interface remodeling converts an inactive de novo nanobody into binders with apparent K_D values of 4.31 and 5.93 nM. Together, these results establish Pallatom2 as a versatile model for protein design, combining efficient atomic modeling, leading in silico screening performance, and experimentally demonstrated capabilities in high-affinity binder discovery, interface transfer, affinity maturation, and recovery of inactive designs.

items.title: A comprehensive temporal proteome and phosphoproteome dataset of Y1 adrenocortical cells under FGF2 stimulation and SOS inhibition
items.corresponding_institution: The AI Center for Health and Biomedical Research (ArCHER), National Institutes of Biomedical Innovation, Health and Nutrition, Japan.
items.abstract: The Y1 mouse adrenocortical tumor cell line is a classic model for cancer studies and ACTH mediated steroidogenesis. The KRAS gene amplification and SOS mediated activation sustain elevated ERK levels, which drive the tumor phenotype of this cell line. In addition, the mitogen FGF2 induces atypical cytotoxic stress and consequent cell death rather than proliferation in this system, imposing a strong perturbation on KRAS ERK signaling dynamics. Recent research from our group revealed that SOS is not solely responsible for KRAS activation in the Y1 cells, indicating a more complex regulatory landscape of GEFs and GAPs. This motivated the generation of a comprehensive time resolved proteome (DIA) and TMT phosphoproteome (DDA) in a 0 to 30 minute time course under FGF2 stimulation or combined with SOS inhibitor, with the presence or absence of FBS stimulation, in technical triplicate using Q Exactive and Thermo Lumos mass spectrometers, respectively. This dataset can enable latent mechanisms between the life and death switch caused by FGF2 signaling and the alternate stress response caused by impaired SOS dependent activation. This analysis yielded 14,512 phosphosites and 8,919 protein groups, where 10,471 phosphosites and 111 protein groups showed differential abundance with statistical significance (limma, FDR < 0.05). This dataset provides a versatile resource for downstream applications, which includes dynamic modeling such as ordinary differential equation based frameworks, for which temporal datasets remain scarce. The data contained in this preprint will be available on jPOST Repository after the publication.

items.title: Cerebellar transcranial AC stimulation produces frequency and phase-dependent changes in Purkinje cell complex spike waveform
items.corresponding_institution: New York University, Grossman School of Medicine
items.abstract: Cerebellar transcranial alternating current stimulation (ctACS) can improve motor learning and may speed rehabilitation. The mechanisms by which ctACS induces long-term changes in brain function that underlie these effects are not known, and knowledge of them could greatly improve the application of ctACS. One potential mechanism is alteration of Purkinje cell (PC) complex spike (CS) activity, as CS activity is a key regulator of cerebellar synaptic plasticity. Thus, we investigated how ctACS modifies CS firing rates and waveform. Extracellular recordings were obtained from cerebellar PCs in anesthetized adult rats while ctACS (250 A) was applied across a range of frequencies (0.5 - 50 Hz). The effect of ctACS on CS waveform was quantified via measuring changes in the overall size of the CS and in the number and amplitude of the spikelets that comprise a CS. ctACS produced phase-dependent modulation of the CS waveform in a majority of PCs at most tested frequencies, with 1 Hz stimulation causing modulation in all PCs tested at the frequency. The modulation reflected changes within the normal range of CS waveforms rather than an expansion of that range. Analysis of individual spikelet periods (windows) revealed that ctACS modified discrete portions of the CS, with 93.8% of PCs showing significant modulation in at least one window. Notably, the strength of phase-dependent CS waveform modulation was relatively consistent across frequencies, in contrast to the frequency dependence of simple spike (SS) entrainment. Significant modulation of spikelet amplitude was found more often than that of spikelet number; however, the relative strength of the modulation when present was similar for the two parameters. CS waveform modulation was correlated with SS entrainment strength and was strongest in PCs located near the cerebellar surface (i.e., near the apices of the folia). Together, these findings demonstrate that ctACS exerts phase-dependent control over CS waveform. Moreover, the differing frequency dependence of the waveform effects and SS firing modulation suggests that it may be possible to target CS-related plasticity selectively, providing a potential strategy for selectively modulating cerebellar learning with ctACS.

items.title: Variable penetrance of schizophrenia in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is associated with impaired, but reversible, neuronal mitophagy.
items.abstract: The 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22qDS) is a major genetic risk factor for schizophrenia (Sz). We found that iPSC-derived neurons (iNeurons) from 22qDS +Sz individuals exhibit weaker mitochondrial energetics, whereas iNeurons from individuals with the same deletion but no psychosis (22qDS -Sz) upregulate expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related genes. Here, we investigated why the +Sz group fails to undergo this compensation, finding that 22qDS +Sz iNeurons have older and more depolarized mitochondria than 22qDS -Sz or controls. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed downregulation of mitophagy-related pathways, and live imaging revealed elevated lysosomal pH. Restoring lysosomal acidity with acidifying nanoparticles improved mitophagy and, remarkably, increased the expression of mitochondrial biogenesis-related transcription factors in the +Sz neurons. We conclude that lysosomal dysfunction and impaired mitophagy differentiate 22qDS individuals who develop schizophrenia from those who do not. Mitophagy could be a novel therapeutic or preventative opportunity for Sz in the context of genetic neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
items.abstract: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear. Here, we investigated tactile distance perception in congenitally blind, late-blind, and sighted individuals. A given tactile distance is typically perceived as longer on the finger than on the forearm, reflecting distortions in cortical topography that is partially rescaled by higher-order representations of body size and shape. Congenitally blind participants showed a greater tendency to perceive identical tactile distances on the index finger as longer than those on the forearm. A similar bias was observed when comparing the forehead and face, suggesting that altered tactile distance perception in congenital blindness is not limited to body regions with extensive sensory-motor experience. Furthermore, within the late-blind group, the similarity of perceptual patterns to sighted controls, relative to congenitally blind participants, was associated with blindness duration. Together, these findings suggest that both early visual and post-blindness experience contributes to the calibration of tactile distance perception across the body, with its influence potentially extending beyond body regions extensively engaged in sensory-motor activities.

items.title: Partially shared representational space for vision and language across objects, scenes, and visual events
items.corresponding_institution: Cambridge Mind and Brain Institute, University of Cambridge
items.abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and behavioural similarity judgements of visual stimuli predict neural responses in visual cortex. Recent work shows that large language model (LLM) embeddings and similarity judgements of language descriptions also predict visual brain activity. These predictors were examined separately across modalities (vision vs language) and types (models vs human behaviour). It remains unclear to what extent these predictors explain shared or unique aspects of visual brain responses, how these contributions vary along the visual hierarchy and category-selective regions, and whether vision-language convergence depends on the stimulus type. We used three fMRI datasets progressing toward naturalistic visual experience, from objects (THINGS) to scenes (NSD) to dynamic events (BMD). For each dataset, we collected similarity judgements of visual stimuli and of their language descriptions from human participants (N = 21-35), extracted vision DNN features and LLM embeddings, and related similarity judgements and model representations to visual brain responses using representational similarity analysis (RSA) and variance partitioning. Vision-language convergence was higher within behaviour than within models. From objects to dynamic events, LLM alignment with vision-based similarity judgements increased, whereas vision DNN alignment remained stable. A shared, predominantly cross-modal component increased along the visual hierarchy and dominated explained variance in high-level visual cortex. LLMs made their largest unique contributions in face- and body-selective regions (FFA and EBA), where shared representations of vision- and language-based human similarity judgements also explained variance beyond the models. In summary, we find a partially shared representational space for vision and language in high-level visual cortex, most clearly in regions representing social information related to people and their actions. As each predictor retained unique variance, combining computational models and human behaviour across vision and language may offer a more comprehensive account of high-level visual representations.

items.title: Distal inhibition is recruited for action but not sensation in the primate superior colliculus
items.abstract: Sensorimotor transformation requires neural circuits to coordinate excitation and inhibition, but how and whether this organization changes as the circuit transitions from processing sensation to action remain unresolved. We recorded laminar local field potentials across superior colliculus (SC) layers in four male macaques and computed current source density to resolve transmembrane currents during saccades to a target at one of eight isoradial directions. During the visual response, excitation was spatially confined to the receptive field, with little modulation at distant sites. During saccade generation, local excitation remained strongest for movements toward the receptive field, while inhibition extended across the SC map, including locations where spiking remained at baseline. Because the same recordings detected distal inhibition during movement, its absence during vision cannot reflect insufficient sensitivity, indicating that distal inhibition is selectively recruited during action. After saccade completion, excitation emerged regardless of saccade direction, potentially reflecting a rebound from, or release of, the preceding inhibition. These patterns were only partly reflected in spiking activity, which primarily captured local excitation, unmasking circuit dynamics largely invisible at the level of neuronal output. Together, our findings reveal a striking reconfiguration of SC population dynamics across sensorimotor transformation, spanning from spatially restricted excitation during sensation, to local excitation coupled with distal inhibition during movement generation, then to global post-movement excitation. Thus, fixed circuit architecture can express a sequence of behaviorally gated excitation-inhibition states largely invisible to spiking output.

items.title: Hormone therapy attenuates menopause-related impairments in motor cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity
items.abstract: The menopause marks the permanent cessation of menstruation via a decline in endogenous hormone production. This transition influences brain health, yet its effects on motor cortical excitability and spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) are poorly understood. Across two sites, 46 females were categorised as pre-menopausal (PRE, age 28{+/-}7 years), perimenopausal (PERI, 50{+/-}3 years), post-menopausal (POST, 60{+/-}8 years), or combined continuous hormone therapy users (HT, 52{+/-}3 years). Transcranial magnetic stimulation was used to measure corticospinal excitability (MEP/Mmax), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) before, then 10 and 30 min after a paired associative stimulation (PAS) protocol (25-ms interstimulus interval). Serum hormone concentrations were quantified from venous blood. Resting corticospinal excitability and SICI were not different between groups before the PAS protocol. However, a group x time interaction (p=0.0152) for MEP/Mmax revealed distinct STDP responses. PRE showed a significant increase in corticospinal excitability following PAS (+48%, p=0.0045), whereas PERI and POST showed no facilitation (p[≥]0.2079). Between groups, both PRE and HT exceeded PERI, and HT also exceeded POST; however, HT users showed a smaller, non-significant increase (+32%, p=0.0666) that collectively distinguished them from the blunted responses of PERI and POST. The magnitude of STDP was not associated with any single hormone or chronological age across the whole sample of participants. These findings provide the first evidence that motor cortical STDP is influenced by menopause stage. With blunted responses in PERI and POST, yet preserved responses in HT users, these data have implications for motor learning and rehabilitation across the female adult lifespan.

items.title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy targeting CD94 for cytotoxic T/NK cell malignancies
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy against pan-B-cell antigens is highly effective, but analogous approaches for T-cell lymphomas risk prolonged T-cell aplasia. We developed a CAR-T therapy targeting a post-thymic antigen, CD94, a receptor with restricted expression in normal tissues and immune cells but enriched in cytotoxic T/NK-cell malignancies. Second generation CD94 CAR T cells generated using a specific and high-affinity anti-CD94 monoclonal antibody showed potent and selective cytotoxicity against CD94-positive tumor cells in vitro and completely eradicated NK-cell leukemia xenografts and patient-derived xenograft models of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma and NK/T-cell lymphoma in vivo. Incorporation of truncated B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) as a safety switch enabled rapid elimination of CAR T cells using anti-BCMA T-cell engagers or anti-BCMA antibody-drug conjugate. Super-resolution microscopy demonstrated intracellular sequestration of CD94 by the CAR, preventing fratricide. Collectively, these findings support anti-CD94 CAR-T therapy as a promising and novel treatment for cytotoxic T/NK-cell neoplasms.

items.title: IFT20 mediates trafficking of ciliary proteins to support mammalian motile ciliogenesis in testicular efferent ductules and respiratory tract.
items.abstract: Cilia are antenna-like organelles that extend from the apical cell membrane and are broadly present in eukaryotes. They are classified as primary and motile types; the later including sperm flagellum and somatic multiciliated cells present within the reproductive and respiratory systems. Intraflagellar transport (IFT) provides delivery of cargo for cilia assembly and maintenance. Of the multiple protein components, IFT20, a component of the intraflagellar transport-B (IFT-B) complex, is required for cargo delivery anterograde during primary cilia and mouse sperm flagellum formation, and is also known to link the Golgi with the primary cilia; however, its role in motile cilia from somatic cells is so far unknown. The objective of this study is to investigate, in mice, the role of IFT20 in motile cilia of somatic cells. We used a FOXJ1-Cre mouse to conditionally delete Ift20 only in motile cilia. We found that most Ift20 conditional knock out (cKO) mice were viable and none showed left-right asymmetry defects nor hydrocephalus, though they exhibited reduced body weight. Compared to control mice, adult cKO males were subfertile with significantly shortened motile cilia and decreased ciliary beating frequency (CBF) in efferent ductules (EDs). Examination of ciliary ultrastructure in EDs revealed partial absence or displacement of the peripheral doublet microtubules (DMTs), as well as defects in both the inner and outer dynein arms and the central pair apparatus. In addition, the lumen of EDs were significantly dilated and filled with aggregated sperm. Sperm aggregation also led to a dilatation of the lumen of the seminiferous tubules and testicular atrophy, accompanied by an increased number of degenerated germ cells that were sloughed into the lumen. The tracheal cilia were minimally shortened and had reduced CBF, however, they had normal appearing ultrastructure. In contrast to control mice, analysis of cKO ciliated cells, in both EDs and trachea, showed an accumulation of the central apparatus protein SPAG16, SPAG17, the outer dynein arm DNAI2, and inner dynein arm DNAH2 in the apical region of the cytoplasm. These data indicate that IFT20 is essential in sperm and somatic ciliated cells from ED and trachea, to sustain flagella/cilia formation and beat frequency and suggest that, IFT20 assists in trafficking ciliary structures from the cytoplasm to the motile axoneme.

items.title: Artifact-guided restoration improves visualization of cellular ultrastructure in cryo-FIB-SEM volumes
items.abstract: Cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) enables volumetric imaging of vitrified specimens, but charging artifacts, high noise and weak membrane contrast hinder the interpretation of biological features. Here we present a two-stage deep-learning-based framework that translates cryo-FIB-SEM images toward the domain of conventional room-temperature FIB-SEM (RT-FIB-SEM), suppressing large-scale charging artifacts and enhancing local membrane signal. Held-out synthetic tests show improved agreement with constructed reference targets, while results on four experimental cryo-FIB-SEM datasets show reduced visible artifacts and clearer membrane features. Processed cryo-FIB-SEM volumes from our two-stage model can be directly analyzed by tools designed for RT-FIB-SEM, and an existing pretrained segmentation model is applied to our model output, yielding extensive predictions of membrane structures. This post-acquisition approach improves the visual interpretability and downstream analysis capabilities of cryo-FIB-SEM data without modifying imaging hardware.

items.title: Pleckstrin Homology-based proximity-labeling reveal lipid-associated interactomes
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Plant & Environmental Sciences, Copenhagen Plant Science Center (CPSC), University of Copenhagen, Thorvaldsensvej 40, 1871 Frederiksberg, Denmark
items.abstract: Phosphoinositides (PIPs) organize membrane-associated signaling, but the proteins associated with specific PIPs and their regulation remain poorly characterized. Here, we establish a lipid-binding domain-based proximity-labeling approach to map PIP-associated proteomes in vivo, and applied it to plant cells. We identify distinct protein networks associated with PI4P and PI(4,5)P2, linking these lipids to membrane signaling, transport, and organization. Using molecular dynamics simulations and in vivo validation we further reveal how two previously uncharacterized PIP effectors, ALTERED RESPONSE TO GRAVITY-LIKE1 (ARL1) and HYPERSENSITIVE RESPONSE 1 (HIR1), engage with PIPs to regulate their membrane localization and nanodomain organization. Finally, we outline how PIP-associated proteomes change in response to prominent abiotic stress conditions, including salt and heat, in Arabidopsis. Our work establishes a platform for investigating lipid-associated proteomes in vivo and reveals how PIP-specific and stress-responsive protein networks contribute to membrane organization and cellular responses.

items.title: Endogenous cAMP production within tissue fibroblasts is required for spontaneous fibrosis resolution
items.abstract: Pathologic myofibroblasts (MFs) are pivotal effector cells in the development of persistent tissue fibrosis following parenchymal injury, and their activation and accumulation has been linked to a failure to phenotypically dedifferentiate and thus to resist apoptosis. The second messenger cyclic AMP (cAMP) has been shown to induce MF dedifferentiation and restore their sensitivity to apoptosis in vitro, but its endogenous role within MFs during fibrosis resolution in vivo has not been explored. To test the hypothesis that cAMP generation and signaling within fibroblasts is essential for fibrosis resolution, we leveraged the spontaneously resolving nature of the single-dose intrapulmonary and subcutaneous bleomycin models in mice with an inducible and fibroblast-specific abrogation of cAMP generation owing to deletion of the stimulatory G protein (Gs). Abolishing cAMP generation in fibroblasts after peak lung fibrosis was established led to a failure of the resolution with single-cell RNA seq demonstrating conspicuous differences in pathway enrichment and cellular cross-talk not only in fibroblasts, but also within macrophages and epithelial cells. Spontaneous resolution of skin fibrosis in a model of scleroderma similarly required cAMP production in dermal fibroblasts. We conclude that cAMP generation within fibroblasts after tissue fibrosis has been established is required for its spontaneous resolution in the lung and skin. Our findings provide new insights into factors governing the outcome of tissue fibrosis as well as a mechanistic basis that helps to explain the therapeutic efficacy and ultimate potential of newly available and emerging cAMP-elevating agents.

items.title: Polarized Canine Liver Organoid Monolayers Capture Features of Western Diet-Induced Hepatic Metabolic Reprogramming Across Transcriptomic, Lipidomic, and Biogenic Amine Signatures
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Chemistry, University of Victoria
items.abstract: Liver responses to Western-diet (WD) exposure remain incompletely defined, partly because conventional rodent models and immortalized hepatic cell lines incompletely recapitulate species-specific features of liver biology. Here, we established polarized epithelial monolayers from canine liver organoids derived from healthy beagles and beagles exposed to a WD for 8 weeks. We then used this platform to characterize diet-induced hepatic reprogramming and to explore differential responses to two SGLT2 inhibitors, dapagliflozin and bexagliflozin. The monolayers developed reproducible apical-basal polarity, with transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) values of 123-335 {Omega} cm2, enabling compartment-resolved sampling. Bulk transcriptomics, lipidomics, and biogenic amine profiling each independently separated WD-derived from healthy monolayers. Periodic acid-Schiff staining provided qualitative support for this diet-associated molecular signature, showing increased carbohydrate-rich material consistent with glycogen accumulation in WD-derived monolayers. By contrast, 24-hour apical exposure to dapagliflozin or bexagliflozin at 20 M produced no detectable transcriptomic differences and only weak, context-dependent metabolomic separation, which was restricted to the apical compartment in the untargeted metabolomics dataset. These findings establish canine liver organoid-derived polarized monolayers as a tractable in vitro platform that captures WD-induced hepatic reprogramming across transcriptomic, lipidomic, and biogenic amine readouts, while providing a foundation for future targeted studies of candidate interventions for diet-associated hepatic dysfunction.

items.title: COPS5 maintains spermatogenesis gene expression and piRNA-mediated transposon silencing
items.abstract: COPS5 (CSN5/JAB1), a multifunctional subunit of the COP9 signalosome, is required for male germ cell survival, but how it acts is unclear. We combined a germ cell specific Cops5 conditional knockout (cKO) mouse model with transcriptomic, proteomic and small RNA analysis of P16 testes. Cops5 loss caused progressive spermatogenic arrest after postnatal day 16. At both the mRNA and protein levels, 59 genes were downregulated, including piRNA biogenesis factors such as PIWIL1/MIWI, PIWIL2/MILI, Tudor domain proteins, DDX4, MAEL and MOV10L1. In Cops5 cKO testes, pachytene piRNAs decreased in abundance and diversity, falling from about 56% to 18~30% of total small RNAs, while the 1U bias was retained. Consistent with this, the transposable elements LINE1 and IAP were activated. In human testes, COPS5 was high in spermatogenic cells but reduced by 56.4% in the germ cells of patients with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). Thus, COPS5 maintains piRNA homeostasis and transposon silencing, and its loss may contribute to human spermatogenic failure.

items.title: Granger-causal inference to study crosstalk between two actin regulators in live cell imaging
items.abstract: Dynamic actin filament assembly at the cell membrane drives cell migration. Its regulation is governed by functionally overlapping actin regulators and complex feedback loops that hinder conventional perturbation-approaches from dissecting actin regulatory pathways. Here we present an extended, perturbation-free statistical framework based on Granger causality (GC). The framework rests on statistical models that capture the interdependence among subcellular fluctuations of molecular and cell morphodynamic activities extracted from three-channel live-cell imaging. Applied to the inference of cause-effect relationships among actin, its regulators and cell-edge movement, the GC analysis identifies distinct regulatory hierarchies of the actin regulators Arp2/3, VASP and mDia1 on actin dynamics and cell edge movement. Notably, we find that mDia1 plays a critical role in translating actin filament assembly into cell-edge movement, whereas Arp2/3 and VASP function primarily as regulators of polymer extension. By imaging three actin reporters simultaneously, we also demonstrate that the GC framework can distinguish the distinct causal roles of filamentous vs monomeric actin in driving cell edge movements.

items.title: Re-evaluating donor-cell identity after hiPSC-RGC transplantation in mouse models of optic neuropathy
items.corresponding_institution: University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine - Philadelphia, PA
items.abstract: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by permanent visual field loss caused by the death of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. We investigated the potential of transplanting human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived RGCs (hiPSC-RGCs) in two mouse models of optic nerve degeneration: N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (NMDA) and optic nerve crush (ONC), and characterized their ability to survive, integrate, and form synaptic connections in a degenerated retina. Follow-up studies, including immunohistochemistry and patch-clamping experiments, one year after intravitreal injections, determined the location, identity, and function of the donor GFP+ve fluorescent cells within the mouse retinas and their similarity to native RGCs. Upon closer inspection, some GFP+ve cells detected in a few retinal sections did not stain for the human-specific marker and were detected in retinal layers outside the expected ganglion cell layer (GCL)/ inner nuclear layer (INL) regions. These findings highlight complications in the interpretation of RGC transplantation studies.

items.title: Joint Analysis of Common Regulatory and Rare Coding Variants for Improved Power in Kernel Association Tests
items.abstract: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. We present PrediXSKAT, a kernel-based rare variant association framework that incorporates the surrounding cis-regulatory landscape by estimating its impact on gene expression via PrediXcan. PrediXSKAT embeds predicted gene expression directly into the Sequence Kernel Association Test kernel through element-wise similarity weighting, concentrating rare variant signal among individuals who share concordant genetic and regulatory backgrounds. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that PrediXSKAT increases power over standard kernel-based testing under biologically realistic conditions where a proportion of tested variants carry small, mixed-direction effects. Type I error rates are controlled in the absence of association. Power gains persist across a range of sample sizes and causal variant architectures. Applied to whole-genome sequencing data from the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, PrediXSKAT recapitulates established disease loci and amplifies signals at previously unreported candidate genes without indiscriminately inflating genome-wide results. PrediXSKAT provides a generalizable and extensible framework for the joint analysis of common regulatory and rare coding variants. The approach can be applied to any kernel-based set test and extended to jointly consider multiple genes within the same biological pathway, offering a principled strategy for improving rare variant discovery in large-scale sequencing studies of complex disease.

items.title: OrthoSimulator: Empirically trained simulations for ground-truth benchmarking of orthology inference
items.abstract: Orthology inference is foundational for comparative genomics, enabling the reconstruction of phylogenetic relationships and transfer of biological knowledge between species. Methods often infer different orthogroups and orthologous relationships, making robust benchmarking essential for evaluating their accuracy.
