In >97% of sporadic ALS patients, nuclear TDP-43 in motor neurons mislocalizes and aggregates in the cellular cytoplasm (gain-of-function). A parallel reduction in nuclear TDP-43 in ALS patients leads to a loss-of-function in mRNA binding and splicing regulation. Using our machine learning platform, we discovered ACE-339, a novel, orally bioavailable small molecule that disrupts insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Using in vitro, in vivo and in silico models, we show that ACE-339 directly targets aggregated forms of TDP-43. ACE-339 interacts directly with TDP-43 hexamers, disaggregates recombinant TDP-43 and rescues both gain- and loss-of-function phenotypes of TDP-43 in cells. ACE-339 functionally rescues TDP-43 dependent mis-splicing and synaptic activity. Lastly, ACE-339 rescues disease associated phenotypes in two independent mouse models of TDP-43 pathology. In addition, we now have a catalog of TDP-43 disaggregating compounds that are being developed further to be tested in clinical trials in patients with ALS and other TDP-43 proteinopathies.

items.title: Dance experience shapes local brain dynamics and shared responses during naturalistic action observation
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Psychology, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China
items.abstract: Skilled action observation unfolds over time: viewers follow changing movements, coordinate what they see with prior experience, and form a response to the performance as a whole. Dance expertise is known to alter action-related activation and the similarity of spectators' responses, but its association with local BOLD dynamics during an extended performance remains unclear. We reanalyzed fMRI from 14 professional dancers and 11 novices watching the same 33-minute dance film; one choreographer provided a separate reference. In the first 678 volumes, we measured voxelwise brain entropy (BEN) using sample entropy before summarizing it in Schaefer 400 parcels and seven networks, calculated windowed entropy from parcel-mean signals, and examined intersubject correlation (ISC) and four group-blind coactivation patterns (CAPs). After adjustment for local gray-matter volume, age, sex, and motion, dancers had higher static BEN in 32 parcels and six networks (FDR q < .05). Dynamic BEN was higher in control and default-mode networks. Dancer-dancer ISC exceeded novice-novice ISC in five networks. Dancers occupied one common CAP less often and another more often, while performer synchrony and acceleration tracked state occurrence across spectators. These converging observations show that dance experience is expressed in local temporal irregularity, shared spectator responses, and the distribution of brain states during naturalistic action observation.

items.title: From Adalimumab to orally administered secretory IgA: preclinical characterization of ABC-301
items.abstract: Reformatting therapeutic immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies into secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) may provide an alternative architecture for mucosal drug delivery. We characterized ABC-301, a recombinant human sIgA1 incorporating the antigen-binding regions of Adalimumab, and evaluated its human tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF) neutralization, oral activity in experimental colitis, tissue biodistribution, and susceptibility to patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibodies. ABC-301 retained human TNF binding and functional neutralization in vitro. Its whole-molecule molar neutralization IC50 was approximately 3.3-fold lower than that of Adalimumab, a difference of approximately 1.6-fold after normalization to theoretical binding-site number. In dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, oral ABC-301 attenuated colon shortening and reduced colonic inflammatory myeloid populations and tissue inflammatory biomarkers relative to untreated DSS controls. Following oral administration, iodine-125-associated radioactivity was predominantly detected in gastrointestinal compartments. In seven patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibody preparations, ABC-301 showed reduced functional susceptibility to inhibition compared with Adalimumab. These findings provide a preclinical proof of concept for IgG-to-sIgA reformatting.

items.title: Intestinal epithelial differentiation factor HNF4α restrains homeostatic interferon signaling and is required for its full induction during Salmonella infection
items.abstract: Intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) must interpret microbial signals to transcriptionally adapt their identity and function. Which transcription factors (TFs) mediate those adaptations, and whether competing transcriptional pathways signal within the same or in different IEC subpopulations, remains unclear. We find that microbiota colonization shifts nearly all IECs toward an interferon-driven inflammatory program at the expense of genes involved in enterocyte differentiation and metabolism. These opposing gene expression programs are associated with different TF motifs and are inversely correlated within individual cells. We discover that HNF4, a TF central to enterocyte differentiation, acts as a brake on interferon signaling in vitro. In accord, loss of HNF4 in IECs in mice elevates baseline interferon-stimulated gene expression but prevents its full induction during infection with the bacterial pathogen Salmonella. Together our findings reveal a novel mechanism by which opposing intestinal epithelial differentiation and interferon signaling programs interact within the same cell to maintain proper transcriptional control and homeostasis.

items.title: Nuclear blebs are rupture-prone restricted compartments of the nucleus
items.abstract: Nuclear blebs are abnormal herniations of the cell nucleus that cause nuclear rupture and dysfunction. The biophysical principles underlying nuclear blebs and ruptures remain to be fully elucidated. Using nuclear localization signal green fluorescent protein (NLS-GFP) we tracked nuclear bleb rupture dynamics. Upon nuclear rupture, the nuclear bleb NLS-GFP loss rate is significantly faster than the nuclear body, whereas non-blebbed nuclei ruptures show no difference in NLS-GFP loss rates between the site of nuclear rupture and body. Micromanipulation compression induced nuclear bleb rupture recapitulates 5-fold nuclear bleb loss rate. Furthermore, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) in the intact nuclear bleb is significantly slower than recovery in the nuclear body. Confocal imaging reveals that the transition from the nuclear bleb to body is significantly constrained. Thus, we reveal the nuclear bleb as a restricted compartment and nuclear rupture site, both of which greatly affect nuclear functions.

items.title: Deciphering the genetic bases of canine longevity
items.corresponding_institution: Univ Rennes, CNRS - UMR6290, IGDR (Institut de genetique et developpement de Rennes) Canine Genetics Team, 35043 Rennes, France. French Cani-DNA Biological Reso
items.abstract: Across dog breeds, the inverse correlation between body size and lifespan is well documented, but its genetic basis remains poorly understood, in part because size and lifespan are confounded at the breed level. Here, we assembled the Cani-DNA discovery cohort of 540 dogs from 27 breeds, with 20 dogs per breed, genotyped by low-pass whole-genome sequencing and imputation. We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of breed-average body weight, breed-median lifespan and individual age at death, and tested the age-at-death loci for replication in the GRLS replication cohort of 3,024 Golden Retrievers. The GWAS of breed-average body weight recovered established body-size loci, confirming that the cohort could detect known associations. Of the 69 breed-weight loci, 30 were shared with breed-median lifespan, and at all of them the allele increasing body weight was associated with shorter lifespan. At the individual level, age at death, with breed-average body weight as a covariate, identified loci distinct from all breed-level loci. Three of them, the CDH4, TSHZ3 and TSC22D2 loci, replicated in the GRLS replication cohort. In humans, CDH4 and TSHZ3 have been implicated in longevity, and the region orthologous to the TSC22D2 locus has been associated with markers of biological ageing. Together, these results identify genetic variation associated with the lifespan of individual dogs beyond breed body size, and support the dog as a model in which genetic leads on ageing can be identified.

items.title: A spatial correlation function approach reveals zonation loss in liver disease
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures the expression of hundreds to thousands of genes in each cell together with the cell's position in the tissue. Here we use spatial correlation functions, which describe how the correlation of gene expression between cells decays with distance, to quantify how the spatial organization of gene expression changes in disease. From the correlation function of each gene, or of each pair of genes, we extract two numbers: a susceptibility, which measures how strongly gene expression is correlated between nearby cells, and a correlation length, the distance over which this correlation extends. Both are in physical units and can be compared directly between samples and conditions. We apply the approach to healthy and fibrotic mouse liver using newly generated data, and to healthy and fibrotic human liver using published data. Correlations between gene pairs identify genes of the same hepatocyte zone, and assign a zone to 1,266 genes that are not known zonation markers. The two fibrotic conditions differ: CCl4 injection in mice produces a moderate reorganization in which some genes lose spatial correlation and others gain it, while in human fibrosis almost every measured gene loses it. Changes in spatial correlation are only weakly related to changes in expression level. For instance Cyp2c29 and Pon1 partially lose their spatial correlation in treated mice, although their average expression does not consistently fall. Spatial correlation functions therefore detect changes in tissue organization that measurements of expression level alone miss.

items.title: Efficient genome graphs indexing, querying and visualization with gfaidx and gfaidx-viz
items.abstract: Genome graphs enable the analysis of genetic variation across many genomes, but exploring individual regions remains computationally demanding. We present gfaidx, a general-purpose indexer giving fast, low-memory access to pangenome, assembly, and de Bruijn graphs in GFA format. It retrieves gene-sized subgraphs and their haplotypes over 100-fold faster than existing tools such as ODGI and vg, and can index human pangenome-scale graphs on a personal computer. The accompanying gfaidx-viz interactively visualizes pre-indexed human pangenomes. Both are freely available at https://github.com/fawaz-dabbaghieh/gfaidx and https://github.com/fawaz-dabbaghieh/gfaidx-viz

items.title: Chimeric and Outward Reads in Short-Read RNA Sequencing Data: A Unified Circular RNA Assembly Framework
items.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are RNA molecules that play important roles in regulating gene expression, yet detecting and assembling them from short read RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data remains challenging. Most methods rely on chimeric reads that cross the back-splicing junction (BSJ), but for lowly expressed circRNAs, these reads are often absent, so many circRNAs go undetected. In this work, we propose TERRACE 2.0, a method that addresses this limitation by leveraging an additional but underutilized signal: outward reads. These are paired-end reads that point away from each other when aligned to the reference genome, which is a direct consequence of sequencing a fragment from a circRNA. Together, this multi-signal framework enables circRNAs to be detected and assembled more accurately from short-read RNA-seq data. TERRACE 2.0 infers candidate BSJs from outward reads by testing which ones give a fragment length consistent with the library, reconstructs each full-length circRNA from a splice graph, and combines outward and chimeric reads in a single representation that selects among the candidates jointly. On eight human tissue samples, TERRACE 2.0 has the best average F-score with and without gene annotations. On an alignment that retains more chimeric reads, it is the most accurate assembler in every sample, while its predecessor TERRACE loses much of its precision. Most notably, outward reads are involved in 36% to 56% of the true circRNAs that TERRACE misses, and on simulated data TERRACE 2.0 also has the highest recall and F-score.

items.title: Optimal Predictivity of Random Signatures: Causes and Good Modeling Practices
items.abstract: In high-throughput omics data, randomly-selected sets of markers ("signatures") have large and often optimal phenotypic predictivity. This creates problems of over-interpretation of biological and predictive importance of signatures, of bioinformatics algorithms and expert knowledge-driven selection. We conduct first an empirical study establishing that the phenomenon occurs across a variety of types of datasets/omics types and algorithms (224 combinations, >120 million models fitted). Random signatures are systematically reproducible across datasets. We develop a comprehensive theoretical framework, encompassing definitions, feasibility and impossibility theorems, and analytical formulas. The theory reveals as necessary and sufficient causes of these anomalous behaviors, the existence of large equivalence classes of optimally predictive feature sets, and their structure of information equivalences. We validate the theory with additional experiments and propose good practices intended to strengthen scientific rigor. Our findings apply to both algorithmic discovery and expert knowledge-driven signature selection, and to both existing and future algorithms and expert criteria. They also extend to all types of data with similar equivalence classes of optimal predictors.

items.title: Harmonized sample metadata and processed cortical and hippocampal transcriptomes from wild-type and Alzheimer's disease model mice
items.abstract: Public mouse brain single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) datasets are difficult to reuse across studies because sample annotations are heterogeneous and incomplete. We harmonized sample-level metadata for 2,005 cortex and hippocampus samples from 389 studies, covering wild-type (WT) controls and Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related mouse models. Usable count data from 1,863 samples in 360 studies were uniformly processed into 12,628,942 cell and nuclear profiles with cell-type annotations. Expression-based indicators were consistent with the annotated sequencing protocol and sex, and integrated microglial profiles recovered established AD-associated signatures. To illustrate cross-study use, we asked whether microglial AD--WT expression differences varied with age and between cortex and hippocampus, using covariate-adjusted expression reconstructed with Kanade. Genes separated into groups with predominantly negative or positive AD--WT contrasts, including a group whose age-associated contrasts differed between cortex and hippocampus. These findings demonstrate the utility of harmonized metadata for investigating age- and region-dependent AD-associated transcriptional differences across studies. The resource supports explicit, reproducible cohort definitions across public mouse brain datasets.

items.title: Decompose and Recompose: Reference-Centered Multimodal Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Enzyme Turnover Prediction
items.corresponding_institution: Faculty of Applied Sciences, Macao Polytechnic University, Macao SAR, China
items.abstract: Predicting enzyme turnover numbers ($k_{\mathrm{cat}}$) from protein sequences and reaction chemistry helps prioritize candidates in virtual screening. Reliable ranking requires distinguishing activity differences between enzyme--reaction pairs. Recent interaction models combine enzyme and chemical information, but two representation challenges remain. First, reactants and products have distinct roles in catalysis: reactants are recognized and transformed, whereas products are formed and released. Yet these models merge the two sides before enzyme interaction, leaving the enzyme's response to each role implicit. Second, enzyme representations produced by cross-attention mix reaction-dependent changes with an enzyme-specific background shared across chemical conditions. This mixture can obscure activity-relevant differences between samples. To address these challenges, we introduce EnzRef, a lightweight multimodal framework that adapts frozen protein language models by decomposing reaction chemistry into reactant and product conditions, expressing each conditioned enzyme response relative to that enzyme's background, and recomposing the responses for activity prediction. Reference-Centered Cross-Attention uses each enzyme's average residue response as an internal reference to expose role-specific conditional deviations. Symmetry-Aware Semantic Recomposition encodes the mean deviation and directed role contrast into a joint activity representation. With 1.72M trainable parameters beyond the frozen encoder, EnzRef achieves state-of-the-art source-domain prediction on CatPred-DB and zero-shot transfer to TurNuP-DB. On unseen enzymes, it improves mean $R^2$ by 19.8% relative to MCKcat, the strongest baseline, without target-domain adaptation.

items.title: Precision in Predicting Catalytic Performance of Medium Chain Dehydrogenase: A Benchmark Data Set and Comparative Metrics
items.abstract: Medium-chain dehydrogenases/reductases are highly versatile oxidoreductases with broad industrial relevance but complex structure-function relationships that continue to challenge catalytic performance prediction. A Benchmark for Medium-Chain Dehydrogenases (MCDBench) is introduced as a rigorously curated benchmark dataset comprising 792 enzyme-substrate-cofactor combinations, including experimentally validated inactive cases obtained under standardized conditions. MCDBench spans 36 chemically diverse alcohol substrates, representative MDR subclasses, and multiple cofactor types, enabling systematic evaluation of model generalization. Benchmarking four representative activity-prediction models (DLKcat, UniKP, TurNuP, and CataPro) shows that correlations with experimental activities remain modest under standardized conditions, and that distinguishing active from inactive catalytic space remains a practical challenge across enzyme classes and substrate types. Analysis points to a positive-data skew inherited from widely used biochemical databases and the relative scarcity of validated negative samples as key factors shaping this behavior. By providing a standardized benchmark that integrates experimentally validated negative cases, MCDBench offers a unified experimental and computational framework to help the field measure and further improve the discrimination of active and inactive catalytic space for biocatalyst design.

items.title: Aging enteric neurons develop chromatin remodeling, DNA damage and a senescence-like phenotype
items.abstract: Aging is associated with gastrointestinal dysfunction, yet the cellular and molecular changes underlying aging of the enteric nervous system (ENS), the cellular network that controls gut motility and digestion, remain poorly characterized. Here, we investigated whether enteric neurons show canonical hallmarks of aging in mice and humans. We assessed age-related changes in enteric neurons of the jejunum and colon in mice aged 2, 13-15, and 22-24 months using immunofluorescence, transmission electron microscopy, calcium imaging, and network morphology analysis, and compared selected markers between young and aged human gut tissue. Enteric neurons accumulated DNA damage with age in both the jejunum and colon, with nitrergic neurons exhibiting a greater burden of damage than cholinergic neurons. Increased H3K9me3-DAPI colocalization, consistent with senescence-associated heterochromatin foci, was already seen at 15 months in both regions, revealing a potentially early driver of age-related gut changes. At 24 months, colonic neuron numbers decreased, while average neuronal soma size was increased and approximately 25-30% of neurons expressed cytoplasmic p21, a marker of senescence. Aged neurons showed enlarged, less circular mitochondria and increased pPDH immunoreactivity, indicative of declining neuronal activity. Consistent with remodeling of myenteric plexus architecture, neuronal calcium responses increased upon electrical stimulation while decreasing after agonist application. DSS-induced colitis did not reproduce the DNA damage, heterochromatin, or p21 changes seen with age, implying a direct role in the latter. Human aged enteric neurons showed higher {gamma}H2AX and H3K9me3 intensities. These data demonstrate that enteric neurons develop a senescence-like phenotype with age, and identify neuronal senescence as an underexplored aspect of ENS aging.

items.title: Elucidating the Sodium Channel-Targeting Anti-Seizure Medication Interactome: A Drug-Target Pathway Analysis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, University of Virginia, Charlottesville, VA 22901, USA; Departments of Neuroscience, Pharmacology, Biomedical Engineering, Microbiology
items.abstract: Epilepsy is a common neurological disorder in both children and adults, primarily managed with anti-seizure medications (ASMs). Sodium channel blockers are among the most commonly used ASMs. These medications exhibit distinct spectra of efficacy and side effect profiles. These likely result from different off-target interactions, protein binding profiles, and subunit selectivity that remain poorly characterized. We developed a neural network-based computational pipeline to systematically elucidate the molecular targets and associated biological pathways of selected sodium channel-modulating ASMs: carbamazepine, lamotrigine, eslicarbazepine, licarbazepine, lacosamide, phenytoin, and cenobamate. Using the DRIFT (Drug-target identification based on chemical similarity) algorithm for proteome-wide target prediction, we identified protein targets for these ASMs. The sodium channel alpha subunit family was the highest-ranked target for every drug except cenobamate, for which it ranked second behind the GABA-A receptor. Pathway mapping in the Reactome database revealed both shared and drug-specific biological processes. Furthermore, molecular docking studies elucidated the atomistic interactions between the drugs and the predicted targets. Specifically, the predicted target landscape varied from eslicarbazepine and licarbazepine (59 predicted targets each) to lacosamide (18). Pathway analysis revealed recurrent enrichment in rapid depolarisation and the interaction between L1 and ankyrins shared across all drugs, alongside predicted off-targets, including the cannabinoid CB1 receptor for phenytoin and the carbonic anhydrases for lacosamide. Molecular docking supported these predictions, with binding scores ranging from -24 to -31 kcal/mol. Overall, this work provides a systems-level view of NaV-targeting ASM pharmacology and a hypothesis-generating framework to prioritize mechanistic and combination studies of these medications in epilepsy.

items.title: Age-associated skeletal muscle dysfunction with spinal cord pathology in an App knock-in model of Alzheimer's disease
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Pharmacotherapeutics and Informatics, Fujita Health University School of Medicine
items.abstract: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is increasingly recognized in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but its pathological basis remains poorly understood. We examined age-associated muscle dysfunction together with skeletal muscle and spinal motor system alterations in male AppNL-G-F/NL-G-F knock-in (App-KI) mice, which develop age-dependent amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) pathology without amyloid precursor protein (APP) overexpression. Middle-aged, but not adult, App-KI mice showed lower strength-related performance than age-matched wild-type mice, whereas skeletal muscle mass and myofiber cross-sectional area were preserved. General motor performance was also preserved, suggesting that the strength-related impairment did not simply reflect generalized motor dysfunction. Middle-aged App-KI mice had higher percentages of centrally nucleated fibers in the gastrocnemius and quadriceps femoris muscles. Transcriptomic and targeted expression analyses further revealed alterations in molecular profiles related to muscle development and myosin, including reduced expression of factors involved in myoblast fusion and selected myosin proteins. Despite evident cerebral A{beta} pathology, no apparent A{beta} immunoreactivity was detected in skeletal muscle. In the lumbar ventral horn, App-KI mice had fewer choline acetyltransferase-positive motor neurons, greater A{beta} deposition, and increased immunoreactivity for glial fibrillary acidic protein and ionized calcium-binding adapter molecule 1; serum interleukin-6 levels were also selectively elevated in middle-aged App-KI mice. Together, these findings indicate that age-associated reductions in strength-related performance in App-KI mice occur without overt muscle atrophy and are accompanied by histological and molecular abnormalities in skeletal muscle and pathological changes in the lumbar spinal cord. Thus, AD-related physical dysfunction may involve abnormalities in both peripheral skeletal muscle and the spinal motor system.

items.title: Scaling up naturalistic narrative research: A reproducible large language model-based tool for evaluating contextual information gain
items.abstract: Narratives are a universal part of natural human experience. As experimental stimuli, narratives allow scientists to study complex mental processes with direct relevance to everyday experience. These analyses typically require manual labeling of key event features. Such characterization of narrative stimuli are extremely labor-intensive and prone to subjectivity. Automated tools could reduce these difficulties and enable scaling to longer, varied stimuli by exposing the exact quantities computed. We address this by introducing a metric that uses open-weight LLMs to compute contextual information gain. Our metric correlates with human ratings of event importance and causal centrality, critically distinguishing the latter from semantic centrality, thus overcoming limitations of existing automated tools. The metric similarly captures shared coactivation in the default mode network, a network implicated in narrative comprehension. Taken together, these results validate an automated, empirically-grounded tool that researchers can use to identify behaviorally- and neurally-relevant computational quantities in naturalistic stimuli.

items.title: C3-targeting siRNA Combined with Oseltamivir Alleviates Inflammation and Lung Injury in H1N1-Infected Mice
items.abstract: Influenza A H1N1 infection can trigger severe inflammatory responses that contribute to pulmonary tissue injury and disease progression. Aberrant complement activation is presumed to contribute to these pathological changes. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether complement C3 serves as a shared upstream regulatory node linking inflammation and hemolytic injury. In this study, we established an H1N1-infected mouse model to dynamically monitor changes in inflammation, hemolysis and complement-related parameters throughout infection. We evaluated the C3-silencing efficacy of RG002, a liver-targeted siRNA against complement C3, as well as the therapeutic efficacy of RG002 combined with oseltamivir against H1N1 infection. Our results showed that H1N1 infection induced prominent inflammatory responses and alterations in peripheral blood cell parameters, accompanied by pulmonary histopathological injury in mice. Hepatic C3 expression and complement activity were simultaneously and markedly elevated. RG002 suppressed C3 expression in a dose-and time-dependent manner and reduced complement-mediated erythrocyte lysis in serum. In vivo therapeutic experiments demonstrated that on the basis of viral replication suppression achieved by oseltamivir, combination treatment with RG002 inhibited excessive complement activation. This combined regimen reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, attenuated pulmonary histopathological injury, and improved selected peripheral blood cell parameters. Notably the low-dose RG002 combination group exhibited superior performance across multiple evaluation indices, suggesting that the degree of C3 suppression is preferable to influence therapeutic effucaty. Collectively, our findings implicate complement C3 in the inflammatory pathology associated with H1N1 infection and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of C3-targeting siRNA as an adjunct to antiviral treatment. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the combination of antiviral therapy and controlled complement modulation as a potential host-directed therapeutic strategy for severe influenza.

items.title: Alkyladenine DNA glycosylase regulates TDG-mediated demethylation and neuronal gene expression by competitive substrate binding
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Clinical and Molecular Medicine, Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Trondheim 7491, N
items.abstract: Endogenous single-strand DNA breaks (SSBs) that arise during active DNA demethylation, regulate neurodevelopmental gene expression. Thymine (TDG) and alkyladenine (AAG) DNA glycosylases recognize oxidized methylcytosines. While TDG is required for excision, role of AAG in active demethylation and neurodevelopment remains unknown. Using mouse neurospheres, hippocampus, and human induced neurons (iNs), we show that AAG is needed for neurogenesis. Loss of AAG contributes to delayed neurodevelopmental and premature synaptic gene expression, evident from single-cell RNA sequencing of differentiating iNs. Synaptic gene expression is co-regulated by both AAG and TDG, with loss of single glycosylase inducing an opposing effect, implying competition. Single-molecule and biochemical assays directly demonstrate this competition, with AAG inhibiting TDG on 5fC. Without AAG, TDG has higher affinity, resulting in reduced global 5fC and increased SSB intermediates. In summary, AAG substrate competition plays an important role in fine tuning active demethylation, thereby regulating gene expression and DNA breaks during neurogenesis.

items.title: A histone hitchhiking mechanism for chromatin maintenance during mammalian transcription elongation
items.abstract: Eukaryotic transcription machinery faces the dual challenge of having to dismantle the nucleosome barrier for efficient elongation and faithfully restore the chromatin landscape in its wake to prevent aberrant transcription. The sequence of molecular events from nucleosome unwrapping to reassembly has yet to be delineated. Here, we use a single-molecule platform to visualize the dynamics of chromatin transcription by mammalian elongation complex (EC) in real time. When supplemented with a set of elongation factors and histone chaperones, the EC can efficiently traverse the nucleosome it encounters and, surprisingly, carry the dislodged histones while continuing translocation on DNA, a phenomenon we termed histone 'hitchhiking'. The formation of this hitchhiking complex is facilitated by the elongation factor SPT6 and IWS1 through distinct mechanisms. On the other hand, the histone chaperones FACT and NAP1L1 promote the transition from histone hitchhiking to nucleosome reassembly. We further showed that the next nucleosome presents a strong barrier against the hitchhiking complex, thus limiting long-range chromatin disruption. Overall, our results revealed that histone hitchhiking by EC is a prevalent intermediate during chromatin transcription, and the timing and location of its resolution are tuned by multiple factors. This mechanism may provide the robustness and flexibility needed to maintain the local organization of transcriptionally active chromatin.

items.title: Magnetic separation screens identify G alpha 15 as a central regulator of degranulation downstream of neutrophil chemoattractant receptors
items.abstract: Neutrophil recruitment and effector functions protect the body from infection. However, their excessive activity is central to inflammatory diseases, in which neutrophil granule proteins damage tissues and amplify inflammation. These proteins are released through degranulation, a regulated secretion process that can be triggered by the same chemoattractant molecules that drive neutrophil recruitment. Neutrophils detect attractants using G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that signal through Gi G-proteins. How the activity of these receptors is channeled to promote degranulation versus chemotaxis in the proper contexts remains unclear. Here, we identify positive and negative regulators of degranulation in HL-60 neutrophils using genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screens that exploit the transient surface exposure of granule membrane proteins. We identify G15 as a critical degranulation-specific effector of the attractant GPCRs FPR1 and LTB4R, and branched actin assembly as the dominant process limiting degranulation. Our results suggest that use of a second G subunit allows a switch to the degranulation output.

items.title: Genome survival and descent in population pedigrees
items.abstract: Motivated by issues of the maintenance of genetic variation in a highly endangered species, we continue earlier studies into the population genetics ancestry and descent of genome segments. In this paper, we focus on the survival and descent of genome in a population pedigree of a diploid dioecious species. We consider a population potentially being maintained from a small founder base, taking the canonical example a random-mating population of 100 males and 100 females. We show how previous methods to examine the ancestry of a single genome in such a population can also be used to account the survival genetic lengths and number of descendant copies of founder genome segments, and explore the variance of these measures. We show the variance of the population distribution over realizations within a pedigree is scarcely smaller then the variance over pedigrees: variation is in meiosis rather than in pedigree. While all founders continue to lose genome over time, the very first generations are critical to determining the amount of surviving genome. Dependence among founders is slight, except for between the two genomes of a founder: however when monogamy is enforced this high dependence extends to founder mates. We briefly consider extensions of population size (both smaller and larger), of mating structure, and of variance in offspring number, including variance in male reproductive success.

items.title: UV-excited autofluorescence uncovers multicopy suppressors of a Cdc14-associated meiotic defect
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Functional Biology and Genomics - CSIC
items.abstract: The Cdc14 phosphatase plays essential roles in meiotic chromosome metabolism and cell-cycle progression, yet the cellular pathways capable of compensating for reduced Cdc14 function remain poorly understood. To explore these connections, we performed a multicopy suppressor screen in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, using a mutant CDC14 allele that severely impairs sporulation. UV-excited ascospore-wall autofluorescence enabled the rapid screening of approximately 14,400 transformants, while subsequent microscopy provided quantitative validation of sporulation phenotypes. Photographic image processing facilitated candidate recovery, and a complementary computational analysis of archived images established the reproducibility of fluorescence-associated detections across different acquisition conditions. Genetic screening and independent plasmid retransformation identified four genomic-library plasmids that reproducibly enhanced sporulation. Molecular characterisation of the strongest suppressors revealed genomic regions associated with chromatin regulation and nuclear-pore organisation. Further analysis prioritised two particularly promising candidate genes: RCO1, encoding a component of the Rpd3S histone-deacetylase complex, and POM34, encoding an integral membrane nucleoporin. Suppressor activity was retained in a reduced POM34-containing construct, strengthening its candidacy for further functional investigation. Together, these findings establish an effective fluorescence-guided strategy for multicopy suppressor discovery and reveal promising genetic connections between Cdc14-dependent meiotic progression, chromatin regulation and nuclear architecture.

items.title: Genome architecture and duplication-associated functional diversification in the carnivorous plant Sarracenia purpurea
items.abstract: The repeated evolution of complex traits raises the question of how genomes generate ecological novelty while preserving developmental organization. We present a chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for the carnivorous purple pitcher plant, Sarracenia purpurea, and investigate how two contrasting modes of gene duplication have shaped its genome and functional repertoire: ancient polyploidy, which leaves duplicated genes in conserved chromosomal regions (syntenic duplicates), and local tandem duplication, which generates neighboring gene copies. We compare these duplication classes across nine angiosperms. The genome shows a mosaic of conserved and fractionated duplicated regions reflecting differential retention and loss of genes following ancient polyploidy and later restructuring. Comparison with noncarnivorous Actinidia (kiwifruit) identifies 18 syntenic and nine tandem Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process term-duplication-class combinations enriched in Sarracenia but not significantly enriched in Actinidia. Syntenic enrichments include meristem maintenance, organ-boundary specification, cuticle development, and hormonal regulation; tandem enrichments include defense responses, oxidative stress, jasmonic-acid biosynthesis, leaf senescence, and oligopeptide transport. Across the carnivorous genera Sarracenia, Nepenthes, Utricularia, and Pinguicula, we identify 19 syntenic and two tandem-associated biological processes showing significant enrichment in all four lineages, revealing striking functional commonalities across multiple evolutionary origins of carnivory despite their divergent trap morphologies and ecological strategies. Among Sarracenia genes differentially expressed in at least one comparison of flower, pitcher-leaf, and root tissues, tandem-class genes exhibit larger maximum absolute expression differences and greater GO richness and effective breadth at matched numbers of annotated homologs. These results highlight the complementary evolutionary contributions of ancient genome duplication and local gene-family expansion to the developmental and ecological diversification of carnivorous plants.

items.title: Pluripotent and differentiated cells display distinct genomic and nuclear landscapes of genome folding variability
items.corresponding_institution: University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School
items.abstract: Chromosome folding varies between cells. It is not known whether cell types differ in the extent of folding variability, whether distinct chromosomal regions in the same cell type display different levels of variability, and how folding variability relates to sub-nuclear location and gene expression. We combined two single-cell Hi-C approaches with 3D genome modeling of pseudo-single cells (IGM), DNA FISH, chromosome painting, and single-cell RNA-seq across a five-stage differentiation trajectory from human embryonic stem cells to hepatocyte-like cells. In all cell types folding variability correlates with compartment status, is highest towards the nuclear interior, decreases as a function of radial position in the nucleus, and is the lowest at the periphery. Loci associated with nuclear landmarks such as speckles, and especially the nuclear periphery display more consistent subnuclear positioning in all cell stages. Moreover, pluripotent and differentiated cells display different overall levels of chromosome folding variability: in H1 pluripotent cells the entire genome displays higher folding and positional variability. In contrast, in differentiated cells folding variability is generally lower along the genome and the number of loci that become consistently positioned at the nuclear periphery increases sharply. The two distinct patterns of folding variability were correlated with cell-to-cell gene expression variation: In pluripotent cells gene expression variation is large, pervasive and seen throughout the genome and the nucleus. In differentiated cells cell-to-cell variation in gene expression is much lower and restricted mostly to genes located near the center of the nucleus, consistent with the restricted pattern of chromosome folding variation. These findings reveal two distinct genomic states: pluripotent cells maintain a variably folded, spatially permissive genome and transcriptional plasticity, whereas differentiated cells mature into a spatially deterministic, more consistently folded organization that correlates with more restricted transcriptional programs.

items.title: Infernal-GPU: accurate E-values and sensitive covariance-model search for structured RNAs
items.corresponding_institution: NLPR, State Key Laboratory of Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Systems (MAIS), Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China; School of
items.abstract: Covariance models (CMs) find structured RNAs by scoring sequence and base pairing together, and they underlie the Infernal software and the Rfam database. Their dynamic programming is expensive, so Infernal relies on two approximations: E-values are calibrated on a short stretch of random sequence, and fast sequence-only filters decide which parts of a target the CM examines. How much accuracy these approximations cost, and where, is largely unknown, because removing them on CPUs is prohibitively slow. We present Infernal-GPU, a GPU implementation of Infernal's CM dynamic programming that matches Infernal's results. Its key step evaluates the one serial recurrence of CM scoring, the self-loop of insert-left states, as two parallel prefix scans. One GPU calibrates all 4,227 Rfam models overnight, which makes calibrations on ten times more random sequence routine. These longer calibrations show that the E-values distributed with Rfam are off by more than twofold for one model in eight. An exhaustive search reference shows that sequence filters discard remote homologs whose similarity lies almost entirely in base pairing; behind permissive filters, Infernal-GPU recovers them with a third of the CPU work that Infernal needs at the same setting. Infernal-GPU is freely available at https://github.com/void-echo/infernal-gpu and from PyPI, together with Rfam 15.0 recalibrated on ten times more random sequence.

items.title: Transferring CRISPRi knockdown responses to new cell lines requires screening part of each line
items.abstract: Perturb-seq screens measure knockdown responses in one cell line at a time. Models that transfer responses to new lines rarely beat simple averages, and standard metrics often ignore noise. It is unclear how much of a response is shared and what a new line must contribute. We studied CRISPR interference Perturb-seq of essential genes in four human cell lines, using noise ceilings and calibrated metrics. We also introduce CASTER, a set-based model that adapts the transferred mean to the target line. After noise correction, responses correlated at a median of 0.52, highest between the TP53 wild-type lines. With 30% of a line screened, a linear model and CASTER scored 0.84 and 0.80 versus 0.44 for the transferred mean (1 equals a technical duplicate). CASTER led only at 2.5% screened (0.62 versus 0.47) and fell below the transferred mean without a screen. Response size tracked general essentiality more than line-specific dependency.

items.title: A Biologically Interpretable Single-Cell Pathology Foundation Model for Molecular Decoding of H&E Images
items.corresponding_institution: Center for Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, Houston Methodist Research Institute, Houston, TX, 77030, USA
items.abstract: The microscopic structure of human tissues encodes molecular information that is not directly accessible by visual inspection. Current pathology foundation models improve histological interpretation but operate at multicellular resolution. It remains unclear whether routine histology contains structured molecular and cellular information recoverable at single-cell resolution, which biological properties are associated with this recoverability, and where its limits lie. Here, we introduce Loki2, a single-cell pathology foundation model trained on UniSeg, a pan-tissue resource integrating 15 million cells with segmentation, lineage annotations and measured or histology-inferred transcriptomic profiles. We examine the above question across cellular representation, molecular recoverability, and patient-level relevance. Loki2 captures cellular identity and continuous morphological variation, with interpretable latent dimensions linked to physical nuclear phenotypes through DAPI validation. Transcriptomic retrieval and in silico protein staining test molecular recoverability, with gene-level analyses revealing the strongest recovery for genes associated with morphologically distinct cellular identities and functions. Then, patient staging and biomarker discovery connect cellular morphology representations to clinical relevance. Together, these findings establish Loki2 as a biologically interpretable single-cell pathology foundation model and provide the opportunities of recovering cellular and molecular information from routine H&E histology at single-cell resolution.

items.title: Age and Sex Differences in Lateral Ventricle Choroid Plexus Volume in a Large, Manually Segmented, Multi-Site MRI Dataset
items.abstract: Introduction The choroid plexus (ChP), which produces cerebrospinal fluid and forms the blood-CSF barrier, has drawn growing interest in psychiatric and neurodegenerative neuroimaging. However, prior volumetric studies have relied largely on automated segmentation tools such as FreeSurfer, which show poor agreement with manual tracing, and have been limited to small, narrow-age, single-site samples. Methods We present DataPlex, a manually segmented lateral ventricle ChP dataset comprising 700 3T T1-weighted MRI scans drawn from 35 study/site categories, spanning a wide range of age, sex, and scanner manufacturer (GE, Philips, Siemens). Using generalized least squares models accounting for within-site dependence, we examined associations between ChP and lateral ventricle (LV) volume, and age, sex, scanner manufacturer, image resolution, a registration-based quality-control metric, intracranial volume, and cognitive performance. Results ChP volume displayed a positive linear association with age and was significantly greater in males than females, while LV volume showed a significant nonlinear relationship with age and no sex difference. Scanner manufacturer and image resolution were significantly associated with measured left LV volume but not with ChP volume, and the quality-control metric was not significantly associated with any outcome. Both ChP and LV volume were significantly associated with several cognitive domains, including emotion recognition, working memory, inhibitory control, and episodic memory. Conclusion These findings demonstrate meaningful differences in ChP volume across age and sex. DataPlex represents the largest demographically and technically diverse manually segmented ChP dataset to date, establishing reference benchmarks for future automated segmentation tools and underscoring the importance of accounting for demographic and technical covariates in choroid plexus research.

items.title: Delayed Reduction in Painful Sensations Evoked by Cervical tSCS Following High-Frequency Stimulation
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Artificial Intelligence Lomonosov Moscow State University
items.abstract: Objective: Transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (tSCS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique with potential effects on pain perception. However, tSCS itself can evoke discomfort or pain at higher current intensities, and it remains unclear whether high-frequency tSCS alters the pain evoked by subsequent low-frequency stimulation. This study examined whether high-frequency cervical tSCS delivered at motor-threshold intensity is followed by changes in pain ratings elicited by low-frequency tSCS in healthy participants. Approach: Twenty-five healthy participants completed a single experimental session. Individual sensory, motor, and pain thresholds were determined using single-pulse tSCS at the C6-C7 spinal level. Pain was assessed using 1-Hz stimulation delivered for 1 min at an individually defined intensity corresponding to 6-7 points on a 0-10 Numerical Rating Scale. Participants then received 80-Hz tSCS for 10 min at motor-threshold intensity, followed by three repeated pain-assessment sessions separated by 5-min intervals. Surface electromyography was recorded from the flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis. Pain analysis included 25 participants, whereas EMG analysis included 18 participants. Main results: Pain ratings were significantly lower than baseline during the second and third post-stimulation assessments. In contrast, ratings obtained immediately after high-frequency stimulation did not differ significantly from baseline. EMG responses showed substantial inter-participant variability. No EMG metric showed a significant omnibus session effect after correction for multiple comparisons, although exploratory comparisons indicated transient increases in ECR AUC and mean rectified amplitude immediately after high-frequency stimulation. Significance: These findings indicate that high-frequency cervical tSCS can exert a measurable short-term influence on pain perception. Pain ratings and stimulation-evoked EMG responses showed different temporal patterns and represent complementary, non-equivalent outcomes of spinal stimulation.

items.title: Electrophysiological dynamics of empathy for self- and other-related pain
items.corresponding_institution: Jena University Hospital, Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy
items.abstract: Empathy requires the ability to generate shared representations of the self and others while maintaining a distinction between them. However, it remains unclear whether, and to what extent, the neural processes involved in sharing and understanding others' pain overlap with those involved in processing one's own pain, particularly with respect to their temporal dynamics. Therefore, the present study aimed to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying empathic processing of self- and other-related painful facial expressions. To this end, EEG signals were recorded from 42 female participants while they viewed self- and other-related painful and neutral expressions. During the early stage of processing, the difference in N2 amplitude between self-related and other-related stimuli was smaller in the painful than in the neutral condition. Nevertheless, self-related painful stimuli continued to elicit more negative N2 amplitudes and greater Alpha/Mu suppression than other-related painful stimuli. In contrast, during the late stage of empathic processing, no distinction was observed between self- and other-related painful stimuli. Instead, painful expressions, regardless of whether they were self- or other-related, elicited larger late positive potential (LPP) amplitudes. These findings suggest that empathic processing is characterized by an early self-other distinction followed by a later convergence in the neural representation of self- and other-related pain.

items.title: Brain Signal Variability and Brain-Behavior Coupling in Adults with Dyslexia
items.abstract: Background: Brain signal variability indexed by fMRI has emerged as a promising transdiagnostic biomarker for neurodevelopmental disorders, demonstrating better predictive utility than time-averaged metrics for diagnosis, yet it remains underexplored in adult dyslexia. The Neural Noise Hypothesis of dyslexia proposes that genetic risk disrupts cortical excitation/inhibition balance, elevating neural noise and affecting processes essential for reading. Here, we examine resting-state fMRI BOLD variability, a metric linked to neural noise, in adults with dyslexia and investigate its links with behavior. Methods: In 30 adults with dyslexia (DY) and 76 typical readers (TR), we computed three complementary BOLD variability metrics: standard deviation (SD) and mean squared successive differences (MSSD) to quantify BOLD amplitude fluctuations, and dynamic regional homogeneity (dReHo) to quantify local temporal coordination. Voxel-wise group comparisons and partial least squares correlation analyses examined brain-behavior associations across a comprehensive behavioral battery spanning reading (e.g., word reading, phonological processing), math, oral language, working memory, and executive function domains. Results: DY showed higher SD and MSSD in the left ventral occipitotemporal pathway and higher MSSD in the cerebellum, whereas TR showed higher dReHo in frontal and temporoparietal regions. SD/MSSD in visual, somatomotor, cerebellar, and subcortical networks significantly covaried with multi-domain behavioral profiles. Conclusions: Adults with dyslexia showed localized, metric-specific differences in brain signal variability and brain-behavior covariance, indicating region-specific rather than global alterations. These results suggest that brain signal variability is a promising candidate task-free phenotype that could potentially index target engagement in interventions for adult dyslexia.

items.title: Automated, high-throughput kinematic analysis of skilled reaching in rodent models of neurological injury
items.abstract: Neurological dysfunction can diminish quality of life by disrupting the movement capacity required to accomplish tasks. Kinematic studies guide treatment development by revealing subtle relationships between patterns of movement and neurological dysfunction. However, these studies produce a large quantity of opaque, multifaceted, and often highly correlated data. Here we present a novel and efficient approach to collecting, analyzing, and interpreting kinematic data with high throughput. We automated a single pellet reaching task in mice and created a video analysis pipeline that scores task success and extracts kinematic features from reaches. To analyze the resulting data, principal component analysis was first applied to group covarying measurements into a few overarching dimensions of behavior. Regularized regression was then applied separately to select reach qualities that best predicted task success. Applied to four nervous system injury models, this approach revealed differences in the effects of injury type and rehabilitative intervention on movement patterns that were not apparent from task success alone.

items.title: MK-6240
items.abstract: Flortaucipir and MK-6240 are two tau imaging agents currently in use for measuring neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) progression in Alzheimers disease (AD). The aims of this study were to use postmortem AD and Down syndrome (DS) brain sections to study three issues: (1) Measure binding affinity of flortaucipir and MK-6240 in AD brain sections by using [125I]IPPI; (2) Evaluate the binding characteristics of [18F]flortaucipir in AD, DS and cognitively normal (CN) brains sections and compare them with [18F]MK-6240, and (3) Assess the binding of [18F]flortaucipir in CN and Parkinsons disease (PD) brain sections to identify any off-target binding. The half-maximal inhibition (IC50) of [125I]IPPI bound to anterior cingulate (AC) in AD brain sections for flortaucipir was 2.91 nM and MK-6240 was 5.99 nM. Using frontal cortex (FCX) and temporal cortex (TCX) of AD, DS and CN brain sections, [18F]flortaucipir displayed high levels of binding in the gray matter (GM) of AD and DS. The average ratio of DSAD GM to CN GM was 15.7 in FCX, while DSAD GM to CN GM was 15.2 for the TCX. In the case of AD, average ratio of AD GM to CN GM was 12.4 in FCX, while AD GM to CN GM was 9.5 for the TCX. Binding of [18F]flortaucipir in brain section of AC from CN and PD cases did not exhibit any off-target binding to monoamine oxidase-A (MAO-A). In summary, both flortaucipir and MK-6240 exhibit similar high affinity to tau and [18F]flortaucipir exhibits higher binding compared to [18F]MK-6240 in DSAD.

items.title: Seroprotection and improved polyfunctional immunity conferred by a YF17D-vectored rabies vaccine
items.corresponding_institution: KU Leuven Department of Microbiology, Immunology and Transplantation, Rega Institute, Virology, Antiviral Drug and Vaccine Research, Laboratory of Molecular Vac
items.abstract: Rabies remains a major public-health challenge, with pre-exposure vaccination strategies constrained by the need for multiple doses and repeated healthcare visits. Here we describe YF-RabG, a live-attenuated rabies vaccine candidate based on the yellow fever 17D (YF17D) vaccine backbone that stably expresses the rabies virus glycoprotein (RabG). YF-RabG exhibited an attenuated phenotype and favourable safety profile compared with parental YF17D across several preclinical models, including neonatal and immunocompromised mice. A single immunization induced robust humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in non-human primates. Rabies virus-neutralizing antibody titres readily exceeded the widely accepted correlate of protection in mice, hamsters and non-human primates by several orders. Accordingly, vaccination conferred protection against lethal rabies challenge in a range of stringent mouse models, maintained seroprotective antibody levels for at least one year, and increased following a boost using a licensed rabies vaccine. Furthermore, the YF17D vector was readily adapted to accommodate glycoproteins from distant lyssaviruses, generating protective vaccine candidates against Mokola, Lagos bat and Lleida bat lyssaviruses. Collectively, these findings identify YF-RabG as a promising single-dose rabies vaccine candidate and highlight the versatility of the YF17D platform for lyssavirus vaccine development.

items.title: Label-Free Lymphocyte Subtype and State Classification by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
items.abstract: Accurate immune cell subtype and functional state profiling are essential for studying immune regulation, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Established single-cell analysis techniques rely heavily on either endpoint, destructive measurements or complex labeling that can potentially affect cell functions. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy offers quantitative, label-free imaging of cells and tissues by providing contrast based on subcellular concentrations of intrinsic biomolecules at high spatial and temporal resolution. Here, we demonstrate that Vision Transformer based hyperspectral SRS imaging classification can accurately and non-destructively classify various lymphocyte phenotypes, including lymphocyte lineage (T and B cells), T cell subset and differentiation state (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, effector, memory, and naive for both), and functional states (naive T, activated T, exhausted T) using fluorescent markers for training. By leveraging attention-based spatial-spectral feature learning, the approach captures biomolecular patterns associated with immune cell identity and state while preserving cells for downstream or longitudinal analysis. This provides a potential platform for label-free immune profiling, live-cell analysis, and longitudinal studies of immune cell type and state transitions.

items.title: SOX4 suppresses vascular calcification via DNA-binding-independent regulation of the USP10-HNRNPC-WNT5A axis
items.abstract: Background: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) osteogenic differentiation drives vascular calcification, yet the endogenous mechanisms that restrain this transition remain poorly defined. SOX4 has recently emerged as a regulator of phenotype switching in endothelial and epithelial cells, but whether it governs VSMC fate and vascular calcification is unknown. Methods: SOX4 expression was examined in human calcified arteries, in vitamin D3 (VitD3)-treated mouse aortas and in phosphate-treated human aortic smooth muscle cells. Loss- and gain-of-function experiments, an HMG-box-deleted SOX4 mutant, co-immunoprecipitation combined with mass spectrometry, ubiquitination and protein stability assays, RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing and mRNA decay assays were combined with VSMC-specific Sox4 knockout mice and pharmacological WNT5A inhibition. Results: SOX4 protein was upregulated in calcified VSMCs and arteries, yet SOX4 loss aggravated and SOX4 overexpression attenuated VSMC osteogenic differentiation. A SOX4 mutant lacking the HMG-box retained anti-calcific activity, placing the function outside DNA binding. SOX4 interacted with HNRNPC and attenuated the HNRNPC-USP10 association, promoting K48-linked ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HNRNPC. HNRNPC bound WNT5A mRNA and was required for its stability, so that SOX4 reduced WNT5A expression. VSMC-specific Sox4 deletion aggravated VitD3-induced aortic calcification together with HNRNPC and WNT5A upregulation. Strengthening this braking axis with the WNT5A antagonist BOX5 attenuated VSMC osteogenic differentiation in vitro and vascular calcification in vivo in both genotypes, identifying WNT5A as a pharmacologically accessible node downstream of SOX4 loss. Conclusions: SOX4 restrains VSMC osteogenic differentiation through post-transcriptional control of cell fate, defining a SOX4-HNRNPC-WNT5A axis and identifying it as a pharmacologically accessible target for vascular calcification.

items.title: CTCF-anchored cohesin loops are a vertebrate-specific innovation
items.abstract: Animal genomes are organized into chromatin loops and topologically associating domains. Cohesin drives loop extrusion, and the architectural factor CTCF halts loop-extruding cohesin. CTCF-anchored loops facilitate interactions between distal cis-regulatory elements and regulate gene expression. However, when CTCF acquired its cohesin loop-halting function remains unclear. We performed interspecies domain-swap experiments, replacing the cohesin-interacting N-terminus of mouse CTCF with orthologous sequences from the fruit fly Drosophila (arthropod), Branchiostoma (chordate), and the inshore hagfish (jawless vertebrate). The hagfish N-terminus halted cohesin, whereas the invertebrate CTCF N-termini did not. Consistently, Micro-C maps from hagfish tissues revealed stripes associated with convergently oriented CTCF sites, a characteristic signature of cohesin-loop halting. Notably, cohesin enrichment at promoters and enhancers was more pronounced in hagfish than in jawed vertebrates. Our findings indicate that CTCF-mediated cohesin loop anchoring most likely evolved in the common ancestor of extant vertebrates and was further strengthened in jawed vertebrates.

items.title: A full-length isoform atlas of the non-failing and failing human heart
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Population Health Sciences, UT San Antonio Health Science Center, San Antonio, TX
items.abstract: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and ischemic heart disease (IHD) are leading causes of heart failure, yet isoform-level changes in the failing heart remain poorly defined because reference annotations are derived largely from healthy tissues and short-read sequencing cannot reliably reconstruct full-length transcripts. We sequenced six human left ventricles (non-failing, DCM, and IHD; n = 2 each) with PacBio HiFi long reads and curated 48,232 isoforms across 11,760 genes, including 15,535 novel NIC and NNC isoforms. Independent evidence supported most novel structures: 81.7% of isoforms with novel splice junctions had short-read support for all novel junctions, and a cardiac CAGE atlas supported the 5' ends of 93% of NIC and 86% of NNC isoforms. Novel isoform diversification was concentrated in sarcomere genes and persisted after accounting for gene complexity, expression, sequencing depth, and transcript length. We then augmented GENCODE v43 with 18,637 non-FSM long-read isoforms and re-quantified two independent short-read cohorts (MAGNet and GSE116250). For most genes carrying a transcript that changed more than 2-fold in DCM, the gene itself changed less than 2-fold, so these changes are not apparent at the gene level. Of 626 transcripts differentially expressed in both cohorts, 98% changed in the same direction, including all 100 long-read isoforms among them. The resource is available through CardioIsoMap, an interactive isoform-centric portal (https://cardioisomap.streamlit.app/). This study provides a comprehensive isoform-resolved reference of the human heart in health and disease.

items.title: Savant: A Fast, Structure-Free Binding Affinity Predictor For Protein-Ligand Drug Screening
items.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity determines which of many candidate molecules is worth synthesizing and assaying, making it the central measurement in early drug discovery. Binding affinity is commonly expressed as the dissociation constant, an equilibrium measure that indicates how easily a complex separates into its components. AI-based generative chemistry and make-on-demand chemical catalogs now produce molecules faster than rigorous method can evaluate them. Leading computational methods co-fold the complex before scoring the binding affinity between the protein and the ligand, which provides high accuracy but requires a graphics processing unit (GPU) and substantial time for every pair evaluated.Here we present Savant, a machine learning model that estimates the dissociation constant using only the protein's amino acid sequence and the ligand's structure written as a line of text (SMILES). Savant needs no 3-dimensional folded structure, no docking, and no GPU. To test Savant fairly, we built a benchmark designed to prevent any training data to leak into the testing set, drawing only on measurements published after the training data was assembled and on molecules chemically unlike anything the model had seen. On an independent benchmark, Savant ranks ahead of every other 3-dimensional structure-free method.Savant is designed to rank compounds against a single protein, and performs as well as other methods that require a GPU, while running only on a central processing unit (CPU). Thus, Savant can screen libraries of 100,000 compounds in minutes with commodity hardware.

items.title: SRAscout: Semantic discovery of public sequencing data through harmonized SRA and BioProject metadata
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas at Austin
items.abstract: The rapid growth of public sequencing data has created great opportunities for data-driven discovery in the life sciences, but it has also made it harder to find relevant datasets. The NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) hosts more than 45 million high-throughput sequencing runs, and the BioProject database, shared by NCBI, the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and the DNA Data Bank of Japan, describes the projects behind them. However, their metadata are often incomplete, inconsistently annotated and difficult to search using keywords alone. We present SRAscout, a web-based platform that enables semantic dataset retrieval by integrating SRA run metadata with the corresponding BioProject records. SRAscout collects and indexes metadata for about 714,000 BioProjects, and harmonizes sample attributes such as cell line, tissue, age, sex and treatment into a compact and consistent schema. For semantic embedding, SRAscout employs a biomedical sentence embedding model based on BioBERT, which generates dense vector representations from the title, name, organism and description of each project. Users can search in three modes, with the DOI or PubMed ID of an article, with free text, or with BioProject and SRA study accessions, and SRAscout finds the most related projects in each case. Free-text queries are processed through a hybrid of semantic and full-text search, which finds conceptually relevant studies even when different terms are used to describe the same biology, while exact terms such as gene names are still matched. Structured filters allow refinement by organism, assay type (for example RNA-seq and miRNA-seq), harmonized sample attributes such as tissue, cell type and disease, tag words, and many additional attributes. For each search, users can download a harmonized metadata table and ready-to-use scripts that fetch the sequencing files from ENA. SRAscout also offers a public API for programmatic access. By combining harmonized metadata with context-aware search in a single interface, SRAscout facilitates dataset discovery, meta-analysis and data reuse. The application is freely available at www.srascout.com.

items.title: Casanovo-TMT: deep learning-based de novo sequencing of TMTpro-labeled peptides and phosphopeptides
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Convergence Medicine, Yonsei University Wonju College of Medicine, Wonju 26426, Republic of Korea
items.abstract: De novo peptide sequencing reads peptides directly from tandem mass spectra, but none of the released deep learning models can sequence peptides labeled with isobaric tags such as TMTpro, which are widely used for multiplexed quantitative proteomics. We extended the residue vocabulary of Casanovo with TMTpro tags and phosphorylation, fine-tuned it on 21 million spectra from our laboratory, most of them TMTpro-labeled, and re-ranked the candidates in the beam by their agreement with the measured precursor mass. The resulting model, Casanovo-TMT, predicted the exact peptidoform for 84.7% of the TMTpro-labeled spectra in our test set and for 87.4 and 79.6% of the spectra in two public global-proteome datasets from other laboratories, whereas the extended vocabulary without fine-tuning gave 0.3%. Discarding the lowest-scoring predictions raised precision to 95% while retaining 81.7% of the test spectra. Casanovo-TMT also predicted the exact peptidoform for 69.2% of the spectra in a public phosphopeptide-enriched dataset and for 66 to 72% of the phosphopeptide spectra in three phosphoproteomic studies from our laboratory that were not used for training. In these studies, it identified numbers of phosphopeptides comparable to or larger than those of database search engines, and proportionally more where database search identified fewer. For the phosphopeptides identified only by Casanovo-TMT, entrapment estimated that more than 90% were correct, and an independent search engine assigned the same sequence to 95 to 98% of the spectra that it identified with confidence. Casanovo-TMT can therefore extend database search in TMTpro-based quantitative proteomics, particularly in studies in which database search identifies few phosphopeptides.

items.title: FasL blockade suppresses liver metastasis and prolongs survival in small-cell lung cancer
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Biochemistry I, University of Cologne
items.abstract: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy characterised by early metastatic dissemination, frequent relapse and poor long-term survival. Despite advances in immunotherapy, durable disease control remains challenging, highlighting the need to identify therapeutic vulnerabilities beyond conventional tumour-cell killing and immune checkpoint inhibition. Here, we uncover an unexpected contribution of Fas-Fas ligand (FasL) signalling to SCLC metastatic progression and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway. Using an autochthonous Rb1/Trp53-deficient mouse model, we show that genetic Fas deletion markedly suppresses liver metastatic disease, identifying a previously unrecognised contribution of Fas signalling to metastatic progression. Notably, despite this antimetastatic effect, Fas deletion during tumour initiation did not improve survival and was accompanied by pronounced alterations in pulmonary tissue architecture. As these alterations may reflect adverse consequences of Fas deletion in non-malignant pulmonary populations, we reasoned that pharmacological FasL blockade in established disease could provide therapeutic benefit while circumventing the detrimental consequences for pulmonary tissue homeostasis associated with genetic Fas deletion. Remarkably, only six administrations of a soluble Fas-Fc fusion protein over three weeks significantly prolonged survival and substantially reduced the incidence and burden of liver metastases. FasL blockade was also associated with enhanced inflammatory and immune-response transcriptional signatures in the liver, while its combination with anti-PD-1 increased pulmonary immune-cell accumulation without conferring additional survival benefit. These data suggest that the biological consequences of targeting this pathway may depend on the timing and cellular context of intervention. Together, our findings identify Fas-FasL signalling as an unexpected regulator of SCLC metastatic progression and establish FasL blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy capable of prolonging survival in established disease beyond conventional immune checkpoint inhibition.

items.title: A Manually Curated Metabolic Model of Alteromonas macleodii MIT1002 and its Ecological Implications
items.abstract: Heterotrophic bacteria are a vital part of the marine carbon cycle. They interact with phytoplankton and rapidly process fixed carbon, respiring it back to CO 2 . Among heterotrophs, Alteromonas macleodii is notable for its colonization of particulate material and its high growth and carbon utilization rates and is commonly used as a model system to study metabolic interactions with the abundant cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus . Understanding how these traits emerge from the interplay of hundreds of reactions requires a formal encoding of the organisms metabolic network. Here, we present a metabolic model of A. macleodii MIT1002, built in a traceable and systematic way to recreate experimental growth phenotypes on 51 unique media compositions. We used this model to generate testable hypotheses about the role of sodium in the electron transport chain, the catabolic relevance of different glycolytic pathways, nitrogen recycling during cross-feeding with Prochlorococcus , and microbial carbon use efficiency.

items.title: Multisensory brain processing is associated with depressive symptoms in youth with chronic pain
items.abstract: Juvenile fibromyalgia (JFM) is a chronic pain condition marked by widespread musculoskeletal pain and often accompanied by physical fatigue, nonrestorative sleep, headaches, anxiety, and depression. Previous studies have found that adolescents with fibromyalgia report augmented unpleasantness and altered brain responses to non-painful multisensory stimuli. Likewise, research in major depression has shown altered neural processing of sensory stimulation. We examined whether augmented brain responses to non-painful multisensory stimulation is associated with depressive symptoms in adolescent girls with JFM. Forty-six female adolescents with JFM (mean - SD, 16.43 - 1.10 years [range 13-18 years]) and 44 healthy participants (mean - SD, 16.09 - 1.06 years [range 13-18 years]) completed validated questionnaires assessing daily-life sensory hypersensitivity and depressive symptoms, alongside undergoing a functional MRI multisensory task. JFM patients reported significantly higher sensory unpleasantness than healthy participants, and this hypersensitivity was positively associated with depressive symptoms. Neuroimaging results in chronic pain patients revealed that greater depressive symptomatology was associated with increased activation in the posterior cingulate cortex (PCC) (pFWE<0.05), a region implicated in self-referential processing and specifically rumination in adults with chronic pain. JFM patients showed increased PCC-left middle temporal gyrus task-dependent connectivity using psychophysiological interactions analysis (PPI). Furthermore, hyperconnectivity between the PCC and brain areas involved in cognitive-affective regulation, sensory integration, and memory processing was strongly correlated with depressive symptoms in JFM patients. These findings underscore the role of depressive symptoms in sensory processing and integration in JFM patients and highlight the complex interplay between sensory processing and emotional/self-referential brain function in patients.

items.title: Zona incerta drives a strategy of persistence during nocturnal predatory hunting in mice.
items.abstract: Prey capture in lab mice is a complex, ethologically relevant behavior that provides us with an opportunity to study how mice integrate internal and external cues to drive goal-directed behaviors. Previous research has established that key parts of this behavior, such as the approach, are visually guided, but it has remained unknown how mice would perform if given exposure to hunting without visual cues. Zona incerta, a potential key locus for the integration of external and internal information, has previously been shown in naive mice to improve prey capture ability by increasing appetitive drive through integrating prey-related sensory information. It remains an open question if this region plays the same role in mice experienced with hunting in both the light and dark. Therefore, we examined the behavioral strategies used by mice with prior experience hunting in both the light and dark, as well as how these strategies are modulated by zona incerta. In experienced mice, we found that mice adjust their strategies to maintain similar success rates with and without visual cues, and that zona incerta further refines these strategies, specifically in the dark. This suggests that the role of zona incerta in these experienced mice is to maintain successful hunting by shifting behavioral strategies under ambiguous sensory conditions.

items.title: Integrating multiple imputation with harmonization in multisite neuroimaging data: implications for site effects and biological inference
items.abstract: Multisite neuroimaging harmonization in Alzheimer's disease research with missing data has received limited attention in the literature. Here, we evaluated the performance of several harmonization methods in conjunction with multiple imputation (MI) to address missing data, using baseline [18F]flortaucipir tau positron emission tomography (PET) data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We compared complete case and MICE-imputed datasets (m = 5) across the original ADNI-preprocessed data and four statistical harmonization approaches: ComBat with and without covariates, quantile normalization, and quantile regression. Weighted average standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) across six Braak regions were analyzed for each dataset-method combination.
