Applying Spec2Function to a 30-organ macaque aging atlas revealed organ-specific metabolic functions and previously unreported functional modules that were supported by independent human and mouse datasets. Together, these results position Spec2Function as a function-centric framework for scalable biological interpretation of structurally unannotated MS2 spectra.

items.title: Generative Data Augmentation for Small-Cohort Glioblastoma Diagnosis from Circulating microRNA: Why Same-Modality Validation Overstates Performance
items.corresponding_institution: National Institute for Research in Environmental Health
items.abstract: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have potential as minimally invasive biomarkers for glioblastoma (GBM), but the small size of discovery groups makes it difficult to develop a classifier. The discovery cohort, GSE122488, comprised 38 patients (n = 38). Generative data augmentation was applied to increase the dataset, although evaluations based on held-out samples from the same cohort or a single validation set make it difficult to distinguish biological signals from cohort- or platform-specific effects. CTGAN and Tabular Variational Autoencoder (TVAE) models were trained on the 38-patient cohort producing 500 synthetic samples each. Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers were trained on augmented datasets and assessed using an escalating validation approach: first on an independent plasma cohort of the same modality (GSE184472, n = 118), and then on a tissue cohort from a different platform (Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA), n = 198). XGBoost using TVAE-augmented data achieved an AUROC of 0.59 (95% CI 0.49-0.70) on GSE184472, compared with 0.42 to 0.53 without augmentation, although no AUROC on this cohort was significantly different from chance. However, this improvement did not carry to CGGA, where AUROC was 0.40 (95% CI 0.32-0.48) before harmonisation and 0.47 after Min-Max harmonisation. After harmonisation, a recall of 1.00 resulted from predicting every sample as GBM, leading to an accuracy of 0.41 and showing poor discrimination. The generalisation gap was examined in terms of modality mismatch, differing class definitions between cohorts, synthetic-data-related class imbalance, and incomplete cross-platform harmonisation. These findings show the need for independent, cross-platform validation before using data augmentation for diagnosis. The escalating validation framework provides a way to evaluate generalizability in small-cohort studies.

items.title: The intestinal microbiome shapes responses to the GD2/GD3 cancer vaccine in children with high-risk neuroblastoma
items.abstract: The intestinal microbiome influences vaccine responses, but its role in therapeutic cancer vaccination remains largely unexplored. We investigated the gut microbiome, vaccine immunogenicity and clinical outcomes in 137 children with high-risk neuroblastoma receiving GD2/GD3 vaccination with oral b-glucan. Microbiome-perturbing antibiotic exposure was associated with inferior progression-free survival (PFS). Among patients vaccinated in first remission, higher a-diversity and enrichment of Lachnospiraceae, including Blautia, were associated with higher anti-GD2 IgG1 responses, while higher Clostridia abundance was associated with superior PFS. Patients had microbiome profiles resembling those of chronologically younger healthy children, consistent with delayed microbiome maturation. A greater discrepancy between patients' chronological age and the age of microbiome-matched healthy children was associated with inferior PFS among patients in first remission. In a complementary mouse model, antibiotic treatment impaired vaccine-induced anti-GD2 IgG responses and accelerated tumor growth. Together, these findings support a role for the intestinal microbiome in therapeutic cancer vaccine responses and identify microbiome maturation as a clinically relevant feature in pediatrics.

items.title: Ventricular proximity associates with survival and immune remodelling in glioblastoma
items.abstract: Glioblastoma is clinically and molecularly heterogeneous, yet whether its position relative to the lateral ventricles shapes tumour biology remains unclear. Here we measured tumour ventricle distance in 57 patients with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and combined survival analysis with RNA sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, proteomics and multiplex immunofluorescence. Proximity to the ventricles was associated with shorter survival. Ventricle-proximal tumours lacked a distinct genomic driver but displayed an inflammatory yet immunoregulatory profile: antigen-presentation, leukocyte-activation and cytokine programmes coexisted with checkpoint and immunosuppressive transcripts, and proteomics revealed concordant complement and myeloid signals. In tissue, these tumours tended to show more Ki67-positive cells and proliferating SOX2-positive stem-like cells, suggesting increased plasticity of the stem-like compartment, without more CD4- or CD8a-positive lymphocytes. Ventricular proximity thus marks a clinically adverse context with a distinct immune-inflammatory profile, providing a framework for validation and patient stratification.

items.title: Tumor-responsive AAV arms cancer cells to enhance CAR-T cell therapy in solid tumors
items.corresponding_institution: School of Biological Science and Medical Engineering, Southeast University, Nanjing 210096, China
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T-cell therapy remains limited in solid tumors by the scarcity of suitable target antigens and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we developed a tumor-responsive recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) strategy that harnesses aberrant NF-{kappa}B activity to establish a shared synthetic CAR target across tumor types. Using an NF-{kappa}B-responsive decoy minimal promoter (DMP), rAAV-SA drove tumor-preferential surface expression of a synthetic antigen (SA), enabling antigen-dependent CAR-T-cell activation, degranulation, and cytotoxicity. Systemic rAAV-SA delivery combined with CAR-T cells produced antitumor activity in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and colorectal cancer xenograft models. We subsequently engineered rAAV-ARMS (antigen redirection and multifunctional secreted effectors), integrating SA expression with tumor-local production of an IL-15/IL-15R sushi-domain fusion, CXCL10, and IFN-{gamma}. Compared with antigen redirection alone, rAAV-ARMS enhanced CAR-T-cell-mediated killing in three-dimensional tumor spheroids and, in a TNBC xenograft model, increased intratumoral T-cell accumulation and improved the efficacy of intravenously administered CAR-T cells, without overt systemic toxicity under the conditions examined. These findings establish a tumor-programmed platform for target-redirected universal CAR-T-cell therapy in solid tumors.

items.title: Focused ultrasound-enhanced carboplatin delivery improves radiotherapy response and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model
items.corresponding_institution: University Grenoble Alpes, INSERM UA7, Synchrotron Radiation for Biomedicine, 38000 Grenoble, France
items.abstract: Rationale Glioblastoma is highly resistant to conventional therapies due to the limited penetration of chemotherapeutics across the blood-brain and blood-tumor barriers (BBB, BTB). Although platinum-based drugs show strong cytotoxic and radiosensitizing properties in several cancers, their inability to achieve therapeutic concentrations within the central nervous system (CNS) severely limits their efficacy in brain tumors. This study investigated whether focused ultrasound (FUS)-mediated BBB/BTB disruption combined with intravenous carboplatin and stereotactic radiotherapy could improve drug delivery, tumor control, and survival in a preclinical glioblastoma model. Methods F98 glioma-bearing rats were treated with a single dose of 15 Gy radiation therapy (RT), carboplatin only, carboplatin + RT, FUS + carboplatin or FUS + carboplatin + RT. FUS-mediated permeabilization was confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and platinum accumulation was quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry and synchrotron X-ray fluorescence. Tumor progression and microenvironmental changes were monitored using multiparametric MRI (diffusion, perfusion, and vascular permeability), followed by voxel-wise clustering analysis and histopathological validation. Results The FUS + carboplatin + RT group demonstrated the strongest therapeutic benefit, compared to all other treatment groups, yielding up to a 122% increase in median survival relative to the untreated group. This treatment also reduced necrotic core expansion and induced a transient increase in tumor perfusion, suggesting improved vascular function. FUS enhanced carboplatin delivery to both the tumor and peritumoral brain, with platinum distribution closely correlating with MRI signal enhancement. Voxel-wise clustering of multiparametric MRI identified biologically distinct tumor regions that were subsequently validated by immunohistochemistry. Conclusion The combination of FUS-mediated carboplatin delivery and radiotherapy represents a safe, non-invasive strategy that enhances drug delivery and improves survival in an aggressive preclinical model of glioblastoma. By overcoming a major limitation of current therapies, this approach shows promising potential for clinical translation. Keywords Glioblastoma, Focused Ultrasound, Blood-Brain Barrier, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy

items.title: Extracellular matrix spatial ecosystems define stem-like niches and predict post-recurrence survival in glioblastomas
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Translational Pathology, Moffitt Cancer Center, Tampa, Florida
items.abstract: Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is a hallmark of glioblastoma (GBM) yet has typically been studied through a reductionist lens, as individual genes or pathways rather than large scale, spatially integrated analyses coordinated with biological states. Focusing on whole matrisome gene expression, we identified three reproducible and spatially coherent ECM transcriptional programs, termed Homeostatic, Stress, and Fibrous, that were associated with specific microenvironmental functions and neoplastic cell states, with the strongest association noted between Homeostatic ECM and neoplastic quiescent stem cell-like (QSC) niches. Ligand-receptor analyses identified FGF1 and BGN as candidate ECM-driven regulators of QSC. In an independent longitudinal bulk transcriptomic cohort, ECM-based models outperformed traditional clinical and biomarker variables for predicting post-recurrence survival, with elevated Homeostatic ECM activity associated with improved post-recurrence survival, while MGMT promoter methylation no longer remained prognostic. Overall, these findings establish ECM organization as a clinically relevant dimension of GBM biology and nominate ECM-associated signaling as candidate therapeutic targets.

items.title: HyperGenie: A method for predicting enzymatic gene essentiality using hypergraph neural networks and genome-scale metabolic models
items.abstract: Identifying essential genes in bacteria is crucial for drug discovery and synthetic biology. Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) evaluated via flux balance analysis remain standard, yet they rely on the often-invalid premise that mutant strains optimize for maximum growth. Recent machine learning approaches circumvent this limitation using random forests or graph neural networks on mass flow graphs (MFGs). However, data-driven tools like random forests discard network topology, while graph-based tools like MFGs decompose multi-component biochemical reactions into pairwise interactions, misrepresenting complex stoichiometry and limiting interpretability. Furthermore, existing methods remain largely uncharacterised in data-scarce regimes and cross-environmental conditions. Here, we introduce HyperGenie, a framework that integrates genome-scale metabolic models with directed hypergraph neural networks by representing metabolites as nodes and reactions as hyperedges. Operating directly on wild-type flux features, HyperGenie eliminates post-knockout optimality assumptions, achieves a 13% PR-AUC improvement over prior objective-dependent methods, and matches computationally demanding, state-of-the-art flux-sampling baselines. Using HyperGenie to guide targeted growth curve assays, we identified latent essentiality misannotations across three genes in the benchmark iML1515 dataset, which we then reconciled and validated experimentally via PCR. In data-scarce regimes, HyperGenie retained robust predictive performance (> 90% PR-AUC) when trained on as little as 40% of the data. To isolate the value of hypergraph message passing, we benchmarked HyperGenie against an independent-reaction multilayer perceptron (MLPGenie) across diverse nutrient environments and uptake rates, where HyperGenie's hypergraph inductive bias yielded consistent accuracy gains (> 2% in glucose; > 4% across six alternative carbon sources). Notably, HyperGenie exhibits robust zero-shot cross-nutrient generalization, accurately forecasting gain-of-essentiality phenotypes on novel carbon sources, though loss-of-essentiality remains challenging. Finally, coupling hypergraph representations with SHAP attribution provides actionable mechanistic insights into metabolic rewiring, establishing a data-efficient, interpretable platform for discovering novel antibiotic targets.

items.title: Context-dependent requirement for neutrophils in retinal regeneration
items.abstract: Innate immune responses shape Muller glia (MG) reprogramming and retinal regeneration, yet the contribution of individual immune cell type remains poorly defined. Neutrophils enter the blood-retinal-barrier (BRB)-damaged retina within hours of injury, but their role in retinal regeneration is unknown. Here we report that neutrophils are required for the regenerative responses in needle-poked, but not NMDA-injured, zebrafish retinas. Pharmacological ablation of neutrophils with Erbb2 inhibitors suppresses MG proliferation, progenitor formation, and subsequent neuronal regeneration after stab injury, whereas neutrophil depletion has no significant effect in the BRB-intact NMDA model. We further show that Cxcl12-Cxcr4b signaling retains neutrophils at the stab injury site, and manipulating neutrophil retention correspondingly alters the regenerative responses. Mechanistically, neutrophils may modulate MG reprogramming and proliferation by regulating microglial reactivity and by secreting a regeneration-promoting factor Hb-egf. These data identify neutrophil as a previously unrecognized regulator of retinal regeneration and establish that their contribution is injury context-dependent.

items.title: A temporal atlas of TDP-43 interactions reveals persistent network remodelling beyond stress granule clearance
items.abstract: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43 is associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and may be promoted by cellular stress. However, the dynamics of TDP-43 protein-protein interactions during stress and recovery remain poorly understood. Here, we combined APEX2 proximity labelling with quantitative mass spectrometry to generate a temporal atlas of wild-type TDP-43 and pathology-mimicking TDP-43dNLS and TDP-43CTF variants. Interactomes were profiled across steady state, oxidative stress, and recovery. We reveal extensive state- and variant-dependent remodelling of TDP-43 interaction networks, uncovering distinct temporal interaction patterns throughout the stress response and recovery. Notably, distinct TDP-43 interaction signatures persisted after stress granule clearance, suggesting a molecular memory of stress. Together, our study establishes a comprehensive temporal resource for investigating TDP-43 interaction dynamics and provides a framework for understanding how stress-induced network alterations may contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathies.

items.title: Neural reactivation of past events tracks narrative understanding as it unfolds
items.abstract: Understanding of episodic experience is not achieved at a single moment: it is a constructive process in which each new event is interpreted in light of relevant past events and prior knowledge. Yet this process is rarely measured as it unfolds, leaving unclear how the brain integrates past events to construct an evolving understanding of the present. We hypothesized that neural reactivation of past events at narrative event boundaries reflects not merely what people experience, but how they interpret their experience. We developed a behavioural paradigm that tracks, as a narrative unfolds, which past events people consider relevant for understanding each new event. By manipulating prior knowledge of the narrative's final plot twist, we examined the process by which the same experience yields different understanding. Across independent behavioural and fMRI cohorts, we found that prior knowledge similarly altered the variability and intersubject similarity of inferred relations between events and their neural reactivation at narrative event boundaries in the Default Mode Network. Moreover, stronger neural reactivation was associated with greater inferred relevance between events, and event pairs showing different behavioural relations across groups also showed corresponding differences in reactivation. These findings suggest that neural reactivation of past events at event boundaries reflects an unfolding inferential process that transforms shared experience into subjective understanding.

items.title: Genetic, neural and early-environmental architecture of resilience
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Economics, National Taiwan University, Taipei, Taiwan
items.abstract: Resilience is shaped by factors ranging from the genome through early-life experience to the brain, yet its biological basis in humans remains unclear because studies have rarely integrated these levels and have been confined to small samples. Using the Brief Resilience Scale (BRS) and multimodal data from tens of thousands of UK Biobank (UKB) participants, with replication in Generation Scotland (GS), we found that resting-state functional connectivity, particularly within the flexibility and valuation networks, is a robust neural correlate of resilience. Resilience also showed a generalizable genetic basis: a polygenic score (PGS) derived from a UKB genome-wide association study predicted BRS in GS. Genes and childhood experiences converged on the flexibility network through distinct routes: the polygenic association with resilience was partly explained by central executive-salience integration, whereas childhood experiences were associated with default-mode-centered integration. By separating genetically anchored from experience-sensitive routes, these findings point to network targets that interventions could tailor to the sources of an individual's vulnerability.

items.title: A radial glial regulatory program bridges progenitor maintenance and neuronal identity
items.abstract: The cerebral cortex acquires its neuronal diversity through successive waves of neurogenesis. How molecular differences among early progenitors relate to their neuronal output remains unclear. Here, we identify a molecular program in early SOX9-high radial glia (S9RGs) that links progenitor maintenance with the regulation of genes associated with neuronal identity. Combining transcriptional and chromatin profiling with in vivo perturbations, we identify a program involving extracellular signaling, cell-cycle regulation, progenitor maintenance, and neurogenesis. We show that SOX9 regulates part of this program, including receptors that contribute to progenitor maintenance, while Notch acts upstream of Sox9 and reproduces several transcriptional and chromatin features of S9RGs. S9RGs express selected later-stage radial glial features and show distinct chromatin accessibility patterns at genes involved in progenitor maintenance, neurogenesis, and neuronal identity. Notch activation reproduces part of these changes, including differences at genes associated with lower- and upper-layer neuronal specification. Interestingly, S9RGs, which preferentially generate upper-layer neurons, share molecular features with the highly proliferative RG population in ferrets and with human outer RGs (oRGs) from cortical organoids, despite their different positions within the developing cortex. Together, our findings suggest that molecular differences among early radial glia could influence both how long they remain as progenitors and the neuronal identities they subsequently generate.

items.title: Gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens
items.abstract: Sexual differentiation of the brain of birds is shaped by gonadal steroid hormones and also by cell-autonomous mechanisms resulting from limited sex chromosome dosage compensation. In this study, we compare gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens treated with the aromatase inhibitor fadrozole to their control counterparts. Consistent with a lack of dosage compensation, we find a robust effect of sex chromosomes on hypothalamic gene expression, and a large portion of differentially expressed genes were on the Z and W sex chromosomes. Despite the presence of developing testes and markedly reduced estrogen concentrations in fadrozole-treated chromosomal female (ZW) birds, we find modest effects of gonadal hormones on gene expression in the brain. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis revealed that the most prominent effects were attributable to interactions between chromosomal sex and treatment. Our results highlight that chromosomal sex and steroid hormones together shape the sexual differentiation of the embryonic avian brain, challenging the primacy of the organizational effects of sex steroids on the brain during development.

items.title: Biphasic glycocalyx remodelling balances immune cell recruitment and tissue damage during influenza infection
items.abstract: The endothelial glycocalyx is a glycan-rich barrier lining blood vessels that regulates immune cell recruitment, whose role in viral infection is unknown. Using a murine influenza model, we reveal that the lung endothelial glycocalyx undergoes coordinated biphasic remodelling: early shedding followed by substantial accumulation during peak immune activation. Genetic deletion of heparanase, the enzyme driving early glycocalyx shedding, reduced immune cell lung infiltration and improved host recovery. Conversely, using a new endothelial-specific glycocalyx depletion mouse model, we demonstrate that this glycocalyx accumulation actively limits immune cell recruitment and prevents excessive tissue damage. Together, these findings reveal that coordinated endothelial and immune cell glycocalyx remodelling is an active and previously unrecognised regulator of the balance between antiviral immune cell recruitment and tissue protection.

items.title: Quiescent Cells Exhibit a Senescence-Like Secretory Phenotype
items.abstract: Cellular quiescence is traditionally considered a reversible state of cell cycle arrest, distinct from senescence, which is associated with a characteristic senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). However, whether quiescent cells exhibit a comparable secretory program remains poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize a Quiescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (QASP) by integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing datasets from human fibroblasts and preadipocytes. We find that quiescent cells exhibit increased expression of genes encoding inflammatory mediators and extracellular matrix-associated proteins, with substantial overlap between the QASP and SASP. This transcriptional program is highly heterogeneous, varying across cell types, quiescence induction methods, and environmental oxygen levels. In particular, contact inhibition induces a stronger inflammatory signature than serum withdrawal in several cellular contexts. Multiplexed cytokine profiling demonstrated active secretion of inflammatory mediators, including IL-1{beta}, IL-6, IL-15, and CCL2, in quiescent fibroblasts, with secretion levels varying by induction method and generally higher following contact inhibition than serum withdrawal. Analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data from human lung tissue further reveals increased QASP-associated gene expression in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), particularly in myofibroblasts, linking this phenotype to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, these findings identify the QASP as a context-dependent secretory program that shares features with the SASP and may contribute to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling in both physiological and pathological conditions.

items.title: GCase deficiency impairs uptake of α-synuclein-loaded ectosome by astrocytes
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves the prion-like propagation of -synuclein. One mechanism for the spread of -synuclein between neurons in PD is ectosomes. But PD is a multicellular disorder in which astrocytes also play a critical role. How astrocytes take up ectosomes and whether this is affected in PD is unclear. Here we show that GCase-deficiency, as occurs in PD, impairs astrocytic uptake of neuron-derived ectosomes containing -synuclein. The defect in ectosome uptake by astrocytes is driven by compromised macropinocytosis and can be rescued by reducing glucosylceramides or restoring lysosomal function. These findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a key regulator of ectosome uptake by primary and iPSC-derived astrocytes. They also support a shift from the uptake and clearance of -synuclein by astrocytes in health, towards the transmission of -synuclein pathology towards neurons in PD.

items.title: Maternal obesity disrupts glucose oxidation and mitochondrial fission in the myometrium at term gestation
items.abstract: Women with obesity experience delayed spontaneous labor onset, slow labor progression, and elevated risk of labor dystocia, but the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. We previously established a mouse model of diet-induced obesity that exhibits decreased uterine contractility, labor dystocia, and elevated fatty acids in the myometrium. Here, we used this model to determine how maternal obesity affects energy production and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium at term. Myometrium tissue and myometrial smooth muscle cells from diet-induced obese mice at term showed decreased pyruvate utilization, inhibition of glucose oxidation, and disruption of mitochondrial fission and mitophagy. Treatment with medium-chain fatty acids in both murine and human primary myometrial cells resulted in significant decreases in abundance of mitochondrial fission proteins. Finally, mitochondrial spare capacity in human myometrial cells decreased with body mass index of the patient providing the cells. Taken together, these findings indicate that fatty acid accumulation dysregulates energy metabolism and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium and may contribute to dysfunctional labor in women with obesity.

items.title: Vertical transmission and community turnover in seed-borne microbiomes: lessons from an aMAIZEing model system
items.corresponding_institution: University of Groningen/State University of Northern Rio de Janeiro
items.abstract: The seed microbiome represents a specialized ecological niche, governed by assembly processes that are only partially coupled to the surrounding soil community. While environmental recruitment and vertical transmission from the maternal plant are both recognized sources of seed-associated microorganisms, the mechanisms that determine their relative contributions and whether these contributions shift across generations remain poorly understood. Here, we used long-read metagenomic sequencing to track seed-borne bacterial community dynamics across a founding seed pool and two subsequent generations in two divergent maize (Zea mays L.) varieties exposed to contrasting organic and mineral fertilisation regimes. We recovered 112 medium- or high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes and combined MAG-level taxonomic and functional analyses with genus-level community profiling to characterize persistence and turnover dynamics within the seed microbiome. While soil taxonomic diversity was high, seed-associated communities showed a near-complete compositional disconnect from soil-dominant assemblages taxa, with a persistent Firmicutes core maintained across generations, consistent with vertical transmission. Priority effects remain a possible explanation for these patterns but were not directly tested. Genus-level source attribution suggested greater environmental recruitment under organic fertilization, with more diverse soil communities and a stronger contribution from the preceding seed generation under mineral fertilization. Seed-associated MAGs also carried genes associated with plant growth-promoting potential, although these detections could not be consistently linked to specific transmission routes. In contrast, maize genotype had no detectable effect on seed microbiome composition. Intergenerational persistence and environmental recruitment jointly shape seed-derived communities under contrasting fertilization regimes. Their relative contributions remain inferred from taxonomic overlap, and the effects of microbial source-pool diversity cannot be separated from the accompanying differences in soil chemistry in this design.

items.title: The pangenome of the Arctic picoeukaryote Micromonas polaris resolves cryptic ecotypes and identifies a polar-specific gene repertoire
items.abstract: Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological breadth has remained unclear. Standard phylogenetic markers such as 18S rRNA are nearly invariant within M. polaris and conceal any internal genomic heterogeneity the species may possess. Here we present a pangenome of 14 M. polaris strains spanning the Arctic basin, integrated with Tara Oceans metagenomes, that resolves the species into two diverged ecotypes invisible to 18S rRNA but recovered consistently by prp8, genome-wide SNPs, ANI, and orthogroup-based phylogenies. The two ecotypes coexist sympatrically, with one lineage consistently enriched deeper in the water column across the basin. M. polaris carries 990 polar-specific hierarchical orthogroups absent from temperate Micromonas, organised around one-carbon metabolism, endocytosis, transmembrane transport, and photo-oxidative stress response. Several components show phylogenetic signatures of horizontal acquisition from co-occurring marine taxa. Atlantification is bringing temperate Micromonas into Arctic margins seasonally, but the polar night likely limits their year-round persistence. M. polaris and its polar-specific toolkit appear positioned to persist through the dark season, suggesting Arctic margins will undergo seasonal turnover rather than stable replacement.

items.title: KORUS: probabilistic ancestry inference beyond variant calls
items.abstract: Ancestry inference typically relies on variant calling and predefined population labels. We present KORUS, a probabilistic framework that infers ancestry from sequencing-derived k-mer representations constructed using ancestry-informative reference variants and encoded in Bloom filters, without requiring explicit variant calls for query genomes. KORUS separates genomic feature representation from ancestry decoding, enabling supervised classification, fractional ancestry inference, and unsupervised population structure discovery within a unified framework. Reference models were constructed from 643 genomes from the 1000 Genomes Project and the Simons Genome Diversity Project. Evaluation on an independent cohort of 22 whole-genome sequencing samples, with comparisons to ntRoot, SNVstory, and ADMIXTURE, showed recovery of continental-scale population structure, with supervised classification accuracy of 72.7-81.8% and ancestry-fraction concordance of R2 = 0.844-0.993 relative to ADMIXTURE and R2 = 0.665-0.983 relative to ntRoot. Ancestry estimates were consistent across alternative k-mer representations. Analyses of ancient human and archaic hominin genomes demonstrated that probabilistic projections quantify affinity to the learned feature space rather than necessarily indicating modern continental ancestry. KORUS provides a unified approach to ancestry inference directly from sequencing-derived representations and is freely available under the GPLv3 license at https://github.com/BirolLab/korus.

items.title: Policy-Enforced Genomic Repositories and Institutional Data Governance for African Pathogen Surveillance with UbuntuBio
items.corresponding_institution: West African Centre for Cell Biology of Infectious Pathogens (WACCBIP), University of Ghana, Legon, Accra, Ghana
items.abstract: Research centers curating pathogen sequence cohorts often operate under constrained bandwidth, multi-institutional data-sharing agreements, and strict biosafety requirements. Global public archives keep released sequences permanently open, external viral portals enforce terms outside local institutional custody, and standard Git Large File Storage (LFS) duplicates identical binaries across repositories without validating taxonomy or geography. We present UbuntuBio (v1.0.0), a Git-native, policy-enforced genomic repository platform deployed at https://ubuntubio.org and developed at the West African Centre for Cell Biology of Infectious Pathogens (WACCBIP), University of Ghana. UbuntuBio integrates four mechanisms under a single storage root: (1) bare Git repositories storing dataset cards, sample sheets, and approximately 130-byte LFS pointers backed by prefix-sharded SHA-256 content-addressed storage (CAS) with visibility-scoped wire deduplication; (2) a four-phase commit pipeline recoverable via cross-plane reconciliation that enforces 55 African Union country codes against offline Natural Earth polygons, core MIxS-derived fields, Taxon 9606 rejection, and server-keyed targeted human-marker screening identically across HTTP commits and Git pre-receive hooks; (3) institutional custody controls combining Data Use Agreements (DUAs), revocable 900-second RS256 capability tokens, key rotation, tamper-evident hash-chained logs, and externally anchorable RS256 audit checkpoints; and (4) an embedded SQLite WAL and FTS5 catalog filtered by access tier. In single-node evaluation, UbuntuBio classified 18/18 policy boundary fixtures consistently across Python, Git, and HTTP paths; showed 0/265,157 false cross-matches on 21/22 RefSeq pathogen sequences (while cross-matching Candida albicans 18S rDNA at 0.113% and Chlorocebus sabaeus Alu repeats in ENA stool reads, confirming targeted marker detection rather than verified human DNA decontamination); matched conditional uniform (n = 2,000; 200-seed 0.01% convergence 19.0% vs. 18.13% expected) and interior (n = 1,000) detection theory while detecting all spike-ins at [≥] 0.5% (30/30); halved two-repository disk usage on 613.83 MiB Nigerian E. coli runs; passed 27/27 structured-filter correctness checks over 10,000 biosamples and reached graded NDCG@10 = 0.920 on independent free-text BM25 queries with zero private leaks; and recovered cleanly across seven injected phase-transition faults.

items.title: Measuring Phylogenetic Information Content Based on Clade Support
items.abstract: Phylogenetic information content is often understood as the degree to which data lend support to hypotheses about the monophyly of clades. This is most commonly expressed in terms of clade support, typically estimated by resampling techniques such as the bootstrap and the jackknife. Here, I discuss how to summarize this aspect of data quality. I show that raw bootstrap or jackknife proportions are unsuitable for this purpose and instead suggest a logarithmic transformation, which can be interpreted as translating the clade support values to the number of characters expected to give the same resampling proportion in parsimony analysis of a homoplasy-free data matrix. The distribution of the number of these "supporting characters" and descriptive statistics derived from this distribution, such as the mean (Mean Character Support, or MCS) and its standard deviation, provide powerful summaries of the quality of the underlying data set. I demonstrate for both empirical and simulated data sets that MCS accurately reflects information content, and that some popular alternative measures of data quality (the ensemble consistency index, the ensemble retention index, data decisiveness and the total support index) do not. Unlike most other measures of data quality, MCS can be applied to trees resulting from a range of alternative phylogenetic methods, including parsimony, distance and maximum likelihood approaches.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Refractive Index Patterns Distinguish CD57-Defined Subsets of Human Memory T Cells
items.corresponding_institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST)
items.abstract: Distinguishing T-cell subsets is important for characterizing immune differentiation, but label-free classification is challenging because closely related subsets have overlapping biophysical properties. We combined holotomography with a three-dimensional convolutional neural network to classify primary human T cells from their refractive index (RI) tomograms. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting defined four reference populations: CD4+, naive CD8+, and CD57- and CD57+ memory CD8+ T cells. The FishNet-inspired classifier achieved 97.04% accuracy in a cell-level held-out test of 270 cells. Dedicated binary classifiers achieved 97.70% accuracy for naive versus CCR7- memory CD8+ cells and 94.44% for CD57- versus CD57+ memory CD8+ cells. Although the memory subsets overlapped in whole-cell descriptors, their volumetric RI patterns supported classification. These findings establish a basis for investigating intrinsic optical phenotypes associated with CD57-defined T-cell differentiation.

items.title: High-throughput identification of changes in cellular localization for RNA-binding proteins during adenovirus infection reveals viral harnessing of nuclear speckles
items.abstract: Adenovirus (AdV) is a human DNA virus reliant on host RNA processing machinery. While research into AdV has yielded landmark discoveries in RNA biology, studies investigating the scope of AdV dependency on specific host RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are lacking. Here we performed optical pooled screening on a cell library where hundreds of RBPs are endogenously tagged. Pooled imaging followed by in situ barcode sequencing revealed a broad view of virus-induced host RBP relocalization patterns, including those recruited to viral replication compartments (VRCs). A targeted siRNA screen of relocalized RBPs demonstrated a requirement for the nuclear speckle (NS) core protein SON during virus infection. Depletion of SON resulted in reduced viral gene expression, impaired NS protein recruitment to early-stage VRCs, and impaired mobility of SRRM2 during infection. These findings suggest a crucial role of SON and NS functions in regulating viral gene expression and demonstrate the power of pooled tagging coupled to optical screening in investigating virus-host interactions.

items.title: Cell-state conditioning predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects
items.corresponding_institution: Department and Institute of Urology, Hubei Provincial Clinical Research Center for Minimally Invasive Treatment of Urology, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical Coll
items.abstract: Second-generation sequence models can be conditioned on a cell state supplied as a single-cell snapshot rather than selected from a fixed catalogue, but whether that conditioning carries an experimentally applied perturbation has not been tested. We conditioned such a model on interferon-{beta}-stimulated and unstimulated monocytes from a published experiment, using cells disjoint from those providing the measurement, and asked whether the predicted expression response tracks the measured one and whether the same conditioning identifies expression QTL specific to the stimulated state. Predicted and measured responses agree at Spearman {rho} = 0.616 across 119 genes (95% CI 0.486 to 0.716), and at 0.607 after all 119 target genes are deleted from the conditioning input; across fifteen conditions the model's response scales with how much each condition's biology genuinely overlaps the target response (slope 0.73, Pearson 0.92), and a near-neighbour monocyte subset receives 0.295 against a measured overlap of 0.336. For stimulation-specific genetic effects we find no reliable evidence: the pre-specified primary arm moves from p = 0.0019 to 0.443 once both conditions must carry a measurable predicted effect, and the separation localises to the resting-condition baseline. Neither model generation's catalogue contains a perturbed sample, 0 of 4,430 tracks and 0 of 2,799 conditions, although both carry activation-state labels, so the gap is experimental perturbation rather than cell state. Two incidental findings apply beyond this model: credible-set membership mislabels over half of putatively condition-specific loci, and gating a ratio statistic on its larger term manufactures signal.

items.title: SpaceMACE: Spatially-Aware Tumour Cell Annotation for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.abstract: Accurate discrimination between tumour and non-tumour cells is essential for interpreting spatial transcriptomics data and identifying spatially resolved therapeutic targets. Existing tumour-cell annotation approaches were primarily developed for single-cell RNA sequencing and do not explicitly incorporate the spatial organization of cells. Here, we introduce SpaceMACE, an extension of the MACE tumour-cell annotation framework for sequencing-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. SpaceMACE first combines reference-based cell-type classification with copy-number-variation-based tumour classification. The resulting consensus annotations are subsequently refined using spatial proximity and gene-expression similarity. We evaluated SpaceMACE across multiple spatial transcriptomics platforms, including Stereo-seq, Visium HD, CosMx and Xenium, and across colorectal, hepatocellular and ovarian cancer datasets. SpaceMACE retained the high precision of the original MACE framework while improving the spatial coherence of tumour-cell annotations. Together, these results demonstrate that SpaceMACE provides a scalable and platform-independent framework for tumour-cell annotation in spatial transcriptomics and supports the spatial investigation of tumour-specific molecular targets.

items.title: statLens enables accurate and interpretable statistical intelligence
items.abstract: Diverse existing approaches and analyses of large-scale biomedical omics datasets along with the complexity of the corresponding statistical analytical workflows pose challenges to the direct application of large language models (LLMs) to data analysis tasks. We present statLens, a model-agnostic AI-driven statistical intelligence framework that integrates LLMs, code and human review. We demonstrate statLens using differential expression analysis across heterogeneous biomedical data as a use case. On 102 benchmark tasks from 74 datasets across six omics modalities, statLens maintained consistently high accuracy (92.5--95.0\%) across seven language models and outperformed LLM-only inference (17.5--46.8\%), whereas autonomous-agent accuracy varied widely (58.7--99.5\%). We also showed that statLens substantially improved the accuracy of the four small language models (92.5--94.4\%) over autonomous agents (58.7--92.2\%) and LLM-only inference (17.5--43.5\%). By decomposing analytical workflows into complementary tasks for code, LLMs and human experts, statLens provides an integrated framework for more accurate, interpretable and reproducible AI-assisted data analysis, particularly in complex omics settings.

items.title: From Calcium-dependent currents to Multitarget Therapy: A Pharmacological Strategy for Glioblastoma
items.corresponding_institution: International School for Advanced Studies (SISSA), via Bonomea 265, Trieste 34136, Italy.
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor with limited treatment options and substantial interpatient heterogeneity. Ion transport and cell-volume regulation may represent pharmacological vulnerabilities in glioma stem cells (GSCs). Here, we characterized membrane currents in patient-derived GSCs, identifying a calcium-dependent anion conductance consistent with volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) and an inward current consistent with Na+/Ca++ exchanger exchanger (NCX) activity. Based on these findings, we investigated individual compounds and developed a multitarget cocktail comprising niflumic acid (NFA), bumetanide (BTN), and R-ketorolac (R-K) to target complementary mechanisms involved in ion homeostasis, cell-volume regulation, and cellular dynamics. The cocktail affected cell viability and mechanical properties and showed synergistic effects in U87 cells and patient-derived GSCs with similar electrophysiological profiles. Treatment did not measurably alter spontaneous activity in cultured hippocampal neurons but caused substantial HMC3 cytotoxicity. Encapsulation in transferrin-functionalized liposomes attenuated HMC3 toxicity while preserving activity against glioblastoma cells, suggesting a potential strategy to improve treatment selectivity. Further pharmacological studies identified a potential vulnerability associated with NCX activity, although its contribution to cytotoxicity remains unclear. Overall, our findings highlight electrophysiological heterogeneity in patient-derived GSCs and support further investigation of ion transport as a therapeutic target in GBM. Combining multitarget pharmacology with targeted drug delivery may help address heterogeneous treatment responses, although further studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms, safety, and vivo efficacy.

items.title: HDAC1/2 maintain TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma
items.abstract: Genomic TERT locus rearrangements define an aggressive high-risk neuroblastoma subgroup characterized by enhancer hijacking, high-level TERT expression and continuous telomerase activation. Although these structural alterations supply a strong transcriptional drive, the post-transcriptional mechanisms preserving TERT mRNA presence remain incompletely understood. We identified histone deacetylases 1 and 2 (HDAC1/2) as essential post-transcriptional guardians of TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma. Pharmacological inhibition or RNAi-mediated depletion of HDAC1 and HDAC2, but not HDACs 3-11, rapidly downregulated TERT transcript levels and suppressed telomerase enzymatic activity. Transcript decay kinetics following transcriptional arrest with actinomycin D confirmed that HDAC1/2 blockade accelerates TERT mRNA decay, reducing transcript half-life by 30-47%. High-resolution ChIP-seq profiling across the translocation breakpoint demonstrated HDAC inhibition does not alter local chromatin accessibility. Array-based DNA methylation profiling showed only a mild, non-specific global reduction in CpG island methylation upon panobinostat exposure and no focal correlation with TERT transcript loss across the breakpoint locus. Depleting TERT mRNA via HDAC1/2 inhibition dismantled a core 50-gene TERT-associated oncogenic expression network. Ectopic re-expression of TERT cDNA partially rescued cellular viability and normalized expression of key signature genes despite continuous HDAC inhibition. HDAC1/2 inhibition significantly attenuated tumor growth, reduced intratumor TERT expression and prolonging overall survival in both preventive and therapeutic TERT-rearranged xenograft mouse models. Our data establish a post-transcriptional rather than transcriptional mode of TERT regulation and confirm tumor suppression is partly driven by depleting TERT transcripts, uncovering a HDAC1/2 dependency in TERT-driven neuroblastoma. We provide a molecular rationale for therapeutic strategies disrupting HDAC1/2-mediated TERT mRNA stabilization.

items.title: Semi-stability and unfolding of a KH domain modulate RNA binding and functions of MEX3A
items.corresponding_institution: Bavarian NMR Center, Technical University of Munich, 85747 Garching, Germany
items.abstract: MEX3A is essential for binding to Ago2/miR-126-5p and inhibition of apoptosis in endothelial cells implicated in cardiovascular health. Here, we discovered that the KH1 domain within the RNA binding region of MEX3A exists in equilibrium with an unfolded conformation. Using NMR spectroscopy and biophysical analysis, we dissect the KH1 folding kinetics and show that increased KH1 stability correlates with higher RNA affinity. The unfolded state of KH1 enables phosphorylation of T162, locking the domain in the unfolded conformation and enables recognition by 14-3-3 {zeta}. Residues in MEX3A KH1 that reduce its stability are located outside the RNA-binding interface and are evolutionary selected compared to human MEX3 paralogs. Semi-stability of KH domains in MEX3A and other multi-KH proteins may provide a general mechanism to tune RNA binding, enable phosphorylation and regulate biological function.

items.title: Prefoldin facilitates the action of FACT on macroH2A1-containing chromatin during transcription elongation
items.abstract: Prefoldin is one of the chaperone complexes that participate in protein homeostasis. Although it was initially described as a co-translational cochaperon that captures newly synthesized polypeptides and facilitates their folding by transferring them to class II chaperonins, nuclear functions have also been reported, including its contribution to transcription elongation and chromatin dynamics from budding yeast to mammalian cells. In this work, we have performed a proteomic search for prefoldin interactors in chromatin. Among others, we detected its physical association to FACT, the main histone chaperon that operates during transcription elongation. Lack of prefoldin provokes phenotypes associated to FACT perturbation, like chromatin-integrity defects in transcribed gene bodies, and derepression of cryptic transcription. It also leads to the specific alteration of FACT transcriptional dynamics in prefoldin-regulated genes. Lack of prefoldin also provokes co-transcriptional defects in histone dynamics, particularly in the eviction of macroH2A1, being this non-canonical histone a prefoldin-interactor itself. Finally, we show that these physical and functional connections with FACT and macroH2A1 respond to a single molecular phenomenon, and propose a model in which prefoldin would play a bridging role, enabling FACT to drive co-transcriptional eviction of macroH2A1-containing nucleosomes.

items.title: Evaluating local assembly strategies for human long-read structural variant calling
items.abstract: Long-read sequencing enables detection of structural variants (SVs) with far greater accuracy and completeness than was previously possible. This advance has spurred the development of many SV callers that implement diverse algorithmic strategies. Commonly, SV calling proceeds in several processing steps. Evaluations of SV callers, however, typically focus on overall performance and conceal which steps drive observed differences. This hinders targeted, evidence-based improvements to existing SV calling approaches. Here, we implemented five consensus computation strategies similar to those employed by popular SV callers that perform a local assembly. We compare their outputs on extensive simulated and real data and reveal that some strategies are more effective for particular input data types. For example, the strategy employed by PacBio's tool Sawfish works very well on HiFi reads and recent ONT data, but fails on the older and noisier ONT reads. While the read error profiles and the read pre-processing has a substantial influence on some strategies, other strategies are more robust overall. These findings guide algorithmic decisions for the development of improved future SV callers.

items.title: Human Endogenous Retrovirus K RNA triggers cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation by initiating pathological nuclear condensates
items.abstract: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear RNA-binding protein TDP-43 is a defining pathology of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and is seen in many cases of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet what initiates this process remains unknown. Here we identify an unexpected trigger: RNA from human endogenous retrovirus-K (HERV-K), an ancient retroviral element embedded in the human genome. Using CRISPR-engineered cells expressing Halo-tagged TDP-43 at endogenous levels, we show that HERV-K activation drives formation of cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregates and functional loss of nuclear TDP-43, measured by aberrant cryptic exon inclusion. Surprisingly, cytoplasmic aggregation is preceded by the appearance of phosphorylated TDP-43 condensates in the nucleus, structures we term Pathological ERV-TDP-43-Associated Nuclear Spheres (PETANS). Live-cell imaging reveals that cytoplasmic inclusions originate directly from these nuclear bodies. This inverts the conventional model to suggest that pathological TDP-43 condensation begins in the nucleus, not the cytoplasm. Super-resolution imaging and structure-function mapping show that HERV-K RNA localizes within PETANS and drives their formation, with a minimal UG-rich non-coding element sufficient to induce the full cascade of nuclear and cytoplasmic pathology. Our findings establish an endogenous retroviral RNA as a direct molecular nucleator of TDP-43 proteinopathy.

items.title: How goals shape naturalistic memories: bias in gaze and narrative recall
items.abstract: Episodic memories are thought to represent information framed by our individual perception and goals, yet personal experiences are hard to evaluate externally. Due to novel methodological advances, we could now trace the development of such goal-shaped memories in a naturalistic experimental setting. We recorded eye-tracking while participants encoded episodic-like memories, and later recorded participants freely narrating their experiences. Naturalistic goal-states were induced by introducing a secret job, which promised to reward participants later for person-based or space-based information. Using computer-vision based semantic segmentation of visual scanning behaviour in movie scenes and data-driven coding of free recall performance, we show that these goals increasingly shift attention during memory encoding and systematically bias narration during retrieval to goal-relevant dimensions. Our findings highlight that we can use data-driven methodology to observe how naturally occurring or induced biases shape how we perceive and remember the world.

items.title: AlphaGenome 2 predicts regulatory activity and variant effects across cell states
items.abstract: Most genetic variants associated with human traits and diseases lie in non-coding DNA, where they can alter gene regulation in specific cell types and states. Single-cell atlases chart these states across tissues and development, but rarely profile enough donors to associate variants with expression directly. Deep learning models could bridge this gap by predicting variant effects from DNA sequence, yet they poorly distinguish related cell states and require fine-tuning for new datasets. Here we present AlphaGenome 2 (AG2), which substantially advances cell-type-specific prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects for gene expression and chromatin accessibility. Trained on organism-wide human and mouse single-cell atlases and bulk functional genomics data, AG2 takes as input a 1-Mb DNA sequence and a condition specifying a target tissue, cell type, or cell state. Conditioning enables AG2 to impute unmeasured epigenomic tracks and predict multimodal variant effects across cell types. Inferring this condition directly from gene expression extends AG2 to unseen datasets and cell states without fine-tuning. AG2 outperforms fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1 and specialized models trained on target datasets, doubling recall of causal single-cell eQTLs at 90% precision. AG2 also achieves state-of-the-art enhancer-gene linking and can pinpoint causal variants at complex trait loci. Across hundreds of human cell types, we generated an atlas of enhancer-gene links and scores for 7 million common variants. As single-cell profiling expands across development, tissues, and disease cohorts, AG2 provides a blueprint for turning observational atlases into variant effect maps.

items.title: Development of a Temperature-Based Method for Repeated Markerless Gene Integration in cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942
items.abstract: Genetic engineering of cyanobacteria can require multiple rounds of genome modification, highlighting the need for flexible markerless engineering tools. Here, we established a temperature-based markerless gene integration method using the temperature-sensitive H1 strain of Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, which, unlike the wild-type strain, cannot grow at 40 {degrees}C. Disruption of nynA, encoding a putative endoribonuclease, allowed H1 to grow at 40 {degrees}C, enabling transformants with genes integrated at the nynA locus to be selected without an antibiotic-resistance marker. Complementation of nynA at a separate genomic locus restored temperature sensitivity, allowing the same selection principle to be reused. Using this strategy, gfp, mScarlet, and luciferase were sequentially integrated, with all three genes retained and expressed. To demonstrate its applicability to metabolic engineering, markerless integration of cnsA, encoding cineole synthase, enabled 1,8-cineole production at 81.4 {+/-} 9.52 {micro}g /g wet cell weight. This strategy enables repeated markerless genome modification in the H1 strain using temperature-based selection.

items.title: Gene network topologies for heterogeneity restoration during self-renewal
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas at Dallas
items.abstract: The ability for a subset of cells to establish a heterogeneous cell population with multi-lineage competency is crucial for the self-renewal capacity of tissues and organs. Restoration of heterogeneous gene expression patterns has been observed in pluripotent and multi-potent stem cells, and the heterogeneity restoration can influence the potential of differentiation into multiple cell types. Similarly, cancer cells can acquire the capacity to establish non-genetic heterogeneity that plays a role in cancer progression and resistance to therapeutics. Specific models of gene regulatory networks have been proposed to explain heterogeneity restoration. However, due to the lack of systematic analysis, it is unclear which network topologies are more efficient for this multicellular function, and what intrinsic and extrinsic factors can determine the optimal choice of network topology. In this work, we use mathematical models describing gene expression of single cells and their underlying population dynamics to examine the influence of network topology on the recovery of multimodal expression patterns originating from a homogeneous population. We found that feedback loops are a key factor contributing to heterogeneity restoration. Negative and positive feedback loops support the existence of heterogeneity restoration, but only positive feedback can accelerate the process with low cost of single-cell-level variations of expression. Furthermore, networks with mixed feedback were the most robust ones for heterogeneity restoration with respect to changes in both kinetic rate constants and noise levels. Using experimentally validated network databases, we showed that genes involved in feedback loops are enriched with functions related to cell fate decisions, and we identified examples of realistic gene regulatory networks cell fate dynamics. Our results suggest multiple potential evolutionary paths towards gene circuits governing heterogeneity restoration and key factors contributing to the dynamics of this process. We expect that this systematic study will enable future discoveries of new gene regulatory networks governing progenitor and cancer cell dynamics as well as therapeutic strategies targeting heterogeneity-enabling circuits.

items.title: Pathogenic human autoantibodies target the soluble CASPR2 ectodomain to induce network hyperexcitability
items.corresponding_institution: CNC, UC, Rua Larga, Edificio FMUC, 3004-504, Coimbra, PT; CIBB, UC, Rua Larga, Edificio FMUC, 3004-504 Coimbra, PT
items.abstract: The mechanisms by which autoantibodies contribute to antibody-mediated neurological diseases remain poorly understood. Autoantibodies targeting the extracellular domain of CASPR2 are found in patients with clinical features consistent with hyperexcitability, including neuromyotonia and seizures. These antibodies are reported to disrupt the functions of membrane-embedded CASPR2. However, given that CASPR2 is also detected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which contains CASPR2 autoantibodies, targeting of CSF-shed CASPR2 may represent an additional pathogenic mechanism, introducing a novel paradigm of soluble antigen modulation by autoantibodies. Here, we found that patient-derived polyclonal and monoclonal CASPR2 antibodies enhanced neuronal network excitability and selectively amplified excitatory synaptic transmission in human and rat primary cortical neurons. In addition, CASPR2 antibodies impaired calcium homeostasis and altered the intrinsic properties of both excitatory and inhibitory neurons. Notably, these antibodies depleted CASPR2 from both neuronal culture medium and patient CSF, suggesting targeting of the shed CASPR2 ectodomain. Knockdown of plasma membrane calcium ATPase 2 (PMCA2), a reported target of the CASPR2 ectodomain, abrogated the observed effects of CASPR2 antibodies. Together, our findings identify shed CASPR2 as a underrecognized pathogenic target of CASPR2 autoantibodies and demonstrate that its neutralization disrupts PMCA2-mediated calcium regulation, driving neuronal network hyperexcitability. More broadly, we identify the neuronal sheddome as a source of autoantibody targets and soluble protein neutralization as a novel disease mechanism, highlighting shed CASPR2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target.

items.title: A Dysregulated Peripheral Immune Landscape Favors the Expansion of Epstein-Barr Virus positive Age-Associated B Cells in Multiple Sclerosis
items.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS), but the underlying mechanisms are not yet known. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing coupled with targeted EBV transcript enrichment to characterize host immune and viral transcriptional dynamics following EBV ex vivo infection of PBMCs from people with active MS compared to healthy controls (HC). Early responses to EBV were dominated by differences in monocyte and NK cells, including EBV transcripts in monocytes prior to ex vivo infection. At later time points, expansion of EBV-infected age-associated B-cells (ABCs) and increased expression of T-cell exhaustion- associated markers were elevated in MS. EBV-infected ABCs were deregulated for EBV lytic genes and cellular pathways associated with interferon-alpha responses, antigen processing and Toll-like receptor signaling. Together, these findings define an MS-associated inflammatory immune state and dysfunctional response that favors the formation of pathogenic EBV-infected ABCs.

items.title: Phosphorylated Pol II CTD supports histone hitchhiking during transcription elongation
items.abstract: Transcription requires RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to disrupt nucleosomes while preserving displaced histones for reuse. How these histones remain available as the polymerase advances is incompletely understood. Here we combine optical trapping and fluorescence imaging to follow Pol II-nucleosome encounters in a simplified mammalian elongation system. Displaced histone particles frequently move with the advancing elongation complex, a behavior termed histone hitchhiking. Phosphorylation of the Pol II C-terminal domain (CTD) reduces nucleosomal blocking and supports histone retention during carriage. Structural predictions suggest that phosphorylated CTD repeats engage basic histone surfaces through variable, charge-complementary contacts. Carried particles can subsequently transfer to upstream DNA, and a broader combination of elongation factors increases upstream transfer. Complexes already carrying a histone particle show increased blocking at a second nucleosome. Other encounters leave one particle on upstream DNA while another moves with the complex, suggesting that transfer of one particle may enable capture and carriage of the next during successive nucleosome traversal. These observations support a model in which reversible contacts with the phosphorylated CTD help Pol II capture and carry histone particles as they dissociate from downstream DNA, keeping them available for upstream transfer and subsequent chaperone-assisted reassembly. Our findings extend the role of the Pol II CTD beyond factor recruitment to histone handling, linking nucleosome traversal to histone preservation.

items.title: Large scale CRISPR genome engineering reveal principles of single nucleotide microhomology in precision editing
items.abstract: The CRISPR/Cas9 system has emerged as a revolutionary tool with diverse applications in genome engineering; however, the role of nanoscale hydrogen bonds between single nucleotides in precision editing remains unknown. Here we systematically compared A-rich and G-rich PAM-recognizing Cas9 editors through comprehensive analyses of ~37,000 targeting sites with about half million libraries of ~0.36 billion types of editing outcomes. We showed that the A-rich Cas9 editors exhibit stronger editing outcome predictability in comparison with the conventional Cas9 editor of the G-rich PAM. In addition, the A-rich Cas9 editors induce a higher frequency of staggered cleavages, resulting in predictable editing with donor-independent templated insertions. Moreover, we identified distinct DNA sequence motifs for predictable insertions with the A-rich Cas9 editors. In particular, we revealed single nucleotides at the -4 position as MMEJ microhomologies in precision engineering via two or three hydrogen bonds with A-rich or G-rich PAM, respectively. Furthermore, we found that PolQ plays a key role in enhanced random insertions. Finally, we developed a discrete-space diffusion model CRIfuser of deep learning for predicting editing outcomes with staggered cleavage. Together, these findings establish PAM-dependent cleavage geometry as a tunable determinant of Cas9 editing outcomes and provide a framework for predictive and precision genome engineering.

items.title: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories
items.abstract: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating the overall disease accumulation of each individual from the diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease trajectories. We apply the model to 348 diseases, 36 polygenic scores, and 34 monogenic conditions across three biobanks and provide an atlas of the age-dependent effects of inherited variation on common human diseases. We show that polygenic effects change significantly with age. Mendelnoulli improved held-out one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested compared with a model whose polygenic effects are constant across age (mean AUC gain 0.023). For individuals with no prior diagnoses, Mendelnoulli identified 8.6 more cases of every 100 new cases than that model, when each flagged the 5\% at highest risk. For genes with an established disease, Mendelnoulli selected that disease for 27 of 30 genes and ranked it first for 17 (7 expected by chance), and recovered known differences in timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2 (peak 48 vs 66 years). Mendelnoulli succesfully models common and rare genetic influences on disease trajectories jointly throughout the life course.

items.title: Wearable-based sleep and activity tracking detects Parkinson's disease and associated pathological hallmarks
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Thessaloniki, Greece
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with sleep and motor function impairment, even in the early stages. Here, we investigated whether passive wearable-based sleep and activity tracking can detect PD and its associated pathological hallmarks, dopaminergic deficit and -synuclein pathology. Sleep and activity metrics (SAM) were derived from free-living wrist accelerometry data of a U.S. cohort and used to train a machine learning model (SAM-PD) to distinguish persons with PD (n = 133) from healthy controls (n = 26). The model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 and an AUPRC of 0.98, demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability, and generalized without retraining to an independent European cohort (n = 40; 50% PwPD) monitored with a different device (AUROC, 0.95; AUPRC, 0.95). REM sleep duration, walking cadence, and low-level acceleration features were most predictive. Applied to a U.S. at-risk cohort, SAM-PD performed comparably to the resource-intensive Movement Disorder Society (MDS) prodromal PD risk score in detecting dopaminergic deficit (AUROC, 0.86 vs. 0.80; AUPRC, 0.45 vs. 0.46; n = 121; 12.4% prevalence) and -synuclein pathology (AUROC, 0.76 for both; AUPRC 0.50 vs. 0.42; n = 114; 16.7% prevalence). A combination with the MDS score modestly improved detection. Findings support further evaluation of wearable monitoring for PD screening and biomarker enrichment in larger populations.

items.title: In-country cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next generation sequencing for pathogen detection in Lima, Peru
items.abstract: Background: Central nervous system (CNS) infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries such as Peru. However, their epidemiology is poorly characterized due to a wide range of endemic and opportunistic pathogens involved and limited access to specialized neurodiagnostic testing. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can detect any pathogen in a single hypothesis-free assay but has largely been confined to reference laboratories in high-income countries due to high cost and infrastructure requirements. We piloted an in-country, research-based CSF mNGS protocol in Lima, Peru, as a proof-of-concept study to assess the feasibility of implementing this approach in a resource-limited setting. Methods: Adults admitted with suspected CNS infection at Hospital Nacional Dos de Mayo, a large public hospital in Lima, were enrolled from August 2024 to April 2025, and approximately 0.5-2 mL of surplus CSF was collected. CSF mNGS (DNA and RNA) was performed in-country on a benchtop sequencer with half-volume library reactions and cloud-based analysis (CZID). Paired sequencing at a significantly higher depth was performed on a subset of samples in the United States for validation. Results: Among 43 participants (median age 48 years; 21% living with HIV), mNGS performed in Peru detected 20 pathogens in 18 samples (42%), of which 65% were not identified by routine clinical testing. Nine of 15 patients treated empirically for tuberculous meningitis were found to have a non-mycobacterial infection. Detected organisms included Toxoplasma gondii, Taenia solium, Treponema pallidum, human T-lymphotropic virus 1, herpesviruses, and, on deeper sequencing, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus. Deep sequencing yielded 3.7-fold (DNA) and 6.9-fold (RNA) more reads and recovered four pathogens missed at shallower-depth. Conclusions: In-country CSF mNGS was feasible in Lima, Peru and recovered a clinically and epidemiologically meaningful spectrum of CNS pathogens, most missed by routine testing. By utilizing available, lower-output sequencers, we overcame a principal barrier to deploying this technology where the burden of undiagnosed CNS infection is greatest.

items.title: Single-cell lung eQTL colocalization implicates alveolar epithelial regulatory effects at COPD lung-function loci
items.abstract: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung function are highly heritable, but for most genome-wide association study (GWAS) loci, the effector gene and the lung cell type in which it acts are unknown. Single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) offer a way to resolve the cell types in which regulatory variants act. Results: We integrated a multi-ancestry GWAS of the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC; Shrine et al., n = 588,452) with single-cell lung eQTLs across 38 cell types (Natri et al., n = 114) by colocalization. We identified 20 candidate colocalizations (posterior probability of a shared causal variant > 0.7) for 13 genes in nine cell types, predominantly epithelial and immune. The two strongest signals localized DSP, an established COPD effector gene, and NRP2, a candidate effector gene, to alveolar type 2 epithelial cells; only these two colocalizations remained supported under a more conservative shared-effect prior. Both signals, together with FAM13A, were also detectable in bulk lung eQTLs, whereas most remaining loci colocalized only in the single-cell analysis. Conclusions: Single-cell eQTL colocalization resolves the alveolar epithelium as a cellular context for DSP and nominates NRP2 as a candidate lung function effector gene in the same compartment, highlighting the additional cellular resolution provided by single-cell data. The remaining candidate colocalizations warrant replication.

items.title: Loneliness is associated with 15-year risk of stroke: The Framingham Heart Study
items.abstract: Psychosocial factors are promising candidates as modifiable risk factors for stroke. Loneliness is of interest given its rising prevalence worldwide; yet the temporal relationship of loneliness with subsequent stroke remains unclear. Aim: To clarify the association between timing of loneliness and incident stroke. Methods: Framingham Heart Study participants free of stroke with at least two assessments of loneliness prior to incident stroke (at baseline exam, and at prior exam up to 15 years before baseline) were included. Loneliness was assessed using response to the I felt lonely item on the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, defined as feeling lonely for 3 days within the past week. The recency of loneliness was defined as prior loneliness (present at the prior exam) and baseline loneliness (present at the baseline exam). The primary analysis tested separately for associations between prior loneliness vs no prior loneliness, baseline versus no baseline loneliness, and incident stroke, with 15 years of follow up. Cox models were adjusted for age and sex (model 1) and additionally vascular risk factors (model 2), depressive symptoms (model 3), and physical activity (model 4). Interactions between loneliness and age and sex were explored. Results: Among 4307 participants (mean age 62{+/-}10 years, 55% women), 198 (4.5%) had an incident stroke over a median 6.5-year follow-up period. Prior loneliness was reported by 177 (4.1%) and 226 (5.2%) reported baseline loneliness. Compared to participants without prior loneliness, those with prior loneliness had nearly 3-fold increase in stroke risk after adjustment for age, sex, vascular risk factors, depressive symptoms, and physical activity (HR=2.85, 95% [CI] 1.51-5.39). The effect was primarily observed in participants <80 years (mean age 60 years.HR=3.21, 95% CI 1.69-6.13). No increased risk of stroke was observed among participants with loneliness at baseline. Conclusion: Our findings support consideration of loneliness as a potentially modifiable risk factor, particularly in midlife, for incident stroke.

items.title: Timing of First Poststroke Seizure and Risk of Seizure Recurrence by Stroke Subtype
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Clinical Neuroscience Center, University Hospital and University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland
items.abstract: Importance: The 7-day cutoff separating acute symptomatic from unprovoked poststroke seizures guides epilepsy diagnosis and long-term antiseizure medication but is consensus based and unvalidated against recurrence risk by stroke subtype. Objective: To determine whether seizure recurrence risk changes abruptly at day 7 and how it varies with first-seizure timing by stroke subtype. Design, Setting, and Participants: This pooled analysis of individual participant data from 36 cohorts in 22 countries (inclusion, 1994-2025) included adults with a first seizure after ischemic stroke, intracerebral hemorrhage, aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, or cerebral venous thrombosis. Exposure: Days from stroke onset (or venous thrombosis diagnosis) to first seizure. Main Outcomes and Measures: The 10-year cumulative incidence of unprovoked seizure recurrence, with death as a competing event, from stabilized inverse probability of treatment-weighted Fine-Gray spline models. Risk zones were based on the likelihood of being helped vs harmed and the 60% epilepsy threshold of the International League Against Epilepsy. Results: Of 2434 individuals (median [IQR] age, 63 [49-75] years; 1181 [48.5%] female), 684 (28.1%) had a seizure recurrence. Risk changed gradually with first-seizure timing, without a day-7 transition; overall 10-year risk differed by subtype (cerebral venous thrombosis, 44%; intracerebral hemorrhage, 43%; ischemic stroke, 40%; subarachnoid hemorrhage, 35%; P < .001). At day 7, the 10-year risk was 24% (95% CI, 17%-32%) after ischemic stroke, 30% (95% CI, 22%-38%) after intracerebral hemorrhage, 41% (95% CI, 22%-53%) after subarachnoid hemorrhage, and 58% (95% CI, 44%-71%) after cerebral venous thrombosis. The 60% threshold was crossed from day 71 after ischemic stroke, day 41 after intracerebral hemorrhage, and day 9 after cerebral venous thrombosis; after subarachnoid hemorrhage, only seizures on days 2 to 3 exceeded it. Mortality was inversely related to recurrence risk. Of 800 first seizures after day 7 following ischemic stroke or intracerebral hemorrhage, which would qualify as epilepsy under current criteria, 335 (42%) had a recurrence risk below the 60% diagnostic threshold.
