Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
items.last_author_affiliation: Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA.
items.abstract: Empirical research so far largely suggests that population policies around the world do not explain a majority of the global fertility decline1-10. Notably, even China's total fertility rate declined little after implementation of the one-child policy in 1979 and 1980, but fertility then fell sharply by more than one-third during the early 1990s. Here we show that strengthening bureaucratic incentives under China's one vote veto policy, which strictly prohibited career advancement for adherence failure, was instrumental in more effective implementation of the one-child policy, and in its delayed impact on fertility. Using provincial variation in implementation timing, we find that the one vote veto explains nearly half of China's total fertility rate decline during the 1990s, driving fertility below the replacement rate. Increases in use of intrauterine devices (the most prevalent form of modern contraception in China) that were recommended by local officials were particularly salient. Overall, our findings suggest that population policy, when more strictly enforced due to stronger bureaucratic incentives, made a greater contribution to low fertility in China than suggested by past research.

items.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular and Cellular Endocrinology, Arthur Riggs Diabetes and Metabolism Research Institute, Beckman Research Institute, City of Hope Medical Center, Duarte, CA, USA. qwang@coh.org.; Comprehensive Cancer Center, Beckman Research Institute, City of Hope Medical Center, Duarte, CA, USA. qwang@coh.org.
items.abstract: Abstract Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity 1–5 . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells) 6 . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by Nr3c1 ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 ( Rgs2 ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of Nr3c1 during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Plant Trait Design, CAS Center for Excellence in Molecular Plant Sciences, Shanghai Institute of Plant Physiology and Ecology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, China. xychen@cemps.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. xychen@cemps.ac.cn.
items.abstract: RNA-derived 2',3'-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1-3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs; 2',3'-cAMP and 2',3'-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3'→5')-guanosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling.

items.abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. lance.li@nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

items.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Immunology and Regenerative Biology, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel. efrat.shema@weizmann.ac.il.; Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics, Berlin, Germany. efrat.shema@weizmann.ac.il.
items.abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1-3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4-7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
items.last_author_affiliation: Division of Gastroenterology, Boston Children's Hospital, Boston, MA, USA. Jonathan.Kagan@childrens.harvard.edu.; Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. Jonathan.Kagan@childrens.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Disconnects between in vitro and in vivo results in experimental biology have long been recognized as potential hurdles to understanding health and disease. A prototypical example of such a disconnect is the NLRP3 inflammasome, which mediates inflammation in diverse settings of disease and protective immunity1,2. Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro requires two signals: (1) priming by pathogen-associated molecular patterns such as bacterial lipopolysaccharides and (2) activation by molecules that disrupt cellular homeostasis1,3. By contrast, the NLRP3 inflammasome in vivo is activated by lipopolysaccharide alone. The mechanisms that underlie the difference between in vitro and in vivo activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome are undefined. Here we report that extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness is a determinant of NLRP3 activities and that in vitro systems using physiological ECM stiffness enable one-signal in vivo-like NLRP3 activities to occur in human and mouse phagocytes. Physiological ECM stiffness induced expression of the transcription factor NRF2, which was found to be necessary for one-signal NLRP3 activation. Mechanistically, we identify Panx1 as an NRF2-regulated gene that promotes NLRP3 activity. Macrophages derived from the stiff matrix of the bone-osteoclasts-had reduced NRF2 levels and impaired NLRP3 activity. Moreover, alveolar macrophages from patients with pulmonary fibrosis displayed reduced NRF2 activity. Finally, NRF2 was required for antitumour immunity induced by cancer vaccines consisting of NLRP3 agonistic adjuvants. These findings indicate that NRF2 may be a transcriptional checkpoint that controls NLRP3 inflammasome activity.

items.abstract: Abstract In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status 1 . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, University College London, London, UK. g.he@ucl.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Abstract Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation 1–9 . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I + –Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I 2 and Al–I 2 batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

I.M.Viola@ed.ac.uk.; Department of Energy and Power Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. I.M.Viola@ed.ac.uk.; School of Aerospace Engineering, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. I.M.Viola@ed.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Abstract The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource 1 . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs 2,3 . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

items.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
authors: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz
items.first_author: Marcia de Almeida Monteiro Melo Ferraz
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biology, The University of British Columbia Okanagan, Kelowna, British Columbia, Canada.; Okanagan Institute for Biodiversity, Resilience, and Ecosystem Services, The University of British Columbia Okanagan, Kelowna, British Columbia, Canada.; Department of Math, Physics, and Statistics, The University of British Columbia Okanagan, Kelowna, British Columbia, Canada.
items.abstract: Abstract Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene 1 , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats 2–7 , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

items.title: Who needs sex? Kelp reproduce asexually when no mate is nearby
Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
items.last_author_affiliation: Network Science Institute, Northeastern University, Boston, MA, USA. barabasi@gmail.com.; Channing Division of Network Medicine, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. barabasi@gmail.com.; Department of Data and Network Science, Central European University, Budapest, Hungary. barabasi@gmail.com.
items.abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems-from the Internet to the brain-derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length3-6. Here we introduce scale-rich metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving orders-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity. Governed by only two parameters, scale-rich networks span orders of magnitude in structural features, overcoming previous constraints in metamaterial design. Translating these network models into physically realizable materials, we use simulations and experiments to show that scale-rich metamaterials exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems, including highly tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation with high energy absorption, enhanced energy dissipation under dynamic loading and programmable elastic-wave control. This network-based framework establishes a minimal and universal model for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical behaviour emerges directly from scale diversity, and also opens avenues of enquiry for network science itself.

items.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
items.last_author_affiliation: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology, Thuwal, Saudi Arabia.
items.abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

items.title: Tracking danger on the peaks
items.last_author_affiliation: Amrit Thapa is a graduate research assistant at the University of Alaska Fairbanks, Fairbanks, AK, USA.
items.abstract: The Earth is warming, but not all regions are warming equally. In high mountain areas, temperatures are generally increasing by 1.5 to 2 times the global average, sometimes with devastating consequences. A small or gradual change in the mountain cryosphere—perhaps progressive thawing of frozen ground or a flood from a small glacial lake—can suddenly turn into a cascade of catastrophes with enormous ramifications. Monitoring systems for the cryosphere in high mountain areas have traditionally been designed to look at individual components and changes. What are the temperature and depth of the permafrost, or how much area is covered by snow, and what is the related avalanche danger? Many of the monitoring and warning systems were designed for historical patterns of snowfall or rainfall, and a river gauge may no longer be adequate if there is greater flow in the rainy season, or increased sediment that could damage the gauge.

items.title: Direct monitoring of breaching in deltaic submarine landslides
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Earth, Energy, and Environment, University of Calgary, Calgary, AB, Canada.
items.abstract: Submarine landslides threaten seabed infrastructure and trigger the transport of globally important amounts of sediment, carbon, and pollutants to deep-sea environments. However, fully submarine landslides have never been directly monitored in nature. Past hypotheses for their failure mechanism and dynamics therefore remain unvalidated for natural settings, including that prolonged upslope-migrating failures (breaching) occur in sandy seafloor environments. In this work, we present direct underwater monitoring of fully submarine landslides at Homathko Delta in western Canada that retrogress slowly upslope, indicating breaching-type failure. Their prolonged rather than instantaneous nature has important implications for the stress that seabed structures must be designed to withstand. Prolonged landslides also initiate sustained sediment flows (turbidity currents) that efficiently transport sediment, carbon, and pollutants further offshore.

items.title: Giant elastoresistance in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.; Department of Physics, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA.
items.abstract: Strongly correlated and topological phases in moiré materials are exquisitely sensitive to lattice geometry at both atomic and superlattice length scales. Twist angle, pressure, and strain directly modify the lattice and thus act as highly effective tuning parameters. Here, we examined electrical transport in twisted bilayer graphene subjected to continuous uniaxial strain. Near the magic angle (≈1.1°), devices exhibited a pronounced elastoresistance that depended on band filling and temperature, with a gauge factor more than two orders of magnitude larger than that of conventional metals. In selected doping regimes, the elastoresistance exhibited a Curie-Weiss–like temperature divergence. We discuss possible microscopic origins, including nematic fluctuations and enhanced electronic entropy from fluctuating isospin moments. Our work establishes uniaxial strain as a versatile probe of correlated physics in a moiré material.

items.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Systems Biology, UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX, USA.; Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX, USA.; Department of Genetics, UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX, USA.; Department of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology, UT MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, TX, USA.
items.abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

items.title: The cryosphere beyond a planetary safe operating space
items.last_author_affiliation: Stockholm Resilience Centre, Stockholm University, Stockholm, Sweden.; Bolin Centre for Climate Research, Stockholm University, Stockholm, Sweden.; Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK), Member of the Leibniz Association, Potsdam, Germany.
items.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Cancer Research, Shenzhen Bay Laboratory, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China.; School of Chemical Biology and Biotechnology, Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China.; Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation (SMART), Shenzhen, Guangdong, China.
items.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
items.last_author_affiliation: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, University of California, San Diego, La Jolla, CA, USA.
items.abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

items.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Veterinary Sciences, University of Turin, Grugliasco, Italy.
items.abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

items.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, The Pennsylvania State University, University Park, PA, USA.
items.abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

items.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
items.last_author_affiliation: New Cornerstone Science Laboratory & Liangzhu Laboratory, the Second Affiliated Hospital & School of Basic Medical Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.; Department of Neurology, the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, Hangzhou, China.; Institute of Fundamental and Transdisciplinary Research, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.; Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA.; Department of Biophysics, the School of Basic Medical Sciences, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.; The State Key Laboratory of Brain-Machine Intelligence, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China.
items.abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

items.title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
items.last_author_affiliation: Earth and Planets Laboratory, Carnegie Institution for Science, Washington, DC, USA.
items.abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth's core. Here we use a new high-pressure method - microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells - to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 [Formula: see text] cm measurement of liquid iron's resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today's lowermost mantle is fully solid.
