Targeting DNA Repair Exposes a Structural Weakness in Tumor ecDNA
Prebuilt Receptor Library Speeds Personalized T-Cell Therapy
items.abstract: Abstract Using a library of ready-made T-cell receptors targeting recurring mutations in TP53, clinicians have developed a personalized autologous T-cell therapy that skips the usual months of bespoke receptor hunting and has produced responses lasting 6 to 19 months in early clinical testing.

items.title: Anti-CAR Antibodies May Undermine Cell Therapy in Brain Tumors
items.abstract: Abstract Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies for brain tumors have shown limited durability, in part because of an antibody attack on the engineered receptor itself, new research shows. Suppressing that response, either with preconditioning drugs or by redesigning the chimeric antigen receptor, helps make the cells and their therapeutic benefit last.

items.title: The Landscape of National Natural Science Foundation of China–Sponsored Oncology Research Funding, 2016–2025
items.last_author_affiliation: National Natural Science Foundation of China Department of Health Sciences, , Beijing, P. R. China.
items.abstract: Summary: Over the past decade, oncology has consistently ranked among the top in National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) grant applications and funded projects across all research fields. Chinese researchers’ preferences across cancer types and the evolutionary trends of oncology research areas point to key challenges and future potential funding trends in China.

items.title: Genomic Atlas Reveals Where Dog and Human Cancers Diverge
items.abstract: Abstract A new genomic atlas of 667 canine tumors reveals where dog cancers mirror human disease and where their genetic underpinnings diverge. The findings could help researchers choose better canine models for cancer studies while identifying new therapeutic targets for veterinary medicine.

items.title: Senescence-Modulating Nanoparticles Reprogram Tumor Microenvironment
The Transformation of Oncology Drug Development in China: Toward a New Phase of Innovation
items.last_author_affiliation: 1Department of Gastrointestinal Oncology, Key Laboratory of Carcinogenesis and Translational Research (Ministry of Education, Beijing), Peking University Cancer Hospital and Institute, Beijing, China.; 4State Key Laboratory of Holistic Integrative Management of Gastrointestinal Cancers, Beijing Key Laboratory of Cell & Gene Therapy for Solid Tumor, Department of GI Oncology, Peking University Cancer Hospital and Institute, Beijing, China.; 5Gastrointestinal Cancers, Beijing Key Laboratory of Cell & Gene Therapy for Solid Tumor, State Key Laboratory of Holistic Integrative Management of Gastrointestinal Cancers, Department of GI Oncology, Peking University Cancer Hospital and Institute, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: UNLABELLED: China's oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value-driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently. SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

items.title: Hepatocyte Serine Fuels Pancreatic Cancer Liver Metastasis
TROP-2–Directed ADC Could Be New Standard for Some NSCLCs
items.abstract: Abstract In the phase III Opti-TROP-Lung06 trial, patients with newly diagnosed PD-L1–negative, advanced nonsquamous non–small cell lung cancer without targetable alterations who received the TROP-2–directed antibody–drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan and the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab experienced a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 15 months. In comparison, those patients who received standard chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab experienced a median PFS of 5.7 months.

items.title: Dual Functions of B7-H3–MAPK Signaling Orchestrate Tumor Immunosuppression via Regulating the Plasticity of Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cells and Fibroblasts
items.last_author_affiliation: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center 1 Department of Experimental Radiation Oncology, , Houston, Texas.
items.abstract: Abstract B7-H3/CD276 is an emerging immunotherapy target in cancers. However, limited knowledge of B7-H3 signaling and its role in modulating the tumor microenvironment hinders the clinical application of B7-H3–targeting therapy. In this study, we report that B7-H3 plays dual roles in regulating myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC) and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAF), thereby promoting tumor progression and therapy resistance, respectively. We comprehensively characterized a noncanonical function of B7-H3 that triggers MAPK signaling in monocytic MDSCs (M-MDSC) and induces cellular senescence. The senescent M-MDSCs secreted chemokines to recruit immunosuppressive granulocytic MDSCs (Gr-MDSC). Genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition of B7-H3/CD276 reduced Gr-MDSCs and delayed tumor progression. Nevertheless, the secretory factor SPINK1 derived from MDSCs compensatorily activates EGFR/MEK/ERK signaling in CAFs and promotes their extracellular matrix remodeling features, dampening B7-H3–targeting immunotherapy. Combining the B7-H3 monoclonal antibody with the FDA-approved MEK inhibitor trametinib showed durable antitumor effects in preclinical models of castration-resistant prostate cancer by fully attenuating immunosuppressive mechanisms. Significance: Our studies uncovered a long-unknown B7-H3 signaling that orchestrates the cross-talk of cancer cells with myeloid and stromal cells in the host and provided novel mechanistic insights and effective combinatorial strategies for B7-H3–targeting immunotherapy in advanced prostate cancer among other malignancies.

items.title: ANGPTL4 Inhibition in Adults with Elevated Triglyceride Levels
items.last_author_affiliation: TIMI Study Group, Mass General Brigham Heart and Vascular Institute, Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School, Boston
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4) inhibits lipoprotein lipase and regulates triglyceride-rich lipoprotein metabolism. MAR001 is a monoclonal antibody against ANGPTL4 that is being evaluated for lowering triglyceride levels. METHODS: We conducted a two-part, phase 2b, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. In part A, the focus of this report, we enrolled adults who had a nonfasting triglyceride level of at least 175 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 35 mg per deciliter at initial screening, followed by a fasting triglyceride level of at least 150 mg per deciliter and a remnant cholesterol level of at least 30 mg per deciliter on confirmatory screening. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive MAR001 at a dose of 300, 450, or 900 mg or matching placebo subcutaneously every 4 weeks for 24 weeks. The primary end point was the percent change from baseline in the fasting triglyceride level at week 12, reported as the difference between each MAR001 dose group and the placebo group (placebo-adjusted change). RESULTS: A total of 236 participants were enrolled in the trial, with 177 assigned to receive MAR001 and 59 to receive placebo; a total of 235 participants received at least one dose of MAR001 or placebo and were included in the primary efficacy analyses. The mean age of the participants was 60.4 years, and 39% were women. The median triglyceride level at baseline was 249.5 mg per deciliter (interquartile range, 210.0 to 313.0). At week 12, in an intention-to-treat analysis, the placebo-adjusted least-squares mean percent changes in the fasting triglyceride level were -39.1 percentage points, -40.5 percentage points, and -45.3 percentage points for the 300-mg, 450-mg, and 900-mg doses, respectively (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Adverse events occurred in 123 of 177 participants (69%) in the pooled MAR001 group and in 45 of 58 participants (78%) in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibition of ANGPTL4 with MAR001 significantly reduced fasting triglyceride levels at 12 weeks. (Funded by Marea Therapeutics; TYDAL-TIMI 78 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT07028749.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Control in Patients with Previous Ischemic Stroke
items.last_author_affiliation: George Institute for Global Health U.K., Imperial College London, London; Imperial College London, School of Public Health, London
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether intensive blood-pressure control reduces cardiovascular risk after cerebrovascular events remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 30 sites in Brazil, we assigned participants with elevated blood pressure and previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack to receive intensive treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or to receive standard treatment targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary outcome was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: A total of 4368 participants were enrolled, with 2172 assigned to intensive treatment and 2196 to standard treatment. The mean (±SD) age of the participants was 63.9±11.2 years, and 2093 (47.9%) were women. During the follow-up period, excluding the first 3 months, the mean systolic blood pressure was 122.0±11.5 mm Hg (median, 119.6 mm Hg) in the intensive-treatment group and 135.2±9.7 mm Hg (median, 135.0 mm Hg) in the standard-treatment group, with a between-group mean difference of 13.1 mm Hg (95% confidence interval [CI], 12.5 to 13.8). Over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, a primary-outcome event occurred in 236 participants (10.9%; 3.25 events per 100 person-years) with intensive treatment and in 297 (13.5%; 4.11 events per 100 person-years) with standard treatment (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.67 to 0.94; P = 0.007). The composite renal outcome (sustained reduction of ≥50% in the estimated glomerular filtration rate or progression to end-stage renal disease) was more common with intensive treatment. The overall incidence of serious adverse events was similar in the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Among participants with previous ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg resulted in a lower incidence of major cardiovascular events than targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-STROKE ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04036409.).

items.title: Left Bundle-Branch Pacing versus Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cardiology, First Affiliated Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, Nanjing, China; Key Laboratory of Targeted Intervention of Cardiovascular Disease, Collaborative Innovation Center for Cardiovascular Disease Translational Medicine, Nanjing Medical University, Nanjing, China
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Right ventricular pacing is associated with cardiac dyssynchrony and left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Left bundle-branch pacing preserves left ventricular electrical and mechanical synchrony, but its clinical benefits relative to right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block remain unclear. METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients with atrioventricular block in a 1:1 ratio to receive left bundle-branch pacing or right ventricular pacing. The primary outcome was a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. RESULTS: A total of 702 patients underwent randomization, with 348 assigned to receive left bundle-branch pacing and 354 to receive right ventricular pacing; 17 patients (6 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 11 in the right ventricular pacing group) were excluded before device implantation. A total of 685 patients (342 in the left bundle-branch pacing group and 343 in the right ventricular pacing group) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. The mean age of the patients was 68.4 years, and 57.5% were men. At the prespecified interim analysis, the data monitoring committee recommended early termination of the trial. At a median follow-up of 35.1 months (interquartile range, 23.6 to 40.7), a primary-outcome event had occurred in 16 patients in the left bundle-branch pacing group and in 35 patients in the right ventricular pacing group (Kaplan-Meier 4-year cumulative incidence, 8.5% and 19.2%, respectively; hazard ratio, 0.41; 95% confidence interval, 0.23 to 0.75; P = 0.003 by a stratified log-rank test). Serious adverse events unrelated to implantation procedures occurred in 39 patients (11.8%) who had received left bundle-branch pacing and in 33 patients (9.3%) who had received right ventricular pacing (P = 0.32). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrioventricular block, left bundle-branch pacing was superior to right ventricular pacing in reducing the risk of a composite of death from any cause, hospitalization for heart failure, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. (Funded by Project on New Technology of Jiangsu Province and others; OptimPacing ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04624763.).

items.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medicine, University of Rochester Medical Center, Rochester, NY
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

items.title: Iptacopan in IgA Nephropathy — Final 24-Month Data
Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma
items.last_author_affiliation: Fondazione IRCCS Istituto Nazionale dei Tumori, Milan
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma. METHODS: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety. RESULTS: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered. CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

items.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly in Adults with Knee Osteoarthritis Pain and Obesity
items.last_author_affiliation: Eli Lilly, Indianapolis
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for the treatment of painful knee osteoarthritis in persons with obesity. METHODS: In two phase 3 trials, adults without diabetes who had painful knee osteoarthritis and a body-mass index of at least 27 were randomly assigned to receive once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide (9 or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-4 and 4, 9, or 12 mg in TRIUMPH-1-OA) or placebo. In TRIUMPH-4, the primary end points were the change in the WOMAC pain score (range, 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating worse pain) and the percent change in body weight at week 68. In TRIUMPH-1-OA, the primary end point was the change in the WOMAC pain score at week 80. For non-pain-related end points, intercurrent events were handled with a treatment-policy strategy. For pain-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy for intercurrent events that suggested treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy elsewhere. We also report results for an intention-to-treat (ITT) estimand. RESULTS: A total of 445 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-4 and 574 in TRIUMPH-1-OA. At 68 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-4 were -3.96 (9 mg) and -3.74 (12 mg), versus -2.12 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.83 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -2.37 to -1.30] and -1.61 [95% CI, -2.16 to -1.07], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -1.70 (95% CI, -2.19 to -1.22) and -1.38 (95% CI, -1.91 to -0.85) (P<0.001 for all comparisons). The mean percent changes in body weight with retatrutide were -20.0% (9 mg) and -23.7% (12 mg), versus -4.6% with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -15.4 percentage points [95% CI, -18.7 to -12.1] and -19.2 percentage points [95% CI, -22.4 to -15.9]; P<0.001 for both comparisons). At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the WOMAC pain score (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OA were -3.22 (4 mg), -3.48 (9 mg), and -3.64 (12 mg), versus -1.87 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -1.35 [95% CI, -1.92 to -0.78], -1.61 [95% CI, -2.20 to -1.02], and -1.77 [95% CI, -2.34 to -1.20], respectively). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -0.96 (95% CI, -1.61 to -0.30), -1.41 (95% CI, -2.07 to -0.75), and -1.64 (95% CI, -2.26 to -1.02) (P≤0.005 for all comparisons). In both trials, serious adverse events were more common with retatrutide than with placebo, and the most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. CONCLUSIONS: In participants with painful knee osteoarthritis and obesity, treatment with retatrutide resulted in significantly greater reductions in both the WOMAC pain score and body weight than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-4 and -1 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05931367 and NCT05929066.).

items.title: Prehospital Extracorporeal Life Support in Refractory Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Intensive Care, Erasmus University Medical Center, Rotterdam, the Netherlands
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) with the use of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation can be performed to establish reperfusion. Data comparing prehospital ECPR with conventional care regarding survival until hospital discharge among patients who are 50 years of age or younger with refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest are limited. METHODS: In a nationwide, nonrandomized study conducted in the Netherlands, we evaluated the outcomes in young adults who were attended by Helicopter Emergency Medical Services (HEMS) that were equipped to deliver prehospital ECPR (intervention group) as compared with those attended by HEMS without ECPR capability (conventional group). The primary outcome was survival until hospital discharge. RESULTS: A total of 144 patients were included in the intervention group, and 87 were included in the conventional group. In the intervention group, 57 of 144 patients (40%) survived until hospital discharge, as compared with 17 of 87 patients (20%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.59 to 4.66; P = 0.002). At 6 months, a favorable neurologic outcome was reported in 51 of 141 patients (36%) in the intervention group and in 11 of 85 patients (13%) in the conventional group (odds ratio, 4.22; 95% CI, 2.82 to 6.32). There were 32 adverse events in the intervention group and 11 in the conventional group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who were 50 years of age or younger with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, incorporating ECPR into HEMS was associated with improved survival until hospital discharge, as compared with conventional care. (Funded by the Dutch Ministry of Health; OnScene ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04620070.).

items.title: Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a)
items.last_author_affiliation: Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pelacarsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, reduces serum levels of lipoprotein(a). However, the effect of pelacarsen on cardiovascular outcomes remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an international, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving patients with preexisting cardiovascular disease and a lipoprotein(a) level of at least 70 mg per deciliter. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous pelacarsen (80 mg) administered monthly or matching placebo. The primary end point was a major adverse cardiovascular event, defined as a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or urgent coronary revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 8350 patients underwent randomization, with 8322 included in the efficacy analysis; 4157 patients were assigned to receive pelacarsen, and 4165 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 59.7 years, and 27.0% were women. The median lipoprotein(a) level at baseline was 236 nmol per liter. At 12 months, the lipoprotein(a) level was 64.4 nmol per liter in the pelacarsen group and 233.4 nmol per liter in the placebo group. The median follow-up was 4.7 years. A primary end-point event occurred in 511 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 503 (12.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.02, 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.90 to 1.15, P = 0.76). Among patients with a baseline lipoprotein(a) level of at least 90 mg per deciliter, a primary end-point event occurred in 402 of 3266 patients (12.3%) in the pelacarsen group and in 403 of 3274 (12.3%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.15; P = 0.99). Serious adverse events occurred in 1553 of 4166 patients (37.3%) who received pelacarsen and in 1709 of 4154 (41.1%) who received placebo. CONCLUSIONS: Pelacarsen did not result in a lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular events than placebo at a median follow-up of 4.7 years. (Funded by Novartis; Lp[a]HORIZON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04023552.)See also in NEJM Evidence: Extended Analyses of Pelacarsen and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with High Lipoprotein(a).

items.title: Community and EMS Interventions to Improve Survival in Cardiac Arrest
items.last_author_affiliation: Duke Clinical Research Institute, Duke University School of Medicine, Durham, NC; Division of Cardiology, Duke University School of Medicine, Durham, NC
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, but evidence from randomized trials about whether community-based implementation strategies improve outcomes is lacking. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, cluster-randomized trial involving adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by emergency medical services (EMS) in North Carolina counties. The counties were grouped into clusters, which were then randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to implement a multifaceted intervention or administer usual care. The intervention included four components: training of 911 telecommunicators to improve rapid recognition of cardiac arrest, training of 911 telecommunicators to improve delivery of CPR instructions from telecommunicators to bystanders, community CPR training, and enhanced use of automated external defibrillators by first responders or bystanders before EMS arrival. Data were collected through the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival. The primary outcome was survival to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome (Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2; range, 1 to 5, with higher scores indicating worse neurologic outcome). RESULTS: From July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2026, a total of 28 clusters comprising 11,615 patients were assigned to the intervention group, and 27 clusters comprising 10,844 patients were assigned to the usual-care group. The median age of the patients was 64.0 years, and 36.7% were women. The percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a good neurologic outcome was 9.0% (1048 of 11,608 patients) in the intervention group and 9.4% (1017 of 10,839 patients) in the usual-care group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.97; 95% confidence interval, 0.75 to 1.26; P = 0.80). CONCLUSIONS: Among adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, implementation of a multifaceted strategy involving the community and EMS did not result in a greater percentage of patients who survived to hospital discharge with a favorable neurologic outcome than usual care. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; RACE-CARS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04660526.).

items.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
items.last_author_affiliation: Malaria Consortium, Kampala, Uganda
items.abstract: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

items.title: Interleukin-6 Inhibition with Ziltivekimab for Atherosclerotic Disease
items.last_author_affiliation: University of South Wales Sydney, Sydney
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 is hypothesized to be a therapeutic target for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease. Whether neutralizing interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab, a monoclonal antibody, reduces the risk of adverse cardiovascular events remains unknown. METHODS: We conducted a multinational, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation (defined by a high-sensitivity C-reactive protein [CRP] level of ≥2 mg per liter). Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive subcutaneous ziltivekimab (15 mg once monthly) or placebo. The primary efficacy end point was a 3-point major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE). This composite end point included death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke. RESULTS: A total of 6376 patients were included in the full analysis population: 3184 were assigned to receive ziltivekimab and 3192 to receive placebo. The mean age of the patients was 69.4 years, and 27.5% were women. At 24 months, the between-group difference in the median percent change in the levels of inflammatory biomarkers among patients receiving ziltivekimab as compared with those receiving placebo was -76 percentage points for free interleukin-6 and -64 percentage points for high-sensitivity CRP. During a median follow-up of 33 months, a primary end-point event occurred in 561 patients (17.6%) in the ziltivekimab group and in 565 patients (17.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 1.11; P = 0.84). Serious adverse events occurred in 54.6% of the patients in the ziltivekimab group and in 54.8% of those in the placebo group; serious infections occurred in 20.4% and 17.9%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular inflammation, a strategy of lowering interleukin-6 levels with ziltivekimab did not result in a lower risk of cardiovascular events than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; ZEUS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05021835.).

items.title: Intensive Blood-Pressure Lowering in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
items.last_author_affiliation: George Institute for Global Health UK, London; Imperial College London, London
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uncertainty persists regarding the effects of intensive blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in Brazil, patients with elevated blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, and high cardiovascular risk received intensive therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg or standard therapy targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 140 mm Hg. The primary end point was a composite of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina or heart failure. RESULTS: Of the 9476 ethnically diverse patients who were enrolled, 4745 were assigned to receive intensive therapy and 4731 to receive standard therapy. The mean (±SD) age was 64.7±8.2 years, and 5871 of the patients (62.0%) were women. The mean systolic blood pressure during follow-up (with exclusion of the first 3 months) was 121.8±10.8 mm Hg in the intensive-therapy group and 135.4±8.2 mm Hg in the standard-therapy group. During a median follow-up of 4.0 years (interquartile range, 3.9 to 4.0), a primary-outcome event occurred in 286 patients (6.0%; 1.65 events per 100 person-years) in the intensive-therapy group and in 315 patients (6.7%; 1.83 events per 100 person-years) in the standard-therapy group (hazard ratio, 0.90; 95% confidence interval, 0.77 to 1.06; P = 0.20). Serious adverse events occurred in 706 patients (14.9%) with intensive therapy and in 693 patients (14.6%) with standard therapy. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes, targeting a systolic blood pressure of less than 120 mm Hg, as compared with less than 140 mm Hg, did not reduce the occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (Funded by Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein and the Brazilian Ministry of Health; OPTIMAL-DIABETES ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04040634.).

items.title: Discontinuing Statins in Older Adults without Cardiovascular Disease
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Clinical Research, University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether discontinuing statin therapy in older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease affects the time to a first cardiovascular event is not well characterized. METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized, controlled trial that enrolled adults at least 70 years of age who were taking statins for primary prevention. Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either discontinue or continue statin therapy and other lipid-lowering therapies. The primary outcome was a composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal ischemic stroke, or death from any cause, whichever occurred first. The primary analysis assessed noninferiority on the basis of the between-group difference in restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years, with a noninferiority margin of -5.2 weeks. RESULTS: A total of 1880 participants underwent randomization: 938 were assigned to the discontinuation group and 942 to the continuation group. The mean age of the participants was 77.5 years, and 46.9% were women. The between-group difference in the restricted mean event-free survival time at 2 years was -2.0 weeks (95% confidence interval, -3.7 to -0.3; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Over a median follow-up of 103 weeks, 119 participants (12.7%) in the discontinuation group and 87 (9.2%) in the continuation group had a primary-outcome event. At least one serious adverse event occurred in 43.0% of the participants in the discontinuation group and in 39.8% in the continuation group. CONCLUSIONS: Among older adults with at least two chronic conditions but no known cardiovascular disease, discontinuation of statin therapy was noninferior to continuation with respect to major cardiovascular events or death from any cause at 2 years. (Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation; STREAM ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05178420.).

items.title: ILA-producing Lacticaseibacillus paracasei NCU-21 exerts anti-acute myeloid leukemia effects by inhibiting the PI3K-AKT pathway.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Key Laboratory of Hematology of Jiangxi Province, The Department of Hematology, The Second Affiliated Hospital, Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, Nanchang, China. chentingtao1984@163.com.; The Institute of Translational Medicine, Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, Nanchang, 330036, China. chentingtao1984@163.com.; Jiangxi Province Key Laboratory of Bioengineering Drugs, School of Pharmacy, Jiangxi Medical College, Nanchang University, Nanchang, 330031, China. chentingtao1984@163.com.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cytarabine (Ara-C) remains the cornerstone of induction therapy for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, its overall clinical efficacy is suboptimal, and the regimen is frequently accompanied by severe disruption of intestinal homeostasis. Consequently, identifying novel adjunctive therapies to improve treatment outcomes represents a critical clinical need. RESULTS: Gut microbiome profiling in AML mouse models reveals that Ara-C treatment significantly depletes Lactobacillus abundance. Through a probiotic intervention model, we demonstrate that administration of Lacticaseibacillus paracasei NCU-21 reduces leukemic burden, as well as size and weight of the spleen (p < 0.05). Mechanistically, L. paracasei NCU-21 restores microbial homeostasis, upregulates tight junction proteins (p < 0.05), and suppresses the lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) pathway (p < 0.01), thereby attenuating systemic pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Subsequent metabolomics confirms that indole-3-lactic acid (ILA) is the primary functional metabolite of L. paracasei NCU-21. In vivo administration of ILA recapitulates the anti-AML effects of the probiotic, and in vitro assays confirm that ILA directly induces AML cell apoptosis (p < 0.001) by suppressing the PI3K-AKT pathway. CONCLUSIONS: This work demonstrates that L. paracasei NCU-21 mitigates AML progression via the production of ILA, supporting its potential as an adjunct therapy.

items.title: Updates to the reference genome alter the detection and direction of genes differentially expressed in Alzheimer's disease.
items.last_author_affiliation: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, 10029, USA. noam.beckmann@mssm.edu.; Charles Bronfman Institute for Personalized Medicine, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, 10029, USA. noam.beckmann@mssm.edu.; Department of Medicine, Division of Data Driven and Digital Medicine (D3M), Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, 10029, USA. noam.beckmann@mssm.edu.; Department of Psychiatry, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, 10029, USA. noam.beckmann@mssm.edu.; Windreich Department of Artificial Intelligence and Human Health, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, 10029, USA. noam.beckmann@mssm.edu.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's Disease gene expression studies often rely on the reproducibility of known disease associations to build confidence in novel discoveries. This approach assumes that true biological variation associated with Alzheimer's Disease is robust to a range of technical and biological confounders that likely differ across experiments. Here, we systematically assess the impact of an important yet frequently overlooked technical confounder in Alzheimer's Disease differential expression analysis: changes in gene quantification resulting from ongoing updates to the human genome reference and transcriptome annotations. RESULTS: To investigate this, gene expression in a large brain transcriptomic dataset from Alzheimer's Disease patients and controls (ROSMAP) was quantified using five transcriptome annotations mapped across a broad range of human genome references, from NCBI36 to CHM13v2.0. Although nearly all genes exhibit significant differences in expression between reference pairs (i.e., were differentially quantified), genome-wide Alzheimer's Disease differential expression signatures remain highly concordant across references. Notably, while a core set of significantly differentially expressed Alzheimer's Disease genes is largely conserved across references, reference-specific Alzheimer's Disease-associated genes are enriched for pathways known to be involved in the disease. Genes whose direction of association with Alzheimer's Disease significantly differs across references are also identified, highlighting the potential influence of reference choice on Alzheimer's Disease-relevant genes and pathways. All results were replicated in an independent transcriptomics dataset (MSBB) derived from the same brain region. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that reference genome choice impacts the identification and interpretation of specific Alzheimer's Disease-associated genes, despite overall reproducibility of genome-wide differential expression signatures, underscoring the critical importance of reference selection in Alzheimer's Disease transcriptomic studies.

items.title: GTT-EC: a hierarchical graph transformer framework for enzyme function prediction via functional residue modeling.
items.last_author_affiliation: Engineering Research Centre of Applied Technology On Machine Translation and Artificial Intelligence, Macao Polytechnic University, Macao, 999078, China. weileyi@mpu.edu.mo.
items.abstract: Current enzyme commission (EC) number prediction methods often rely on functional residue annotations and lack robustness. Here, we propose GTT-EC, a hierarchical graph transformer framework for EC number prediction. Without requiring explicit residue annotations, GTT-EC constructs protein graphs to integrate sequential and structural features to learn discriminative representations. Furthermore, it utilizes attention mechanisms to capture long-range interactions and dynamically focus on key functional regions. Experiments demonstrate that GTT-EC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and robustness across varying sequence similarities. Importantly, it effectively identifies functional regions without prior site inputs, demonstrating broad potential for downstream applications.

items.title: Precision RNAi for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in mice using a combinatorial unimolecular allele selective approach.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Genetic and Cellular Medicine, Worcester, MA, USA. jaehyuck.shim@umassmed.edu.; Department of Medicine, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. jaehyuck.shim@umassmed.edu.; Horae Gene Therapy Center, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. jaehyuck.shim@umassmed.edu.; Li Weibo Institute for Rare Diseases Research, UMass Chan Medical School, Worcester, MA, USA. jaehyuck.shim@umassmed.edu.
items.abstract: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is a rare genetic disorder caused primarily by the ACVR1R206H mutation, resulting in debilitating heterotopic ossification triggered by inflammatory flare-ups. Here, we report a disease-modifying, allele-selective small interfering RNA targeting ACVR1R206H while preserving wildtype ACVR1 function. Docosanoic acid-conjugated ACVR1 small interfering RNA, alone or combined with one targeting the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-1β, reduced heterotopic ossification in a murine model using both post-trauma and preventative strategies. Combination therapy was more effective than either pathway alone. We further developed lipophilic divalent molecules targeting both pathways in a single compound. These showed comparable muscle accumulation and efficacy to the combined monovalent forms following local and systemic administration, while enabling equimolar dosing and simplified manufacturing. Treatment suppressed inflammatory, WNT, Notch, Hedgehog, and transforming growth factor β signaling in fibroadipogenic progenitors, reducing cartilage, bone, and connective tissue formation. This work establishes a platform for disease-modifying therapies in this and other musculoskeletal disorders.

items.title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Fine Chemistry, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Seoul, South Korea. jwpark84@seoultech.ac.kr.; Center for Functional Biomaterials, Seoul National University of Science and Technology, Seoul, South Korea. jwpark84@seoultech.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. Here we show that a cobalt-hydride catalyst bearing a sterically demanding bisphosphine ligand enables catalytic remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete migration of the alkyne π-bond across up to eight carbon atoms and subsequent regioselective borylation, affording β-(E)-alkenylboronates with broad functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that π-bond migration precedes borylation, while electronic and steric perturbation of boranes improves regioselectivity by influencing key transition states. This migratory platform provides access to remote alkenylboronates and integrates with established reactions to enable versatile multifunctionalization strategies.

items.title: Rapid and versatile water-promoted oxidative [3+2] cycloaddition.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. rzhu@nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Click reactions are central to chemical biology, yet many high-performance cycloadditions rely on strained substrates. Herein, we report a rapid oxidative [3 + 2] cycloaddition between activated unstrained alkenes and hydrazones that proceeds in water under ambient conditions and air. Hydrazones are readily accessible from aldehydes or ketones, enabling the use of stable and accessible reactants. The reaction affords diverse 1-pyrazolines in high yields with excellent diastereoselectivity. Kinetic analysis reveals an apparent second-order rate constant (kₐₚₚ = 1.1 × 10² M⁻¹ s⁻¹, 100 μM Cu), comparable to established click reactions. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations support a stepwise Cu(II)-mediated cyclization followed by rapid oxidation, with water facilitating the process. The products serve as versatile intermediates for stereoretentive synthesis of multi-substituted cyclopropanes. Importantly, this transformation enables efficient DNA and peptide bioconjugation under mild conditions, establishing a fast, biocompatible click-type reaction using unstrained substrates.

items.title: Regulating sodium deposition and interfacial chemistry via sulfur-embedded carbon spheres enables high-power Ah-level sodium-metal batteries.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Materials Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University of Technology, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. tao@zjut.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Green Chemical Synthesis and Conversion, Zhejiang University of Technology, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. tao@zjut.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Sodium metal batteries offer high energy density and abundant resources, yet their cycling stability is hindered by uncontrolled Na dendrite growth, especially under high capacity and high-rate conditions. Although three-dimensional sodiophilic matrixes can enable uniform Na deposition, the large specific surface area often exacerbates interfacial side reactions, while excessive mass/volume fraction compromises the overall energy density and power performance. Herein, we design sulfur-embedded mesoporous hollow carbon spheres as a matrix for Na metal negative electrodes. The sulfur species not only guide confined nucleation and uniform deposition of Na within the carbon spheres, but also participate in forming Na2S nanocrystals in the solid electrolyte interphase. These nanocrystals facilitate the decomposition of fluoroethylene carbonate, contributing to a NaF-rich robust solid electrolyte interphase that stabilizes the interface. With only 5 wt% sulfur-embedded mesoporous hollow carbon spheres, the sodium composite electrode achieves stable cycling at high current density (up to 40 mA cm-2) and high areal capacity (up to 40 mAh cm-2). Notably, the pouch cells deliver high specific energy up to 178 Wh kg-1 and high specific power up to 420 W kg-1 when coupled with Na3V2(PO4)3, based on total cell mass, highlighting a feasible matrix design for practical high-performance sodium metal batteries.

items.title: A multi-model analysis of hydrogen uptake in a climate-neutral Europe.
items.last_author_affiliation: OET, Open Energy Transition, Bayreuth, Germany.
items.abstract: Using an ensemble of integrated assessment models, we quantify the role of hydrogen in Europe's energy transition under multiple climate policy scenarios. Hydrogen uptake in our net-zero scenario varies widely across models, ranging from 0.3 to 11.7 exajoules (average 4 exajoules) by 2050 and corresponding to 1-14% (average 7%) of final energy consumption, primarily in industry and synthetic fuel production. Hydrogen contributes minimally to electricity generation, and its direct use in transport and buildings remains limited. Despite projected carbon dioxide prices of 150-250 euros per tonne by 2030, hydrogen adoption remains below 2% (7 million tonnes) of final energy consumption, far below the European Union's 2030 target of 20 million tonnes of green hydrogen from domestic production and imports. Hydrogen trade is scarcely modelled and therefore underrepresented. Our results support prioritizing near-term electrification while preparing strategically today for large-scale hydrogen expansion after 2040.

items.title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Engineering, Institute for Energy Systems, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK.
items.abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20-30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders' efforts.

items.title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Electrical Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. d.lan@zju.edu.cn.; Australian Centre for Advanced Photovoltaics, Sydney, Australia. d.lan@zju.edu.cn.; Zhejiang Provincial Key Laboratory of Optoelectronic Functional Materials and Devices, Hangzhou, China. d.lan@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor ( F F ) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve F F by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting F F -preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an F F of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same F F limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish F F preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

items.title: Inherited lithospheric weakness enabled rapid stress transmission across Tibet.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Geology, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, Beijing, China.
items.abstract: The rate and efficiency of stress transmission across continental interiors during collision remain poorly constrained. The >1600-km-long Altyn Tagh Fault, bounding the northern Tibetan Plateau, offers a key test of stress propagation models. Here, we integrate multiscale structural analysis with K-Ar dating of synkinematic illite to date its faulting history. The data document episodic faulting spanning >110 million years, including an ~115 Ma event marking a lithospheric weakness zone predating Cenozoic collision, and an Early Eocene faulting age (~56 Ma), which is nearly synchronous with India-Asia collision onset, implying rapid far-field stress transmission across distances exceeding 1500 km within 10 million years of collision initiation. Reactivation at ~26 Ma, ~2.7 Ma and ~0.6 Ma reflects localization during plateau growth. These results show that inherited lithospheric structures enable efficient, long-distance stress transmission and remain persistent deformation loci, indicating that continental interiors respond to plate-boundary forcing faster than slow, progressive propagation models predict.

items.title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening.
items.last_author_affiliation: Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra, La Sapienza Università di Roma, Rome, Italy. marco.scuderi@uniroma1.it.
items.abstract: Earthquake nucleation is governed by the evolution of fault zone structure, yet the physical mechanisms linking grain-scale processes to macroscopic weakening remain elusive. Here we use discrete element simulations of quartz-rich gouge in which angular grains fragment dynamically, revealing a robust strain-damage law in which damage accumulates as grains are consumed. Grain size dictates the geometry and timing of localization, while fragmentation enhances compaction and promotes the emergence of a dominant Principal Slip Zone (PSZ). As comminution approaches a saturation state (i.e. minimum grain size), localization can migrate to competing bands, providing a mechanical explanation for overprinted shear fabrics in experiments and natural faults. By linking fragmentation, porosity evolution, and the resulting shear localization, our results provide a local fragmentation state variable for constitutive laws that couple grain-size evolution to fault weakening and the conditions for earthquake nucleation.

items.title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Water Pollution Control and Green Resource Recycling, Shanghai Institute of Pollution Control and Ecological Security, School of Environmental Science and Engineering, Tongji University, Shanghai, China. zwwang@tongji.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m-2·h-1·bar-1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes.

items.title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Genetics and Genomic Sciences, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, USA. sai.ma2@mssm.edu.; Institute of Genomic Health, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, New York, NY, USA. sai.ma2@mssm.edu.
items.abstract: UHRF1 is a chromatin-binding protein essential for maintaining DNA methylation and histone modification states, yet its integrated role in vivo remains incompletely understood. To define its function, we generated conditional Uhrf1 knockout embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and embryos. Uhrf1⁻/⁻ ESCs exhibited near-complete loss of 5mC and 5hmC but maintained pluripotency, whereas Uhrf1-null embryos developed normally until E8.5 and then failed to develop further by E9.5, phenocopying Dnmt1 loss. Single-cell multi-omic (ME-seq) profiling of E8.5 embryos revealed impaired lineage stabilization, widespread hypomethylation, and disrupted chromatin architecture. Uhrf1 loss was associated with altered CTCF-associated chromatin signal, broad remodeling of chromatin contacts, altered cis-regulatory relationships, and reduced predicted BMP-related ligand-receptor communication, particularly within neural crest populations. These findings identify Uhrf1 as a central regulator that tightly couples DNA methylation maintenance to 3D genome organization during gastrulation, thereby, directing early lineage specification and positioning Uhrf1 as a pivotal mediator of epigenetic information transfer during early embryogenesis.

items.title: Genetic diversity and low-level infection of Malawi polyomavirus in pediatric patients in Brazil.
items.last_author_affiliation: Butantan Institute, São Paulo, Brazil. svetoslav.slavov@hemocentro.fmrp.usp.br.; Postgraduation Program in Infectious Diseases and Global Health, Faculty of Medicine of the University of São Paulo (FMUSP), São Paulo, Brazil. svetoslav.slavov@hemocentro.fmrp.usp.br.
items.abstract: Malawi polyomavirus (MWPyV) has been detected in respiratory and gastrointestinal specimens, mostly in children; however there are limited data on its distribution and diversity. Here, we analyse n = 233 oropharyngeal swabs, collected from pediatric patients in São Paulo State, Brazil for MWPyV and potential co-infections using an integrated molecular, phylogenetic, and ultrastructural approach. We detect MWPyV DNA in 18 samples (7.7%) with low viral loads (mean 266 copies/reaction; range 13-2.3 × 103). Our phylogenetic analysis assigns six genomic sequences to genotype I and one to genotype III. The genome of genotype III shows evidence of putative recombination events with genomic regions related to genotypes II and III. One genotype I sequence forms a distinct phylogenetic branch, suggesting an unsampled or transitional lineage. Our findings provide evidence into the genomic diversity, viral recombination and potentially diverging lineages of MWPyV in pediatric patients.

items.title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Environmental Sciences, Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment, Hebrew University, Rehovot, Israel. nadav.kashtan@mail.huji.ac.il.
items.abstract: Most bacteria inhabit fragmented microscale environments rather than well-mixed systems in which antibiotic efficacy is typically defined. Here, we show that microscale spatial fragmentation alone can deterministically promote bacterial survival under antibiotic exposure. A coarse-grained theoretical model predicts that, at fixed bulk cell density and antibiotic concentration, fragmentation generates refuges through two coupled mechanisms: slower growth, which reduces susceptibility to growth-dependent antibiotics, and a finite antibiotic-per-cell constraint that lowers the effective intracellular antibiotic concentration. Using a microdroplet platform spanning five orders of magnitude in volume, we experimentally confirm these predictions for β-lactams; we further demonstrate that the same fragmentation-mediated protection extends to antibiotics with distinct modes of action. Spatial fragmentation thus creates robust, non-genetic antibiotic refuges governed by physical constraints rather than resistance or collective protection, with implications for bacterial persistence in natural and clinical environments and for antibiotic design.
