items.title: Mechanistic insights into NET1-UNC5B complex formation and Its targeted disruption by NP137 fab and NET1 peptide competitors.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. Jorg.stetefeld@umanitoba.ca.
items.abstract: Netrin‑1, a secreted protein initially characterized for its role in axon guidance, has emerged as a critical mediator of cancer progression. Preclinical studies with the anti‑netrin‑1 antibody NP137, which blocks the netrin‑1-UNC5B interaction, have demonstrated reactivation of tumor suppressor functions and sensitization of cancer cells to chemotherapy. Here, we identified the molecular binding interface of the netrin‑1-UNC5B complex using integrative structural and quantitative biophysical analyses. We then determined how NP137 binding inhibits this interaction by sterically blocking key contact points within the interface. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we rationally designed peptides that disrupt the netrin‑1-UNC5B complex through interfering with heparin-mediated stabilization of the complex by binding to shared heparin-binding sites. This comprehensive structural and mechanistic analysis advances understanding of netrin‑1 signaling and establishes strategies for therapeutic intervention in netrin‑1-driven malignancies.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemical Engineering, National Tsing Hua University, Hsinchu, Taiwan. ychu@mx.nthu.edu.tw.
items.abstract: CRISPR-based RNA cleavage holds promise for gene knockdown but its applications in metabolic engineering remain largely unexplored. Here we reconstitute three mammalian CRISPR-based RNA cleavage systems to arrest the intermediate metabolic reactions in the yeast Candida viswanathii to produce hydroxydecanoic acid (HDA), an important nylon precursor. We identify hfCas13d as the optimal effector and next develop a circular guide RNA (CgRNA) precursor architecture to enhance and extend the knockdown of genes involved in HDA production. This hfCas13d/CgRNA precursor platform also represses genes in other yeasts and E. coli, demonstrating broad microbial applicability. Single and dual CgRNA precursor arrays enable multiplexed pathway repression, with dual arrays reducing byproduct formation and increasing HDA titer to 17.8 g/L in shake flasks. Bioreactor fermentation further boosts HDA production to 37.2 g/L. Together, this work establishes hfCas13d/CgRNA as a programmable RNA regulatory platform for engineering microbial cell factories.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biomedical Engineering, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.; Institute for NanoBioTechnology, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.; Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.; Department of Oncology, Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.; Translational Therapeutics and Regenerative Engineering Center, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.; Johns Hopkins Center for Microphysiological Systems, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, MD, USA. jphillip@jhu.edu.
items.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process often characterized by increased vulnerability to disease, infection, and death. This increased vulnerability is mechanistically linked to a progressive and functional decline of the immune system. In humans, aged T cells lose their ability to effectively surveil complex microenvironments, thereby decreasing their capacity to clear infections, eradicate diseases, and maintain physiological homeostasis. However, specific mechanisms by which aged T cells lose this capacity to surveil remain unclear. Here, we profile three core characteristics of T cell surveillance at single-cell resolution, specifically migration, deformability, and sensing. While aged human T cells retain their capacity to migrate ex vivo, they exhibit impaired cellular deformability and deficiencies in sensing local biological signals. To modulate this surveillance defect, we perform mechanical reprogramming using elevated fluid viscosity. Results indicate that acute priming of aged T cells with elevated fluid viscosity recovers a transient young-like surveillance phenotype, particularly within CD4+ memory T cell populations. This recovered young-like phenotype is mechanistically linked to elevated SDF-1α receptor expression together with increased membrane tension, cortical F-actin, and Arp3 expression. Altogether, these findings identify a key source of surveillance defects among aged T cells and offer an effective mechano-inducible strategy for modulating single-cell behaviors.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Absorbing exceptional point of coherent vortex beams.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Acoustics, School of Physics Science and Engineering, Tongji University, Shanghai, China. yongli@tongji.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Coherent perfect absorption at an exceptional point (CPA-EP) combines complete wave absorption with a non-Hermitian scattering degeneracy. Here, we realize CPA-EPs in chiral spaces using topological vortex beams and acoustic metasurfaces with tailored symmetry. We show that chiral CPA-EPs (CCPA-EPs) arise from the delicate interplay of mode channels encoding different topological charges (TCs), and TC channels supported by orbital angular momentum significantly boost the channel capacity of CCPA-EPs. Through rotational operations, the chiral system enables dynamic switching of absorption capacity and degenerate state transformation, where the introduced geometric phase amplifies the CCPA-EP response to significantly enhance sensitivity. We further demonstrate the coexistence of sensitivity (in EP state) and robustness (in CPA state) within the chiral space. Our findings broaden CPA-EP research and enable advanced devices on chiral wave systems.

items.title: Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Life Sciences, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China. zefangwang@tju.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Synthetic Biology, Tianjin University, Tianjin, China. zefangwang@tju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Most characterized anti-CRISPR proteins act via well-defined core inhibitory mechanisms, yet how auxiliary structural elements modulate and potentiate these canonical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AcrIIC1Boe represses Nme1Cas9 activity through an integrated, loop-coupled regulatory mode. Based on canonical occlusion of the HNH catalytic site, the extended loop of AcrIIC1Boe provides an additional coupled regulatory layer to remodel sgRNA spacer arrangement and R-loop progression, thereby enhancing Cas9 inhibition. Loop deletion largely abrogates robust inhibition, indicating that this loop module is indispensable for full AcrIIC1 inhibitory potency. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1Nme1 efficiently elevates its inhibitory performance. Our findings identify a loop-mediated regulatory strategy that potentiates the canonical HNH occlusion mechanism, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence across AcrIIC1 homologs, and offer a modular engineering principle for the rational design and optimization of anti-CRISPR proteins with enhanced potency.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds.
items.last_author_affiliation: International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT), Dakar, Senegal.
items.abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94-1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Revisiting genome-guided RNA localization in bacteria.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, Weizmann Institute of Science, Rehovot, Israel. daniel.dar@weizmann.ac.il.
items.abstract: Elucidating the intracellular organization of bacterial transcriptomes may reveal new modes of gene regulation. Recent work reported that chromosomal gene position determines mRNA localization within Escherichia coli cells, implying a widespread genome-guided organizing mechanism. Yet this interpretation contrasts with biophysical expectations based on translation and diffusion and may be confounded by nascent transcription. Here, we examine this phenomenon by analyzing intracellular spatial transcriptomics datasets spanning different methods, bacterial species, growth conditions, and thousands of genes. We confirm the presence of genome-associated localization signatures that track chromosome macrodomain dynamics across the cell cycle and establish causality by repositioning a gene at distinct chromosomal loci. Quantitative analysis, however, shows that these signatures generally involve only a minority of transcripts and are of magnitudes consistent with reported rates of nascent transcription. Moreover, genome-associated patterns preferentially occur in weakly translated and unstable mRNAs. Together, our results indicate that genome-guided localization is unlikely to be a dominant driver of transcript positioning in bacteria.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Geography, Planning and Environment, Concordia University, Montréal, Quebec, Canada.
items.abstract: Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

items.title: Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory for Mesoscopic Physics & Department of Physics, Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter & Frontiers Science Center for Nano-optoelectronics, Peking University, Beijing, PR China.; Key Laboratory for Advanced Optoelectronic Integrated Chips of Jiangsu Province, Peking University Yangtze Delta Institute of Optoelectronics, Nantong, PR China.; Collaborative Innovation Center of Extreme Optics, Shanxi University, Taiyuan, PR China.; Hefei National Laboratory, Hefei, PR China.
items.abstract: Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

items.title: Archean subduction-derived noble gases in the lithospheric mantle beneath the São Francisco Craton.
items.last_author_affiliation: Programa de Pós-graduação em Geologia, Instituto de Geociências, Universidade de Brasília, Brasília, Brazil.
items.abstract: While mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB) and ocean island basalts (OIB) are well characterized in terms of helium, neon, argon, and xenon isotopes, the continental lithosphere, especially cratonic domains and subduction settings, remain poorly constrained. Here, we report noble gas (He, Ne, Ar, Kr, and Xe) isotope ratios in peridotite, pyroxenite, and eclogite xenoliths from the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton, Brazil. Helium isotopes reveal a strong radiogenic component, while neon shows MORB-like and nucleogenic signatures. This divergence indicates the recycling of subduction-derived materials within the stratified cratonic mantle (2.0-5.5 GPa). Xenon reveals a cratonic lithosphere where air and fissiogenic (crustal) components variably mix with a MORB source. The recycling of ancient hydrated oceanic crust and overlying sediments, characterized by high (U+Th)/(3He, 22Ne, 132Xe) ratios, is associated with a complex and long-lived subduction system established along the SW margin of the São Francisco Craton since the Archean.

items.title: USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Jiangsu Key Laboratory of TCM Evaluation and Translational Research, Department of Pharmacology of Chinese Materia Medica, School of Traditional Chinese Pharmacy, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China. junpingkou@cpu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28-NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

items.title: Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. guoqi.li@ia.ac.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Brain Cognition and Brain-inspired Intelligence Technology, Beijing, China. guoqi.li@ia.ac.cn.
items.abstract: A prevailing view holds that although neuroscience historically inspired AI, its role in the recent evolution of AI, driven by the scaling of foundation models, is minor. We challenge this perspective by establishing a biological analogy between simplified dendritic neuron models and the attention mechanisms central to AI foundation models. We show that AI attention mechanisms bear direct mappings to internal neuronal complexities arising from dendritic organization, rather than to the mere inter-neuronal connections of simple point neurons. This re-conceptualization not only offers a neuroscience-informed perspective for understanding core AI methodologies beyond their formulation as abstract mathematical operations, but also paves the way for neuro-inspired foundation models that leverage neuroscientific insights to sustainably advance modern AI beyond scaling laws. As an example of this paradigm, we introduce a dendritic-inspired complexity framework, and design a hybrid-attention foundation model with dendritic-inspired sparse computation, which enhances memory capacity while reducing computational demands. Our model supports a 50M context window-equivalent to roughly 40 volumes of Shakespeare-demonstrating superior long-term memory capabilities. This work pioneers a paradigm that harnesses intra-neuronal dynamics to drive sustained advances in modern AI, while also offering a potential route to understanding dendritic computational mechanisms.

items.title: Brain-wide pathways for object identity and location are dominated by internal strategies.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medical Neurobiology, Faculty of Medicine, The Institute for Medical Research Israel-Canada (IMRIC), The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem, Israel. ariel.gilad@mail.huji.ac.il.
items.abstract: It is long thought that higher-order sensory processing is divided into two specialized cortical streams that encode in parallel either the identity of an object or its location (i.e., 'what' and 'where' streams). Here, using the mouse whisker system, we demonstrate an existence of two alternating brain-wide (beyond cortex) subnetworks that are primarily driven by internal strategies, rather than external parameters. We combine simultaneous brain-wide neuronal recordings in male mice trained to identify or locate a certain stimulus. We find that mice deploy either an active search or a passive sensation strategy during task performance. These strategies respectively drive two distinct brain-wide subnetworks, frontal and posterior related to an active and passive strategy respectively. Using a computational framework, we show that the posterior subnetwork encoded additional internal strategic parameters such as trial history, the first task of the day, and training history. When discarding the dominance of the frontal subnetwork, specific areas within the posterior subnetwork encoded meaningful task information regarding object identity and location. Integrated together, these two subnetworks may comprise optimal sensory integration.

items.title: SLITRK2 knockdown rescues axonal and functional neuromuscular junction deficits in human iPSC-derived mutant FUS-ALS motor neurons.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Translational Neuroscience, University Medical Center Utrecht Brain Center, Utrecht University, Utrecht, The Netherlands. R.J.Pasterkamp@umcutrecht.nl.
items.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3' UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA, previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3'UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

items.title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Plant Sciences and Centre for Global Wood Security, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK. dpe29@cam.ac.uk.; Conservation Research Institute, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK. dpe29@cam.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

items.title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (-)-ganocins A-C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Lab of Functional Molecular Engineering of Guangdong Province, School of Chemistry & Chemical Engineering, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou, PR China. cezqma@scut.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Natural and Biomimetic Drugs, Peking University, Beijing, PR China. cezqma@scut.edu.cn.; School of Chemical Science and Technology, Yunnan University, Kunming, PR China. cezqma@scut.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A-C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (-)-ganocins A-C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI2-mediated 4-exo-trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

items.title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of EcoHealth, School of Public Health, Cheeloo College of Medicine, Shandong University, Jinan, Shandong, P. R. China. caowuchun@126.com.; State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity, Beijing, P. R. China. caowuchun@126.com.
items.abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential.

items.title: Myosin filaments of vertebrate skeletal and cardiac muscle are highly similar, but not identical.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Molecular Biophysics, Florida State University, Tallahassee, FL, USA. ktaylor@fsu.edu.
items.abstract: Striated muscles consist of two filament types, one based on actin, one based on myosin. All striated muscle actin filaments are highly similar. Invertebrate myosin filaments are heterogeneous; those of vertebrates are homogeneous. Mouse and human cardiac muscle myosin filaments are highly similar. How similar are they to those of skeletal muscle? Using Mavacamten for myosin head stabilization, we find the relaxed thick filaments of rabbit skeletal, human cardiac and mouse cardiac muscles are highly similar, differing primarily in the positioning of myosin binding protein C domains, C5-C7. In isolated cardiac thick filaments, C5-C7 lie along the filament backbone. In mouse and human cardiac myofibrils, C7 extends radially toward the thin filament. Here we show in isolated rabbit skeletal muscle thick filaments, C7 also extends outward but with C6 bending azimuthally to position C5 onto titin suggesting a thick filament architecture highly adaptable to multiple functions with relatively simple structural changes.

items.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Trauma and Chemical Poisoning, Department of Cell Biology, Third Military Medical University, Chongqing , China.; Department of Wound Infection and Special Drugs Research, Medical Center of Trauma and War Injury, Daping Hospital, Third Military Medical University, Chongqing , China.; Jinfeng Laboratory, Chongqing , China.
items.abstract: Microvascular anastomosis, the surgical suturing of small-caliber blood vessels, is technically demanding, time-consuming, and prone to failure from complications such as thrombosis. Existing adhesives are ineffective in the dynamic, wet surgical field, particularly for the limited cross-sectional interface of blood vessels. We present an integrated microneedle-interlocking adhesive system (iMAS) bioinspired by plant root anchoring. This platform combines a hydrophobic polymeric matrix with tetrahedral microneedles, creating robust, three-dimensional bonding for rapid, secure anastomosis. An embedded artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted wireless sensor enables continuous, real-time monitoring of vascular hemodynamics and cardiac graft health, facilitating predictive identification of complications such as stenosis and transplant rejection. In rat models, iMAS reduced procedural time by 78% and suppressed neointimal hyperplasia. iMAS streamlines microvascular anastomosis and enables proactive graft monitoring in transplantation.

items.title: Mapping lineage and functional diversity of the mammary epithelium in women at high risk of breast cancer.
items.last_author_affiliation: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University Health Network, Toronto, ON, M5G 2C1, Canada. thomas.kislinger@utoronto.ca.; Department of Medical Biophysics, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, M5G 1L7, Canada. thomas.kislinger@utoronto.ca.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer risk is shaped by the vast heterogeneity of mammary epithelial cells, comprising basal, luminal progenitor, and mature luminal populations. While transcriptional variation among these lineages has been extensively studied, protein-level features-particularly in high-risk women-remain underexplored, limiting insight into early cellular and molecular determinants of susceptibility. Moreover, little is known about how clinical covariates influence clonogenic capacity, proteomic states, and epithelial proportions. RESULTS: We combine low-input proteomics with functional clonogenic assays to profile mammary epithelial cell subpopulations from a cohort of 22 breast tissues encompassing different germline mutation backgrounds, parity status and age. We quantify 5,555 proteins and observed marked inter-donor variation in epithelial composition, proteomic programs, and colony-forming capacity. Multivariable modeling reveals that clinical covariates-including age, parity, and germline mutation status-modulate both global proteomic architecture and lineage-specific pathway activity. Parity is associated with reduced basal cell abundance, altered luminal progenitor and mature luminal proteomes, and changes in clonogenicity. Pathway analyses identify both conserved and lineage-restricted responses to shared risk factors. Projection of clonogenic signatures onto METABRIC and TCGA tumors further links functional programs to tumor subtypes and molecular phenotypes. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the most comprehensive proteomic atlas of cell-type resolved diversity in the high-risk breast to date. By defining how clinical covariates shape epithelial composition and molecular state, it clarifies key sources of biological variability that challenge controlled study design and offers a resource for improving mechanistic insight, risk assessment, and prevention strategies.

items.title: Benchmarking DNA foundation models for zero-shot variant effect prediction shows the importance of context, training, and architecture.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Information Engineering, University of Florence, Florence, Italy. alberto.magi@unifi.it.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: In this study, we systematically evaluate the performance of several DNA foundation models (NT, DNABERT, HyenaDNA and Evo 2) in predicting the functional impact of genetic variants using Zero-shot scoring, a method that does not require task-specific fine-tuning. We assess the models' sensitivity to sequence alterations introduced by Single Nucleotide Variants (SNVs), comparing their ability to capture both local and extended contextual effects. RESULTS: Using pathogenic, benign, and uncertain SNVs from ClinVar, we show that large multi-species NT models outperform other architectures in detecting functional consequences, not only at the SNV site but also in adjacent regions. These models exhibit superior discriminative power across variant categories, especially when aggregating Zero-shot scores over multiple surrounding tokens. Conversely, models trained solely on human sequences or relying on a next-token prediction objective, such as DNABERT, HyenaDNA, and Evo 2, exhibit limited contextual awareness and a reduced ability to differentiate variant effects. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the critical importance of model size, training objective, and training data diversity in shaping model performance. Furthermore, we discuss current limitations in modeling long-range dependencies in genomic sequences and suggest that innovations in transformer architectures, such as sparse attention or memory-augmented models, may provide viable paths toward scalable, genome-wide variant effect prediction.

items.title: Mitochondrial base editing for disease modeling and therapeutic correction.
items.last_author_affiliation: BK21 Graduate Program, Department of Biomedical Sciences, Korea University College of Medicine, Seoul, 02841, Republic of Korea. hjlee102@korea.ac.kr.; Department of Convergence Medicine, Korea University College of Medicine, Seoul, 02708, Republic of Korea. hjlee102@korea.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Recent development of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) editors has made it possible to generate experimental models carrying patient-relevant mtDNA mutations, characterize disease-associated phenotypes in cells and animals, and directly correct pathogenic variants in vivo. Here, we summarize the current landscape of mtDNA base editors and discuss key considerations for their application to mitochondrial disease model generation, including target selection, cross-species conservation, editing window constraints, strand bias, sequence-context dependence, and the balance between editing efficiency and safety. We further review strategies for validating mtDNA-edited models at functional, molecular, and organismal levels, and highlight recent studies demonstrating therapeutic rescue in animal models.

items.title: A systematic evaluation of in-context learning in large language models for antibody characterization.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biomedical Sciences, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, New Territories, Hong Kong SAR, China. qcao@cuhk.edu.hk.; Shenzhen Research Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, China. qcao@cuhk.edu.hk.; Hong Kong Bioinformatics Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, New Territories, Hong Kong SAR, China. qcao@cuhk.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Large language models can learn new tasks through in-context learning (ICL), yet this ability remains underexplored for biological sequence classification. We evaluate ICL across 20 large language models on three antibody tasks: species-origin, antibody specificity, and isotype class classification. Few-shot prompting improves over zero-shot performance, but matching the performance of protein language model classifiers requires sequence-similar demonstrations. Building on this observation, we introduce a sequence similarity-based strategy for ICL in antibody sequence classification, Sim-ICL. Using 32-shot prompting, Sim-ICL achieves competitive performance on two of three tasks. Its simplicity makes few-shot ICL promising for antibody characterization, especially for researchers with limited coding expertise.

items.title: Loss of CDK12 drives renal lipotoxicity and fibrosis through NCEH1 intronic polyadenylation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Nephrology, Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University School of Medicine, Nanjing, Jiangsu, 210000, China. wangbinhewei@126.com.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cyclin-dependent kinase 12 (CDK12) has been identified as a susceptibility locus for kidney function, but its role in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear. RESULTS: We generated tubule-specific CDK12 knockdown and overexpression mice and establish CKD models via adenine-induced and unilateral ureteral obstruction. We assessed renal injury, lipid metabolism, and transcriptional alterations using histology, functional assays, full-length transcriptome sequencing, and mechanistic rescue experiments. We detected significant reduction of CDK12 expression in renal tubular epithelial cells in human patients and experimental chronic kidney disease models. We find tubule-specific CDK12 knockdown exacerbates renal dysfunction, fibrosis, and lipid accumulation, whereas CDK12 overexpression confers protection. Mechanistically, CDK12 deficiency induces intronic polyadenylation of NCEH1 (neutral cholesterol ester hydrolase 1), resulting in reduced NCEH1 expression and cholesteryl ester accumulation. Restoring NCEH1 partially rescues lipid dysregulation and renal injury, identifying it as a key downstream effector. CONCLUSIONS: This study reveals that CDK12 protects against CKD progression by suppressing NCEH1 intronic polyadenylation and maintaining lipid homeostasis. The CDK12-NCEH1 axis represents a previously unrecognised mechanism linking transcriptional regulation to renal lipotoxicity and fibrosis, and may provide a potential therapeutic target.

items.title: Evolutionary remodeling of the ventral retina enables aerial vision in the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biological Sciences, Louisiana State University, Baton Rouge, LA, US. pschneider@lsu.edu.
items.abstract: The emergence of evolutionary novelties remains a central challenge in biology, particularly for complex organs such as the vertebrate eye. Here, we use the four-eyed fish Anableps anableps to investigate adaptation to simultaneous aerial and aquatic vision. Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics reveal that the ventral retina, which processes aerial light, is developmentally expanded and exhibits region-specific opsin expression. Ventral PR1 cones express opn1mw2 rather than the longer-wavelength-sensitive opn1lw paralogs expressed dorsally. Machine-learning predictions indicate that Opn1mw2 is red-shifted relative to Opn1mw1 but remains blue-shifted relative to dorsal Opn1lw pigments. Dorsal-ventral patterning markers further reveal an overrepresentation of ventral retinal identities. Comparative spatial profiling of developing and adult Anableps and killifish indicates dorsal displacement of the retinal boundary, producing a proportionally larger ventral domain. Thus, Anableps evolved aerial vision through developmental expansion of the ventral retina and regional reconfiguration of opsin expression within conserved cone subtypes.

items.title: Observation of dark magnons in a van der Waals antiferromagnet/ferromagnet interface.
items.last_author_affiliation: International Quantum Academy, Shenzhen, China. chenjilei@iqasz.cn.
items.abstract: Magnons, the quanta of spin waves, offer a promising platform for low-power information processing owing to their charge-free propagation. Dark magnon modes, which are intrinsically decoupled from electromagnetic fields, exhibit high robustness against environmental perturbations and enable stealth-like propagation, making them highly attractive for magnonic applications. However, the excitation and detection of dark magnons in antiferromagnets remain highly challenging. Here, we report the direct observation of a magnon dark mode in a van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr interfaced with a ferromagnetic insulator YIG. In CrSBr, the canted (spin-flop) phase is nearly bypassed and the spin-flip phase has two magnon branches, one of which, the dark mode, has nearly zero net dynamic magnetization. We demonstrate that the interfacial exchange interaction enables the experimental detection of the magnon dark mode, while its presence is confirmed by the observation of coherent magnon-magnon coupling between YIG and CrSBr magnons. Micromagnetic simulations and a theoretical model reveal that the dark mode in CrSBr at the heterostructure interface hybridizes with YIG magnons via interfacial exchange interaction. Our results provide a new route for detecting dark magnon modes in antiferromagnets and open up opportunities for stealth-like magnon transport and hybrid magnonic devices based on van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Surface carbonation governs olivine reactivity for rapid CO2 mineralization.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Systems Innovation, School of Engineering, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan. tsuji@sys.t.u-tokyo.ac.jp.
items.abstract: Ultramafic rocks are a global resource with vast potential for permanent CO2 mineralization. However, the origin of the striking reactivity difference between Ca- and Mg-bearing olivine remains poorly understood. Here we show that this difference arises not merely from the type of cation, but more fundamentally from how these cations modulate the oxygen reactivity. Nonbridging oxygens serve as the oxygen source for CO2 surface reactions, which in Ca-olivine reduce the Ca2+ dissolution barrier by 60% and accelerate ion release by six orders of magnitude. The calculated apparent dissolution rate constants reproduce the experimentally observed complete conversion of Ca-olivine within hours under 1 atm CO2. This multiscale framework reveals how surface reactions govern silicate carbonation and provides a predictive basis for modeling and engineering large-scale CO2 mineralization in both synthetic materials and basaltic reservoirs.

items.title: Designing nonlinear perturbative metamaterials that compute.
items.last_author_affiliation: AMOLF, Amsterdam, the Netherlands. m.serragarcia@amolf.nl.
items.abstract: Designing metamaterials that compute is challenging; the space of possible geometries is very large, and the relation between structure and function is complex. Perturbative metamaterials, consisting of weakly interacting unit cells, can be efficiently designed by combining simple geometric building blocks. However, perturbative metamaterials are conventionally defined in terms of linear wave physics, which prevents their use in information-processing applications that require nonlinearity. Here, we introduce a nonlinear formulation for perturbative metamaterials that allows us to identify material geometries that perform target computations. The design is enabled by a nonlinear, localized map connecting metamaterial deformations to a discrete tight-binding model that encodes the computation. We demonstrate the generality of this approach by designing three information-processing metamaterials based on three different computing paradigms: an Ising machine that solves combinatorial optimization problems through energy minimization, a mechanical racetrack device for in-memory computing, and a speech classification metamaterial based on analog neuromorphic computing.

items.title: Origami-inspired folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels for thermal insulation.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Light Industry & Food Engineering, Guangxi University, Nanning, China. huangcx21@163.com.; Guangxi Key Laboratory of Clean Pulp & Papermaking and Pollution Control, School of Light Industry and Food Engineering, Guangxi University, Nanning, 530004, China. huangcx21@163.com.
items.abstract: Nanofiber aerogels (NFAs) are promising thermal insulation materials for extreme environments; however, simultaneously achieving mechanical robustness, resilience, and low thermal conductivity remains a long-standing challenge in layered NFAs, where interlaminar instability often compromises structural reliability. Here we present an origami-inspired structural engineering strategy to construct folded-interlocked nanofiber aerogels. A folded-interlocked origami skeleton, integrated with a tailored interlaminar structure, introduces geometric confinement and fiber-mediated interlaminar toughening. As a result, the aerogels exhibit high compressive strength (548.02 kPa at 80% strain) and a near-zero Poisson's ratio. Importantly, the robust interlaminar network enhances resistance to delamination, allowing the aerogels to sustain tensile deformation up to approximately 40% strain before interlaminar failure. Meanwhile, interlaminar-guided heat-flow redistribution yields a low axial thermal conductivity of 0.035 W m-1 K-1 and pronounced anisotropic thermal insulation. This work provides an architectural strategy for designing folded-interlocked NFAs for thermal protection in aerospace and other harsh environments.

items.title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals inter-household networks of gut-colonising ESBL-producing Escherichia coli in two rural Malawian districts.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Tropical Disease Biology, Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, Liverpool, United Kingdom. adam.roberts@lstmed.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Infection with extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli (ESBL-Ec) is a global health concern that disproportionately affects sub-Saharan Africa. Gut mucosal colonisation is thought to precede invasive infection. Understanding ESBL-Ec colonisation and transmission across communities is therefore essential. Here, we investigate the genomic epidemiology and spatial structure of 159 gut-colonising ESBL-Ec isolates from the faeces of 211 people in two rural Malawian villages using longitudinal sampling (2023-24), whole-genome sequencing and household mapping. Colonisation prevalence rose from 34.1% (95% CI: 27.8-41.0) to 54.2% (95% CI: 46.0-62.3) over one year. Isolates belonged to 33 sequence types (STs), most commonly ST38 and ST131, harbouring 46 distinct antimicrobial resistance gene types. Fifteen strains were identified in ≥3 households that were typically separated by short geographic distances ( < 400 m). Of 190 pairwise comparisons between same-strain isolates from different households sampled concurrently within villages, 88.9% differed by ≤10 single nucleotide polymorphisms, consistent with multi-household involvement in community transmission networks. Lineage-specific ST38 and ST131 network analyses linked rural isolates to urban Malawian isolates collected within the last decade. Our findings provide a transferable framework for inferring ESBL-Ec flow in community settings and highlight the need for One Health surveillance and improved sanitation infrastructure to limit transmission.

items.title: Effects of time-restricted eating and supervised exercise on intrahepatic fat and cardiometabolic health in adults with obesity: the TEMPUS randomized controlled trial.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physical Education and Sports, Faculty of Sport Sciences, Sport and Health University Research Institute (iMUDS), University of Granada, Granada, Spain. ruizj@ugr.es.; Instituto de Investigación Biosanitaria, Ibs.Granada, Granada, Spain. ruizj@ugr.es.; Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red Fisiopatología de la Obesidad y Nutrición (CIBERobn), Instituto de Salud Carlos III, Madrid, Spain. ruizj@ugr.es.
items.abstract: Lifestyle interventions targeting intrahepatic fat remain limited. We investigated whether 8-hour time-restricted eating (TRE), supervised exercise, or their combination reduced intrahepatic fat fraction (IHFF) more than usual care (UC; Mediterranean diet and physical activity education) and each other. This investigator-initiated, parallel-group randomized controlled trial was conducted in Granada, Spain. Participants were recruited from May 2023 to April 2024, and the trial was completed on 5 September 2025. Primary outcome assessors and statisticians were blinded to group allocation, whereas intervention personnel were not. All 187 randomized adults with obesity (50% women) were included in the primary intention-to-treat analysis: UC (n = 48), TRE (n = 46), Exercise (n = 47), and TRE+Exercise (n = 46). The primary outcome was change in IHFF measured by magnetic resonance imaging after 12 weeks. IHFF change did not differ with TRE (-0.4%; 95% CI, -2.0 to 1.2; P = 0.93), Exercise (-0.8%; -2.4 to 0.8; P = 0.54), or TRE+Exercise (-1.1%; -2.7 to 0.5; P = 0.28) compared with UC, nor among intervention groups. These findings do not support greater short-term IHFF reductions with TRE, exercise, or their combination than with UC or between intervention groups. Trial registration: NCT05897073.

items.title: High fiber diet mitigates exposure risk of nanoplastics in male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Environmental Health, School of Environment and Energy, South China University of Technology, Guangzhou, China. eddyzeng@scut.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Potential health risk associated with dietary intake of nanoplastics has emerged as a global health concern, yet approaches for reducing gastrointestinal nanoplastic exposure remain poorly explored. Here, we investigated whether increasing dietary fiber intake influences the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics in male mice utilizing a visible/near-infrared dual fluorescence labeling technique combined with non-invasive imaging. The estimated retention rates of nanoplastics-associated fluorescence are decreased by two and seven times in male mice fed with medium fiber diet and high fiber diet compared to those with standard fiber diet, 24 h after oral intake. High fiber diet is associated with attenuated nanoplastics-induced epithelial damage to intestinal tract and declined detectable NIR fluorescence in important organs such as liver during 28-d oral exposure to nanoplastics. In vitro simulations show that dietary fiber physically encapsulates and adheres nanoplastics to decrease their bioavailability. Understanding how dietary constituents influence the gastrointestinal fate of nanoplastics may provide a scientific basis for the future development of dietary strategies aimed at reducing nanoplastic exposure.

items.title: A South Atlantic atmospheric river dipole as a key precursor of Amazon wildfires.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Earth System Science, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. deliangchen@tsinghua.edu.cn.; Institute for Carbon Neutrality, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. deliangchen@tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Wildfires in the Amazon have far-reaching climatic and ecological impacts, yet their predictability remains limited. Here we identify a large-scale atmospheric precursor of August-September Amazon wildfires: a June-July dipole mode of South Atlantic atmospheric rivers (ARs), characterized by suppressed AR activity in the north and enhanced activity in the south. This dipole is strongly linked to interannual variability in Amazon wildfire activity through land-atmosphere feedbacks associated with reduced precipitation and humidity, enhanced surface warming and solar radiation, and increased vegetation stress. We estimate that wildfire-related forest loss associated with this AR dipole mode accounts for approximately 26% of the observed interannual variability in total forest loss. Adding the South Atlantic AR dipole to predictors based on May-June sea surface temperature anomalies and June-July wildfire activity yields substantial predictive skill for August-September burned area (R² = 0.67). Climate model projections further indicate a future intensification of the South Atlantic AR dipole mode, implying increased wildfire-driven ecological degradation in the Amazon under continued warming.

items.title: Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage.
items.last_author_affiliation: IRCCS Humanitas Research Hospital, Via Manzoni 56, 20089, Rozzano, Milan, Italy. davide.pozzi@hunimed.eu.; Department of Biomedical Sciences, Humanitas University, Via Rita Levi Montalcini 4, 20072, Pieve Emanuele, Milan, Italy. davide.pozzi@hunimed.eu.
items.abstract: Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) - a key cytokine upregulated during MIA - perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: The claustrum contributes to working memory maintenance in mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Basic Neurosciences, Faculty of Medicine, University of Geneva, 1 rue Michel-Servet, Geneva, Switzerland. alan.carleton@unige.ch.
items.abstract: Working memory (WM) enables the temporary maintenance and manipulation of sensory information to guide behavior, yet the neural circuits supporting this process remain incompletely defined. The claustrum is a highly interconnected brain structure positioned to integrate distributed cortical activity, but its contribution to WM has remained unclear. Here, we combined microendoscopic calcium imaging, chemogenetic and optogenetic manipulations in mice performing sensory-guided WM tasks to examine the role of the claustrum in WM. Claustrum neurons exhibited cue-evoked activity that persisted across delay periods and evolved dynamically over time, with population states retaining information about cue identity on single trials. Reducing claustrum excitability during encoding, delay maintenance, or target comparison similarly impaired WM performance across sensory modalities, without affecting sensory processing, motor output, arousal or inhibitory control. Together, these findings reveal an important causal contribution of the claustrum to WM maintenance.

items.title: EphrinA4/EphA4 controls blood pressure via arterial sympathetic innervation in male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Interdisciplinary Research in Biology (CIRB), College de France, UMR INSERM 1050, CNRS 7241, Université PSL, F-75005, Paris, France. isabelle.brunet@college-de-france.fr.
items.abstract: The autonomic sympathetic nervous system innervates peripheral resistance arteries, thereby controlling arterial diameter and modulating blood supply to organs and arterial tone. Despite its fundamental role in blood flow regulation and cardiovascular adaptation to challenging situations, how sympathetic arterial innervation develops remains poorly understood.We here show that sympathetic arterial innervation is regulated by the axonal guidance molecule EphrinA4 in arterial Smooth Muscle Cells (SMCs), which repels sympathetic axons via the EphA4 receptor. Using the EphA4flox-THCRE mouse, we specifically inactivated EphA4 in sympathetic axons, inducing a loss of repulsion and increased sympathetic innervation of peripheral arteries throughout life. Functional consequences included a significant increase in arterial tone, including resistivity and vasoconstriction, associated with elevated systemic arterial blood pressure at rest and a marked increase during acute stress. These findings identify a pathway that negatively regulates sympathetic arterial innervation and could contribute to elevated systemic blood pressure in male mice.

items.title: Replacing anaerobic fermentation with reverse β-oxidation enables growth-coupled evolution for enhanced fatty-alcohol production.
items.last_author_affiliation: Joint BioEnergy Institute, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Emeryville, CA, USA. keasling@berkeley.edu.; Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA. keasling@berkeley.edu.; The Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Biosustainability, Technical University of Denmark, Kongens Lyngby, Denmark. keasling@berkeley.edu.; QB3 Institute, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA. keasling@berkeley.edu.; Department of Bioengineering, University of California, Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA. keasling@berkeley.edu.
items.abstract: Engineering robust fermentation hosts remains a barrier to scalable biomanufacturing. In this work we replace canonical mixed-acid fermentation in Escherichia coli with a redox‑balanced reverse β‑oxidation (rBOX) pathway that produces medium‑chain fatty alcohols and is bioenergetically equivalent to ethanol fermentation. This synthetic fermentation restores anaerobic growth, tightly coupling fitness to product formation and enabling adaptive laboratory evolution that selects for mutations increasing rBOX flux. Evolved strains increase maximum productivity fourfold (110 ± 0.15 mg/L/hr) and titer more than threefold up to 4.0 ± 0.28 g/L compared to the unevolved strain. Proteomic analyses of evolved strains indicate differential expression of enzymes at key metabolic nodes and activation of latent genes with functions overlapping those of rBOX enzymes. These results establish redox-balanced growth coupling as a powerful tool for strain improvement and demonstrate rBOX as a practical synthetic fermentation pathway.

items.title: RNF130 ameliorates renal injury and inflammation by inhibiting macrophage pyroptosis through ubiquitination degradation of PDCD4 in male mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: MOE Medical Basic Research Innovation Center for Gut Microbiota and Chronic Diseases, School of Medicine, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, China. sunhaijian927@163.com.; Department of Anesthesiology, Affiliated Hospital of Jiangnan University, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, China. sunhaijian927@163.com.; State Key Laboratory of Natural Medicines, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing, China. sunhaijian927@163.com.; State Key Laboratory of Food Science and Resources, Jiangnan University, Wuxi, China. sunhaijian927@163.com.
items.abstract: Macrophage pyroptosis has been identified as a contributor to acute kidney injury (AKI), but the underlying mechanisms involved remain unclear. Herein, we identify that ring finger protein 130 (RNF130) RNF130 is significantly downregulated in both mice and patients with AKI. Myeloid cell-specific loss of RNF130 aggravates renal pathological damage and facilitates macrophage pyroptosis in AKI mouse models. Proteomics analyses and experimental validation show that RNF130 deficiency prevents the ubiquitination of programmed cell death 4 (PDCD4) dependent on the lysine 402 of PDCD4. Activated PDCD4 promotes the phosphorylation of NF-κB and STAT3, triggering NLRP3 inflammasome activation and caspase-1-mediated cleavage of GSDMD, contributing to macrophage pyroptosis. Overexpression of PDCD4 nullifies the beneficial role of RNF130. High-throughput screening of a compound library identified that Nystose effectively mitigated renal injury in ischemic AKI mice by targeting and upregulating RNF130. These findings highlight the potential of RNF130 as a promising target for AKI.

items.title: Fever enhances host bacterial defence while limiting mitochondrial damage.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics and Astronomy, University of California Irvine, Irvine, CA, USA. sgross@uci.edu.; Department of Developmental and Cell Biology, University of California Irvine, Irvine, CA, USA. sgross@uci.edu.
items.abstract: Infection triggers the fever response, but the response's effect on antimicrobial peptide (AMP) function remains unknown. We discovered that human AMP LL-37 antibacterial activity is temperature-dependent and were curious as to why. Its temperature dependence is not an accident, as AMPs from other animals with different body temperatures have distinct temperature sensitivities. We find that AMP temperature sensitivities are tuned to animals' body temperatures, and that for animals able to raise their body temperature, this is used to increase the AMP's antibacterial efficacy. This effect reflects a balance between optimizing antibacterial killing while minimizing mitochondrial damage. In contrast, cold-blooded animals that are unable to raise their body temperature use a different strategy to avoid mitochondrial damage. Together, this study suggests that fever is beneficial for antimicrobial defense by raising AMP activity towards bacteria while reducing mitochondrial damage when pathogens are absent.

items.title: Genotype-phenotype single-cell transcriptomics for massive parallel assessment of genetic variants.
items.last_author_affiliation: Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM), Armenise/Harvard Laboratory of Integrative Genomics, Pozzuoli, Italy. d.cacchiarelli@tigem.it.; Department of Translational Medicine, University of Naples "Federico II", Naples, Italy. d.cacchiarelli@tigem.it.; Genomics and Experimental Medicine Program, Scuola Superiore Meridionale (SSM, School of Advanced Studies), Naples, Italy. d.cacchiarelli@tigem.it.
items.abstract: Predicting the pathogenic effect of rare genetic variants is significantly hampered by the limited cohort of diagnosed patients and the difficulty in functionally evaluating the effect of existing and novel variants. To address this issue, we leveraged a protein Multiplexed Assay of Variants Effect (MAVE) to functionally assess the effect of ~ 2200 missense variants of the TP63 gene, some of which cause autosomal dominant developmental disorders. The activity of each variant was measured using an optimized fibroblast-to-keratinocyte conversion protocol, and a subset of mutants was validated through multiple orthogonal biochemical and genomics functional assays to assess consistency and robustness. To systematically expand MAVEs beyond predefined assay, we here introduce SCRAMseq (Single Cell RNAseq Associated with MAVEs by sequencing). This generalizable platform leverages full-length scRNAseq for high-throughput, single-cell genotype-to-phenotype mapping. We validate SCRAMseq across different experimental and genetic contexts to demonstrate its reproducibility and accuracy. SCRAMseq provides a robust and versatile workflow poised to accelerate the discovery and dissection of gene variant effects on any potential disease-driving pathway, thereby significantly broadening MAVEs applicability to virtually any possible disease-driving gene.

items.title: A swing-type solid-state host-guest system enabling spontaneous adsorption-desorption cycling.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Automobile Materials, MOE, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Jilin University, Changchun, PR China. jrwu@jlu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Macrocycle-based solid-state adsorbents offer molecularly precise platforms for the selective capture of volatile organic molecules. However, regeneration of these materials commonly relies on thermal or solvent stimulation, limiting energy efficiency and the recovery of adsorbed molecules. Developing solid-state adsorption systems that enable reversible guest release under mild conditions remains challenging, particularly for structurally similar volatile molecules. Here we show a swing-type solid-state host-guest system based on a fluorinated pillar[5]arene that enables reversible adsorption-desorption cycling of volatile methylpyridines at ambient temperature without heat or solvent stimulation. Competitive binding of nonvolatile electron-deficient acceptors drives the transformation of volatile guest inclusion phases into charge-transfer phases, releasing the volatile guests and producing a visible chromic response. Re-exposure to excess volatile vapor reverses the phase transformation, with the direction and extent of switching influenced by the relative stability of the competing host-guest assemblies and further modulated by guest size and lattice accessibility. These findings highlight an appropriate degree of thermodynamic proximity between competing solid-state complexes as an important design consideration for reversible guest exchange. More broadly, this strategy provides a route to adaptive macrocycle-based adsorbents for low-energy, visually traceable adsorption-desorption processes.

items.title: Electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds enables programmable pore gating in metal-organic frameworks.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Coordination Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China. syuan@nju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising host matrices for molecular encapsulation, yet their application is often limited by fixed pore apertures that exclude guest molecules larger than the pore openings. Herein, we overcome this limitation by electronic tuning of dynamic imine bonds to induce reversible pore gating that transiently expands framework accessibility beyond its intrinsic aperture. By incorporating imine-based linkers bearing electron-donating/withdrawing substituents into a robust Zr-based MOF scaffold via postsynthetic linker exchange, we systematically modulate imine dissociation equilibria while preserving crystallinity. A linear correlation between Hammett substituent constants and imine bond stability establishes electronic effects as a predictive handle for programming framework dynamics. Systematic variation of substituents establishes an optimal metastable regime in which reversible linker dissociation permits size-adaptive guest uptake without structural degradation. As a proof of concept, paclitaxel and other therapeutics are efficiently encapsulated, and the resulting materials exhibit good biocompatibility together with programmable, environment-responsive release kinetics under physiological conditions.

items.title: A robust and accurate two-sample Mendelian randomization method with a large number of genetic variants.
items.last_author_affiliation: MOE Key Laboratory of Geriatric Diseases and Immunology, Soochow University, Suzhou, Jiangsu, PR China. ypei@suda.edu.cn.; Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, School of Public Health, Suzhou Medical College of Soochow University, Suzhou, Jiangsu, PR China. ypei@suda.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Horizontal pleiotropy poses challenges in Mendelian randomization (MR) by biasing causal estimates, particularly when using numerous instrumental variables (IVs). We propose MRZ, a method that leverages IV-outcome association z-scores modeled as a mixture distribution to distinguish causal effects from IV-specific pleiotropy. MRZ classifies IVs into three categories: valid, uncorrelated pleiotropic, or correlated pleiotropic, enabling simultaneous estimation of causal and pleiotropic parameters through likelihood-based inference. Simulations demonstrate MRZ's superior robustness and accuracy across diverse pleiotropic scenarios. When applied to investigate appendicular lean mass (ALM) and lipid traits, MRZ identifies significant negative causal effects of ALM on total cholesterol (TC) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), with no evidence of reverse causation. In contrast, existing methods frequently suggest bidirectional effects. Randomized controlled experiments in mice validate MRZ results, confirming ALM's causal effects on TC/LDL-C but not vice versa. By addressing key limitations of conventional approaches vulnerable to horizontal pleiotropy, MRZ advances causal inference in complex trait architectures.

items.title: Fatty acid metabolism controls plasma membrane cholesterol accessibility via ATGL-dependent phospholipid remodeling.
items.last_author_affiliation: Departments of Biochemistry and Medicine, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, CA, USA. mkinnebr@stanford.edu.
items.abstract: Accessible cholesterol, the pool of membrane cholesterol with high chemical activity, regulates vital processes including vertebrate development and pathogen evasion. The mechanisms that govern plasma membrane (PM) cholesterol accessibility are incompletely understood. Using a genome-wide screen we find that acetyl-CoA carboxylase alpha (ACC1) loss causes a ~10-fold increase in PM accessible cholesterol in cells and a male mouse model. We demonstrate that reduced fatty acyl-CoA levels, achieved by targeting metabolic enzymes including ACC1, fatty acid synthase (FASN) or acyl-CoA synthetases long chain (ACSL1, 3 and 4), results in the activation of adipose triacylglycerol lipase (ATGL). ATGL activation elevates polyunsaturated diacylglycerols even in triacylglycerol-deficient backgrounds, suggesting that ATGL acts independently of triacylglycerol hydrolysis. These diacylglycerol species are utilized to generate polyunsaturated phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylethanolamine, which raises PM fluidity and cholesterol accessibility. Conversely, ATGL inhibition rigidifies the PM, reducing PM accessible cholesterol. Increased PM fluidity impairs cholesterol transport, triggering SREBP2 activation. This study reveals a surprising link between fatty acid metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis, demonstrating how ATGL-dependent lipid remodeling tunes membrane fluidity to regulate intracellular cholesterol signaling.

items.title: Rapid Renin Angiotensin Aldosterone System inhibitor optimisation in patients with chronic kidney disease and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction using potassium binder: a randomised, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medicine, School of Health and Medical Sciences, City St George's University of London, London, UK.
items.abstract: Renin-angiotensin-aldosterone inhibitors (RAASi) improve outcomes in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), but their use is often limited by hyperkalaemia in chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised trial evaluated whether sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) enables RAASi up-titration in HFrEF patients with CKD stages 3-5 and serum potassium of 5.0-5.5 mmol/L over 14 weeks. The primary binary outcome was defined as achieving the target dose of RAAS inhibition therapy without reaching hyperkalaemia (serum potassium ≥5.6 mmol/L) over 14 weeks or otherwise. Participants (n = 112) were randomised 1:1 to receive sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) or placebo. The per-protocol (PP) analyses included 43 out of 53 (81%) in the SZC arm and 53 out of 59 participants (90%) in the placebo arm; the intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses included all 112. At the end of the trial, 24 of 43 participants (56%) in the SZC group achieved the target RAASi dose without developing hyperkalaemia compared with 15 of 53 patients (28%) in the placebo group (PP analysis, p = 0.006, ITT analysis, p = 0.007,). Participants in the SZC group were 3 times more likely to reach the target dose without reaching potassium 5.6 mmol/L (OR = 3.16; 95% CI 1.35-7.39; p = 0.008) than in the placebo group (ITT analysis). No significant differences in adverse events between the two groups were observed. SZC appears to safely support rapid RAASi optimisation in HFrEF patients with CKD. This trial was funded by AstraZeneca via Externally Sponsored Scientific Research grant ESR-19-20174. Trial Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov NCT05004363 and EudraCT number 2020-002946-18.

items.title: Genome-wide studies define genetic mechanisms of IgA vasculitis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Medicine, Division of Nephrology, Columbia University, Vagelos College of Physicians & Surgeons, New York, NY, USA. kk473@columbia.edu.
items.abstract: IgA vasculitis is a pediatric disease with skin and systemic manifestations. Here, we conduct genome, transcriptome, and proteome-wide association studies in 2170 IgA vasculitis cases and 5928 controls, generate IgA vasculitis-specific maps of gene expression and splicing from blood of 255 pediatric cases, and reconstruct myeloid-specific regulatory networks to define disease master regulators modulated by the identified genes. We observe significant association at the HLA-DRB1 locus (OR = 1.55, P = 1.1 × 10-25) and fine-map specific amino-acid risk substitutions in DRβ1. We find two novel non-HLA associated loci: FCAR (OR = 1.51, P = 1.0 × 10-20), encoding a myeloid IgA receptor FcαR, and INPP5D (OR = 1.34, P = 2.2 × 10-09), encoding an inhibitor of FcαR signalling. The FCAR risk locus co-localizes with a cis-eQTL that increases FCAR expression; the risk alleles disrupt a PRDM1 binding motif within a myeloid enhancer of FCAR. Another risk locus is associated with higher genetically predicted levels of plasma IL6R. The IL6R risk haplotype carries a missense variant contributing to accelerated cleavage of IL6R into a soluble form. Applying network-based approaches to blood single cell transcriptomes, we predict, independently replicate, and experimentally validate 21 IgA vasculitis master regulators co-modulated by FCAR, INPP5D and IL6R signalling in myeloid cells.

items.title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, Monash University, Melbourne, VIC, Australia.
items.abstract: Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

items.title: Global expansion of compound drought-heatwave risk.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA.
items.abstract: The increasing frequency of compound drought and heatwave (CDHW) events poses a growing threat to water security, agriculture, and ecosystems. However, the evolution, expansion, and spatial reorganization of CDHW hotspots across global land regions remain largely unexplored. Here we track more than 2500 CDHW events using a three-dimensional connected-component (CC3D) labeling approach and show that CDHWs, often treated as spatially stationary extremes, exhibit systematic displacement over time. Larger and longer-lasting events tend to travel farther and faster, expanding the spatial footprint of compound heat and moisture stress. Most contiguous events persist for 6-12 days, displace by up to ~500 km, and reach peak daily spatial extents of 2-5 × 10⁵ km². Migration is strongest in the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes and is predominantly eastward. We identify emerging hotspots of increasing CDHW migration potential across the European Plains, western North America, the Amazon, the West African Sahel, Central Asia, and northern Australia. These shifts are linked to evolving large-scale atmospheric circulation and are reinforced by downstream drying through reduced moisture transport and strengthened land-atmosphere coupling. Increasing CDHW migration potential over agricultural landscapes may expand exposure to compound heat and moisture stress, particularly in grazing-dependent regions vulnerable to pastureland-to-scrubland transitions.

items.title: Nationwide implementation of digital non-communicable diseases screening in Indonesia's primary care system.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Systems Medicine for Cancer, Center for Single-Cell Omics, School of Public Health, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China. huiwang@shsmu.edu.cn.; Hainan International Medical Center, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Qionghai, Hainan Province, China. huiwang@shsmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Non-communicable diseases require screening systems that can operate across large and diverse health systems, yet evidence from national implementations in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. Here we show how Indonesia's Aplikasi Sehat IndonesiaKu mobile application, integrated with the national digital health platform SATUSEHAT and the legacy Sistem Informasi Penyakit Tidak Menular reporting system, supports routine screening across primary care and community settings. We analyse records from January 2023 to April 2024, comprising 116,013,364 screening visits among 75,822,322 individuals and reporting from 10,131 primary healthcare centres across all 38 provinces. Blood pressure and anthropometric measurements are recorded substantially more often than cholesterol and cancer screening. Among participants with relevant measurements, 27.98% meet the screening definition for hypertension, 19.28% for obesity, and 32.18% for central obesity. Screening volume varies markedly across provinces, while recorded outcomes differ by age and sex. These findings indicate that interoperable digital infrastructure can support population-scale monitoring of non-communicable disease, but equitable implementation also depends on workforce, equipment and service readiness.
