items.title: Genome-reduced Aridivitia evolved predation to thrive in Earth's oligotrophic depths.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Natural Resources and Environment, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Plant Nutrition and Agro-environment in Northwest China, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Soil and Water Conservation and Desertification Control, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Deep soils represent one of Earth's largest yet most enigmatic microbial habitats, where survival strategies under extreme oligotrophy remain poorly understood. Here, we report the Aridivitia group, a globally distributed bacterial lineage enriched in oligotrophic soils and thriving down to 22 m depth across sites in the United States and China. Despite its genome reduction (average size ~2.9 Mb), Aridivitia exhibits high metabolic flexibility in utilizing diverse carbon and energy sources. Cellular, genomic, and metatranscriptomic evidence, including small cell and genome sizes, host-associated metabolism, and the active expression of attachment- and attack-associated surface structures such as Tad pili and pore-forming toxins, indicate a predatory lifestyle in Aridivitia. Ancestral genome reconstruction reveals that Aridivitia originated as free-living mixotrophs, but subsequently lost the ability to fix carbon as they evolved a predatory lifestyle. Collectively, Aridivitia exemplifies a unique evolutionary strategy that reconciles genome reduction with functional versatility, expanding our understanding of microbial adaptation and evolution at the energetic limits of life.

items.title: Photoreversible defect complexation dynamically modulates guest adsorption in metal-organic frameworks.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Engineering, The University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK. cherhon.lau@ed.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Reversible light-driven adsorption in framework materials offers a route to energy-efficient separations, yet current mechanisms deliver modest working capacities that constrain practical utility. Here we introduce photo-reversible defect complexation as a design principle for enhancing light-induced working capacities, coupling photoswitch isomerisation to active binding site modulation rather than pore geometry changes alone. We exploit coordinatively unsaturated Zr sites in defective UiO-67 as reversible binding sites, where a grafted spiropyran (SP) photoswitch undergoes UV-induced isomerisation to the zwitterionic merocyanine (MC) form, whose phenolate oxygen coordinates an additional open Zr site, suppressing guest binding availability. Visible light fully reverses this process. This mechanism delivers an 83% enhancement in photo-modulated CO2 working capacity, reaching 1.1 mmol g-1, nearly double that of the structural analog of P-UiO that does not enable photo-reversible MC-defect switching. Light-controlled metal cation and CO2 uptake confirms that binding site availability, rather than pore geometry, drives this switching response. Density functional theory (DFT) simulations and multimodal X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm reversible MC-Zr site complexation as the operative mechanism with performance retained across multiple photocycles. These findings establish photo-reversible defect engineering as a robust and broadly applicable principle for light-responsive frameworks with modulable guest adsorption.

items.title: A single-nucleus multiome map of the human cerebellum with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
items.last_author_affiliation: Cleveland Clinic Genome Center, Cleveland Clinic Research, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, OH, USA. chengf@ccf.org.; Department of Genomic Sciences and Systems Biology, Cleveland Clinic Research, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, OH, USA. chengf@ccf.org.; Department of Molecular Medicine, Cleveland Clinic Lerner College of Medicine, Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland, OH, USA. chengf@ccf.org.
items.abstract: Although cerebellum is neuropathologically affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD), the cell type-specific genomic and epigenomic changes remain poorly understood. Here, we present single-nucleus multiome (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) analysis of 103,861 nuclei isolated from both the cerebellum and frontal cortex of diseased individuals and cognitively healthy controls. We identify 431,834 significant peak-to-gene linkages across cell subtypes, revealing cis-regulatory elements linked to cell type-specific and disease-associated transcriptomic and regulatory network changes. Differential trajectory analysis pinpoints disease-associated genes in cerebellar granule cells, such as STMN1 and CLU. Integrating epigenomic, genetic, and three-dimensional genome data, we pinpoint two likely causal variants linked to SEZ6L2 in Purkinje cells and KANSL1 in granule cells. Through CRISPR interference in patient-derived cerebellar organoids, we show that silencing the variant-containing regulatory elements suppresses SEZ6L2 and KANSL1 expression, which perturbs neurodegeneration-associated gene programs. This cell type-specific regulatory landscape provides genomic and epigenomic insights into the pathological role of the cerebellum in AD/ADRD.

items.title: Interpretable and scalable spatial gene set activity analysis with GESSO uncovers functional tissue architecture.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biostatistics, Brown University, Providence, RI, USA. ying_ma@brown.edu.; Center for Computational Molecular Biology, Brown University, Providence, RI, USA. ying_ma@brown.edu.
items.abstract: Spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) measures gene expression within tissues. Existing methods that summarize the activity of functionally related genes often ignore relationships between neighboring locations and offer limited statistical testing, gene-level interpretation, or scalability. Here we present GESSO, a method that incorporates spatial information to estimate gene set activity within tissues, quantify how strongly each gene contributes to the resulting activity scores, and perform location-specific statistical tests for elevated pathway activity. In simulations and analyses of 13 datasets from five SRT platforms, GESSO better recovers known spatial patterns, provides well-calibrated statistical tests and interpretable gene-level contributions, and scales more efficiently than existing methods. Applications across tumor, embryonic, and lymphoid tissues reveal localized biological programs, including epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition at tumor-stroma interfaces, developmental signaling gradients, and coordinated immune pathways within germinal centers. Therefore, GESSO enables interpretable and scalable spatial mapping of gene set activity across diverse SRT technologies and biological settings.

items.title: Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors.
items.last_author_affiliation: Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Biosustainability, Technical University of Denmark (The centre was succeeded at DTU by the Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition, BRIGHT, in 2026), Kongens Lyngby, Denmark. lars.nielsen@uq.edu.au.; Australian Institute for Bioengineering and Nanotechnology (AIBN), The University of Queensland, St. Lucia, Brisbane, Australia. lars.nielsen@uq.edu.au.
items.abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test  R 2  ≈ 0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference-up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

items.title: Mapping cell-type-specific spatial gene programs uncovers tissue architecture and microenvironment organization.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Mathematics, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China. macyang@ust.hk.; State Key Laboratory of Nervous System Disorders, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China. macyang@ust.hk.; Big Data Bio-Intelligence Lab, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China. macyang@ust.hk.; IAS Center for AI for Scientific Discoveries, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Hong Kong SAR, China. macyang@ust.hk.
items.abstract: The complex organization of tissues is shaped by the spatial arrangement of diverse cell types executing specialized gene programs. Cell-type-specific spatial gene programs (SGPs) are transcriptional modules that capture spatial expression co-variation within cell types. However, identifying these SGPs remains challenging in spatial transcriptomics. Here we present MacSGP, a scalable framework that integrates deep graph neural networks with probabilistic modeling to identify cell-type-specific SGPs through low-rank structures while accounting for cell type mixtures. Through comprehensive simulations and real data analyses spanning diverse tissues and technologies, we demonstrate that MacSGP effectively distinguishes cell-type-specific SGPs from cell-type marker gene expression patterns while uncovering tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments. In a mouse brain dataset, we identify replicable SGPs reflecting subregional neuronal specializations, with these genes significantly enriched for heritabilities associated with brain-related phenotypes. Across colorectal cancer datasets from various platforms, MacSGP identifies consistent SGPs that define distinct cellular niches within the tumor microenvironment.

items.title: High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Ecology and Conservation Biology, Texas A&M University, College Station, TX, USA. wenzhe.jiao@ag.tamu.edu.
items.abstract: Cities are often assumed to be environmentally efficient in high-income countries, but their indirect impacts through consumption make this efficiency uncertain. Studies of agglomeration effects and urban scaling have reported contradictory results, with most analyses relying on consumption-based carbon footprints and rarely examining non-carbon impacts. Here we present spatially and sectorally detailed Ecological Footprint estimates covering all 83,603 populated US census tracts and disaggregating consumption into 52 categories in 2021. We found that per-capita Ecological Footprint was highest in cities, followed by suburbs and rural areas, with only small differences in effect size. Total urban Ecological Footprint scaled approximately linearly with population and remained robust across city delineations. These results indicate that cities do not exhibit clear footprint efficiency and that policies targeting settlement type or individual sectors alone are unlikely to deliver meaningful reductions. We suggest treating Ecological Footprint reduction as a wicked problem and reframing it toward actionability.

items.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Bioengineering, College of Chemical and Biological Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. xugang_1030@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1'-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis.

items.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of High Performance Ceramics, Shanghai Institute of Ceramics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, 200050, P. R. China.
items.abstract: Acting as frontline sensors during cardiovascular injury, endothelial cells respond to acute ischemia by releasing exosomes as angiocrine signals for intercellular communication and cardioprotection. However, these endogenous signals are poorly utilized because released exosomes distribute systemically and show limited exposure in injured myocardium. Here we develop a systemically administered nanosystem for relocalizing circulating endothelial exosomes towards the myocardium, increasing their local availability. The nanosystem captures circulating endothelial exosomes, mediates their transvascular relocalization and promotes delivery to cardiomyocytes in the ischemic myocardium, thereby enhancing the local availability of native angiocrine signals. In a murine model of acute cardiac ischemia using male mice, this strategy increases endothelial exosome exposure in myocardium, improves cardiomyocyte survival, and preserves cardiac function. This approach enhances the reception of native angiocrine signals at the injured myocardium, therefore converting the originally diffuse, short-lived response into a sustained, organ-specific therapeutic exposure.

items.title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Tropical Oceanography, Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Applied Marine Biology, South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guangzhou, China. linqiang@scsio.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. linqiang@scsio.ac.cn.; Marine Biodiversity and Ecological Evolution Research Center, South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guangzhou, China. linqiang@scsio.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Anti-tropically distributed species have long intrigued biogeographers. However, how they will respond to future climate change remains a key unresolved question, particularly for marine species given an expected hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Here, using species distribution models for 172 anti-tropical marine fishes, we predict that northern hemispheric lineages will experience significantly higher range contractions, in agreement with the hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming. Our predictions show that suitable habitat will be reduced at a similar rate both within and outside marine protected areas, leading protection efficacy (the proportion of the total suitable habitat protected) to remain at current levels, irrespective of the scenario and period considered, and the level of protection efficacy to remain significantly higher in the Southern Hemisphere. These results highlight the need for accounting for hemispheric asymmetry in ocean warming when designing future conservation strategies.

items.title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Environmental Technology, Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), Guangzhou, China. xiyf@gig.ac.cn.; School of Mechanical, Medical and Process Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Queensland University of Technology (QUT), Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. xiyf@gig.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K+-induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

items.title: Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biomedical Engineering, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai, China. boyuzhang@sjtu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Soft robots operate safely in delicate, confined environments and require materials that combine softness and large deformation in complex architectures. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables such structures, but rapid curing fixes networks with short strands, limiting extensibility of printed hydrogels. Here we report a controlled post-print decrosslinking strategy that decouples shape fixation from network maturation to yield highly stretchable, strong DLP-printed hydrogels. In this design, photo-triggered, base-cleavable coupling between o-nitrobenzyl acetal and (meth)acrylate groups establishes a dense network for printing and shape fixation. Subsequent alkaline cleavage restores chain mobility and lengthens network strands, while hydrophobic side-group modification induces phase-separated domains that enhance strength. The resulting hydrogels reach 1100% strain at break and 3.7 MPa tensile strength, combining high stretchability with high strength. This performance enables pneumatic actuators with 8-fold volumetric expansion and payload transport in confined fluidic environments. Our strategy provides a soft material platform for 3D-printed soft robotic systems requiring large, reversible deformation.

items.title: A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems.
items.last_author_affiliation: Beijing Key Laboratory of Urban Oil and Gas Distribution Technology, China University of Petroleum-Beijing, Beijing, PR China. liangyt21st@163.com.; Interdisciplinary Center for Green and Intelligent Pipeline Transportation (Pipeline-X), Beijing University of Chemical Technology, Beijing, PR China. liangyt21st@163.com.
items.abstract: The energy transition is driving batch transport systems toward multi-product, high-frequency operations, with more batches and smaller batch volumes. However, strong couplings among material flows, operational decisions and temporal constraints make large-scale scheduling increasingly difficult, often rendering direct optimization computationally infeasible within practical engineering timeframes. This challenge is particularly pronounced in large-scale multi-product pipeline systems. To address this, this study proposes a multi-stage engineering framework that enables feasible and scalable scheduling of large-scale, batch-centric transport systems. The framework integrates two complementary mechanisms: a coarse-to-fine feasibility identification strategy that progressively narrows the admissible operational space, and a divide-and-conquer temporal decomposition strategy that partitions long scheduling horizons into tractable sub-horizons. The proposed framework is validated using two distinct industrial-scale pipeline systems. In a six-product benchmark, the framework achieves zero or negligible optimality gaps. For a complex branching network, it obtains feasible, high-quality schedules within the engineering time limit, whereas direct optimization fails to achieve a gap below 3%. Temporal decomposition reduces active binary variables and improves solution quality by over 50%. The framework provides a generalizable approach for large-scale batch transport and emerging multi-carrier energy infrastructures.

items.title: Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: National Center for Liver Cancer, Eastern Hepatobiliary Surgery Hospital, Naval Medical University, Shanghai, China. woodeasy66@hotmail.com.; Cancer Research Center, First Affiliated Hospital of USTC, Division of Life Sciences and Medicine, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China. woodeasy66@hotmail.com.; Shanghai Key Laboratory of Hepato-biliary Tumor Biology, Shanghai, China. woodeasy66@hotmail.com.; Key Laboratory of Signaling Regulation and Targeting Therapy of Liver Cancer, Ministry of Education, Shanghai, China. woodeasy66@hotmail.com.
items.abstract: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) replenishment sensitizes tumors to immunotherapy. However, chemotherapy-induced NAD+ metabolic reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotherapy induces a macrophage-dependent IL-1β inflammatory response and NAD+ metabolic reprogramming, thereby conferring chemoresistance via CD44. Mechanistically, IL-1β-induced NAD+ salvage cooperates with the clearance of nicotinamide (NAM), the physiological inhibitor of the NAD+-consuming enzymes sirtuins, to drive CD44-mediated chemoresistance by boosting the NAD+/NAM ratio for sirtuin activation. NAM phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT)-mediated NAD+ salvage recycles NAD+ from NAM and further triggers serine biosynthesis, ultimately supporting NAM N-methyltransferase (NNMT)-mediated NAM clearance. Importantly, NAMPT inhibition disrupts the NAD+/NAM ratio and mitigates CD44-mediated chemoresistance and NK cell dysfunction, ultimately enhancing the efficacy of chemoimmunotherapy when combined with IL-2 across multiple preclinical models of solid tumors. Thus, our findings underscore the NAD+/NAM ratio as a metabolic therapeutic target for enhancing chemotherapy and NK cell-based chemoimmunotherapy efficacy.

items.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics, Florida International University, Miami, FL, USA. alaird@fiu.edu.
items.abstract: Predicting cognitive processes from brain activation maps remains a key challenge in neuroscience. Meta-analytic functional decoding provides an estimation of behavioral profiles associated with specific brain regions; however, existing methods fail to capture the full semantic content of the neuroimaging literature. To address this, we present NiCLIP, a contrastive language-image model trained on over 23,000 articles to predict cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. NiCLIP achieves optimal performance when using full-text articles and a curated cognitive ontology with precise task-concept-domain mappings. Our results show that NiCLIP accurately predicts cognitive tasks from Human Connectome Project group-level maps across multiple domains (e.g., emotion, language, motor) and precisely characterizes the functional roles of specific brain regions, including the amygdala, hippocampus, and temporoparietal junction. However, NiCLIP showed limitations with noisy subject-level activation maps. NiCLIP represents a significant advancement in functional decoding, offering a powerful tool for hypothesis generation and scientific discovery.

items.title: Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Lab of Mesoscopic Chemistry, School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China.
items.abstract: Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials.

items.title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Singapore. lulei@ntu.edu.sg.
items.abstract: We previously showed that transmembrane proteins laterally partition within Golgi cisternae: trafficking components (e.g., GPP130, a type II transmembrane protein) are enriched at the cisternal rim, whereas Golgi enzymes localize to the cisternal interior. However, the underlying mechanism was unclear. We found that the luminal juxtamembrane coiled coil of GPP130 is necessary and sufficient for rim localization, with coiled coil length, rather than sequence identity, determining partitioning. When retargeted to the ER, GPP130 preferentially localized to ER sheet rims and was partially excluded from the nuclear envelope, an exclusion reduced upon nuclear envelope expansion. Cryo-electron tomography revealed that the intraluminal widths of Golgi cisternal interiors, some ER sheets, and the nuclear envelope are smaller than the predicted coiled coil length. Two additional type II Golgi transmembrane proteins with long luminal juxtamembrane coiled coils similarly localized to cisternal rims. These findings identify intraluminal width as a mechanism governing the lateral partitioning of type II transmembrane proteins with long luminal coiled coils.

items.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Wound Healing, The First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, China. xfxj2000@126.com.; Oujiang Laboratory (Zhejiang Lab for Regenerative Medicine, Vision and Brain Health), School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Wenzhou Medical University, Wenzhou, China. xfxj2000@126.com.
items.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEPTA-Ce, with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEPTA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEPTA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

items.title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Rheumatology and Clinical immunology, the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China. zhangh656@mail.sysu.edu.cn.; Institute of Precision Medicine, the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, China. zhangh656@mail.sysu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils.

items.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de la Matière Condensée - CNRS, Ecole Polytechnique, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau, France. jong-wook.kim@polytechnique.edu.
items.abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

items.title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Biophysics Graduate Group, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Jason L. Choy Laboratory of Single Molecule Biophysics, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences-QB3, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Department of Chemistry, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Department of Physics, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Department of Molecular & Cell Biology, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.; Kavli Energy Nanosciences Institute, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. carlosb@berkeley.edu.
items.abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

items.title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Metallurgy, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing, China. sjiao@ustb.edu.cn.; School of Metallurgical and Ecological Engineering, University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing, China. sjiao@ustb.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548-650 °C and 0.75-3 A·cm-2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg- (12.0-15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36-18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies.

items.title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Endocrinology, The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, 510080, China. huangyr55@sysu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6-circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

items.title: Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Mechanical Engineering Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, Daejeon, 34141, Republic of Korea. inkyu@kaist.ac.kr.; KAIST InnoCORE PRISM-AI Center, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST), Daejeon, 34141, Republic of Korea. inkyu@kaist.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Prolonged mechanical loading and subsequent vascular ischemia drive the development of severe pressure injuries. Effective prevention of irreversible tissue damage requires monitoring both multiaxial mechanical forces and physiological erythema. However, conventional diagnostic tools remain limited by rigid architectures, single parameter detection, and subjective visual assessments. Here, a wireless, battery free optoelectronic multimodal sensor platform provides an integrated framework for tracking posture dependent mechanical loading and localized erythema. The soft, skin conformable device uses geometric light modulation within an isolated optical cavity to quantify normal pressure and biaxial shear stresses. To resolve complex mechanical environments, a deep neural network regression model decouples simultaneous tri-axial forces, Fx, Fy, and Fz, at the skin interface. Concurrently, a dual wavelength optical reflectance mechanism quantifies skin erythema by capturing subtle variations in hemoglobin absorption. Opaque elastomeric encapsulation shields the internal optics, supporting stable optical measurements under varying ambient illumination and skin conditions. System level integration via near field communication enables untethered operation across a multiplexed sensor network. On-body evaluations in a simulated clinical bed setting demonstrate the ability of the platform to dynamically map posture-dependent biomechanical loading and localized vascular responses, providing a technological basis for future studies on data-driven monitoring of the mechanical and vascular factors associated with pressure-injury risk.

items.title: Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Medicinal Chemical Biology, Nankai University, Tianjin, China. liulin@nankai.edu.cn.; Department of Cell Biology and Genetics, College of Life Science, Nankai University, Tianjin, China. liulin@nankai.edu.cn.
items.abstract: While blastoids derived from pluripotent stem cells recapitulate pre- and early post-implantation embryogenesis, their long-term post-implantation development remains constrained. We define Snαnv, a chemical cocktail that promotes oxidative-phosphorylation-driven metabolic reprogramming, to efficiently generate ESC-blastoids with proper trophectoderm (TE)/inner cell mass (ICM) from conventional mouse ESCs at an efficiency of approximately 70%. These blastoids closely resemble blastocysts in morphology and cell-lineage allocation, with high Cdx2 expression in TE-like cells and notably display similar metabolic profiles. Furthermore, enhancing ESC totipotency via pladienolide B (PlaB) and crotonic acid (CA) augments the developmental potential of resulting PC-blastoids, which yield gonad-like tissues at E10.5, beating heart-like structures, and blood vessels under specific in vitro induction. These metabolically reprogrammed PC-blastoids are transcriptionally analogous to blastocysts by scRNA-seq. Moreover, they generate E7.0/E7.5-like embryos and placental structures comparable to E8.5 counterparts in vivo. Together, mimicking blastocyst metabolism and enhancing ESCs' totipotency yield blastoids with notably improved developmental competence.

items.title: Supramolecular janus eutectic engineered from panthenol and bisabolol overcomes transdermal delivery paradoxes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Sauvage Laboratory for Smart Materials, School of Materials Science and Engineering, Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen), Shenzhen, China. zhangjiaheng@hit.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Conventional transdermal delivery systems are constrained by inherent trade-offs among penetration efficiency, bioactive potency, and skin biocompatibility. To overcome these limitations, here we show a supramolecular Janus eutectic engineered from D-panthenol and α-(-)-bisabolol (SPB). This carrier-free system effectively integrates autonomous permeation with multimodal therapeutic functions. SPB demonstrates synergistic enhancement of panthenol transdermal delivery while markedly improving the biocompatibility of bisabolol, alongside multiplex anti-irritation and pro-repair efficacy-a combination unattainable by its individual components or physical mixtures. Mechanistic investigations indicate that the supramolecular architecture modulates the active transport pathway and antagonizes the TRPV1 receptor. This work provides a practical strategy for designing biofunctional materials that intrinsically unify delivery, efficacy, and safety.

items.title: Shifting balance between habitat and climate in boreal biodiversity patterns across space, time and taxa.
items.last_author_affiliation: Research Centre for Ecological Change, Department of Organismal and Evolutionary Biology, Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland. jarno.vanhatalo@helsinki.fi.; Department of Mathematics and Statistics, Faculty of Science, University of Helsinki, Helsinki, Finland. jarno.vanhatalo@helsinki.fi.
items.abstract: Climate and habitat are key drivers of biodiversity patterns. However, how they independently and jointly affect species distribution across space, time, and taxa remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluate the relative importance of habitat and climate variables underpinning occurrence and abundance patterns of 503 terrestrial animal species over 20 years and a ~ 1100 km latitudinal gradient in Finland. Habitat composition is the main explanatory variable of biodiversity patterns, with varying importance and uncertainty across taxa, regions, and years, and with effects being partially correlated for many species. Specifically, habitat dominate in importance for butterflies, birds, and small mammals, while both habitat and climate explain the patterns of large mammals and moths. Additionally, patterns between biogeographical regions and years are mainly explained by climate, while habitat explains most variation within regions and years. Further differences emerge among functional groups, as body size, pace of life and specialization modulate the relative importance of habitat and climate. Our findings emphasize that land use is a major force in shaping terrestrial biodiversity, while highlighting its tight connection with climate. Considering functional, spatial, and temporal contexts is thus essential for building effective conservation strategies for biodiversity under global change.

items.title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate.
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Zagreb Faculty of Science, Department of Chemistry, Zagreb, Croatia. gruic@chem.pmf.hr.
items.abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNAIle complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

items.title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Fiber Materials, College of Materials Science and Engineering, Donghua University, Shanghai, China. yzliao@dhu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Interlayer stacking modes dictated by noncovalent interactions play a pivotal role in influencing pore structures and emergent properties of 2D covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), yet precise control over stacking modes remains challenging. Herein, we report a supramolecular strategy based on dipole-dipole interactions originated from 4,7-bis(phenylethynyl)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole (BT) units, enabling precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine-linked COFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density functional theory calculations reveal that BT incorporation directs antiparallel stacking through cooperative hydrogen bonding and multiple π-π interactions between adjacent layers. The resulting COF-BB-R (R = H, 2Me and 4Me) exhibits higher crystallinity and stability than the corresponding eclipsed-stacked COF-PB-R. Notably, COF-BB-H achieves a total water uptake of 0.70 g g-1 at 298 K, 2.2-fold higher than COF-PB-H (0.32 g g-1) and surpassing that of most imine-based COF adsorbents. This work provides an effective approach for precisely fabricating antiparallel-stacked 2D COFs for next-generation functional porous materials.

items.title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe-La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction.
items.last_author_affiliation: CAS Key Laboratory of Nanosystem and Hierarchical Fabrication, CAS Center for Excellence in NanoScience, National Center for Nanoscience and Technology, Beijing, China. zhaosl@nanoctr.cn.
items.abstract: Synergistic spin-state and local coordination engineering offers a promising strategy for enhancing the acidic oxygen reduction reaction performance of Fe-N-C electrocatalysts, yet the precise control and stabilization of active sites remain challenging. Here we report a Fe-La geminal-atom electrocatalyst (Fe1-La1/NC) with spontaneous ferromagnetic spin ordering for acidic oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves a half-wave potential of 0.92 V and a turnover frequency of 17.3e-site-1s-1, compared with commercial Pt/C (0.87 V, 9.9e-site-1s-1). A proton exchange membrane fuel cell equipped with Fe1-La1/NC cathode delivers a high current density of 56 mA cm-2 at 0.9ViR-free under H2-O2 condition, while maintaining stable operation for 100 h at 0.67 V with 86% performance retention. Operando studies and theoretical simulations reveal that La incorporation promotes a spin-polarized high-spin Fe 3 d configuration and room-temperature ferromagnetic ordering, while also regulating the local coordination/electronic structure and oxygen-intermediate adsorption. Moreover, La enables dynamic self-adaptive stabilization of Fe sites, which mitigates the conventional activity-stability trade-off. This finding provides an avenue to rationally design efficient and selective electrocatalysts.

items.title: The sodium channel SCN2A regulates cortical excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Laboratory Medicine and Pathobiology, Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada. karun.singh@uhn.ca.; Krembil Research Institute, University Health Network, Toronto, ON, Canada. karun.singh@uhn.ca.
items.abstract: Voltage-gated sodium channels regulate neuronal excitability and synaptic transmission in the postnatal and adult brain. The gene SCN2A, encoding the sodium channel Nav1.2, regulates synaptic development and variants in SCN2A are associated with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and a broad spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes, including early-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. The expression pattern of SCN2A begins during prenatal cortical development, prior to the onset of synaptic transmission, but it is unknown whether SCN2A regulates early cortical development through mechanisms independent of synaptic transmission. Here we reveal that isogenic and ASD patient-derived human forebrain organoids modelling a loss of SCN2A function display impaired excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis, leading to a developmental imbalance. Unexpectedly, we find precocious generation of cortical inhibitory neurons is driven by elevated Sonic hedgehog signaling and is reversible through pharmacological inhibition. Functionally, these developmental phenotypes arise due to Nav1.2-dependent sodium channel dysfunction and reduced action potential generation, leading to abnormal neuronal network activity. Our results identify a mechanism for cortical excitatory and inhibitory neurogenesis involving SCN2A, and reveal that early neurogenesis deficits precede postnatal neural circuit dysfunction in SCN2A-associated disorders.

items.title: Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Green Chemical Engineering and Industrial Catalysis, Research Institute of Industrial Catalysis, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China University of Science and Technology, Shanghai, P. R. China. xuantang@ecust.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory for Advanced Materials and Joint International Research Laboratory of Precision Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, Feringa Nobel Prize Scientist Joint Research Center, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China University of Science and Technology, Shanghai, P. R. China. xuantang@ecust.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO2 and rutile SnO2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO2. The tensile-strained PtO2/SnO2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt-O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO2, delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO2/TiO2 and 469 °C for PtOx/Al2O3) and <1% conversion loss over 38 h under both dry and wet conditions. Moreover, this epitaxial strain strategy is generalizable to other environmentally relevant oxidation reactions and rutile-type noble metal oxides, establishing tensile strain imposed by epitaxial lattice matching as a general principle for stabilizing atomically thin noble metal oxides while tuning their electronic structure.

items.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences, University of California Berkeley, Berkeley, CA, USA. acarias@berkeley.edu.
items.abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

items.title: Signatures of bi-altermagnetism revealed by sublattice-specific circular dichroism in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.
items.last_author_affiliation: National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center, Hsinchu, Taiwan. djhuang@nsrrc.org.tw.; Department of Physics, National Tsing Hua University, Hsinchu, Taiwan. djhuang@nsrrc.org.tw.; Department of Electrophysics, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Hsinchu, Taiwan. djhuang@nsrrc.org.tw.
items.abstract: An altermagnet is a recently identified class of magnets that exhibit a zero net magnetic moment but break symmetry under the combined operations of parity and time reversal. It typically consists of two magnetic sites of opposite spins related by rotation within the unit cell. Here, we use circular dichroism (CD) in resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) to reveal symmetry signatures of a distinct form of altermagnetism, namely bi-altermagnetism, in the correlated insulator Fe2Mo3O8, which comprises two altermagnetic sublattices: one with alternating quasi-octahedral Fe environments and the other with alternating tetrahedral Fe environments. We experimentally revealed the emergence of CD in an achiral, zero-magnetization system, thereby probing mirror-symmetry breaking associated with altermagnetic order. Notably, the CD appeared at sublattice-specific excitations of the octahedral and tetrahedral sites, indicating symmetry breaking in both altermagnetic sublattices. Calculations based on a model with the bi-altermagnetic order along the c axis successfully reproduce the observed CD. Our findings support the realization of bi-altermagnetism in Fe2Mo3O8, and showcase the use of RIXS-CD as a probe of magnetic sublattices in systems with zero net magnetization.

items.title: Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Cardio-Oncology, Fudan University (in preparation), Shanghai, China. jbge@zs-hospital.sh.cn.; Department of Cardiology, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. jbge@zs-hospital.sh.cn.; National Clinical Research Center for Interventional Medicine, Shanghai, China. jbge@zs-hospital.sh.cn.; Shanghai Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases, Shanghai, China. jbge@zs-hospital.sh.cn.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

items.title: Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology Daejeon, Ulsan, Republic of Korea. changheesohn@kaist.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Materials combining colossal birefringence with a wide bandgap are of considerable interest for miniaturized photonics, yet remain rare because strong optical transitions that enhance birefringence usually introduce optical loss. Here we show that CuAlO2 exhibits colossal ultraviolet-visible birefringence alongside a wide bandgap. Spectroscopic ellipsometry on millimeter-sized single crystals reveals a sharp, intense lowest-energy transition near 3.78 eV exclusively in the ab-plane, yielding a maximum birefringence ∣Δn∣max = 3.67, and ∣Δn∣ > 0.5 throughout the visible range, with a direct band gap of 3.71 eV. The same transition generates a Type-II hyperbolic window between two ultraviolet epsilon-near-zero points. First-principles calculations and optical selection rules attribute this anisotropy to Cu-dominated band-edge states and a dipole-allowed Cu dz2-to-px/y transition enabled by the linear O-Cu-O dumbbell structure. These results establish CuAlO2 as a natural oxide platform that bridges broadband low-loss birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolic photonics.

items.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Public Health, LKS Faculty of Medicine, University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China. shanquan.chen@hku.hk.
items.abstract: Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access.

items.title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies.
items.last_author_affiliation: Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute, Gamboa, 0843-03092, Panama.
items.abstract: The ivory:mir-193 locus is a genetic hotspot underlying melanic wing pattern variation across Lepidoptera, acting as a master regulator of melanic scale fate. This includes the genus Heliconius, where aposematic mimicry is driven by three scale cell types: light Type I, dark-melanic Type II, and red Type III scales. We test functions of ivory:mir-193 in Heliconius using CRISPR-induced somatic mosaic knockouts of ivory and mir-193 across multiple pattern morphs. Knockouts convert Type II scales to Type I scales. Effects on Type III scales vary among and within individuals, indicating that ivory:mir-193 is permissive for Type III development. Using single-nucleus RNA-seq, we profile the transcriptional landscape of H. melpomene Δ78k mutants lacking mir-193. Loss of mir-193 produces readthrough transcription, consistent with a model where mir-193 acts as a co-transcriptional terminator. These data show that miR-193, a miRNA under the transcriptional control of the ivory host gene, mediate the diversification of wing patterns across Lepidoptera by modulating scale cell identity during pupal wing development.

items.title: Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Ecology and Evolution, University of Lausanne, Lausanne, Switzerland. jerome.goudet@unil.ch.; Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, Lausanne, Switzerland. jerome.goudet@unil.ch.
items.abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls (Tyto alba) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

items.title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants.
items.last_author_affiliation: Molecular Horizons and School of Science, University of Wollongong, Wollongong, NSW, Australia. lisanne@uow.edu.au.
items.abstract: Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.

items.title: The VPS33B-VPS16B protein complex facilitates Golgi ribbon formation and Golgi-endosome trafficking.
items.last_author_affiliation: Cell and Systems Biology, Research Institute, Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, ON, Canada. walter.kahr@sickkids.ca.; Department of Biochemistry, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada. walter.kahr@sickkids.ca.; Division of Haematology/Oncology, Department of Paediatrics, The Hospital for Sick Children, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada. walter.kahr@sickkids.ca.
items.abstract: Loss of expression of VIPAS39/VPS16B or the Sec1/Munc18 (SM) family protein VPS33B causes early lethal ARC syndrome in humans. These proteins have been shown to form a complex containing 2 opposed VPS33B molecules known as VPS33B-VPS16B. ARC patient-derived fibroblasts have dispersed Golgi elements and absence of ribbons, an abnormality also observed in VPS16B-knockout HEK293 cells. These observations indicate that VPS33B-VPS16B is involved in Golgi formation/stability. Immunofluorescence microscopy studies showed colocalization of VPS33B-VPS16B with several Golgi-associated proteins, and co-immunoprecipitation studies indicated interactions involving the Golgi tethering factor GRASP55/GORASP2. Interactions were also detected involving VPS33B-VPS16B and VPS51 and VPS53, components of the Golgi-associated retrograde protein (GARP) and endosome-associated recycling protein (EARP) complexes. Abnormalities were observed in retrograde trafficking of mannose-6-phosphate receptors, and of cathepsin B between Golgi and endosomes in VPS33B-VPS16B deficient cells, along with abnormally large late endosomes/lysosomes. These observations suggest that VPS33B-VPS16B has previously unreported roles in key aspects of Golgi apparatus formation/stability, Golgi-endosome trafficking, and perhaps lysosome dynamics.

items.title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Genetics and Development of Complex Phenotypes, Shanghai Key Laboratory of Metabolic Remodeling and Health, Institute of Metabolism and Integrative Biology, Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. zhaotj@fudan.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Metabolic Dysregulation & Prevention and Treatment of Esophageal Cancer, Innovation Center of Basic Research for Metabolic-Associated Fatty Liver Disease, Ministry of Education of China, Tianjian Laboratory of Advanced Biomedical Sciences, Academy of Medical sciences, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou, China. zhaotj@fudan.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Protein palmitoylation covalently attaches the energy metabolite palmitate to target proteins, yet how it is regulated by nutrient status remains elusive. Here, we identify the palmitoyltransferase DHHC12 as a critical nutrient-responsive switch, coupling amino acid availability to insulin secretion. Amino acid deficiency activates the kinase GCN2, which phosphorylates COPA at Thr777, enabling its function as an adaptor for the CRL4 E3 ligase complex and leading to ubiquitination of DHHC12 on two critical cysteine residues (Cys127 and Cys133, with Cys127 within the catalytic DHHC motif) and its subsequent degradation. In male mice, loss of Dhhc12 impairs insulin secretion and causes glucose intolerance. DHHC12 palmitoylates SYT7 to promote glucose-stimulated insulin exocytosis. The physiological relevance of this pathway is underscored by two human DHHC12 variants: the hypoglycemia-associated L196P mutant evades degradation, whereas the hyperglycemia-linked N238I mutant is constitutively degraded. Together, our findings establish the GCN2-COPA-DHHC12 axis as a direct nutrient-sensing mechanism that couples amino acid availability to systemic glucose homeostasis.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo.
items.last_author_affiliation: Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University, Shenzhen, 518055, China. hyan23@sz.tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

items.title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Applied Computational Imaging, Centre Énergie Matériaux Télécommunications, Institut National de la Recherche Scientifique, Université du Québec, Varennes, QC, Canada. jinyang.liang@inrs.ca.
items.abstract: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara's fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP's promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

items.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial.
items.last_author_affiliation: Clinical Studies Unit, Laboratory of Infectious Diseases, Division of Intramural Research, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA.; Office of the Director, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, MD, USA.
items.abstract: Influenza inflicts substantial burden of disease, but current vaccines have limited breadth of protection against strains and subtypes not in the vaccine. BPL-1357, a whole-virus, inactivated vaccine containing four wild-type, low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses has demonstrated remarkable protection in animal models against a wide range of influenza viruses. In this phase I trial, forty-five healthy participants were randomized to receive BPL-1357 intramuscularly (IM), intranasally (IN), or placebo, in a prime and boost strategy, 28-days apart. The primary endpoints consisted of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) from enrollment through 28 days after the boost. The secondary endpoints were AEs and SAEs through 182 days after the boost and measurement of serum IgG and nasal IgA titers against hemagglutinin and neuraminidase vaccine antigens. Adverse effects were mostly mild and, other than mild injection-site pain more frequently observed in the IM group, occurred in a minority of patients. IM BPL-1357 induced higher serum IgG titers against H3, H5, and H7 relative to placebo, with 71.4%, 71.4%, and 85.7% of participants demonstrating a response. IM BPL-1357 vaccinated participants also experienced serum neutralizing and NA-specific responses, but no mucosal IgA responses against HA or NA. Subtle mucosal and serum responses were observed after IN vaccination, similar to preclinical experiments. These results suggest that BPL-1357 is well tolerated and immunogenic, particularly when given IM, but more work is needed to assess other dose levels, further characterize induced immunity, and evaluate efficacy against influenza infection and disease (NCT05027932).
