items.title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Genetics, Faculty of Biology and Chemistry, Justus Liebig University Giessen, Giessen, Germany. Sigurd.Braun@gen.bio.uni-giessen.de.; BioMedical Center (BMC), Division of Physiological Chemistry, Faculty of Medicine, LMU Munich, Munich, Germany. Sigurd.Braun@gen.bio.uni-giessen.de.
items.abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.
items.type: Journal Article; Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't

items.title: Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Gene Expression, Zhejiang Key Laboratory of Precise Synthesis of Functional Molecules, Department of Chemistry, School of Science, Westlake University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. wumingxuan@westlake.edu.cn.; Westlake Laboratory of Life Sciences and Biomedicine, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. wumingxuan@westlake.edu.cn.; Institute of Natural Sciences, Westlake Institute for Advanced Study, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. wumingxuan@westlake.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Lysine methylation is a classic posttranslational modification, yet most studies focus on histone methylation. Although emerging evidence demonstrates the significance of nonhistone lysine methylation, current approaches that investigate individual proteins of interest are relatively low throughput. Proteomics provides an ideal strategy for comprehensively studying cellular posttranslational modifications, but current enrichment methods typically allow the identification of only a few hundred methyllysine sites because of insufficient enrichment efficiency for low-abundance methyllysine-containing tryptic peptides. Here we report a comprehensive lysine methylation profiling method based on covalent enrichment-enhanced quantitative proteomics, termed DEKmeP. In practice, DEKmeP enables systematic nomination of candidate substrates and their monomethylation sites regulated by lysine methyltransferases. Through subsequent biochemical and cellular experiments, we validate dozens of nonhistone substrates of lysine methyltransferases. Moreover, we characterize the functional effects of SMYD2-mediated c-Jun K288 methylation. Therefore, DEKmeP may shift lysine methylation studies from the investigation of individual proteins of interest to systematic exploration of the methyllysine proteome, thereby expanding the understanding of lysine methyltransferase catalysis and nonhistone lysine methylation.

items.title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neurobiology, School of Basic Medicine, Fourth Military Medical University, Xi'an, China. baolguo@fmmu.edu.cn.; The Shaanxi Province Key Laboratory of Brain Function Analysis and Modulation, Xi'an, China. baolguo@fmmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC-DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model.

items.title: IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages.
items.last_author_affiliation: HSS Research Institute and David Z. Rosensweig Genomics Research Center, Hospital for Special Surgery, New York, NY, USA. IvashkivL@hss.edu.; Immunology and Microbial Pathogenesis Graduate Program, Weill Cornell Medicine, New York, NY, USA. IvashkivL@hss.edu.; Department of Medicine, Weill Cornell Medicine, New York, NY, USA. IvashkivL@hss.edu.
items.abstract: Investigation of crosstalk between antagonistic pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines has focused on mechanisms and functional consequences of cross-inhibition. Here, we investigate cross-regulation between proinflammatory tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and anti-inflammatory interleukin-4 (IL-4) in primary human monocytes and in a skin wound-healing model. Surprisingly, TNF functioned mainly as a costimulator of IL-4-induced gene expression, whereas IL-4 selectively inhibited the TNF-induced IFN response, leaving inflammatory gene expression mostly intact. TNF and IL-4 synergistically induced gene sets that are important in the regulation of inflammation and tissue repair, which were highly induced during the phase of wound healing when these cytokines are co-expressed. Crosstalk between TNF and IL-4 was mediated by epigenetic chromatin-mediated mechanisms associated with cooperation between NF-κB and STAT6 transcription factors, erasure of negative histone mark H3K27me3, and selective inhibition of IRF1. These results identify a mechanism for expansion of the IL-4 response and highlight the complexity of crosstalk between antagonistic cytokines, including cooperation for select gene responses that are important for immune responses and tissue repair.

items.title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination.
items.last_author_affiliation: Section of Structural and Synthetic Biology, Faculty of Medicine, Imperial College London, London, UK. Xiaodong.zhang@imperial.ac.uk.; Laboratory of DNA Processing Machines, Francis Crick Institute, London, UK. Xiaodong.zhang@imperial.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51-DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B's ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B's critical role in genome maintenance.

items.title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases.
items.last_author_affiliation: Science for Life Laboratory, KTH - Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden. adilm@scilifelab.se.; Centre for Host-Microbiome Interactions, Faculty of Dentistry, Oral & Craniofacial Sciences, King's College London, London, UK. adilm@scilifelab.se.
items.abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition-specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA-protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

items.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets.
items.last_author_affiliation: Environmental Microbiome Engineering and Biotechnology Lab, Department of Civil Engineering, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China. zhangt@hku.hk.; School of Public Health, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China. zhangt@hku.hk.
items.abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG-mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG-eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied to 11,976 sewage-derived SAGs. This approach yielded 4,198 SAGs passing Scellmate's whole-SAG curation, which captured pronounced heterogeneity masked by bulk methods. At the species level, we resolved extensive hidden diversity within abundant taxa such as Aliarcobacter that was unresolved by matched metagenome-assembled genomes; at the strain level, we pinpointed a distinct Agathobacter rectalis cluster carrying specialized carbon-utilization pathways, suggesting niche differentiation. Leveraging these curated SAGs, we identified 6,474 host-mobilome linkages across 2,378 SAGs; these linkages not only showed high concordance with host-association data within the Integrated Microbial Genomes (IMG) system but also significantly expanded species-level host assignments. Furthermore, we detected frequent inter-species sharing patterns of diverse cryptic plasmids within the order Bacteroidales. Together, this work demonstrates that high-throughput single-cell genomics, empowered by the robust framework, resolves fine-scale heterogeneity and host-mobilome dynamics, advancing culture-independent microbiome research.

items.title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Microbial Diversity and Innovative Utilization, Institute of Microbiology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. fengj@im.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae, predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

items.title: Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging.
items.last_author_affiliation: Center for Rehabilitation Medicine, Rehabilitation & Sports Medicine Research Institute of Zhejiang Province, Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Cancer Center, Zhejiang Provincial People's Hospital (Affiliated People's Hospital), Hangzhou Medical College, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, 310014, China. caiyu@hmc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI-, B(C2O4)2-, or BF4-) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

items.title: De novo design of miniprotein inhibitors of bacterial adhesins.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA. dabaker@uw.edu.; Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA. dabaker@uw.edu.; Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, USA. dabaker@uw.edu.
items.abstract: The rise of multidrug-resistant bacterial infections necessitates the discovery of novel antimicrobial strategies. Here, we show that protein design provides a generalizable means of generating new antimicrobials by neutralizing the function of bacterial adhesins, which are virulence factors critical in host-pathogen interactions. We de novo designed high-affinity miniprotein binders to FimH and Abp chaperone usher pili adhesins from uropathogenic Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, respectively, which are implicated in mediating both uncomplicated and catheter-associated urinary tract infections (UTI) responsible for significant morbidity worldwide. The designed antagonists have high specificity and stability, disrupt bacterial recognition of host receptors, block biofilm formation, and are effective in treating and preventing murine models of uncomplicated and catheter-associated UTIs in vivo.

items.title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer's disease.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neuroscience, Mayo Clinic, Jacksonville, FL, USA. Springer.Wolfdieter@mayo.edu.; Neuroscience PhD Program, Mayo Clinic Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, Jacksonville, FL, USA. Springer.Wolfdieter@mayo.edu.
items.abstract: Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD.

items.title: Model-data synthesis of benthic isotopes suggests a warmer Miocene Climatic Optimum.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Ocean and Earth Science, University of Southampton, Southampton, UK.
items.abstract: The Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO,  ~ 15 Ma) offers insights into warm-climate dynamics and future climate change. However, its global warmth magnitude remains uncertain due to limitations in surface and benthic proxy records. Here, we develop long-run Miocene simulations featuring deep-ocean equilibration and water isotope capability, and present a probabilistic inference framework integrating them with a global compilation of benthic foraminiferal δ18O to better constrain the MCO warmth. Our approach yields a maximum likelihood estimate of MCO global mean surface temperature of 7.5∘C above preindustrial, significantly warmer than previous benthic δ18O-based reconstructions, implying a higher MCO-derived estimate of Earth system sensitivity. The corresponding surface temperature field shows among the best agreements with independent surface temperature proxies. This study highlights the importance of deep-ocean equilibration and proxy-model integration for accurately estimating both deep-ocean and surface temperatures, and offers a method applicable to improving global climate reconstructions across other time intervals.

items.title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys.
items.last_author_affiliation: Beijing Key Lab of Microstructure and Property of Advanced Materials, College of Materials Science & Engineering, Beijing University of Technology, Beijing, China. xdhan@bjut.edu.cn.; Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China. xdhan@bjut.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe48Mn32Co10Cr10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

items.title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network.
items.last_author_affiliation: DMSN, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Mestre, Italy. guido.caldarelli@cnr.it.; CNR-Institute for Complex Systems (ISC), Rome, Italy. guido.caldarelli@cnr.it.; ECLT Ca' Bottacin, Venice, Italy. guido.caldarelli@cnr.it.; LIMS, Royal Institution, London, UK. guido.caldarelli@cnr.it.
items.abstract: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

items.title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neurobiology, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA. marlenecohen@uchicago.edu.; Neuroscience Institute, University of Chicago, Chicago, IL, USA. marlenecohen@uchicago.edu.
items.abstract: High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks.

items.title: Spinons, solitons and random-singlet-like behaviours in the spin-chain compound copper benzoate.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Physics and Key Laboratory of Quantum State Construction and Manipulation (Ministry of Education), Renmin University of China, Beijing, China. wqyu_phy@ruc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The S  = 1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain is a paradigmatic quantum system hosting exotic excitations. Using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) on copper benzoate, we characterise three distinct types of excitations by tuning the magnetic field at ultra-low temperatures. At 0.2 T, a nearly constant spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T1) and a divergence-like spin-spin relaxation rate (1/T2G) upon cooling provide experimental evidence for spinon excitations. Below 0.4 K, an additional relaxation channel, characterised by 1/T1 ∝ T with spectral weight growing as - ln ( T / T 0   )  and a divergence of the NMR Knight shift (Kn), reveals random-singlet-like behaviours. Above 1 T, a field-induced spin gap Δ ∝ H2/3 signifies the onset of soliton excitations. This work offers NMR identification of spinons, solitons, and the low-energy behaviours of a random-singlet-like state in copper benzoate, and establishes this material as a unique platform for studying the interplay of quantum integrability and disorder.

items.title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Climate, Environment and Energy, Jeonbuk National University, Jeonju, South Korea.
items.abstract: Extreme precipitation poses severe societal and economic risks under elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), yet current understanding of how it will respond to various future CO2 removal scenarios remains limited. Focusing on East Asia, a region highly vulnerable to monsoonal dynamics and anthropogenic influences, here we assess the hysteresis of extreme precipitation responses under four CO2 concentration thresholds and two emission reduction rates using climate model simulations. The extreme precipitation indices based on intensity and frequency exhibit an increase during the CO2 peak, but fail to fully return to their initial states even after CO2 levels decline to their initial levels. This hysteresis behavior is amplified by delayed and slower emission reductions. The hysteresis is linked to increases in mean monsoon precipitation associated with hysteresis in tropical Pacific warming patterns and subsequent atmospheric teleconnections. Moisture budget analysis further indicates that enhanced precipitation is attributed to increased moisture transport into East Asia, driven by early-summer rises in specific humidity (thermodynamic factor) through mean circulation and late-summer intensification of monsoon circulation (dynamic factor). These findings reveal the mechanisms shaping East Asian extreme precipitation under different carbon removal pathways and highlight the critical role of both timing and pace of emission reductions in determining regional climate outcomes.

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle-mediated epithelial-macrophage crosstalk contributes to macrophage dysfunction during PEDV infection.
items.last_author_affiliation: MOE Joint International Research Laboratory of Animal Health and Food Safety, College of Veterinary Medicine, Nanjing Agricultural University, Nanjing, PR China.
items.abstract: Mucosal immune defense depends on coordinated communication between epithelial and immune cells, yet pathogens can disrupt this crosstalk through diverse mechanisms. Here we show that porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV), an enteric alphacoronavirus, reshapes epithelial small extracellular vesicle (sEV) signaling to impair macrophage function. Despite detection by the intestinal innate immune system, PEDV promotes the release of epithelial sEVs enriched in immunoregulatory noncoding RNAs. Among this cargo, miR-190a targets the actin-regulating protein TMOD3 and disrupts F-actin remodeling, reducing macrophage migration. In parallel, the long noncoding RNA TS2083 promotes annexin A2 degradation, impairing phagocytic cup formation and suppressing phagocytosis. Moreover, serum sEVs from PEDV-infected piglets are enriched in both RNAs and impair isolated alveolar macrophage migration and phagocytosis, suggesting distal macrophage modulation. Collectively, these findings implicate sEV-mediated macrophage reprogramming in PEDV-mediated immune evasion and highlight sEV-associated RNAs as potential biomarkers of PEDV infection and therapeutic targets for restoring macrophage-mediated mucosal immunity.

items.title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Blackett Laboratory, Imperial College London, London, UK. m.kim@imperial.ac.uk.; Korea Institute for Advanced Study, Seoul, South Korea. m.kim@imperial.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

items.title: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD.
items.last_author_affiliation: Berlin Institute of Health, Charité-Universitatsmedizin Berlin, corporate member of Freie Universität Berlin, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Berlin, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.; Experimental and Clinical Research Center, a cooperation of Charité-Universitatsmedizin Berlin and Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine, Berlin, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.; Max Delbrück Center for Molecular Medicine in the Helmholtz Association, Berlin, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.; German Centre for Cardiovascular Research, Partner Site, Berlin, Berlin, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.; Structural and Computational Biology Unit, European Molecular Biology Laboratory, Heidelberg, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.; Cluster of Excellence ImmunoPreCept (EXC 3118), Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin, Berlin, Germany. Sofia.Forslund@mdc-berlin.de.
items.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized among people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, yet the mechanisms linking airway microbial ecology to chronic inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we study 200 adults stratified by HIV and COPD status, including 160 participants with two-year longitudinal follow-up, using an integrated multi-omics framework combining sputum 16S rRNA profiling, bacterial outer membrane vesicle quantification, airway cytokine profiling, CyTOF immune phenotyping, bulk transcriptomics of induced sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage and peripheral blood, and bronchoalveolar lavage single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution. We find that sputum microbial communities are shaped predominantly by temporal ecological turnover rather than HIV or COPD status. Although microbial diversity, microbiome instability, outer membrane vesicle burden and inferred airway cellular composition remain largely preserved, HIV-associated COPD exhibits disease-specific microbial signatures together with inflammatory transcriptional remodeling concentrated in induced sputum. Integrated analyses identify selective host-microbe interaction networks linking discrete microbial taxa with inflammatory, immune and transcriptional programmes.

items.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda).
items.last_author_affiliation: Royal Ontario Museum, Department of Natural History, Toronto, ON, Canada. davide@rom.on.ca.; University of Toronto, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, Toronto, ON, Canada. davide@rom.on.ca.
items.abstract: The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi-the first for the clade-reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit-which shaped early Cenozoic flora-remains unclear.

items.title: ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, University of Missouri, Columbia, MO, USA. chengji@missouri.edu.; NextGen Precision Health, University of Missouri, Columbia, MO, USA. chengji@missouri.edu.
items.abstract: Cryogenic Electron Tomography (cryo-ET) is an emerging experimental technique used to visualize cell structures and macromolecules in their native cellular environment. Accurate segmentation of cell structures in cryo-ET tomograms, such as cell membranes, supports the study of cellular organization and function. However, several inherent limitations in cryo-ET, including the very low signal-to-noise ratio, missing wedge artifacts from limited tilt angles, and other noise artifacts, collectively hinder the reliable identification and delineation of these structures. In this study, we present ETSAM, a two-stage Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2)-based fine-tuned AI method that effectively segments cell membranes in tomograms. It is trained on a diverse dataset comprising 83 experimental tomograms from the CryoET Data Portal (CDP) database and 28 simulated tomograms generated using PolNet. On an independent test set of 17 experimental tomograms for which ground-truth annotations are available, ETSAM outperforms other deep learning based methods by robustly identifying cell membranes with high sensitivity while also maintaining better precision.

items.title: HERC2-UBE3A structure uncovers a domain-motif protein network potentially altered in Angelman and related syndromes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Equipe Labellisée Ligue 2015, Département de Biologie Structurale Intégrative, Institut de Génétique et de Biologie Moléculaire et Cellulaire (IGBMC), INSERM U1258/CNRS UMR 7104/Université de Strasbourg, Illkirch, France. gilles.trave@unistra.fr.
items.abstract: UBE3A and HERC2 are two mutually interacting HECT E3 Ubiquitin ligases whose genes are altered in 15q11.2-13.1 Duplication (Dup15q) Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome (AS) and other phenotypically-related syndromes associated with intellectual disability. Using quantitative binding assays, X-ray crystallography and sequence conservation analysis, we characterize the core interface of the HERC2-UBE3A complex, involving the RLD2 domain of HERC2 and a "DxDKDxD" sequence from a disordered region of UBE3A. The sequence determinants of the interface are conserved in numerous animals with a central nervous system. HERC2 also binds similar DxDKDxD motifs within a handful of other proteins relevant to brain development (DOCK10, PCM1, USP35, BAZ2B, ARID4A, ARIP4, RERE and MYT1). We further investigate the interaction of HERC2 with DOCK10, a RAC1- and CDC42-GEF protein that regulates dendritic spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons. siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC2 affects the GEF activity of DOCK10, and mutagenesis of the HERC2-binding motif in DOCK10 disrupts both its GEF activity and its ability to drive dendritic spine formation. In developing brains, an abnormal dosage of either HERC2 or its dominant partner UBE3A may thus alter the proportions of RLD2-mediated complexes, including HERC2-DOCK10, and may thereby perturb dendritic spine morphogenesis and neurodevelopment.

items.title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Medicine, University Vita-Salute San Raffaele, Milan, Italy.; Research Department of Behavioural Science and Health, University College London, London, UK.
items.abstract: Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23-1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26-1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

items.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Urology, Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital, Affiliated Hospital of Medical School, Nanjing University, Nanjing, China. yangr@nju.edu.cn.; Department of Urology, Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital Clinical College of Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine, Nanjing, China. yangr@nju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Dynamic remodeling of immune cell-surface glycans reflects cellular state and immune activity. Despite advances in single-cell glyco-profiling, current methods primarily capture pre-existing glycan epitopes, providing limited information on dynamic sialoglycans. Here, we present GlycoStamp-seq, a method to profile nascent sialoglycan dynamics by coupling Ac₄ManNAz-based metabolic glycoengineering with single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing (scRNA/TCR-seq) and scDyna-seq. We apply GlycoStamp-seq by injecting Ac₄ManNAz into oxaliplatin-treated mice with subcutaneous bladder tumors, days before extracting tumor-derived single-cell suspensions for sequencing. Following oxaliplatin treatment, a subset of CD8⁺ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment exhibits elevated nascent sialoglycan activity, enhanced effector programs, and increased clonal expansion. Furthermore, elevated nascent sialoglycan levels mark antigen-reactive CD8⁺ T cells with increased anti-tumor efficacy in vitro and in vivo. GlycoStamp-seq may thus serve as a versatile platform for profiling nascent sialoglycan dynamics in complex tissues, thereby expanding the single-cell multi-omics toolkit and providing insights into sialoglycan dynamics during therapeutic response.

items.title: ATRX deficiency drives aberrant type I interferon signalling through cGAS-dependent transcriptional dysregulation.
items.last_author_affiliation: MRC Human Genetics Unit, Institute of Genetics and Cancer, University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, UK. yanickcrow@mac.com.; Laboratory of Neurogenetics and Neuroinflammation, INSERM UMR 1163, Imagine Institute, Université Paris Cité, Paris, France. yanickcrow@mac.com.
items.abstract: The X-linked α-thalassaemia intellectual disability syndrome (ATRX) protein is a chromatin remodeller involved in transcriptional regulation and genome stability. While the importance of ATRX in development and malignancy is well recognised, its role in innate immunity is less well defined. Here we describe three unrelated patients with ATR-X syndrome carrying missense mutations in the ATPase domain of ATRX, each manifesting features of severe inflammation accompanied by persistent upregulation of interferon-stimulated gene expression in whole blood. Studies in patient-derived cells, CRISPR-engineered fibroblasts and neuronal models demonstrate that ATRX loss-of-function mutations drive enhanced type I interferon signalling through a cGAS-dependent mechanism uncoupled from the DNA sensing activity of cGAS. Mechanistically, ATRX deficiency disrupts the chromatin distribution of DAXX and H3.3, with cGAS essential for the changes in nucleosome composition and gene expression mediated by loss of ATRX. Thus, our study highlights a link between ATRX dysfunction and inflammation involving a non-canonical role of cGAS.

items.title: FtmOx1-catalyzed diverse C(sp3)-H oxyfunctionalization enables versatile late-stage diversification of phenethylamines and tetrahydroisoquinolines.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Glyco-drug Research of Zhejiang Province, School of Pharmaceutical Science and Technology, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, 310024, Hangzhou, China. hliu@simm.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, 100049, China. hliu@simm.ac.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Drug Research, Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai, 201203, China. hliu@simm.ac.cn.
items.abstract: The enzymatic late-stage functionalization of C(sp3)-H bonds has emerged as a transformative strategy in medicinal chemistry. Verruculogen synthase (FtmOx1) is known to catalyze the endoperoxidation of its native substrate, fumitremorgin B. Here, we demonstrate the catalytic versatility of FtmOx1 by showing its ability to mediate diverse C(sp3)-H transformations on non-native substrates-phenethylamine and tetrahydroisoquinoline derivatives (1) -including β-hydroxylation, β-ketone formation, dealkylation, and α,β-desaturation. A total of 48 structurally diverse substrates prove suitable for this method, substantially expanding the biocatalytic repertoire of FtmOx1. Mechanistic studies, combined with crystallographic and mutagenesis analyses, reveal the distinct molecular basis for this diverse C(sp3)-H oxyfunctionalization compared to native pathway. Notably, the relative flexibility of the phenethyl and benzyl chains of 1, assisted by specific substitutions that allow the two chains to swing, enables high β-selectivity for hydroxylation and prevents secondary oxidation. This C(sp3)-H activation platform efficiently generates structurally diverse oxyfunctionalized derivatives, including 1,2-amino alcohols (2), 1,2-amino ketones (3), and enamines (4), accelerating lead discovery for modulators of the human relaxin family peptide receptor 4 (RXFP4). Collectively, our work establishes FtmOx1 as a powerful biocatalytic tool, expanding the frontiers of C-H functionalization in drug discovery.

items.title: CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Cell & Systems Biology, University of Toronto, Toronto, ON, Canada. hosung.rhee@utoronto.ca.; Department of Biology, University of Toronto, Mississauga, ON, Canada. hosung.rhee@utoronto.ca.
items.abstract: Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

items.title: Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Ecology, Shenzhen Campus of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangdong, China. mazlong@mail.sysu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Plant invasions are threatening the long-term sustainability of ecosystem functions. Yet, how plant invasions impact the temporal stability of community cover across spatial scales remains poorly understood, hindering effective invasion management. Using the National Ecological Observatory Network dataset, we examine how plant invasions influence multi-scale stability of total community abundance (used total community cover) via altering community functional diversity, as well as growth and dispersal strategies. We find that invasion-associated losses of functional α diversity and functional shifts toward acquisitive strategies, reduce species asynchrony and species stability, respectively. These changes ultimately lead to lower temporal stability at the local scale (α stability). Meanwhile, invasion-associated functional shifts toward acquisitive seed dispersal strategies weaken functional β diversity, which reduces asynchrony community dynamics among local communities (spatial asynchrony). These concurrent declines in α stability and spatial asynchrony collectively destabilize metacommunity-scale stability. Our findings reveal that plant invasions may trigger destabilizing effects across spatial scales, associated with changes in functional diversity as well as growth and dispersal strategies, underscoring the need for a multi-scale invasion management framework focusing on both local diversity and the connectivity among local communities.

items.title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability.
items.last_author_affiliation: Frontiers Science Center for Critical Earth Material Cycling, Nanjing University, Nanjing, P. R. China.; School of Earth Sciences and Engineering, Nanjing University, Nanjing, P. R. China.
items.abstract: Global resource allocation is increasingly shaped by foreign direct investment (FDI) and international trade, yet their combined effects on distribution of critical mineral availability across countries remain poorly quantified. Here, we develop a dual-attribution framework covering 193 countries and 36 territories that attributes primary cobalt availability according to corporate ownership and secondary availability according to international trade. We compare these estimates with a combined baseline scenario using geographic-production and pre-trade perspectives to assess how ownership and trade reshape country-level cobalt availability. Relative to this baseline, total cobalt availability is higher in 63.6% of countries, while 72.7% show a positive composite change when primary and secondary availability are equally weighted. Although these mechanisms do not alter the global total amount of cobalt available, they reduce its concentration across countries. Our findings highlight how FDI and trade reshape cobalt distribution and support resource-governance policies that account for both host and exporting countries.

items.title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Florida, Gainesville, FL, USA. yingyingwu@ufl.edu.
items.abstract: In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

items.title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Materials Chemistry, National Institute of Chemistry, Hajdrihova 19, 1000, Ljubljana, Slovenia. nejc.hodnik@ki.si.; Institute of Metals and Technology, Lepi pot 11, 1000, Ljubljana, Slovenia. nejc.hodnik@ki.si.; University of Nova Gorica, Vipavska 13, 5000, Nova Gorica, Slovenia. nejc.hodnik@ki.si.
items.abstract: Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

items.title: Topological diversity and scintillating dynamics of dipolar surface twists in a van der Waals magnet.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Advanced Materials, College of Smart Materials and Future Energy, Fudan University, Shanghai, P. R. China. rcche@fudan.edu.cn.; Shanghai Key Lab of Molecular Catalysis and Innovative Materials, Fudan University, Shanghai, P. R. China. rcche@fudan.edu.cn.; State Key Laboratory of Coatings for Advanced Equipment, Fudan University, Shanghai, P. R. China. rcche@fudan.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Realizing diverse configurations and dynamics of skyrmionic solitons offers additional topological and dynamical degrees of freedom for energy-efficient, topology-based spintronic devices. Extending these solitons into three dimensions further amplifies their potential, enabling the selective exploitation of surface- or bulk-topological characteristics, a regime that remains largely unexplored. Here, we report high-density dipolar-interaction-stabilized surface twists atop bulk stripe domains under zero magnetic field, through a systematic investigation of three-dimensional domain architectures in the room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2. Unlike conventional skyrmions with integer topological charges, these surface twists carry fractional charges and assemble into diverse composite configurations under field swapping, including aggregates of up to 13 surface twists and ring-like structures. Current-driven experiments uncover two distinct dynamic modes: scintillation, marked by the nucleation, annihilation, and helicity switching of surface twists, and ordered motion of bulk skyrmion strings. These behaviors arise from the interplay between spin-transfer torque and local pinning, establishing surface twists as tunable surface-localized topological states whose dynamics are decoupled from their bulk counterparts, thereby enabling versatile hybrid spintronic functionalities.

items.title: Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Guangdong Provincial Key laboratory of Colorectal and Pelvic Floor Disease, The Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, 510655, China. wangwy63@mail.sysu.edu.cn.; Guangdong Institute of Gastroenterology, The Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, 510655, China. wangwy63@mail.sysu.edu.cn.; Biomedical Innovation Center, The Sixth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, 510655, China. wangwy63@mail.sysu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Identifying targets to enhance tumor immunity is an urgent need. Although nucleic acid sensors play critical roles in promoting tumor immune clearance, their exceptionally low mutation rate in cancers suggests potential unexplored roles in tumor progression. Here, we demonstrate that the RNA sensor melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA5) promotes immune evasion, and its high expression is strongly predictive of poor survival and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) therapy in patients. Targeting MDA5 reshapes the tumor microenvironment, strengthening immune memory responses and enhancing effector CD8⁺ T cell activity in preclinical models in female mice. Mechanistically, MDA5 deficiency triggers unfolded protein response driven immunogenic cell death through induction of damage-associated molecular patterns, leading to enhanced dendritic cell-mediated antigen engulfment and T cell activation. Additionally, MDA5 loss primes the ASK1-JNK/P38 signaling pathway, sensitizing tumor cells to TNF-α/IFN-γ, further amplifying this process. Consequently, targeting MDA5 enhances the efficacy of ICB therapy across multiple cancer types, positioning it as a promising therapeutic target.

items.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance.
items.last_author_affiliation: Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou), Guangzhou, China.; State Key Laboratory of Satellite Ocean Environment Dynamics, Second Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, Hangzhou, China.
items.abstract: Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007-2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3-5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7-6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change.

items.title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage.
items.last_author_affiliation: Centre for Human Brain Health, School of Psychology, University of Birmingham, Birmingham, UK. P.L.Lockwood@bham.ac.uk.; Department of Experimental Psychology, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. P.L.Lockwood@bham.ac.uk.; Wellcome Centre for Integrative Neuroimaging, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. P.L.Lockwood@bham.ac.uk.; Institute for Mental Health, School of Psychology, University of Birmingham, Birmingham, UK. P.L.Lockwood@bham.ac.uk.
items.abstract: Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

items.title: Quantum-sensing-based super-resolution live cell microenvironment imaging.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Experimental Physical Biology, Department of Chemistry, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. jiandong.feng@zju.edu.cn.; College of Optical Science and Engineering, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. jiandong.feng@zju.edu.cn.; Institute of Fundamental and Transdisciplinary Research, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China. jiandong.feng@zju.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Direct monitoring the multifaceted intracellular microenvironment is fundamental for deciphering localized cellular behavior and function. However, performing nanoscale spatiotemporal sensing of the dynamic physiochemical environment within a live cell has remained challenging, mainly limited by the lack of robust, biocompatible method which satisfies the requirements for spatiotemporal resolution, sensitivity, multi-physical sensing capability and long-term viability. Here we present a super-resolution-based quantum biosensing approach, namely Super-resolution Multi-physical field Imaging with Deconvolution, implemented in our custom-built setup which integrates nitrogen vacancy center-based quantum sensing with structured illumination microscopy. This enables quantitative, super-resolved, and long-term tracking of intracellular physical fields, featuring spatial resolution of 136 nm, temporal resolution of 150 ms, and field of view of 180×180 μm2. We further perform super-resolution multimodal imaging in a live cell, revealing the spatially heterogeneous reactive oxygen species dynamics under external stimulation. Our work enables the dynamic assessment of localized physiochemical dynamics under super-resolution quantum biosensing.

items.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability.
items.last_author_affiliation: Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke), Helsinki, Finland. bartosz.adamczyk@luke.fi.
items.abstract: Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

items.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Engineering Research Center of Advanced Rare Earth Materials, Department of Chemistry, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. wangxun@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn.; Engineering Research Center of Advanced Rare Earth Materials, Department of Chemistry, Institute of Tsinghua University (Hebei), Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. wangxun@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Piezoelectric electronic skin (PE-skin) offers a significant advantage in detecting minute forces, making it highly promising for human-computer interaction in health management and medical rehabilitation. However, PE-skin often faces challenges in real-time, wireless transmission of sensing data, which can compromise both data accuracy and user comfort. Here, we report the synthesis of an inorganic piezoelectric polyoxometalate-based subnanowire, ZnBiPMo12, which possesses intrinsic flexibility and chirality, a piezoelectric coefficient of 24.9 pC/N, and notable ferroelectricity. Leveraging its piezoelectric response, ZnBiPMo12-based PE-skin (1) demonstrates high elasticity and sensitivity to tiny pressures in the range of 0.045-0.319 N. Building on this, a wireless, wearable bioelectronic (WBE) device (1A) is fabricated through multi-level assembly, enabling non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals, including subtle muscle contractions, blinking, breathing, and all-day heart rate. By integrating a machine learning system, a 1-based facial-computer interface (1B) can accurately recognize nine emotional expressions and twelve spoken words. This work not only introduces a typical inorganic piezoelectric material with intrinsic flexibility but also demonstrates scalable manufacturing from subnanomaterials to wireless WBEs, paving the way for non-invasive, multimodal monitoring of human physiological signals and advanced human-computer interaction.

items.title: A cryptic binding pocket regulates the metal-dependent activity of Cas9.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of California Los Angeles, Los Angeles, CA, USA. gpalermo@ucla.edu.
items.abstract: Cas9 is a metal-dependent nuclease used for genome editing across diverse cells and organisms exhibiting distinct ionic environments, yet how metal ions regulate its catalytic function, and consequently its editing efficiency remains unclear. Here, molecular simulations, Markov state models, and mixed quantum-classical approaches reveal that divalent metals promote activation of the catalytic HNH domain through formation of a divalent metal-binding pocket (DBP) at the HNH-RuvC interface. This cryptic pocket emerges dynamically during HNH activation and is supported by NMR measurements revealing metal-dependent structural perturbations within the HNH-L2 region. Mutations targeting the DBP disrupt HNH activation and impair the coupled catalytic activity of both nucleases, identifying the pocket as a key regulator of Cas9's metal-dependent activity. Together with quantum-classical simulations revealing distinct catalytic behaviours among divalent metals, these findings uncover an ion-dependent regulatory mechanism in Cas9 with insights for genome editing across diverse biological environments.

items.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Quantitative Synthetic Biology, Center for Synthetic Biochemistry, Shenzhen Institute of Synthetic Biology, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shenzhen, China. xz.luo@siat.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)-an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning-directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7-78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products.

items.title: CROSS: A cross-species chromosome substitution platform for dissecting chromosome architecture and activity.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Organ Regeneration and Reconstruction, Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. liwei@ioz.ac.cn.; Beijing Institute for Stem Cell and Regenerative Medicine, Beijing, China. liwei@ioz.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. liwei@ioz.ac.cn.
items.abstract: The functional integrity of a mammalian chromosome depends on its long-term co-evolution with species-specific nuclear environment. How chromosomes co-adapt with their native environment to define 3D architecture and transcription remains unclear, largely due to a lack of experimental models that dissect this co-evolution. Here, we report cross-species chromosome substitution (CROSS), a method enabling stable, scarless replacement of host chromosomes with divergent orthologs. We integrate microcell-mediated chromosome transfer with CRISPR/Cas9 to import the intact 152-Mb rat X chromosome into male mouse embryonic stem cells, and subsequently replace the mouse X chromosome, maintaining its stability and integrity. Rat-specific LINE1 and RatSatRep2 repeats recruit mouse SETDB1 inefficiently, causing local H3K9me3 loss. This triggers 3D remodeling, characterized by de novo topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries that aberrantly activate adjacent genes, including Rhox5, impairing differentiation. We provide a platform for dissecting sequence and epigenome cooperation in chromosome regulation, and evaluating fidelity of large-scale heterologous DNA.

items.title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biological Sciences, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. katehong@andrew.cmu.edu.; Neuroscience Institute, Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, PA, USA. katehong@andrew.cmu.edu.
items.abstract: Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

items.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering, Peking University, Beijing, China. yhzhang@pku.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is a crucial urban source of HOx radicals, promoting surface ozone (O3) and secondary fine particle (PM2.5) formation, yet its long-term evolution and air-quality impacts remain poorly constrained. Here, using a deep neural network established on worldwide field campaigns, we reconstruct global surface HONO distributions. Typical megacities exhibited contrasting trends in 2005-2021, marked by a sharp decline in Beijing (-47.4% in 2013-2021), an increase in Delhi (+10.0% in 2005-2018), and slight decreases in London, New York and Los Angeles. These HONO changes are identified as major driver of O3 and particulate nitrate variations, outweighing contributions of conventional NOx and volatile organic compounds abatement in Beijing and Delhi, while showing comparable impacts in the remaining cities. A fused data-driven framework further uncovers regime-dependent HONO reduction strategies, prioritizing NOx control in summer and co-reduction of NOx, PM2.5 and direct combustion emissions in winter, to accelerate O3 and PM2.5 joint mitigation.

items.title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Neuroscience, Washington University in St. Louis Medical School, St Louis, MO, USA. linda.richards@wustl.edu.; The University of Queensland, Queensland Brain Institute, Brisbane, Australia. linda.richards@wustl.edu.
items.abstract: The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency.

items.title: Reconstruction of PAM-interacting domains to broad PAM compatibility.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Animal Embryo Engineering, College of Animal Science, State Key Laboratory for Diagnosis and Treatment of Severe Zoonotic Infectious Diseases, The First Hospital of Jilin University, Changchun, 130062, China. lizj_1998@jlu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirement limits CRISPR-Cas9 targetability. Here, we develop REPAM, an ancestral sequence reconstruction-based strategy that re-engineers PAM-interacting domains to expand PAM recognition. REPAM broadens the PAM specificities of Nme1Cas9 and Nme2Cas9 from N4GATT/N4CC to N4CNH, while additional mutations further extend Nme2Cas9 recognition to N4VHH. Applied to SpaCas9, REPAM expands PAM compatibility from NNGYRA to NNHH, increasing theoretical target coverage by approximately 36-fold. The engineered SpaCas9 achieves up to 76.6% editing efficiency in HEK293T cells, outperforming SpRY. Corresponding base editors efficiently generate protective variants and precise splice-site mutations, highlighting REPAM as a versatile platform for CRISPR engineering.

items.title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures.
items.last_author_affiliation: Engineering Research Center of Advanced Rare Earth Materials, Department of Chemistry, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. wangxun@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn.; Research Center for Sub-Nanometer Scale Materials Chemistry, Institute of Tsinghua University Hebei, Hebei, China. wangxun@mail.tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm-2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm-2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction.

items.title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of California, Davis, Davis, CA, USA. yxxue@ucdavis.edu.
items.abstract: Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μm thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.
