Here we introduce the semiparametric pairwise discordance regression, a unified framework for longitudinal data that directly models pairwise contrasts to simultaneously characterize mean trajectories, between-subject heterogeneity, and within-subject temporal variability. By targeting pairwise discordances rather than latent variance components, the proposed approach enables robust inference without specifying full parametric distributions for latent components or error terms, provided the specified conditional moment restrictions hold. Pair-level covariate encodings further accommodate flexible covariate structures and allow variability parameters to be interpreted through pairwise contrasts or dissimilarities. Estimation and inference are carried out via (weighted) U-statistic-based generalized estimating equations (UGEE) with a valid sandwich variance estimator, and we extend the fitting procedure to accommodate missing-at-random dropout. We establish the asymptotic distributions of the resulting estimators under mild regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate reliable finite-sample performance in the settings considered, including non-Gaussian errors and misspecified working correlation structures, whereas likelihood-based parametric fits can be sensitive to distributional assumptions or numerically unstable. An application to longitudinal blood pressure during pregnancy illustrates the framework on real data.

items.title: Arrest-associated transcriptional programmes outweigh apoptosis-associated programmes in treatment-naive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Background: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is driven by mutant KRAS, and RAS inhibitors now extend survival in previously treated metastatic disease. Whether treatment shrinks a tumour or only halts its growth depends partly on whether cancer cells die or stop dividing, yet how untreated PDAC cells are balanced between these programmes is unknown. Aims: We aimed to characterise the balance between apoptosis-associated and arrest-associated transcriptional programmes in treatment-naive PDAC and to examine their relationships with tumour subtype, TGM2 expression, tissue organisation, survival and drug sensitivity. Methods and results: We scored 52,999 malignant cells from 18 untreated patients in the Hwang atlas using a transcriptional contrast between genes associated with apoptosis and genes associated with resistance to apoptosis or cell-cycle arrest. In every patient the contrast was shifted toward the arrest-associated side: using equality between the two sides as the dividing threshold, 86.3% of cells with an informative score fell on that side, although the proportion depends on the threshold chosen. The shift recurred in the independent Steele atlas (median 71.6% per sample, range 37.1% to 90.8%). In the discovery cohort, tumours with higher basal-like scores had fewer arrest-side cells, and TGM2 expression was modestly higher on the arrest-associated side in both cohorts. The contrast did not track cell-line drug sensitivity or survival in bulk tumours. Conclusion: Untreated PDAC cells show a reproducible transcriptional bias toward anti-apoptotic and cell-cycle-arrest programmes. Whether this bias predicts cellular responses to treatment remains to be tested.

items.title: Hyperactivity preferentially disrupts scotopic retinal circuits in the early stages of diabetic retinopathy
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of blindness worldwide. In this disease, visual impairments result from neurovascular dysfunction in the retina. However, the specific retinal circuits and the mechanisms underlying their dysfunction remain unclear. Here, in mouse models of diabetes, we evaluated scotopic (night vision) and photopic (day vision) retinal circuit function in the early stages of the disease. Using a combination of immunohistochemical, behavioral and electrophysiological techniques, we show that vision impairments early in the disease are not associated with widespread degeneration of the retinal circuitry but with abnormalities localized to scotopic circuits. Specifically, we observed swelling of axon terminals in rod but not cone bipolar cells. Importantly, these abnormalities were closely linked with bipolar cell activity, as rod bipolar cells showed higher intrinsic activity than cone bipolar cells, and inducing hyperactivity in control retinas was sufficient to recapitulate the pathology in diabetic rod bipolar cells. Further, the swollen rod bipolar cell terminals exhibited an increase in oxidative stress, consistent with cellular dysfunction. In line with this notion, electrophysiological measurements demonstrated that the contrast sensitivity of retinal ganglion cells was preferentially attenuated under scotopic conditions. Finally, behavioral experiments showed that visual sensitivity under scotopic conditions was affected earlier in disease progression compared to photopic conditions. Together, these findings reveal that scotopic circuits are preferentially affected in the early stages of diabetic retinopathy and that hyperactivity is sufficient to drive these abnormalities.

items.title: A biomimetic deep encoder for auditory restoration by cortical stimulation
items.abstract: Cochlear and auditory brainstem implants are the primary treatments for profound deafness. However, the inherently low resolution of electrical stimulation used by these devices limits information transfer to a small number of independent stimulation channels and results in perceptual difficulties. An alternative approach is to target the auditory cortex, a brain region large enough to accommodate hundreds of stimulation channels and whose stimulation evokes sound percepts. Although modern brain interfaces offer large channel counts and spatial resolution, developing encoding algorithms capable of accurately transmitting interpretable sound information remains challenging. Here we introduce Braincodec, a deep network that optimizes both sound information transmission and the alignment of stimulation patterns with the spatial, temporal, and high-level properties of the auditory cortex neural code. Braincodec operates online and requires only a few hundred channels to transmit sufficient information for the reconstruction of natural sounds with high fidelity, a performance inaccessible to cochlear implant encoders. Moreover, mice equipped with a Braincodec-driven auditory cortical prosthesis matched the accuracy of non-implanted mice in discriminating real sounds. Braincodec therefore enables the development of high-throughput cortical neuroprosthetics with the potential to overcome the limitations of current auditory implants and provides a generic framework applicable to other sensory modalities.

items.title: CD300f is required for efficient lipid handling during cuprizone-induced demyelination
items.abstract: Microglia play a crucial role in central nervous system homeostasis and response to demyelination, yet the mechanisms that coordinate the sensing and processing of myelin-derived lipids remain poorly understood. CD300f is a lipid-sensing innate immune receptor expressed by myeloid cells that has been implicated in tissue damage sensing, phagocytosis, and lipid metabolism. Here, we investigated the role of CD300f in the cuprizone-induced demyelination model. Using CD300f-deficient mice, we demonstrate exacerbated demyelination, increased lipid droplet accumulation, impaired microglial responses, and reduced remyelination accompanied by motor coordination deficits. Bulk RNA sequencing of the corpus callosum at the peak of demyelination revealed enrichment of homeostatic, disease-associated (DAM), and foamy microglial signatures, together with increased expression of genes involved in lysosomal function, phagocytosis, inflammation, and lipid metabolism. Notably, these transcriptional changes were associated with marked lipid droplet accumulation in microglia and enrichment of microglial states previously linked to chronic demyelinating lesions. These findings suggest that CD300f is required for efficient handling of myelin-derived lipids and for microglial metabolic adaptation during demyelination. Our study identifies CD300f as a critical regulator of microglial function and lipid homeostasis and highlights this receptor as a potential therapeutic target in demyelinating diseases.

items.title: Active eye modeling: a tool for estimating retinal image quality across the visual field in everyday life
items.abstract: Purpose: The "visual diet," the totality of visual experience, shapes retinal image formation and thereby refractive development, but measuring retinal image statistics during everyday behavior is challenging. Limits in mobile eye tracking, egocentric video, and full-field optical measurement leave gaps in our understanding of how environmental and behavioral factors shape image quality across the retina. Methods: We introduce active eye modeling, a computational platform combining optically validated, wide-field, accommodating eye models (Hastings et al. 2024) with realistic three-dimensional virtual environments and gaze behavior derived from human data. This approach enables systematic estimation of retinal blur across the visual field under parametrically controlled conditions, including varying viewing distances, ambient light levels, and environmental depth structure. Inputs may be simulated and/or drawn from real-world measurements: scene depth, video, and gaze/pupil recordings. Results: During simulated far work, peripheral image quality is depth-tolerant, owing to wide depth-of-field from off-axis aberrations. Near work under dim indoor lighting substantially increases peripheral blur, reducing contrast at mid and high spatial frequencies. This contrast reduction is comparable in magnitude to a moderate diffusing filter (Bangerter 0.4 strength) that affects eye growth when imposed experimentally in animal models. A consistency check with eye-tracked virtual driving confirms peripheral depth-tolerance during far work. Conclusions: Active eye modeling provides a flexible framework for investigating how visual experience shapes the retinal image, relevant to refractive development, display and lens design, and peripheral vision. Applied to common visual behaviors, the platform identifies optical conditions during indoor near work that warrant empirical investigation, complementing measurement-based approaches.

items.title: Clinical relevance of diffusion tensor imaging-based parameters estimated with deep learning: the effect of model retraining
items.abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based approaches have recently become powerful tools for characterizing microstructural properties of brain tissue from diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. These techniques enable depicting microstructural features with significantly reduced acquisition schemes while preserving relatively high image-quality metrics compared with non-DL-based approaches. Learning-based methods have increasingly been applied to diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and more advanced multi-compartmental biophysical models, with the potential to facilitate multiparameter analyses of brain microstructure in clinical settings. However, independently trained DL models-while maintaining image-quality properties-do not appear to preserve the statistical properties of groupwise analyses across independently trained models. In this study, we systematically evaluate the statistical properties of DL-based DTI parameters across independently trained neural networks under the same architecture to preserve group-level effects in bipolar disorder. We examine the impact of model retraining and its dependence on reducing the number of gradient directions compared with the nonlinear least-squares (NLLS) procedure. Our results show that initializing model weights randomly from a uniform distribution, while keeping the network architecture and training hyperparameters the identical in the experiment, leads to significant variation in the statistical properties of DTI measures inferred from independently trained models. The analyses showed that the true positive rate in groupwise analysis using the DL-based DTI parameters ranges from 0\% to 100\% compared with the NLLS-based analysis. As the number of gradient directions increased, the NLLS procedure yielded more stable groupwise statistical results, whereas independently trained DL models showed greater variability despite similar image-quality agreement with reference maps. The results indicate that the DTI maps retrieved from a single trained network should be treated with great caution before drawing clinical conclusions.

items.title: Apparent sequential effects due to trial-to-trial fluctuations in decision criterion
items.abstract: Decision making is shaped by sequential effects, whereby preceding stimuli and responses influence current decisions. Computational models typically explain these effects by assuming that decision parameters are causally updated as a function of experimental history. Here, we challenge this assumption by showing that several hallmark sequential effects can instead emerge from slow fluctuations in the decision criterion. Using simulations based on Signal Detection Theory (SDT), we demonstrate that trial-to-trial criterion fluctuations, independent of experimental history, generate three commonly observed sequential effects: the repulsive effect of the previous stimulus (i.e., a tendency to alternate), the influence of previous response (i.e., choice history bias), and the modulation of choice history bias by previous confidence. To disentangle causal effects from effects driven by criterion fluctuations, we used the Hierarchical Model for Fluctuations in Criterion (hMFC), which simultaneously estimates both processes. Applying hMFC to 14 empirical datasets revealed that the repulsive effect of the previous stimulus was fully explained by criterion fluctuations. Accounting for criterion fluctuations also substantially altered choice history bias estimates: attractive biases disappeared in all four affected datasets, while three datasets revealed a previously masked tendency to alternate and two showed stronger alternation. In contrast, the modulation of choice history bias by previous confidence was largely unaffected by concurrent estimation of criterion fluctuations. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that criterion fluctuations account for a substantial portion of sequential effects and highlight the importance of explicitly modeling them to avoid confounded interpretations of behavioral and neuroimaging data.

items.title: Individual differences reveal shared computational structure in perceptual decision-making
items.abstract: To discover computational mechanisms of cognition, models typically specify a fixed psychological architecture, treating individual differences as variations within a predefined parameterization. Here, we take a different approach by using the population structure of individual differences to directly drive model discovery. We develop a low-rank neural network that uses this `population geometry' to learn shared computational components and participant-specific weights from trial-level choices, allowing cross-subject variation to constrain the model's architecture. Applied to perceptual decision-making in the Bernoulli Clicks Task across primary and replication datasets, out-of-sample prediction reveals a six-dimensional representation for individual differences: two continuous dimensions of temporal evidence weighting and two of choice-outcome history dependence, alongside participant-specific side bias and signal-to-noise ratio. This low-dimensional organization replicated in an independent dataset. Together, these findings reveal that seemingly disparate decision heuristics reflect different weightings over a small set of shared computational components, and establish a principled methodology for using behavioral variability to discover the mechanistic architecture of cognition.

items.title: Dopamine synthesis capacity and tau pathology differentially modulate rest-to-task functional network dynamics
items.abstract: Optimal cognition relies on large-scale functional brain networks which balance segregation at rest with selective integration during task performance. In aging, these network dynamics are altered. We examined two prominent features of brain aging: dysregulated dopamine function and Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related pathology to examine impacts on brain network dynamics. Young adults and cognitively unimpaired older adults completed resting-state and task-based fMRI and PET imaging of dopamine synthesis capacity ([18F]fluoro-m-L-tyrosine). Older adults were classified as {beta}-amyloid negative/positive using [11C]Pittsburgh Compound-B PET(PiB- or PiB+) and underwent tau-PET scanning ([18F]flortaucipir). Greater rest-to-task network stability and task-related network segregation were associated with better subsequent memory. Compared to young adults, PiB+ older adults showed reduced network stability and both PiB+ and PiB- older adults showed reduced segregation during rest. Higher ventral striatal dopamine synthesis capacity was associated with greater stability within associative networks in young adults, but this relationship was attenuated in older adults and absent in PiB+ participants. In PiB+ older adults, higher tau burden was associated with a task-induced collapse of network segregation across large-scale networks. These findings reveal dissociable influences of dopamine and tau on rest-to-task network organization, highlighting the value of integrating neuromodulatory and pathological markers in aging research.

items.title: Circuit and cell-type mechanisms of the spectrolaminar motif of cortical oscillations
items.abstract: Oscillations are a key feature of cortical activity, coordinating spike timing across areas, layers, and cell types. Recent work suggests these rhythms follow a stereotyped organization across cortical depth, the spectrolaminar (SL) motif, with higher-frequency gamma prominent in superficial layers and lower-frequency alpha/beta in deep layers, yet the mechanisms generating it remain poorly understood. Using a bio-realistic model of mouse primary visual cortex, we reproduced the SL motif and found it preserved across diverse visual stimuli. Systematic cell-type- and layer-resolved perturbations showed that the alpha/beta component was intrinsic to every layer, whereas the 50-80 Hz gamma component was predominantly generated within layer 4 (L4) and propagated network-wide through inter-laminar connections. Pvalb interneurons were the principal regulators of gamma, Sst cells shaped low-frequency power, and Vip cells controlled oscillation magnitude. The temporal properties of L4 Pvalb-to-excitatory synapses were especially influential in generating the SL motif. These models and simulation results thus offer a plausible description of circuit mechanisms underlying cortical oscillations and the SL motif and are publicly available to facilitate further studies.

items.title: Reinforcement sculpts synaptic ensembles for operant dendritic control
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning requires the selective modification of synapses that contribute to outcome-relevant neural activity, yet the principles underlying these selective modifications remain unclear. Here we combined longitudinal two-photon imaging of identified dendritic spines with a closed-loop optical brain-machine interface (BMI), in which activity from selected apical dendrites of layer 5 motor-cortical neurons controlled an auditory cursor, with target acquisition triggering optogenetic reinforcement. Mice learned to reliably generate the specific dendritic activity that leads to reinforcement. Learning was accompanied by selective strengthening and weakening of individual spines on reinforced dendrites. At individual synapses, the direction of plasticity depended on both the timing of activity relative to reinforced dendritic events and the pre-existing temporal organization of that activity. Furthermore, plasticity was enriched in small task-relevant synaptic groups: spines in synergistic groups were preferentially strengthened, whereas those in antagonistic groups were preferentially weakened. These changes were accompanied by the emergence of increasingly reproducible, selectively recruited, and temporally focused synaptic ensembles, and the incorporation of newly formed spines into these ensembles. Finally, blocking striatal dopamine receptor signaling impaired BMI learning and cortical synaptic reorganization of target dendrites, demonstrating a role for striatal reinforcement in cortical plasticity. Together, these findings reveal how reinforcement of specific dendritic activity sculpts synaptic ensembles that support learned operant dendritic control.

items.title: A mammalian fibroblast zoo reveals barriers to cross-species virus replication and differential regulation of antiviral immunity
items.abstract: Virus zoonosis represents a continual threat to humans. Viruses emerge in humans directly or indirectly through interactions with mammals. However, our understanding of virus-host susceptibility across the diversity of mammals is limited and experimental model systems are restricted to a very small set of model organisms. Mammals are highly diverse and different habitats, lifestyles, diets, and exposures to different pathogens have driven substantial genetic diversity. We generated a library of primary fibroblasts across 86 mammalian species and used these cells to build an atlas of virus-host susceptibility across a panel of arboviruses that infect diverse mammals including humans. Perturbing the innate immune system revealed some virus-host pairs where restriction is controlled by the immune system and others where there is an incompatibility with host factors. Transcriptomic profiling of the library in response to virus sensing mimicked by poly(I:C) or antiviral signaling with type I interferon reveals a core set of conserved genes that respond as well as substantial species- and order-specific responses. Together these data provide a comparative atlas of innate immune responses across mammals and offer a window into how these systems have evolved across animals.

items.title: Monounsaturated fatty acid depletion is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis surveilled to activate p38 MAPK innate immunity
items.abstract: Pathogen infection profoundly remodels host metabolism. Whether hosts sense specific pathogen-induced metabolic changes to identify microbial infection is not known. Here, we find that depletion the monounsaturated fatty acid oleate is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis, specifically surveilled by the nematode C. elegans to identify active infection with a bacterial pathogen. We previously demonstrated that the enzymatic TIR (Toll/interleukin-1 receptor/resistance)-domain containing protein, TIR-1/SARM1, the key upstream activator of p38 MAPK PMK-1 immunity, is a guard protein in an effector-triggered immune response, positioned specifically on the surface of lysosome-related organelles to sense the toxic effects of bacterial infection. Here, we show that acute loss of oleate in intestinal cells during bacterial infection causes lysosome-related organelles to collapse, which induces the aggregation and activation of TIR-1/SARM1. Further, we find that oleate deficiency is a host vulnerability that concomitantly activates the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) KGB-1 nutrient sensing pathway, an adaptive response that promotes expression of TIR-1/SARM1 on lysosome-related organelles and is required for survival during infection. These data establish a mechanistic connection between fatty acid nutrition and innate immune regulation, and reveal that specific changes in host metabolism are surveilled to identify pathogen attack.

items.title: Stoichiometric Encoding of Amplification Kinetics Enables High-Level Multiplexing in Single-Channel TaqMan Real-Time PCR
items.corresponding_institution: Imperial College London; Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
items.abstract: Multiplexing in TaqMan real-time PCR (qPCR) is limited to four-six targets per reaction by fluorophore spectral overlap. Amplification curve analysis (ACA) can discriminate several targets within one fluorescence channel from amplification curves (AC) kinetic features, but has been confined mainly to digital qPCR (dqPCR) and is sensitive to domain shifts between instruments and specimen types. Here, we co-design biochemical encoding of target-specific information into ACs and their computational decoding to achieve single-channel 8-plex TaqMan qPCR on a standard thermocycler. Using asymmetric PCR, we show that forward primer, reverse primer and probe concentrations act as a programmable encoding mechanism, generating a 27-condition design space of reproducible non-canonical ACs, conserved from digital to bulk qPCR. Applying this stoichiometric encoding to an 8-plex central nervous system pathogens panel increased inter-target separability, raising the mean silhouette score from 0.329 to 0.711. To decode ACs without labelled target-domain bulk qPCR data, we pretrained a transformer encoder by self-supervised learning on more than 170,000 unlabelled dqPCR curves and aligned source and target domains using conditional domain adversarial training. On contrived clinical specimens, the framework classified a canonical 7-plex respiratory virus panel with 83.6% accuracy (versus 67.7% for a supervised baseline) and the encoded 8-plex panel with 89.8% accuracy. Furthermore, stoichiometric encoding enabled resolution of double- and triple-target co-amplification events with 98.7% accuracy in controlled dqPCR experiments. This approach expands the information capacity of existing qPCR instrumentation without new hardware, fluorophores or oligonucleotides, offering a low-cost route to syndromic molecular diagnostics.

items.title: Global repression of mesenchymal genes in epithelial cells by the histone demethylase LSD1
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Structural and Chemical Biology and Division of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of Leicester, Leicester, LE1 7RH
items.abstract: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is an essential process in development, tissue repair, and tumour metastasis, and is triggered by SNAI, ZEB and TWIST transcription factors, that recruit lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) to repress epithelial genes such as E-cadherin. In mesenchymal cells, LSD1 inhibition restores E-cadherin expression and reduces migration and invasion, consistent with LSD1 inhibition reverting EMT, and offering a therapeutic modality for EMT-associated disease. Recent data, however, suggest context-dependent roles for LSD1, as its inhibition in epithelial cells increases mesenchymal marker expression, potentially promoting EMT. To investigate this discrepancy, we mapped genome-wide binding of LSD1 in HCT116 epithelial cells and used rapid degron-mediated ablation of endogenous LSD1 to measure changes in nascent and steady-state transcription and chromatin accessibility. In epithelial cells, LSD1 binds constitutively-accessible, primed mesenchymal promoters. These are rapidly derepressed after LSD1 ablation, with activation of SNAI2 and ZEB1, which repress epithelial hallmarks such as E-cadherin. Re-introduction of LSD1 downregulates SNAI2 and ZEB1 but, surprisingly, further represses E-cadherin, indicating sustained loss of epithelial characteristics. Collectively, our results show that LSD1 maintains epithelial identity by repressing mesenchymal genes, questioning the therapeutic utility of LSD1 inhibition for EMT control.

items.title: Stepwise assembly and mechanical stability of nsP3 Helical Scaffolds in Chikungunya Virus
items.abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4. In this study, we focused on nsP3, which comprises three distinct domains: the alphavirus unique domain (AUD), the long and intrinsically disordered hypervariable domain (HVD), and the enzymatic macrodomain (MD). Notably, nsP3 assembles into helicoidal macrostructures, termed helical scaffolds (HSs), which are components of the CHIKV replication complex and are involved in the formation of macromolecular traps in the cytoplasm of the infected cell called Alphagranules (AGs). HSs form tubular helical scaffolds assembled through the AUD, with the MD and HVD flexibly deployed to the scaffold exterior. Despite their functional importance, the mechanisms governing HS formation remain poorly understood. Using High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy (HS-AFM) and Electron Microscopy (EM) we achieved new findings on the structure, mechanics and assembly of these macrostructures. Our results show the nsP3 monomers follow intermediate steps before completing the assembly into full helical scaffolds, with each nsP3 domain contributing differently to this process. The macrodomain (MD) provides mechanical stability, yet it fractures under tens of piconewtons of force. This rigidity acts as a mechanical regulator that constrains the position of the HVD, which in turn mediates interactions with host factors and neighboring HSs. Through this interplay, nsP3 achieves both structural cohesion and functional adaptability, promoting the higher-order organization of HSs into honeycomb-like networks.

items.title: Optogenetic induction of TAD boundary pairing promotes gene activity
items.abstract: The genome folds inside the nucleus into distinct structures across multiple levels of organization. Topologically associating domains (TADs) are a ubiquitous architectural feature of genomes delineated by boundaries enriched in the CTCF protein and the cohesin complex. TADs are dynamic structures as their boundaries undergo continuous, short-lived pairing events. Whether the structural integrity of TADs contributes to regulation of the genes within the TAD is unclear. To directly test the structure-function relationship of TADs, we have developed OptoTet, an optogenetic tool to rapidly and directly manipulate chromatin contacts in a controlled fashion using light without the need for mutation or protein depletion. Using the TADs containing the ERRFI1 or MYC gene as model systems, we show that OptoTet promotes TAD boundary looping. When applied to probing the structure-function relationship of TADs, light-induced pairing of TAD boundaries promoted transcriptional activity of ERRFI1 as indicated by increased gene bursting. In contrast, bursting of MYC was insensitive to boundary pairing. Enhanced TAD boundary pairing also partially rescued the effect of depletion of cohesin components on ERRF1 but not on MYC. Our results suggest that TADs boundary pairing dynamics can contribute to gene regulation in a gene-specific manner.

items.title: Persistent and recyclable myosin II minifilaments drive cortical contractility in the early C. elegans embryo
items.abstract: Non-muscle myosin II is a key regulator of cell and tissue morphogenesis, yet the cortical dynamics of myosin minifilaments in vivo remain poorly understood. Here, we combine SIM-TIRF and single-molecule TIRF microscopy to characterize the structure and dynamics of myosin minifilaments in an early developing embryo. High-temporal-resolution SIM-TIRF imaging revealed diverse minifilament behaviors, including partition-like events, long-range alignment of multiple minifilaments into collective structures we called proto-stress fibers, partial unbinding, and sequential unbinding and rebinding to the cortex. Photoconversion experiments showed that minifilaments persist as intact units after cortical unbinding, diffuse through the cytoplasm, and can be recycled over long distances rather than disassembling upon detachment. Despite these dynamic behaviors, minifilaments are predominantly stationary when bound to actin. Numerical simulations demonstrated that this static behavior is essential to sustain cortical stress within a continuously remodeling actin network. Using myosin motor-domain mutants, we further investigated the contribution of motor activity to these behaviors. Together, our results reveal that myosin minifilaments can persist as stable units while cycling between the cortex and cytoplasm, and that their predominantly static behavior when bound to actin enables sustained force generation in a continuously renewing cortical network. These findings provide new insights into myosin organization, recycling, and force generation during early embryonic development.

items.title: Multicellular Perturb-seq Reveals Lineage-Specific Transcriptional Control During Human Cardiac Organoid Development
items.abstract: Heart development requires the coordinated differentiation of multiple cell lineages, including cardiomyocytes (CMs) and endothelial cells (ECs). Transcription factors (TFs) orchestrate lineage specification, morphogenesis, and maturation, yet how cardiac and vascular TFs shape multicellular organization and their interactions remain poorly understood. Many TFs exhibit pleiotropic and stage-dependent effects across cardiac lineages, particularly in cardiac progenitor cells, suggesting the presence of shared regulatory networks that synchronize cardiac and vascular programs during development and in response to stress. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) differentiated cardiac organoid provides a physiologically relevant 3D model to study these multicellular interactions, enabling simultaneous differentiation of ECs and CMs within a human genetic context. When combined with CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) based Perturb-seq, this system allows systematic, high-throughput dissection of TF-driven regulatory programs at single-cell resolution. In this study, we investigated how cardiac and vascular TFs coordinate lineage commitment and the cross-lineage signaling in human cardiovascular differentiation.

items.title: A multipotent mouse distal airway secretory cell population that contributes to both airway and alveolar regeneration
items.abstract: The distal airway is a spatially distinct compartment whose contribution to lung repair remains poorly defined. We have identified an epithelial cell population enriched in the most distal airways of the mouse lung, that is not present in the alveolar epithelium. Using lineage tracing tools based on Cldn10 expression which marks these cells, we show that the Cldn10+ lineage in homeostatic conditions marks distal airway secretory cells in a highly specific manner, with only a small contribution to multi-ciliated cells and no contribution towards the basal stem cell lineage. Remarkably, these Cldn10+ distal secretory cells proliferate and display a high degree of multi-potency across the lung epithelial axis after injury, generating basal cells, multi-ciliated cells, and alveolar epithelium. In severely remodeled regions after injury, we show that Cldn10 lineage-labeled cells migrate from the airways and differentiate into alveolar epithelial cells. These findings establish the Cldn10 lineage that defines a distal airway secretory facultative progenitor with both intrapulmonary airway and alveolar potential, providing a genetic system for studying distal lung repair.

items.title: Deep transcriptomic analysis of molecular mediators of complex traits in heterogeneous stock (HS) rats
items.corresponding_institution: University of California San Diego, La Jolla, CA
items.abstract: Rats are a powerful model organism for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of physiological and behavioral traits. Heterogeneous Stock (HS) rats, which were created by intercrossing 8 inbred rat strains, are heavily used for this purpose because of their genetic diversity and accumulated recombinations due to over 100 generations of outbreeding, which improves mapping precision. However, functional genomics resources for post-GWAS interpretation of genomic findings have been limited. We processed 3,160 RNA-seq samples, 1,932 of which were previously unpublished, from 13 tissues as part of RatGTEx. We used Pantry to quantify six modalities of transcriptome regulation (expression, isoform ratio, intron excision ratio, alternative transcription start site (TSS), alternative poly(A), and RNA stability) in each sample, which allowed us to identify 144,876 independent quantitative trait loci (QTL) for 22,599 genes. We performed a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) with 19,796 unique genes across tissues and transcriptional modalities and 308 traits collected from 14 studies using FUSION, which identified 7,473 significant gene-trait associations. This work presents a significant expansion of the RatGTEx resource in terms of samples, modes of transcriptome regulation, and genetic analyses. Our findings provide molecular evidence for the involvement of specific genes in mediating GWAS signals through a range of transcriptome regulatory mechanisms. These gene-to-phenotype relationships can be easily applied to genetic analyses in humans and other species. Further experiments can use this evidence to confirm these molecular mediators and target them for the treatment of behavioral and physiological traits and disorders. To facilitate use of these results, we have updated results on RatGTEx.org and provided a new interactive TWAS web portal (twas.ratgtex.org).

items.title: Genomic and Epigenomic Relationships Capture Different Patterns of Genotype-by-Environment Interaction in Grapevine Clones
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Plant Breeding, Hochschule Geisenheim University, Geisenheim, Germany
items.abstract: Genotype-by-environment interaction (GEI) challenges selection in clonally propagated perennial crops by reducing the consistency of clone performance across years. In perennial crops, both genetic and epigenetic variation are likely to contribute to complex trait variation among clones. However, the extent to which each molecular source contribute to GEI remains poorly understood. Here, we used UMR-seq, an assay that recovers SNPs and unmethylated-region (UMR; DNA methylation) profiles from a single library, to generate paired genomic and epigenomic profiles for 206 Riesling (Vitis vinifera L.) clones phenotyped for yield and juice quality traits across nine growing seasons. We then partitioned the contribution of each omic layer to clonal variation and GEI, and examined the genomic distribution of their effects. In models without explicit GEI, environmental and residual effects were the largest source of phenotypic variance and the clonal main effect was modest. Genomic relationships accounted for most of the clonal variance in four of five traits, and adding an epigenomic relationship matrix (ERM) to the genomic relationship matrix (GRM) had little effect. In contrast, when GEI effects were modelled using factor-analytic covariance structures, the epigenomic layer captured a substantial proportion of GEI variance and exceeded the genomic contribution in four of five traits. The two omic layers differed not only in the amount of GEI captured, but also in the pattern of clone re-ranking across years. When back-solved effects were aggregated into genomic windows, the largest genomic and epigenomic effects tended to fall in different regions, with overlap no greater than expected by chance. Together, these results show that genomic and epigenomic relationships capture complementary components of year-to-year variation in clone performance, with the epigenomic contribution expressed primarily through GEI. These findings provide a basis for investigating the molecular drivers of GEI and for testing whether genomic and epigenomic information can inform selection for stable clonal performance across variable environments.

items.title: Long-read DNA sequencing reveals global hypomethylation and focal hypermethylation in SDHx-deficient pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma
items.abstract: Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGL) are highly heritable neuroendocrine tumors of the autonomic ganglia. Genomic DNA in most cancer cells is hypomethylated. However, DNA in PPGLs secondary to mutations in succinate dehydrogenase complex (SDHx) genes is reportedly hypermethylated due to succinate-mediated inhibition of DNA demethylases. We used nanopore long-read sequencing to characterize the methylome of tumor and white blood cell DNA from SDHx and non-SDHx PPGL patients, alongside normal adrenal medulla. We find that both SDHx and non-SDHx PPGLs are globally hypomethylated, particularly at centromeres. In normal adrenal medulla, CpG islands marked by H3K4 methylation are hypomethylated, whereas CpG islands lacking H3K4 methylation are hypermethylated. In SDHx-related PPGL, some H3K4me-marked CpG islands are hypermethylated, but most are not. We propose that DNA methylation in SDHx-related PPGL reflects the global hypomethylation generally observed in tumors, partly offset by succinate-mediated inhibition of TET DNA demethylases. Opposing effects of succinate may alter the balance between DNA methylation (indirect inhibition of the DNMT3A/B DNA methylases via inhibition of H3K4me demethylases) and DNA demethylation (inhibition of TET DNA demethylases) at active CpG islands.

items.title: Genomic characterization and evolutionary path of human satellite 1B in primates highlight a dynamic relationship with transposable elements
items.abstract: Human Satellite 1B (HSat1B) remains one of the least characterized classical human satellite DNAs, despite its massive abundance on the human Y chromosome. Its tripartite ~2.5 kb monomer - comprising an AluY fragment, a GC-rich unit (here named H1B) and an AT-rich block - points to an evolutionary origin tightly linked to transposable elements (TEs). Here, we present the first comprehensive comparative genomic, phylogenetic and transcriptional characterization of HSat1B across 10 primate species using Telomere-to-Telomere (T2T) and chromosome-scale long-read assemblies, combined with DNA-FISH, RNA-FISH and long-read transcriptomic analyses. We demonstrate that while canonical tandem HSat1B arrays are restricted to Homininae (human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla), the core H1B unit and its structural variants (H1Bsv1 and H1Bsv2) occur across all 10 primate genomes, including strepsirrhines (lemur). This indicates that the H1B sequence predates the assembly of the composite HSat1B monomer by at least 60 million years. H1B variants consistently map within TE-rich genomic contexts, supporting a stepwise, TE-mediated model of satellite diversification and mobilization. Within Homininae, humans exhibit a dramatic lineage-specific expansion driven by Yq12 amplification (~14.2 Mb; 92% of total genomic content), whereas non-human great apes carry smaller, highly polymorphic autosomal and Y-linked arrays. Finally, we show that H1B-containing sequences are transcriptionally active in human and gorilla nuclei via RNA-FISH and characterize heterogeneous H1B/Alu chimeric non-coding transcripts in the human male germline. Collectively, our findings uncover the birth and Homininae-specific expansion of a composite satellite DNA seeded by an ancient primate sequence module and sculpted by transposable elements.

items.title: Transcriptome reallocation during infection reshapes synonymous codon demand in Botrytis cinerea
items.abstract: While genomic codon usage is fixed within an individual isolate, the synonymous codons represented in its RNA pool can change when transcription shifts among genes. We tested whether this transcript-level phenotype accompanies infection by reanalyzing 39 libraries from three public Botrytis cinerea RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) time series in S. lycopersicum, Arabidopsis thaliana, and Physcomitrium patens. Gene counts were corrected for coding length, combined with fixed gene-specific codon inventories, and analyzed as centered log ratios within synonymous amino-acid families. Sampling time accounted for 95-98% of fungal codon-demand variation in each series. The association persisted after effective-length correction, unique-only competitive mapping, host-homology exclusion, depth equalization, protein-family weighting, and removal of translation-associated genes. Change vectors over the interpolated, time-aligned 16-24-h interval were positively aligned among studies, whereas later trajectories diverged. Matched reassignments of complete expression trajectories showed more full-series organization than expected in S. lycopersicum and Arabidopsis, but not in P. patens. Codon-preference-weighted abundance and expression breadth also changed through infection, although their directions were not universal. Across systems, large non-translation contributors repeatedly carried ATP-synthase/respiratory and extracellular annotations, although their timing and companion functions differed. Infection-associated transcriptional reallocation therefore repeatedly restructures the synonymous composition of the inferred fungal transcript pool. This establishes a dynamic allocation phenotype and a basis for testing consequences for RNA stability and translation during host-pathogen interactions.

items.title: scCont: Interpretable Contrastive Learning for Functional Characterization of Cellular State Transitions
items.abstract: Timecourse single-cell RNA (scRNA) datasets have become indispensable biological tools for studying and uncovering the underlying regulatory processes driving continuous cell-state transitions such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, these highly fluid, non-linear gene program dynamics remain difficult to disentangle. While deep neural network models can effectively map complex topologies, they are biological black boxes, lacking the gene-level interpretability required by experimental practitioners. Here, we introduce scCont, a fully unsupervised contrastive learning framework for extracting interpretable functional transition units from scRNA-seq data. Rather than relying on explicit temporal labels or clustering priors, scCont uses an unsupervised k-nearest neighbors approach to project local transcriptomic neighborhoods into a low-dimensional embedding. During post-training analysis, scCont employs Shapley network attribution to determine gene-latent relationships, mapping latent dimensions directly into functional gene programs. We quantitatively and qualitatively validate this representation by demonstrating that scCont captures biologically interpretable dynamics more effectively than baseline methods such as LDVAE. Evaluated across 13 diverse EMT timecourse datasets and four simulated datasets, scCont exposes interpretable functional dynamics and effectively maps context-dependent functional groups, helping to bridge the gap between deep learning representation and translational biological utility. scCont is an open source software available on GitHub (https://github.com/nramani611/scCont).

items.title: QUANTA: A quantum annealing framework for species tree estimation using weighted quartet amalgamation
items.corresponding_institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology
items.abstract: Reconstructing species trees from genome-scale data is challenging due to pervasive gene tree discordance. Maximizing quartet consistency is a widely used approach for species tree inference from multi-locus data. Quartet amalgamation approaches, such as Quartet Fiduccia-Mattheyse (QFM) and Quartet MaxCut (QMC) families, have emerged as highly accurate quartet-based species tree inference techniques, but their reliance on computationally expensive classical bipartitioning heuristics, such as Fiduccia-Mattheyses (FM) and MaxCut, limits their scalability. Here, we introduce QUANTA, a quantum annealing-based quartet amalgamation method that, to our knowledge, represents the first quantum formulation of quartet-based approaches and the first species tree estimation method for multi-locus data that runs on real quantum hardware. At the core of QUANTA is a novel, general formulation of weighted quartet bipartitioning as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem that enables quantum annealing to replace the classical bipartitioning strategies underlying the QFM and QMC families of methods. We prove that our formulation uses the minimum possible number of qubits to represent bipartitions and that its energy function correctly orders satisfied, deferred, and violated quartets for any positive penalty weights. We implemented QUANTA on real D-Wave quantum annealing hardware, and evaluated it on a wide range of simulated and biological datasets. QUANTA achieves accuracy comparable to the state-of-the-art methods, including ASTRAL and wQFM, under challenging evolutionary conditions. We also reanalyzed several biological datasets, including the avian phylogenomic dataset comprising 14,446 genes across 48 genomes, on which QUANTA reconstructed a species tree with a higher quartet score than wQFM. Remarkably, despite running on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware, QUANTA's bipartition technique achieved 4100x speedup over the FM bipartitioning technique in wQFM on bipartition containing 90-200 taxa, while maintaining comparable tree accuracy. By establishing a theoretically grounded, hardware-independent quantum optimization framework for weighted quartet amalgamation, QUANTA opens a new direction for quantum-assisted phylogenomics and provides a foundation for increasingly scalable and accurate species tree estimation as quantum computing hardware advances. QUANTA is publicly available at https://github.com/QuitttCat/QUANTA-Phylogenomics.

items.title: Theoretical prediction of assembly contiguity
items.abstract: Theoretical methods for predicting the performance of assembly algorithms have the potential to guide experimental design on a scale that simulations cannot. A fundamental question of experimental design is how deep to sequence in order to obtain an assembly with long-enough contigs. More precisely, given a certain read length and coverage, what is the expected contig length that an assembler would produce on a given genome? The foundational work of Lander and Waterman tackled this question, but their method is not applicable to modern high-throughput sequencing. In this paper, we derive what we call a Z-value, which is a formula that takes as input the read length, coverage, and basic properties of the genome, and returns a prediction of the mean contig length produced by a simple single-k assembler on error-free data. We show on a benchmark of 14 genomes that the Z-value is highly accurate, with a mean absolute prediction error of less than 2 percent. We further show how this formula can be used to determine the best choice of k for the assembler and how to choose a coverage level that gives contig lengths within a desired fraction of the optimal. Finally, we show how the Z-value can also predict the performance of a more complicated assembler like Velvet and how it can be used to guide the choice between instruments when there is a tradeoff between coverage and read length and the budget is limited.

items.title: Virtual dynamics of spatiotemporal single-cell interactions
items.abstract: Building virtual cells and tissues requires reconstructing how interacting cell populations evolve in space and time, yet spatial omics experiments provide only sparse snapshots of this process. Here, we introduce CytoBridge, a computational method that reconstructs continuous virtual cell dynamics from discrete spatial transcriptomic data. Starting from a joint transcriptomic-spatial space, CytoBridge learns stochastic trajectories of cell states, positions, and population sizes through an unbalanced mean-field Schrodinger bridge formulation that explicitly incorporates cell-cell interaction as a dynamical driver. A time-varying interaction graph built from spatial proximity and ligand-receptor priors allows the velocity to be decomposed into an interaction component estimated from observed neighborhoods and ligand-receptor features, and an intrinsic-context component that captures intrinsic regulatory processes and unmeasured contextual influences. Applied to five datasets across three spatial transcriptomics platforms and spanning development, regeneration, and neurodegeneration, CytoBridge accurately generates tissue dynamics at unmeasured time points, follows ligand-receptor signaling through measured and unmeasured stages, and supports hypothesis-generating in silico perturbation. CytoBridge provides a general method for turning heterogeneous spatiotemporal transcriptomic measurements into continuously evolving virtual tissues.

items.title: Contrastive Learning Improves Generalization on M2OR Olfactory Binding Dataset
items.abstract: Olfaction-based biosensors stand to have profound impacts in fields such as medical diagnostics, national security, and drug discovery. A promising mode of vapor phase biodetection mimics volatile organic compound-olfactory receptor (VOC-OR) interactions with target-specific protein or peptide probes; however, lack of experimental coverage remains a core bottleneck. Current computational approaches aim to improve prediction of VOC-OR binding to reduce experimental burden, and current machine learning approaches fail to demonstrate a level of generalization that addresses current engineering challenges. Here, using the Molecular to Olfactory Dataset (M2OR) and Insect Olfactory Binding Protein Database (iOBPdb) datasets, data partitioning methods and their performance are evaluated on a neural network and contrastive learning framework on such VOC-OR binding datasets, varying: model training, architecture, and structure of the input data distribution. It was found that holding out certain chemical or proteomic motifs from the training data diminished model performance with a two layer neural network model. The model was able to generalize to state of the art performance (0.88 AUCROC) on every data split by applying a contrastive learning objective defined by shared molecular constituents and a stochastic sampler. This suggests the contrastive objective provides a strong inductive bias for neural networks to predict novel VOC-OR pairs. These findings highlight that model performance on pairwise biological interaction datasets can be inflated through identity leakage from constituent overlap, and emphasize the need for more robust evaluation protocols. Furthermore, we show contrastive regularization mitigates dataset degeneracy through enforcement of compatibility in the models latent geometry that may extend to other binder target-datasets where identity leakage confounds evaluation.

items.title: QRAFT: Scaling coalescent-based species tree inference to one million taxa
items.corresponding_institution: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology
items.abstract: Species tree inference from multi-locus data under the multispecies coalescent has not kept pace with phylogenomic datasets that now span hundreds of thousands of species. We present QRAFT, a statistically consistent method for estimating species trees by maximizing quartet support on phylogenomic datasets at unprecedented scales. For n taxa and k gene trees, QRAFT achieves near-linear running time of O(kn log^2 n) when its recursion is balanced, which is within a polylogarithmic factor of the O(kn) time required simply to read the input. It also achieves asymptotically optimal O(kn) memory, so its memory requirements grow only linearly with the input size. QRAFT infers a million-taxon species tree from 1,000 genes in just three hours using only 298 GB of RAM, 64 CPU threads, and no GPUs. We estimate that the same analysis with ASTRAL-MP, a scalable parallel implementation of the widely used method ASTRAL, would take about 36 years (>100,000 times longer) and require prohibitive amounts of memory, far beyond practical computational limits. QRAFT maintains accuracy comparable to, and in many cases better than, leading species tree estimation methods. Notably, QRAFT reconstructed a microbial tree of life comprising 199,330 genomes in just a few hours using modest CPU resources. Thus, QRAFT brings highly accurate statistically consistent coalescent-based species tree inference to the unprecedented million-taxon regime and enables phylogenomic analyses towards the scale of the tree of life. QRAFT is publicly available at https://github.com/risenfromashes/qraft.

items.title: Towards a foundation model for raw nanopore signal through discrete tokenization
items.abstract: Nanopore sequencing reads nucleic acids as changes in ionic current that carry information beyond the base sequence. Self-supervised pretrained models have advanced genomic sequence modeling and single-cell analysis, but remain underexplored for raw nanopore signals, which are continuous and lack a native token vocabulary. Here we present Brieno, an approach combining reconstruction-based tokenization through residual vector quantization with a Transformer for contextual representation learning. We pretrain the Transformer using masked-token prediction on raw nanopore signals from 118 million reads. With frozen or fine-tuned features, the model identifies species without requiring reference genomes. It complements Dorado by accurately classifying reads left unclassified in native-barcode demultiplexing, approaches Dorado's basecalling performance across six genomes, and exceeds Dorado's specialized 5-methylcytosine model as well as a dedicated 6-methyladenine caller. Brieno also supports accurate CpG methylation detection with limited labeled data. Across tasks, pretrained contextual representations improve downstream performance over non-pretrained baselines and generalize across sequencing runs. Together, these findings support self-supervised pretraining as a basis for transferable representations of raw nanopore signals.

items.title: Hybrid RY-mers increase aDNA alignment sensitivity
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Mathematics, Science for Life Laboratory, Stockholm University, 106 91, Stockholm, Sweden
items.abstract: One of the key steps in ancient DNA data analysis is the accurate identification of endogenous short reads that originate from the ancient genome. Currently, this step is performed using general-purpose sequence aligners, such as BWA-aln, with parameter settings optimized for sensitivity. This approach results in increased runtime, even relative to standard DNA alignment workflows, and is not sufficient for aligning samples that are highly divergent from a reference database. We introduce hybrid RY-mers, a seed construct designed to incorporate aDNA-specific sequence damage. We adapt hybrid RY-mers to the existing concept of multi-context seeds and implement them in the read aligner strobealign. On simulated genomic and metagenomic datasets, we show that hybrid RY-mers result in higher mapping accuracy, while also reducing runtime by 4-6 times compared to the state-of-the-art aDNA alignment method BWA-aln. Furthermore, substituting aDNA aligner MALT in the metagenomic tool-suite aMeta with our new alignment approach demonstrated that aMeta gave a faster and less memory consuming detection of ancient taxa present in the samples.

items.title: DisCell: Separating Spillover from Niche Response in Spatial Transcriptomics
items.corresponding_institution: KTH royal institute of technology stockholm, SciLifeLab
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics at single-cell resolution measures every cell in its place in the tissue, but diffusion and segmentation errors also add transcripts of neighboring cells to a cell's counts. This spillover makes a cell resemble its neighbors, and a response to the niche makes cells in the same niche resemble each other. Both tie a cell's expression to its surroundings. The count data alone cannot tell the two apart. Findings from single-cell transcriptomes, such as a gene program that is higher in one niche than in another or signaling genes that change depending on the neighborhood, may therefore be artifacts of spillover. Current models describe a cell by its intrinsic state together with either its niche response or spillover, but none models all three. We present DisCell, the first method that models all three components jointly and measures how robust each finding is to spillover. DisCell is a generative model that describes single-cell gene expression profiles in terms of two latent variables, an intrinsic state and a response to the niche, and adds spillover from its neighbors as a separate term. DisCell fits the model at increasing levels of spillover and recomputes each finding on the spillover-free expression to see how much spillover it withstands. DisCell also estimates the most spillover a section can contain, and a finding that holds even at that amount is not explained by spillover. In simulated tissue, DisCell recovers each cell's intrinsic state and response and tells findings created by spillover apart from genuine responses. On five sections of ovarian and lung tissue, the intrinsic state keeps more of each cell's own properties, measured by its cell-cycle phase, than any competing method that holds as little of its neighborhood. Within each cell type, the model partitions the variation of each gene into intrinsic state, niche response and spillover. Using DisCell, we rank findings about niches by their robustness to spillover and confirm that a previously reported finding withstands spillover, that esophageal cancer cells in niches infiltrated by immune or stromal cells express more of an epithelial-mesenchymal transition program. DisCell also predicts what the gene expression of a cell type would be in another niche, with its spillover part separated, at lower error on most tasks than the competing method built for this purpose. Training the model takes under ten minutes on one consumer GPU for sections of up to 400,000 cells.

items.title: Growing a Root from Its Genome : Emergent Tissue Layers and Zones in a GPU-Native Simulation of the Arabidopsis Root Tip
items.abstract: Models of the Arabidopsis root tip usually take its cell identities as given. Here we grow a root tip from a single genome. In a two-dimensional median section, every cell reads the same network of 62 genes (26 core genes from an earlier, unpublished model of callus and 36 added for the root) and starts with the same expression; the only spatial cues are the polarity of auxin transport, auxin from the shoot and the free surface. Identities and zones are never given to the simulation; they are read from gene expression. Cells are polygons of a shared mesh, relaxed towards mechanical equilibrium under turgor at every step. In 48 simulated hours, a tip-shaped template grows into a root of 3 000-4 500 cells with epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle and stele in order along most of its length, SHORT-ROOT and SCARECROW in the endodermis, an auxin maximum, a quiescent centre and a cap at its tip, and meristem, elongation and mature zones. A WOX5 gate built from published interactions and one hypothesis keeps a quiescent centre to 48 h in 17 of 20 simulated roots that were not used for tuning (85%; Wilson 95% interval 64-95%; criteria fixed before the run), against 9 of 20 roots used for tuning, before the gate. The niche is not maintained beyond 48 h: grown on to 73 h, only 6 of these 20 roots still have a quiescent centre (30%; 15-52%). All pre-registered criteria hold in only 1 of 20 roots, because the quiescent centre is too wide at 0 h; without that count, 12 of 20. The meristem is too long, and cortical cells made after the start of growth elongate only three- to four-fold instead of eightto thirty-fold, a limit set in large part by the numerical growth scheme. Mutants are a major weakness: several look like their published phenotype, but an exploratory re-run of a mutant benchmark fixed in advance for our first model passes one of nine predictions. Nor does the root regenerate: cut near its tip, it re-forms an auxin maximum and a columella but no quiescent centre. On a first, simpler model and without any polarity cue, a mass of identical cells still sorts into concentric layers and, when PIN carriers follow the auxin flux, concentrates auxin into a few foci, but forms no stem-cell niche: the genome lacks a lateral inhibition between foci. We state the limitations and the next stages.

items.title: Predicting Transcriptional Responses to Unseen Compounds through Context Modeling and Multi-View Transfer
items.corresponding_institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Predicting drug-induced transcriptional responses could support in silico screening of new compounds, yet existing models barely use the compound: on a drug-blind L1000 benchmark, removing the drug input from seven published models changes accuracy by at most 0.012 Pearson correlation. They capture shared cellular and experimental variation while overlooking the compound-specific signals that distinguish drug effects. We present UnDetect, a framework that separates contextual variation from compound effects to predict responses to transcriptionally unprofiled compounds. UnDetect integrates chemical structure, annotated targets, mechanisms of action and Cell Painting morphology into a normalized multi-view kernel that accommodates incomplete compound information, and transfers residual responses within and across profiled cell lines, so that pharmacological and phenotypic relationships inform predictions beyond chemical similarity. On a drug-blind benchmark, where the paired control reveals the assay plate, UnDetect is the only model to beat a network that ignores the compound, in every fold; on a within-plate score that is zero for any compound-blind prediction, it reaches 0.117 against 0.092 for the strongest published model. On DeepCE's benchmark it reaches 0.602 Pearson correlation against the reported 0.491. Transfer across cell lines improves 28 of 28 LINCS L1000 and, at the two higher doses, 47 and 49 of 50 Tahoe-100M cell-line evaluations. These results show that separating context from compound effects and integrating complementary compound information improves transcriptional prediction and extends the utility of perturbation atlases for virtual screening.

items.title: Residual barcode-like sequences and barcode-associated artifacts after Dorado and Barbell preprocessing of metagenomic reads
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Transfusion Medicine, University Hospital Ulm, 89081 Ulm, Germany
items.abstract: Background Residual barcode-like sequences after preprocessing are a quality-control concern in multiplexed Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing data, particularly in low-biomass, host-dominated samples such as blood. Using blood datasets spiked with a microbial mock community and prepared with the Native Barcoding Kit 96 V14 (SQK-NBD114.96), we compared Dorado 1.1.1, Dorado 2.0.0, and Barbell 0.3.2. Results Dorado demultiplexing reduced barcode-positive reads to approximately 2% of reads, with internal barcode-like matches in 0.17-0.19% of reads. Barbell 0.3.2 applied to untrimmed Dorado basecalls yielded an approximately 50-fold lower detector-defined internal-match rate (0.0035-0.0037%) while retaining 91.2-91.8% of input reads. In the NCBI core_nt release of 12 September 2026, the focused screen identified complete, ungapped 24 nt identity for 64 of the 96 barcodes (66.7%), comprising 505 distinct barcode-accession pairs across 482 accessions and 195 exported TaxID groups of mixed taxonomic ranks. Records annotated as rRNA genes, chromosomes/genomes, and plasmids accounted for 35.6%, 23.2%, and 22.4% of the pairs, respectively. The barcode was located within its native ligation flanks in 224 pairs (44.4%), including 170 (33.7%) with the complete Dorado barcode search window and 3 (0.6%) with the full adapter construct. Conclusion Barbell combined 91-92% read retention with lower detected internal barcode signals. After demultiplexing, barcode-like sequences remained in sample data. Moreover, kit barcode sequences, often within their native ligation flanks, were detected in reference records. Both findings call for careful preprocessing, reference inspection, and downstream validation. Further research should determine whether barcode-associated artifacts in reads and reference records affect taxonomic classification in clinical metagenomic workflows.

items.title: Single-Cell Transcriptomics Reveals Tumorigenic Lineages and Interactions Persisting and Evolving From Premalignancy to Cancer in the Stomach
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Microbiology and Immunology, University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, Miami, FL, USA
items.abstract: Background & Aims Gastric cancer is often diagnosed at advanced stages, making the premalignant window critical for early detection. However, the epithelial changes that characterize this stage remain poorly defined. We used CTLA4-knockdown (CTLA4KD) mice, which model human CTLA4 insufficiency-associated gastric cancer, that develops autoimmune gastritis, metaplasia, and adenocarcinoma, to define molecular changes across disease progression. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing and 40-color spectral flow cytometry were performed on gastric tissue across premalignant and cancer stages. We evaluated epithelial lineage relationships, cell-cell communication pathways, and candidate markers at the transcript and protein levels in murine and human gastric adenocarcinoma. Results We identified a metaplastic/tumorigenic population in CTLA4KD mice that emerged in premalignancy with a chief cell transcriptomic origin. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed a progressive increase in fibronectin (FN1) signaling from premalignancy through cancer, transitioning from stromal to autocrine signaling in the metaplastic/tumorigenic population. Expression of Embigin (EMB), a fibronectin receptor, increased at both transcript and protein levels in premalignancy and remained elevated in cancer. EMB epithelial cells co-expressed CD133, a cancer stem cell marker, consistent with a stem-like phenotype. EMB expression was also higher in human gastric adenocarcinoma than in matched normal tissue. Conclusions Using a model that captures the full histopathological cascade of gastric tumorigenesis, we delineate single-cell transcriptional programs that persist and evolve from premalignancy to adenocarcinoma. In-depth computational analyses identified novel markers involved in cell-cell communication during tumorigenesis, including EMB, an epithelial marker that persists from premalignancy through cancer in the murine model and validated in human gastric adenocarcinoma, suggesting EMB as a marker of premalignant progression.

items.title: Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 Alters Extracellular Vesicle Secretion and Cargo Composition in Cellular Models
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, San Diego State University, San Diego, California, USA
items.abstract: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and confer the neomorphic production of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D2HG), which drives epigenetic remodeling. Growing evidence suggests this neomorphic activity may also affect how tumor cells communicate; small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are elevated in gliomas, though how mutant IDH1 shapes sEV production and cargo remains poorly understood. Using glioblastoma and chondrosarcoma cell models, we show expression of mutant IDH1 correlates with a trend of increased sEV secretion, and that D2HG is packaged into sEVs that are taken up by cells. Cell-permeable D2HG treatment dose-dependently increased sEV release from IDH1 wild type cells. Untargeted proteomics showed that mutant IDH1 expression remodeled sEV cargo in a cell type-specific fashion, with mutant chondrosarcoma sEVs enriched in one-carbon metabolism enzymes, and mutant glioma sEVs in lysosomal luminal proteins and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperones. Mutant IDH1 glioma cell transcriptomics suggested expanded ER folding capacity and reduced ribosomal pathways, and sEVs from these cells decreased nascent protein synthesis in IDH1 wild type recipient cells. Together, this suggests sEVs can serve as carriers of mutant IDH1 phenotypes.

items.title: Targeting REV1 Exposes Context-Dependent Therapeutic Responses in Colorectal Cancer
items.abstract: Translesion synthesis (TLS) promotes DNA damage tolerance and contributes to chemotherapy resistance by enabling replication across damaged DNA templates. REV1, a central TLS regulator, is a potential therapeutic target to enhance the efficacy of genotoxic chemotherapy. Here, we investigated the therapeutic consequences of pharmacologic and genetic REV1 targeting in colorectal cancer (CRC) and evaluated the sensitivity of patient-derived CRC organoids to the REV1 inhibitor JH-RE-06. JH-RE-06 enhanced oxaliplatin sensitivity in HCT116 cells and 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) sensitivity in HT-29 cells, whereas reciprocal combinations produced limited sensitization, indicating treatment- and cellular context-dependent responses. siRNA-mediated REV1 depletion similarly enhanced chemotherapy sensitivity, supporting REV1 involvement in these responses. MNNG sensitivity assays and MLH1 expression analyses did not reveal consistent treatment-associated changes in mismatch repair function, while targeted HPRT1 sequencing identified no detectable sequence alterations in the region examined. Chemosensitization was not accompanied by consistent increases in caspase-3/7 activation under the conditions tested. REV1 inhibition also caused LC3-II accumulation and, after prolonged inhibitor exposure, reduced beta-tubulin abundance, indicating additional autophagy-associated and cytoskeletal responses. In two patient-derived CRC organoid models, JH-RE-06 exhibited single-agent growth-inhibitory activity, with mean IC50 values of 2.01 micromolar and 1.4 micromolar, respectively. Together, these findings demonstrate context-dependent chemosensitization and organoid growth inhibition following REV1 targeting, suggesting that its therapeutic consequences may extend beyond canonical TLS-mediated DNA damage tolerance.

items.title: Cross-excitation in dorsal root ganglia redistributes coding capacity from stimulus intensity to stimulus location
items.corresponding_institution: Center for Bio- and Medical Technologies
items.abstract: The phenomenon of cross-excitation between neurons of dorsal root ganglia (DRGs) of mammals is widely known, yet its exact mechanism remains underexplored. In this work, we analyze the phenomenon as part of the signal processing performed by the body's somatosensory system. We argue that, if the mechanism is indeed as prevalent as it is reported in experimental works, it should provide a significant computational advantage. Here, we created a model network in which sensory A-type neurons are interconnected only via a chemical agent and showed that such a connection, when fitted with parameters similar to those observed in experiments, improves the stimulus-localization properties of the ganglia at the expense of intensity-encoding accuracy. Although this exchange is near-neutral in raw bits, it becomes favorable once the logarithmic compression of intensity perception - the Weber--Fechner law - is taken into account, since the sacrificed intensity capacity is largely perceptually redundant. We therefore propose that cross-excitation is not an imperfection of somatic isolation but an effective, chemically mediated pre-processing stage that sharpens spatial localization.

items.title: Towards an analytical framework for investigating the neurophysiological influence of social context in speech perception
items.abstract: Social information plays an important role in everyday speech communication, yet existing neurophysiological approaches provide limited means of isolating its contribution during naturalistic speech perception. Here, we present an analytical framework that combines the large language model (LLM) Mistral-Instruct, fine-tuned on conversational language, and temporal response functions (TRFs) to investigate the influence of social context on word-level speech processing. The framework disentangles local context (LC) from speaker-specific social context (SC) when generating LLM-derived lexical expectation measures, enabling such predictions to be generated under either matching or mismatching speaker contexts for the same speech material. This provides a direct way of isolating the contribution of social information to lexical predictions. We first show that speaker-related social context carries information about speech register and conversational role beyond that available from previous local context alone by interrogating Mistral-Instruct. We then demonstrate that lexical expectations generated from socially congruent contexts produce small but reliable improvements in EEG prediction relative to expectations generated from incongruent social contexts. These effects were observed despite identical acoustic input and neural recordings, indicating that the influence of social context on lexical expectations explains dissociable variance in neural responses to speech. Together, these findings provide a proof of concept for using LLM-derived lexical expectations to isolate and measure the influence of social context on speech processing. More broadly, the proposed framework offers a flexible approach for generating and testing hypotheses about how different forms of contextual knowledge shape neural responses during naturalistic language comprehension.

items.title: Extended Pavlovian conditioned approach training and devaluation in Long-Evans rats using time-restricted feeding
items.corresponding_institution: University of Cincinnati College of Medicine
items.abstract: Pavlovian conditioned approach (PCA) is a useful tool in studying compulsive- and addictive-like behaviors. PCA pairs a cue with reward delivery and rats typically differentiate into three phenotypes (sign-trackers, goal-trackers, and intermediates) based on behavior during the reward-paired cue presentation. Sign-trackers, who preferentially interact with the cue, are more likely to engage in compulsive behaviors and have decreased behavioral flexibility compared to goal-trackers, who preferentially interact with the food cup. However, one limitation to PCA is the use of food deprivation conditions that maintain rats at 80-90% of ad libitum weight, likely increasing stress which may bias animals towards sign-tracking behavior. Furthermore, most behavioral analysis only examines lever pressing and food cup entry, overlooking other behaviors that may better define phenotypes. In the current study male and female Long-Evans rats underwent an extended PCA training paradigm followed by satiety-induced reward devaluation under time-restricted feeding (TRF) conditions. Under TRF, rats continued to gain weight across PCA training and maintained caloric intake relative to ad libitum intake.
