In conditional chemical and genet-ic screens of primary human CD8+ and CD4+ T cells, PertVI separates memory-precursor adju-vants from toxic phenocopies, resolves co-clustered regulators into directional kinetic trajectories and biphasic rebounders obscured by standard workflows, and reveals that treatment-induced phe-notypic shifting is decoupled from broad transcriptional perturbation responses and instead gov-erned by state-specific impulses. Altogether, PertVI brings unique mechanistic granularity to sin-gle-cell perturbation response modeling, serving as a proof of principle for biology-informed, struc-ture-guided variance disentanglement in dynamic cellular systems.

items.title: KLONE: An Imbalance-Robust k-NN Ensemble for Cross-Modal Single-Cell Clone Assignment
items.abstract: Single-cell DNA sequencing (scDNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enable the inference of copy number clones and transcriptional states in tumor studies. However, these two assays usually profile different cells of the same tumor, requiring computational assignment of unpaired scRNA-seq cells to clones identified by scDNA-seq to link clonal genotypes with transcriptional profiles. This task is challenging because the only connection between the two modalities is a weak, gene-dependent dosage effect, and the absence of clone labels for RNA cells precludes supervised learning of this relationship. Moreover, clonal distributions may differ between the two modalities because the cells are profiled independently, while the inherent clonal imbalance of real tumors can leave minority subclones underrepresented, further compromising assignment accuracy. To address these challenges, we present KLONE, a per-clone $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) ensemble that assigns RNA cells directly to copy-number clones based on cross-modal Pearson similarity, without the need for a parametric model or clone labels for RNA cells. To ensure a fair assessment of each clone's compatibility with a given RNA cell, KLONE allocates an identical neighborhood budget to every clone, preventing majority clones from dominating the affinity assessment solely through their greater abundance. We compare KLONE with six existing methods on three colorectal cancer patients, using cells profiled in both modalities as ground truth. KLONE is the most accurate method and recalls minority clones at 100\%. Despite discrepancies in clonal distribution between the two modalities, KLONE recovers the clonal distribution of RNA cells almost perfectly ($\rho = 0.99$).

items.title: ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA): An Agentic Framework for Feature Discovery and Cross Site Generalization in Autism fMRI Classification
items.abstract: Classifiers of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from resting state functional MRI rarely generalize across sites, and many reported accuracies are inflated by data leakage.We show that an agentic artificial intelligence framework, ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA), whose language model agents propose features from the literature and researcher input while fixed tools perform every calculation, can search auditably for site independent classifiers while controlling the leakage. In 1,028 participants from 17 ABIDE I centers, ANA tested 71 pipelines and selected a ComBat harmonized ensemble of tangent space connectivity models from six parcellations and 98 public connectivity derivatives. In leave one center out testing, the ensemble reached an area under the curve of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.773 to 0.841), outperforming ASD DiagNet and ASD SAENet. Predictive connectivity was mainly reduced in ASD. Agentic AI offers a systematic and efficient approach to exploring, evaluating, and identifying pipelines as model selection grows complex.

items.title: Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
items.abstract: In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units--cells, bins or multicellular spots--into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p-values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene-gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p-values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

items.title: CPDD: Adapting an autoregressive DNA language model for bidirectional phage genome modeling
items.abstract: Autoregressive DNA language models generate sequences ef[fi]ciently from left to right, but many genome-analysis and sequence-editing problems are naturally conditioned on both [fl]anks. We introduce CreatiPhage, a 144.5M-parameter autoregressive DNA language model for bacteriophages, and its diffusion extension, CreatiPhage Diffusion DNA-LM (CPDD). CPDD is a 147.5M-parameter bidirectional discrete diffusion model initialized from the six-epoch CreatiPhage checkpoint. CPDD retains the pretrained Transformer, block attention residuals, and Engram conditional memory, while introducing non-causal attention, a MASK-aware base-5 Engram, centered depthwise convolution, and position-aligned nucleotide readout. Training combines masked and GIDD-style uniformly substituted bases with nucleotide- and amino-acid-level losses over a 10 kb, 32 kb, and whole-source context curriculum. On a screened panel of 522 phage CDSs, CPDD achieves higher random-mask restoration accuracy than a comparable diffusion model and performs well above codon-level references. In a mixed-corruption test, it restores 42.4% of visible incorrect bases. Frozen CPDD representations also support infA [fi]tness prediction and seven-class phage virion protein subtype classi[fi]cation. Controlled evaluations further characterize how restoration depends on visible context and identify opportunities to improve longer-range sequence recovery. Together, these results support scaffold-conditioned sequence modeling as a step towards modular design of phage genomes.

items.title: Maternal separation remodels Purkinje cell circuits and impairs cerebellar synaptic plasticity
items.abstract: Introduction: Early-life adversity has been associated with cerebellar abnormalities, but the cellular and circuit-level changes involved and their persistence across development remain poorly understood. We examined whether maternal separation (MS) disrupts cerebellar circuit maturation and whether these changes are accompanied by alterations in synaptic function and behavior. Methods: CD1 mice underwent daily maternal separation from postnatal day 2 to 18, whereas control litters remained undisturbed. Cerebellar alterations were assessed using transcriptomic and DNA methylation profiling, RT-qPCR, immunoblotting, Purkinje-cell morphometric analysis, and VGLUT1/VGLUT2 immunofluorescence. Patch-clamp electrophysiology was used to examine synaptic transmission and plasticity. Motor coordination, spontaneous locomotion, social approach, and stress-coping behavior were also evaluated. Results: RNA sequencing of whole cerebellar tissue revealed early transcriptional remodeling, involving synaptic transmission, neuronal architecture, and plasticity-related pathways. Consistent with this profile, we found that MS altered Purkinje cell dendritic arborization and excitatory input remodeling, together with deficits in cerebellar long-term synaptic plasticity and reduced BDNF-related signaling. In parallel, methylation analysis revealed hypermethylation of the glucocorticoid receptor promoter and reduced cerebellar receptor expression, indicating that early-life stress also engages stress-related epigenetic mechanisms in this region. Importantly, these neurobiological changes were associated with motor coordination deficits, altered stress-coping behavior, and impaired social interaction. Discussion: These findings identify the developing cerebellum as a target of early-life adversity and suggest that disrupted cerebellar maturation may contribute to lasting functional consequences. This study extends our understanding of the effects of maternal separation beyond the brain regions traditionally associated with stress responses.

items.title: Multimodal Reorganization of Gut--Brain Physiology During the Cephalic Phase of Digestion
items.abstract: The vagus nerve plays a central role in gut--brain communication, yet the physiological dynamics associated with cholinergic vagal signaling remain difficult to characterize non-invasively in humans. The cephalic phase response, which prepares the gastrointestinal system for food ingestion through anticipatory vagal pathways, offers a unique opportunity to investigate these interactions. Here, we used simultaneous recordings of cortical, gastric, cardiac, and swallow physiology in healthy adults to characterize brain--body responses during food anticipation and subsequent ingestion. Food-related sensory cues increased gastric myoelectric activity as well as swallow and heart rate while eliciting frequency-specific changes in cortical oscillations. Strikingly, anticipation was accompanied by opposing changes in physiological coordination: synchronization within cortical and gastric networks decreased, whereas coupling between the brain and stomach increased. These changes largely returned toward baseline following ingestion, suggesting a distinct anticipatory organization of brain--body activity. Moreover, gastric responses were associated with various aspects of subjective appetite, whereas cortical responses were selectively associated with craving. Both gastric and cortical responses independently explained the variation in participants' self-reported craving. Together, these findings reveal that food anticipation reorganizes physiological coordination within and across central and peripheral systems, establishing the cephalic phase as a non-invasive framework for investigating brain--body interactions associated with cholinergic vagal signaling in humans.

items.title: Subcellular Spatial Profiling Unveils Links Between Neuritic Plaques with Selective Tau Vulnerability in Alzheimer's Disease
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) features widespread extracellular amyloid-{beta} plaques but selective intraneuronal tau accumulation in cortical layers II/III and V, while layer IV remains relatively resistant. Here, we combined subcellular spatial transcriptomics with co-registered A{beta} and pTau immunohistochemistry to determine why neurons exposed to comparable plaque-associated pathology differ in somatic pTau accumulation. Plaque-associated neuritic stress occurred similarly across layers, but layer IV neurons showed attenuated pTau accumulation and reduced somatic expression of a shared neurite-soma stress program involving DCTN1, CALM3, NORAD, and PIN1. Trajectory analysis within layers identified tau-vulnerable and resistant neuronal states implicating calcium signaling, retrograde transport, and lysosomal function. Notably, astrocytic APOE-neuronal LRP1 co-expression increased significantly along the pTau-vulnerable trajectory, and APOE {epsilon}4 was associated with stronger coupling of local plaque pathology to pTau-associated molecular programs. These findings reveal neuronal programs and neuron-glia interactions underlying selective tau vulnerability and resistance in AD, highlighting potential tau-targeting therapeutics.

items.title: Tendon-specific PIEZO1 activation enhances neural drive to muscle during ballistic movement
items.abstract: Tendons are generally regarded as passive structures that transmit muscle force to bone, yet they contain the Golgi tendon organ (GTO), whose Ib afferents act on motor neurons either inhibitory or excitatory depending on movement context. Whether a change in tendon mechanical properties alters the neural drive to muscle during movement remains unknown. We therefore recorded electromyography (EMG) and ankle kinematics during jumping in male mice carrying a tendon-specific gain-of-function (GOF) mutation in the mechanosensitive channel PIEZO1, which renders the tendon more compliant. In wild-type (WT) mice, gastrocnemius EMG amplitude increased with jump distance but not tibialis anterior activity, identifying the gastrocnemius as the muscle that scales with jump demand. At their maximum jump distance, which was longer in GOF than in WT mice, GOF mice showed a larger gastrocnemius EMG amplitude with unchanged burst duration. No genotype difference was detected at a submaximal distance, indicating that this enhancement depends on load. Kinematics showed the same specificity: GOF mice reached a deeper peak dorsiflexion before takeoff only at maximum jump distance, and the EMG difference emerged only after maximal dorsiflexion, not at burst onset. Muscle mass and myogenic gene expression were unchanged, whereas tendon marker genes were elevated, indicating that the enhancement was not of muscular origin. These findings indicate that a change in tendon mechanical properties alters the neural drive to muscle in a load-dependent manner, most plausibly through positive force feedback from the GTO, and identify the tendon as a sensory organ whose mechanical properties shape motor output.

items.title: Replication-stress response shapes Leishmania genome plasticity through non-equivalent RAD9 and HUS1 functions.
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology, Ribeirão Preto Medical School, University of São Paulo, Ribeirão Preto, 14040-900, SP, Brazil
items.abstract: Genome plasticity, manifested as gene copy-number variation and mosaic aneuploidy, enables adaptation in Leishmania , yet how genome-surveillance pathways shape this variation remains unclear. Here we show that partial depletion of HUS1 or RAD9, subunits of the conserved 9-1-1 checkpoint clamp, produces opposing replication-stress responses and contrasting patterns of genome remodelling in Leishmania major . During methotrexate selection HUS1 deficiency restricted DHFR-TS amplification and favoured linear amplicons, whereas RAD9 deficiency was associated with extensive circular amplification. This divergence extended to genome-wide scale: HUS1-deficient cells carried fewer but larger candidate rearrangements, whereas RAD9-deficient cells retained a largely wild-type rearrangement burden. These differences were accompanied by distinct HUS1 and RAD9 occupancy profiles around repetitive DNA implicated in gene amplification. Deficiency of either of these factors also resulted in differing effects on aneuploidy. While HUS1-deficient cells showed limited shifts towards chromosome disomy, RAD9-deficient cells exhibited broader chromosome copy-number gains and losses. Together, these findings identify replication-stress surveillance as a determinant of parasite genome plasticity, revealing that perturbing individual subunits of the same checkpoint complex can produce opposing genome-remodelling outcomes and reshape the variation available for adaptation.

items.title: Lifestyle-mediated shifts in the gut microbiome and host genetics modulate gene expression in intestinal organoids
items.abstract: Industrialization-associated shifts in the gut microbiome have been linked to disease, but the mechanisms by which microbial communities influence host gene regulation remain poorly understood. We developed a live microbiome-colonic organoid (colonoid) co-culture system to investigate genotype-dependent host responses to gut microbial community variation. Colonoid 2D monolayers from healthy donors were co-cultured with live gut microbial communities from individuals living urban or rural lifestyles, followed by RNA-sequencing. Urban and rural microbiomes elicited largely shared transcriptional responses, however they induced distinct host genetic effects on gene expression. We identified 511 host genes with microbiome-dependent allele-specific expression (ASE) which were involved in epithelial architecture, cell-matrix interactions and structural integrity. Notably, 149 host genes had distinct allelic effects between Urban and Rural microbiomes (urban-rural condition specific ASE or cASE), revealing genotype-dependent host responses to lifestyle-associated microbiomes. Urban-rural cASE was associated with microbial community composition, predominantly involving Prevotella and Bacteroides species. Targeted Prevotella copri spike-in recapitulated Prevotella-associated allelic effects at specific loci, including one in the IBD-associated autophagy gene, ATG4B. Together, these findings establish an experimental framework to investigate genotype-by-microbiome interactions, and demonstrate that lifestyle-mediated shifts in the microbiome modify host cis-regulatory genetic effects on gene expression.

items.title: Telotrons: spliceosomal introns composed of telomeric repeats
items.abstract: Spliceosomal intron numbers vary widely across eukaryotes, but the only established mechanism for large bursts of intron gain is the spread of transposable introner elements. We describe telotrons, spliceosomal introns composed predominantly of telomeric repeats. In a survey of 10,310 eukaryotic genome assemblies, we identified 7,008 introns with >85% telomeric repeat coverage and an additional 44,423 with >50% to [≤]85% coverage, in 25 genomes spanning haptophytes, dinoflagellates, a cryptophyte, stramenopiles, the apicomplexan Eimeria, and the nematode Mesorhabditis. Most telotrons carry GT-AG or GC-AG splice boundaries, and RNA-seq supports their splicing. Their repeat orientations are consistent with telomerase extension of broken DNA ends, and intron absence at corresponding positions in orthologs supports widespread de novo gain. In Eimeria and Mesorhabditis, telotrons instead occupy positions where orthologs carry ordinary introns, suggesting modification of existing introns. Telotrons thus point to telomerase as an endogenous driver of structural innovation through intron creation and remodeling.

items.title: Genomes2Genes: A Progressive Cactus Gene Analysis Pipeline
items.abstract: Whole-genome alignments are fundamental resources in comparative genomics, because they place genes and their surrounding sequences in a shared evolutionary context. Progressive Cactus aligns large numbers of genomes without a reference genome and reconstructs ancestral sequences along the input phylogeny. However, its Hierarchical Alignment Format output has mainly been used for visualization, phylogenomics, and pangenome studies, and gene-level analyses of these alignments remain difficult. Here, we present Genomes2Genes, a pipeline that converts Progressive Cactus graph-based alignments into validated coding sequence alignments of extant species and their reconstructed ancestors. The pipeline extracts exon alignment blocks, handles atypical genomic jumps, stitches exons into transcripts, and reports start codons, stop codons, and frameshifting indels across species, with validation steps throughout and a base-by-base audit of the final alignments. It catches both biological and technical artifacts and can be run on any part of the genome. We anticipate that this pipeline will be useful in identifying and removing problematic regions used in the potential reconstruction of species or gene phylogenies. We developed and tested the pipeline on a whole-genome alignment of 21 Brassicaceae species and 2 outgroups and found that, among 45,491 lineage-specific genes, the pipeline supported 22,376 candidate de novo genes, of which 1,811 had complete evidence of enabler mutations. Genomes2Genes is publicly available and extends whole-genome alignments to gene-level questions in comparative genomics and evolutionary biology.

items.title: A Y-specific translocated gsdf copy is a candidate master sex-determining gene in common dab (Limanda limanda)
items.abstract: Sex-determining systems in flatfishes are highly diverse, and even closely related species can differ in both sex-determining loci and heterogametic systems. In common dab (Limanda limanda), the genetic basis of sex determination has not yet been established. Here, we investigated sex determination using pooled whole-genome sequencing combined with long-read genome sequencing of females and males from Iceland and Norway. Genome-wide allele-frequency analyses identified sex-associated regions consistent with male heterogamety (XX/XY), with the strongest signal on chromosome 16. Comparison of the existing reference assembly, which represents an X haplotype at this locus, with a haplotype-resolved male PacBio HiFi assembly revealed a [~]21.5 kb Y-specific insertion on chromosome 16. The insertion showed complete coverage in male pools but little or no coverage in female pools from either population. It contained a translocated genomic segment including a copy of gonadal soma-derived factor (gsdf) and a predicted gene of unknown function. Comparative genomic analyses were consistent with this segment originating from an autosomal gsdf-containing region on chromosome 1. Given the recurrent recruitment of gsdf as a sex-determining factor in teleosts, we designate the Y-linked copy gsdfY and identify it as the strongest candidate for the master sex-determining gene in common dab. Additional broad sex-associated differentiation on chromosome 19 was restricted to the Icelandic samples and may reflect population-specific expansion of the sex-linked region, although its structural basis remains unresolved. Together, these findings provide the first genomic characterization of sex determination in common dab and demonstrate how gene duplication and translocation can contribute to the evolution of novel sex-determining systems in flatfishes.

items.title: The neural circuit implementation of distributional reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Distributional reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms outperform traditional RL by representing the full probability distribution of future outcomes rather than its mean. Neural signatures consistent with distributional coding have been observed in dopamine neurons and in striatal value representations. However, how distributional RL is implemented within the anatomical circuit organization of the basal ganglia remains unknown. Uncovering how representations of outcome distributions are organized across brain circuits has broad implications for both fundamental and clinical neuroscience, providing new insights into how the brain represents uncertainty and how these representations shape risk-sensitive learning and decision-making. Here, we investigated how representations of outcome distributions are organized across dopamine projections to the striatum by combining striatum-wide fiber photometry of dopamine axonal activity with Neuropixels recordings from projection-defined dopamine neurons. We found that distributional reward prediction error signals are preferentially encoded in lateral ventral striatum-projecting dopamine neurons, but that reward distribution information is shared between the ventral and the dorsal striatum. Additionally, an anatomical gradient of optimism in the midbrain supports the diversity of value predictions required for distributional RL. Our findings extend the actor-critic framework proposed for the basal ganglia by revealing distributional prediction errors in a subpopulation of mesolimbic dopamine neurons capable of training parallel striatal regions thought to implement different types of behavioral control.

items.title: Open-BEATBox: an open-source autonomous operant chamber for high-throughput data acquisition of complex behaviour
items.abstract: Behavioural neuroscience increasingly relies on rodent models to investigate the neural mechanisms underlying cognition in health and disease. However, conventional operant testing is typically restricted to short daily sessions that require frequent experimenter intervention and often rely on food or water restriction. These constraints limit behavioural sampling, disrupt natural activity patterns, and introduce variability associated with handling and experimental schedules.Here, we present the Open Platform for Experimental Neuroscience Behavioural and Autonomous Box (Open-BEATBox), an open-source, autonomous home-cage platform that enables continuous, self-paced assessment of complex cognitive behaviour in mice. By allowing animals to live in the testing environment throughout the experiment, Open-BEATBox supports longitudinal behavioural assessment across different cognitive tasks while minimizing experimenter intervention and preserving natural circadian activity. The platform is modular, customizable, and designed to accommodate a broad range of operant paradigms and integration with chronic neural recording and neuromodulation technologies.Using a visual reversal-learning task, we show that continuous autonomous testing generates approximately ten times more completed trials during reversal learning than conventional session-based protocols while reducing experimenter workload without evidence of major adverse effects on the welfare measures assessed. The flexibility of the platform further enables implementation of additional cognitive paradigms, including uncertainty-based decision-making tasks.Together, Open-BEATBox provides an accessible open platform for longitudinal cognitive phenotyping, facilitating the collection of large longitudinal behavioural datasets and creating new opportunities to combine continuous behavioural assessment with modern systems neuroscience approaches.

items.title: Protecting host mitochondria with vitamin B3 preserves bioenergetics and thermogenesis during antibiotic treatment
items.abstract: Antibiotics that target bacterial translation can also impair mitochondrial function because mitochondria retain bacterial-like ribosomes. As antibiotic resistance continues to increase and the use of several broad-spectrum antibiotics has been limited by their mitochondrial toxicity, there is a growing need to understand their off-target effects in host physiology, and to identify strategies that can mitigate antibiotic-induced mitochondrial dysfunction. We demonstrate that antibiotic chloramphenicol (CA) induces a dose-dependent reduction in mitochondrial respiration and mitochondrial thermogenesis in Drosophila S2 cells, human HEK293T cells and in developing Drosophila larvae. In vivo, CA exposure triggers female-biased aberrant innate immune activation of hosts carrying naturally occurring mitochondrial rRNA variants. Metabolomic profiling revealed alterations in vitamin B3 metabolism in Drosophila during and following CA exposure. Among the vitamin B3 vitamers examined, nicotinamide (NAM) exhibited the strongest protective effect, mitigating the CA-induced impairments in mitochondrial respiration and thermogenesis, as well as aberrant immune activation. We identify mitochondrial thermogenesis as a previously unrecognized target of antibiotic-induced mitochondrial perturbation and a sensitive marker of mitochondrial stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that co-supplementation of CA with NAM mitigates antibiotic-induced mitochondrial toxicity through evolutionarily conserved mitochondrial pathways. Finally, we establish Drosophila as a powerful model for investigating antibiotic-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and for developing therapeutic strategies to protect host mitochondria during antibiotic treatment.

items.title: LIMBER: A Hybrid RNA Foundation Model for Predicting and Understanding RNA Structure and Function
items.abstract: RNA foundation models offer a promising route to decoding the relationships between RNA sequence, structure and function, yet how model architecture shapes the acquisition and organization of biological information remains poorly understood. Here we introduce Layer-Interleaved Mamba-Bidirectional Encoder for RNA (LIMBER), a hybrid foundation model integrating bidirectional self-attention with selective state-space modeling, pre-trained on 40.5 million non-coding RNA sequences. With task-specific fine-tuning, LIMBER achieves leading performance on secondary-structure prediction and non-coding RNA classification benchmarks, while demonstrating strong transferability to translation-related tasks and RNA--small-molecule interaction prediction. Beyond model development, we establish a unified, task-agnostic framework to systematically evaluate and interpret the biological knowledge intrinsically acquired by RNA foundation models. This framework validates LIMBER's strong capabilities in recovering RNA structures and predicting mutational effects, while uncovering a hierarchical, task-dependent organization of biological information across model layers. In addition, we demonstrate distinct scaling behaviors across structural, evolutionary, and functional capabilities by training and evaluating a broad panel of model variants spanning model capacity, training duration, and dataset size. Taken together, these findings establish LIMBER as a versatile RNA foundation model and provide insight into how architectural design, internal representations and scaling shape the learning of RNA sequence-structure-function relationships.

items.title: Uncovering Viral Signals Across Cell Populations in Colorectal Cancer
items.corresponding_institution: University of Hawaii John A. Burns School of Medicine
items.abstract: Viral sequences have been detected in colorectal cancer, but their cellular and anatomical distribution remains poorly resolved. We aimed to establish a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon. We repurposed human-unmapped reads from single-cell RNA sequencing libraries generated in ten publicly available studies. We retained cell-barcode and unique molecular identifier information, removed duplicate molecules, and aligned reads to a curated human-associated viral reference using three aligners. Viral signals were analysed across cell types, tissue conditions, and colorectal segments. We used participant-grouped repeated cross-validation to evaluate tissue-condition classification and screened an independent paired colorectal cancer proteomics cohort for compatible peptide matches. The study included 547 libraries from 112 participants, including 49 with matched colorectal cancer and tumour-adjacent normal samples, and approximately 415,000 cells spanning ten major cell populations. Viral reference-associated RNA signals differed across epithelial, immune, stromal, and vascular compartments, tissue conditions, and anatomical regions of the colon. Of 318 independent healthy-reference viral-load comparisons, seven involving six virus-cell-type groups remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, including plasma-cell HHV-7 and HHV-6B and mast-cell HCV-2. Cell-type-resolved viral features distinguished colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon in participant-grouped validation; random forest achieved a macro-AUC of 0.957 (SD 0.028), with HERV-K113 as the leading quantitative feature. An independent proteomic screen identified peptide matches compatible with 20 candidate viral groups. We established a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal tissue conditions and anatomical regions. By identifying candidate viral signals in epithelial and immune compartments, this map provides a basis for investigating virus-host pathways involved in tumour biology, immune regulation, and antigen-presentation states, and could help prioritise future combination strategies pairing virus-directed or virus-mimetic approaches with standard treatment or immune checkpoint blockade.

items.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale
items.abstract: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundation models, we adapted Cellpose-SAM, raising cell segmentation F1 from 0.37 to 0.84 and recovering cell compositions concordant with matched single-nucleus RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics. Across 14,765 images from 69 postmortem donors, identical Alzheimer's disease pathology models found no significant associations after false discovery rate correction using zero-shot masks, versus four using fine-tuned masks; three linked higher OLIG2-positive fractions to greater neurofibrillary tangle and plaque burden. Using the fine-tuned masks, a graph attention network over nuclear neighborhoods classified four cell types without marker information, and differential expression analysis linked cell morphology to gene expression. This provides a pipeline for fine-tuning foundation models to segment complex tissues, enabling biological discovery in spatial proteomics at the population scale.

items.title: Evaluation design shapes estimates of cross-donor generalization in single-cell classification of cell-type
items.abstract: Motivation: Single-cell cell-type classifiers are often evaluated using random cell-level splits, although cells from the same donor are not independent. We asked how evaluation design affects estimates of cross-donor generalization. Results: Across PBMC and lung datasets, random cell-level splitting consistently yielded higher macro F1 than donor-held-out evaluation across multiple expression representations. This gap persisted after batch covariate adjustment and donor-level mixed-effects modeling. In contrast, evaluation gaps were generally minimal in highly separable, trivially easy kidney, pancreas, and blood classification settings and in a randomized-label setting with no meaningful predictive signal. These results show that evaluation bias depends on the underlying classification difficulty and that donor-held-out evaluation is necessary when claims concern generalization to unseen individuals. Availability and Implementation: Code and analyses are available on GitHub at https://github.com/danielchen05/scRNA-cross-donor-generalization/. Processed data are archived at Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19717558. Contact: ajbattle@jhu.edu

items.title: EWSR1::ATF1 hyperactivation via TRIM11 depletion triggers lethal metabolic rewiring in clear cell sarcoma
items.abstract: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is an ultra-rare and aggressive soft tissue sarcoma driven by the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion oncoprotein. Currently, no effective and well-tolerated treatment options are available to CCS patients. Direct inhibition of fusion transcription factors is precluded by the absence of defined ligand-binding pockets, whereas their abundance is under the control of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), offering an alternative avenue for biology-guided treatment. Here we show the abundance of EWSR1::ATF1 is tightly regulated by the UPS, and that release of this constraint is lethal to CCS cells. A reporter-based CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screen of UPS components identified TRIM11 as an E3 ligase that regulates turnover of EWSR1::ATF1, which it recognises as a neosubstrate without altering wild-type EWSR1 or ATF1. Depletion of TRIM11 increased nuclear fusion protein abundance, amplified the fusion-driven transcriptional programs and reduced viability. Proteomic analysis identified the cataplerotic enzyme phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1), a direct EWSR1::ATF1 target, as the key mediator of lethal effects of fusion hyperactivation. Extracellular flux analysis, isotope tracing and quantitative metabolomics revealed excessive cataplerotic carbon withdrawal and impaired oxidative phosphorylation as the underlying mechanism. In patient tumors, high PCK1 expression associated with metastatic transcriptome programs and disease presentation, as well as shorter survival. Taken together, we report that hyperactivation of EWSR1::ATF1 opens a metabolic vulnerability, establishing TRIM11 as an actionable dependency and PCK1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker in CCS.

items.title: A distinct chondrogenic progenitor population from human umbilical cord derived mesenchymal stromal cells for osteoarthritis therapy
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Clinical Medicine, Zhanjiang Central Hospital, Guangdong Medical University
items.abstract: Stem cell-based cartilage regeneration remains constrained by functional heterogeneity and phenotypic drift in conventional cell sources, compromising durable structural repair. Human umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (UC-MSCs) represent an accessible, off-the-shelf cell source; however, their broad clinical utility is hampered by cellular heterogeneity, leaving the key chondrogenic subpopulation responsible for cartilage repair unresolved. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics with functional assays, we identified and prospectively isolated a distinct, highly expandable subpopulation of skeletal stem cell-like progenitors (U-CPCs) from the human umbilical cord, establishing an extra-skeletal cell source uniquely primed for joint restoration. Single-cell transcriptomics reveal their inherent regulatory landscape, uncovering a distinct transcriptional state uniquely primed for chondrogenesis. In comparison with conventional stem cells and other tissue-derived SSC-like populations (from umbilical cord, bone marrow, adipose tissue, and dental pulp), U-CPCs exhibit a markedly enhanced chondrogenic capacity. In both a mouse cartilage injury model and a rat osteoarthritis model, the administration of U-CPCs effectively mitigates joint degeneration and drives the restoration of a structurally sound, hyaline-like matrix. Mechanistically, U-CPCs secrete extracellular vesicles enriched with microRNA Let-7a-5p, which specifically modulates DUSP7/MAPK/ERK signaling in recipient chondrocytes, thereby restoring extracellular matrix homeostasis and promoting cartilage repair. By characterizing these specialized extra-skeletal progenitors and elucidating both their intrinsic chondrogenic priming and paracrine regulation of host tissue, this study establishes U-CPCs as a robust, lineage-restricted cellular source for osteoarthritis therapy.

items.title: Urban enrichment of molestus ancestry and opposing temperature clines in a metropolitan Culex pipiens hybrid zone
items.abstract: Hybridization between ecologically distinct lineages can fuel rapid adaptation when introgressed alleles are locally favored. The North American Culex pipiens assemblage, a principal West Nile virus vector east of the Mississippi, comprises three lineages---temperate Cx. pipiens f. pipiens, urban-specialist Cx. pipiens f. molestus, and subtropical Cx. quinquefasciatus---that meet in a mid-Atlantic hybrid zone where temperature and urbanization gradients intersect. Using whole-genome Pool-seq of 24 field populations and three lineage-reference pools across the Baltimore--Washington corridor, we find a weakly differentiated, Cx. pipiens f. pipiens-like background, richer in molestus- and quinquefasciatus-like ancestry toward the warmer end of the corridor. Urbanization impacts allele frequencies across the genome: molestus-like ancestry rises with impervious surface, independently of temperature and position, while Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry does not. An 11.6 Mb chromosome 3 inversion is molestus-like in every population, most of all in urban ones, and tracks genome-wide molestus-like ancestry. Temperature acts locus by locus. On chromosome 1, a cluster of six CYP6 paralogs, a family implicated in insecticide resistance and thermal-stress response, shows rising Cx. quinquefasciatus-like ancestry and read depth with temperature. A chromosome 2 interval centered on a Yan ortholog, a repressor of cell differentiation, shows non-quinquefasciatus ancestry increasing with temperature, consistent with selection against Cx. quinquefasciatus-like introgression. Urban populations therefore carry more ancestry from the human-commensal lineage, while temperature moves Cx. quinquefasciatus ancestry both ways at individual loci. Both molestus and Cx. quinquefasciatus donors carry human-contact traits, so these patterns bear on how warming and urbanization will reshape arboviral risk.

items.title: Time-resolved single-cell screening reveals the dynamic regulatory architecture of human cardiogenesis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Genetics, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, CA, USA
items.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) originates during early embryogenesis, yet when disease genes act cannot be determined from existing data. Human fetal heart atlases lack critical time points, and perturbation screens that systematically assess gene function currently profile at most a few time points. Here we combined single-cell CRISPR screening of 400 disease-relevant genes in cardioids, sampled daily over seven developmental days (~975,000 cells), with a matched multiome atlas. Perturbation phenotypes were strongly dependent on developmental stage. Perturbations that reshaped cell-fate allocation or gene expression were enriched for CHD-linked genes, and most acted already during progenitor stages. Timing was largely independent of the target gene's own expression, marking instead when a cell state became functionally dependent on it, and some effects persisted after expression declined. Consensus gene regulatory networks integrating perturbation and multiome data recovered stage-specific regulators and nominated HOXB2 and HOXB3 as candidate cardiac regulators. Many perturbations converged on shared downstream programmes, which were reorganised through differentiation. Effects correlated in progenitors were maintained in differentiated cells, split into distinct programmes, converged with other perturbations or disappeared entirely, indicating that gene function is highly context dependent. Beyond advancing our understanding of the developmental regulatory logic underlying CHD, our work provides a resource for developing context-dependent models for in silico prediction of perturbation effects.

items.title: Homogeneous network inference for subtype-stratified master regulator analysis in cancer
items.abstract: Master-regulator analysis of 34 TCGA tumour cohorts (cancer x molecular subtype; n between 27 and 562 tumours) requires one regulatory network per cohort. Mutual-information (MI) networks inferred with ARACNe3 are the usual choice, but they are not available for the smallest cohorts; filling the gap with correlation networks would mix two methods inside the very comparison between subtypes that the analysis is meant to make. We therefore infer every network with a single procedure, fixed-size Spearman regulons (FSR): rank correlation between regulator and target, a fixed effect-size threshold rho >= 0.2, the per-target data-processing-inequality (DPI) pruning implemented in corto, bootstrap support, and truncation to the 100 best-supported targets per regulator. We quantify what this choice concedes and what it provides, labelling each claim as a standard result, a heuristic, or an empirical result. Rank correlation is more powerful than the MI estimators we simulated for n = 95) they overlap in 0.7 of the top-20 regulators, the same as two filterings of the same ARACNe3 network, although the rank correlation of the full score vector shows a measurable method effect in the tail. Subsampling large real cohorts indicates that networks inferred from fewer than 60 tumours do not reliably reproduce their own cohort's master regulators, that 60-100 is a grey zone, and that a cancer-wide network does not rescue small subtypes. We present FSR as an adequate and uniform choice for multi-cohort analysis, not as a statistically superior one.

items.title: Working memory capacity is linked to directed exploration: behavioral, computational, and electrophysiological evidence
items.abstract: Balancing the exploitation of known rewards against the exploration of uncertain options is central to adaptive decision making, yet the cognitive limits on strategic exploration are poorly understood. Directed exploration, the deliberate sampling of uncertain options for information, may depend on working memory (WM), but whether WM capacity (WMC) is selectively related to it, and through which processes, is unknown. 52 participants from the upper and lower tails of an operation-span distribution (26 high-WMC, 26 low-WMC) performed an adapted Horizon Task during EEG recording. We combined behavioral strategy classification, hierarchical Bayesian reinforcement learning, stimulus-locked event-related potentials (ERPs), and an exploratory Bayesian mediation analysis. High-WMC participants showed more directed exploration and less exploitation, with no group difference in random exploration. A model in which accumulated sampling history discounts option value best explained choices in both groups, and the discounting parameter {omega} was larger in the high-WMC group. Statistically, {omega} accounted for the association between WMC and directed exploration (indirect effect ab = 0.64, 95% CrI [0.28, 1.05]). Frontocentral P2 amplitude (180 to 280 ms) during directed exploration was larger in the high-WMC group, and the P2 difference between directed exploration and exploitation correlated with behavioral preference for directed exploration (r = .29, p = .040). These findings suggest that individual differences in exploration may reflect not only the willingness to seek information but also the capacity to use what has been sampled. The WMC-related difference lay in information use rather than choice noise and was already visible in early option evaluation.

items.title: Brain Network Dynamics from Neuronal Avalanches for Longitudinal Motor-Imagery Decoding
items.corresponding_institution: Sorbonne University, Paris Brain Institute, INRIA Paris
items.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) offer opportunities for personalized neurorehabilitation, but inter-session variability, repeated calibration, and the need for expert supervision limit their use beyond supervised settings. We propose a longitudinal BCI framework that integrates neuronal avalanches dynamics, reflecting cascades of propagation neural activity, with graph-theory and data-driven region of interest analysis to extract computationally efficient and neuro-physiological interpretable features. Source-reconstructed EEG from 20 BCI-naive participants performing right-hand motor imagery (MI) and rest across four training sessions was represented by a directed weighted connectivity network based on neuronal avalanches. Local, mesoscopic, and global network measures revealed task-related changes predominantly in contralateral sensorimotor regions and distributed reorganisation across training. We modelled here the learning-related evolution of feature distributions across previous sessions and used this trajectory to predict class-conditional distributions in an unseen fourth session, anticipating future brain states before new session calibration. PageRank-based ROI selection achieved an AUC of 73.5 +/- 7.9%, compared with 64.5 +/- 10.6% using all ROIs, while reducing computational time by approximately 39% relative to performance-driven selection. The proposed framework provides interpretable, compact descriptions of avalanche propagation and exploits training-related changes for prospective decoding. Moving spatial selection and model optimization to an initial offline phase may reduce subsequent calibration demands and facilitate more autonomous BCI use.

items.title: NeuroDisco: Interfacing neuronal populations - cell by cell, millisecond by millisecond, day by day
items.corresponding_institution: Goettingen Campus Institute for Dynamics of Biological Networks, University of Goettingen, Goettingen, Germany
items.abstract: Neuronal cultures offer comprehensive access to living networks, but their value as functional models is limited by synchronized bursts that drive pathologically strong neuronal depolarization. Theory attributes such bursting to a lack of external input. Here we present NeuroDiscos, compact {micro}LED and OLED projectors that operate inside standard incubators and deliver patterned, long-term optogenetic stimulation, synchronized with submillisecond precision to multi-electrode array recordings. Weak, uncorrelated NeuroDisco stimulation dispersed the bursts but left the population firing rate largely unchanged. In this asynchronous regime, neuronal activity reproducibly follows the weak stimulation, and stimulus-response relations characterize receptive fields and putative functional connections. At hardware costs of {euro}500-1,000, NeuroDiscos offer a scalable route to functional characterization of primary and patient-derived cultures.

items.title: LuCEMe: An accessible luciferase-based method to functionally assess cellular metabolism across model systems
items.corresponding_institution: Catholic University of Louvain, Universite Catholique de Louvain
items.abstract: Metabolic profiling approaches such as extracellular flux analysis, metabolomics, stable isotope tracing and cytometry-based assays have transformed our understanding of cellular metabolism in physiological and pathological contexts. However, most techniques require specialized equipment or reagents, and do not allow differential metabolic analysis in intact multicellular systems. Here, we present LuCEMe, a luciferase-based metabolic phenotyping approach that combines acute metabolic perturbations with quantitative ATP measurements to resolve glycolytic and mitochondrial dependencies and capacities under native culture conditions, including in complex coculture and ex vivo systems without prior cell separation. The assay can also be adapted to increase metabolic resolution and distinguish between glycolytic activity, glucose oxidation and fatty acid/amino acid-driven mitochondrial ATP production. We use LuCEMe to reveal profound metabolic differences between leukemia cells cocultured with macrophages, stromal cells or adipocytes, and demonstrate distinct metabolic rewiring during macrophage polarization, osteogenic and adipogenic differentiation, and T cell activation. Ex vivo LuCEMe analysis identified a particular metabolic adaptation associated with chemotherapy response in acute myeloid leukemia that was not evident from conventional analyses. LuCEMe thus provides an accessible, robust and versatile framework for direct functional metabolic phenotyping across in vitro, ex vivo, and multicellular systems that complements existing metabolic profiling technologies.

items.title: In situ single-cell CRISPR screens uncover context-dependent rewiring of glioma states and immune recruitment
items.abstract: In vivo single-cell CRISPR screens can resolve perturbation effects in native tissues, but few combine cell-type-restricted delivery, somatic tumor initiation, and combinatorial perturbation. Here we developed an RCAS-TVA-based single-cell CRISPR screening approach coupling oncogenic transformation with single- or dual-guide perturbation in defined neural progenitors. In glioma, tumor suppressor loss produced distinct genotype-dependent transcriptional states, including an NF1-loss-associated increase in mesenchymal programs. Introducing a fixed Cdkn2a(ARF) perturbation altered malignant-cell state composition, immune-cell abundance, and the effects of additional tumor-suppressor perturbations, including increased representation of Pten- and Rb1-deficient cells, suggestive of the relief of an ARF-dependent genetic barrier. These perturbations converged on transcriptional states resembling pharmacologic p53 activation in human glioblastoma. Across mouse tumors and human glioblastoma models, this response was associated with increased astrocyte-like state representation. These findings establish a framework for single-cell analysis of context-dependent somatic perturbations during tumor initiation in vivo.

items.title: spSheaf: sheaf-theoretic spatial domain inference from raw molecules without cell segmentation
items.abstract: Spatial-transcriptomics pipelines usually require cell segmentation and discard 20-60% of transcripts. We introduce spSheaf, a segmentation-free spatial domain inference method built on cellular sheaf theory. Within a domain, neighbouring regions have compatible local expression structure; across a transition between programs they remain discordant after alignment of their local subspaces. spSheaf quantifies this alignment-adjusted disagreement and attenuates transitions during clustering. On the MERFISH hypothalamus benchmark it attains mean ARI 0.571 and NMI 0.655, ranks first of twelve on NMI, and leads SSAM, Points2Regions and FICTURE by 0.16 ARI on held-out slices. On three further annotated sections, every method tuned, it leads on one, ties on one and trails SSAM by 0.06 ARI. The sheaf weighting adds +0.102 ARI where domains are distinct programs and is neutral on laminar cortex. One domain above the annotated count, it divides the BST into the territories of two atlas neuronal populations on both adjacent sections.

items.title: LingoCell interprets gene perturbations through natural language and tissue niches
items.corresponding_institution: Human Genome Center, The Institute of Medical Science, The University of Tokyo, Tokyo, Japan; Department of Computational Biology and Medical Science, The Unive
items.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are general tools for resolving cell identities and disease states, but struggle to interpret changes in expression magnitude in biological language, to transfer to sparse spatial measurements, and to explain cellular niches. We introduce LingoCell, a foundation model connecting single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. It aligns cell representations with language while keeping gene expression editable, supporting cell annotation, cross-batch integration, description generation, and disease-language readouts of single-gene and combinatorial in silico perturbations. Extended to tissues, it annotates cells without single-cell references, learns identity-conditioned niche embeddings, and performs spatial in silico perturbation by replacing and editing neighbor expression. In lung adenocarcinoma, LingoCell revealed synergistic disease responses to jointly weakening alveolar differentiation programs and strengthening malignant programs. In colorectal cancer, it revealed different programs conveyed by the same fibroblast state to T cells, macrophages, and tumor cells. LingoCell provides a unified framework for prioritizing target combinations and stromal intervention programs.

items.title: Membrane Geometry Reveals Strengths and Limitations of AlphaFold-Predicted Transmembrane Protein Complexes
items.abstract: High-confidence protein complex predictions do not necessarily represent physically or biologically plausible assemblies. This limitation is particularly relevant for transmembrane (TM) proteins, whose interactions are constrained by the lipid bilayer. Here, we systematically evaluated membrane compatibility in the recently expanded AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, analysing 189,469 high-confidence AlphaFold-Multimer TM-TM complexes and additional TM-soluble assemblies. Most predictions exhibited plausible membrane geometry: among 125,657 evaluable complexes with TM proteins possessing more than two TM helices, 95.4% had joint hydrophobic thicknesses within the expected range of 15-35 angstroms. Nevertheless, some complexes displayed substantial inconsistencies in membrane positioning or protomer orientation despite favourable prediction confidence. Interactions between TM proteins, particularly those containing only one or two TM helices, were frequently dominated by extramembrane contacts. Among TM-soluble complexes, 77.4% showed no penetration of the soluble partner into the hydrophobic membrane core. We further investigated whether AlphaFold3 (AF3) could overcome limitations of AlphaFold-Multimer. Although AF3 recovered an experimentally supported SERCA-phospholamban interaction, it failed to reproduce the cholesterol-mediated norepinephrine transporter homodimer. A benchmark of 173 cholesterol-containing membrane protein targets further revealed limited accuracy in predicting cholesterol-binding poses, particularly for structures released after the AF3 training cutoff. Together, these findings demonstrate that membrane-specific geometric constraints provide a valuable complement to conventional confidence metrics and highlight the persistent challenges of predicting assemblies involving lipids.

items.title: Development of a Thyroid Cancer to Lung Metastasis-on-a-Chip Model
items.abstract: Background: Study of the metastatic cascade in differentiated non-medullary thyroid cancer (NMTC) is hampered by the relative lack of preclinical models that metastasize from primary tumors to other organs. We previously identified regulator of calcineurin 1 isoform 4 (RCAN1.4) as a suppressor of NMTC cell growth, invasion, and metastasis using in vitro systems and tail vein injections in immunocompromised mice. We then reported a microfluidic device mimicking the mouse tail vein injection where cancer cells were allowed to flow directly to lung organoid constructs. We now report the development of a full primary tumor to lung metastasis-on-a-chip (MOC) model for TC. Methods: Resin molds for primary and secondary sites connected by a channel were 3D printed and filled with polydimethylsiloxane to create a molded silicone elastomer. The primary site was seeded with an organoid composed of a hyaluronic acid and collagen-based hydrogel into which FTC236 and HTh74 NMTC cells with and without knockdown of RCAN1.4 were engrafted. The secondary site consisted of a hydrogel organoid into which bronchial epithelial cells and lung fibroblasts were seeded. Culture media was circulated and movement of NMTC cells to the secondary site was assessed. Results: Both cell lines that expressed RCAN 1.4 metastasized to the secondary lung site. RCAN1.4-reduced FTC236 cells had increased metastatic behavior vs controls while HTh74 was less affected by RCAN1.4 loss, similar to prior studies. To determine if the MOC could be used for incorporation of immune components and therapeutic modeling, NK-92 cells were added and were shown to be reduce metastases for both cell lines in the presence or absence of RCAN1.4. Analysis of MOC circulating fluid revealed elevated levels of granzyme B, consistent with NK-92 cell activation. Cytokine profiling identified elevated probable NMTC and NK-92-derived factors. Conclusions: These results indicate that NMTC metastatic behavior can be modeled using a novel MOC system for mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies.

items.title: Miniaturized Traceless Staudinger Ligation Enables Direct-to-Biology Screening of Potent BRD4 PROTACs
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Goethe University Frankfurt
items.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) approaches accelerate PROTAC discovery by enabling biological screening of crude reaction mixtures without intermediate purification. However, the range of chemical transformations compatible with these workflows remains limited. Herein, we establish a miniaturized, base-free traceless Staudinger ligation platform diversifying linker chemistry for a preexisting library of E3-ligand-linker adducts bearing azide moieties. As a proof-of-concept target, BRD4 was chosen, yielding amide-linked BRD4-targeting PROTACs. By combining phosphine-functionalized JQ1 derivatives with 72 selected azide building blocks, reactions were performed on a 5 L scale in 384-well plates, achieving a mean LC-MS conversion of approximately 65%. Spiking experiments confirmed that the phosphine starting materials had no significant impact on BRD4 degradation, supporting the direct biological evaluation of crude reaction mixtures in the presence of residual starting material. Cellular screening identified 23 hits at 250 nM screening concentration, reducing BRD4 levels below 40%. Two resynthesized and purified PROTACs were subsequently validated, displaying pDC50 values of 8.2 and 7.0 and a Dmax of 90% and 96%, respectively. This work establishes traceless Staudinger ligation as a complementary D2B strategy for the rapid discovery of amide-linked PROTACs.

items.title: Developing a Multimodal miR-15a Mimic to Overcome Gemcitabine and RAS(ON) Inhibitor Daraxonrasib Resistance in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Gemcitabine remains a mainstay of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) treatment, while the RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib has recently demonstrated improved survival in previously treated metastatic disease. However, acquired resistance to both therapies remains a major clinical challenge. Here, we developed MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a, a multimodal microRNA (miRNA)-based therapeutic, by chemically modifying tumor-suppressive miR-15a with methotrexate (MTX), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and gemcitabine (Gem) to combine sequence-specific gene regulation with disruption of nucleotide metabolism. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a exhibited low-nanomolar potency across five PDAC cell lines and retained activity in gemcitabine- and daraxonrasib-resistant models under vehicle-free conditions, substantially exceeding that of stoichiometrically matched free antimetabolites. Treatment induced S-phase accumulation, increased DNA damage and apoptosis, and suppressed checkpoint and survival-associated proteins, including WEE1, CHK1, YAP1, and BCL-2. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed increased DNA replication, replication-stress, and repair-associated programs, together with reduced oncogenic signaling. In gemcitabine-resistant cells, treatment restored the gemcitabine-activating enzyme dCK, reduced ABCC1 and ABCC3 expression, and suppressed resistance-associated signaling programs, indicating partial remodeling of resistance-associated pathways. MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a also synergized with daraxonrasib (mean Bliss synergy score, 22.52) and activated tumor-cell-intrinsic STING-TBK1 signaling, accompanied by increased interferon stimulated gene expression and IFN-{beta} and CXCL10 secretion. Finally, MTX-5-FU-Gem-miR-15a retained low-nanomolar potency in three patient-derived PDAC organoids and significantly suppressed metastatic tumor growth in vivo at 4 mg/kg. Together, these findings support a multimodal miRNA therapeutic strategy that combines replication-associated DNA damage, checkpoint protein suppression, and innate immune activation-associated responses to target therapeutic resistance in PDAC.

items.title: Maternal deprivation impairs social recognition by diminishing the number of adult-born granule cells in the dentate gyrus
items.abstract: Childhood neglect increases the likelihood of developing neuropsychiatric disease in adulthood. Maternal separation and early weaning (MSEW), a rodent model of maternal deprivation, was used to investigate effects on social recognition, a commonly impaired function in neuropsychiatric disorders in humans. We found that in adulthood, MSEW male mice showed social recognition impairments, and that MSEW female mice showed greater preference fo social novelty. MSEW male, but not female, mice had diminished numbers of adult-born granule cells (abGCs) in the dentate gyrus, as well as a lower density of abGC axons in the CA2 region compared to controls. MSEW males also showed a reduced rate of sharp wave ripples (SWRs) in the CA2 region in response to novel mouse exposure, as well as a reduction in differential SWR rates in response to novel and familiar mouse exposure. Living in an enriched environment restored the number of abGCs in the dentate gyrus of MSEW males to control levels and improved social recognition. Furthermore, chemogenetic activation of 4-6 week old, but not older, abGCs in a double transgenic model improved social recognition and partially restored CA2 SWR patterns in MSEW mice. These findings suggest that MSEW impairs social recognition through diminished adult neurogenesis, which can be restored in adulthood by living in a proneurogenic environment or by increasing the activity of existing abGCs.

items.title: Pupil size reflects effort but not motor fatigability during a sustained motor task
items.abstract: Pupil size has been shown to reflect physical effort during brief, discrete motor tasks. It remains unknown whether pupil size similarly scales with effort during sustained repetitive movement, or whether it also reflects the accumulation of motor fatigability, a reduction in motor performance during prolonged movements. In our previous work, sustained maximal tapping induced motor slowing, a subtype of motor fatigability, characterized by decreasing movement speed and associated with increased antagonistic muscle coactivation. Next to these behavioural effects, pupil initially dilated and then gradually decreased over time. Whether this temporal change in pupil size is shaped by physical effort alone or also by motor fatigability remains unclear. Here, we combined a repetitive wrist tapping paradigm with force measurement, electromyography, and pupillometry, and paced participants at three different tapping speeds to dissociate physical effort from motor slowing, which has been shown to be speed-dependent. Fatigability-related motor slowing emerged selectively at the fastest speed. Moreover, we showed that antagonistic muscle coactivation increased more steeply at faster speeds, even in the absence of motor slowing, suggesting it may reflect an early change in motor control. While we found clear evidence that pupil size scaled with overall tapping speed, we did not find evidence that the temporal change of the pupil was pacing-dependent. These findings extend the pupil effort relationship to sustained, dynamic motor tasks and suggest that pupil size is a marker of physical effort but not motor fatigability during sustained repetitive movement.

items.title: Multiplexed mapping of long-range projections with FluoCode, a combinatorial fluorescent barcoding system
items.abstract: Comprehensive mapping of long-range projections remains a major challenge in neuroscience. Conventional virus tracing labels only one or a few pathways per animal, and inter-individual comparison requires registering whole-brain images to a standard atlas. However, inter-individual variability in morphology and wiring limits fine-scale mapping. Here we report "FluoCode", a combinatorial fluorescent barcoding system for multiplexed projection mapping within single animals. We developed adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors that express two of seven different fluorescent proteins, yielding 21 distinct color codes, and a "FluoCode Reader" that automatically classifies neurite signals by color combinations and morphology. Using FluoCode, we mapped projections from up to 21 cortical areas to subcortical regions in individual mice, revealing fine-scale topographic maps in small subcortical nuclei. In the marmoset, mapping from the primary visual cortex demonstrated topographic projections in higher visual areas and thalamic nuclei. FluoCode thus enables fine-scale, within-animal comparison of long-range projections in rodents and primates.

items.title: PhyMorphS: A Physics-Guided Framework for Mesh-Based Morphological Synthesis of White Matter Microstructures
items.abstract: Numerical phantoms provide controlled 3D representations of brain tissue microstructure for developing and evaluating biophysical models of diffusion-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI). Existing phantom synthesizers employ different geometric primitives and optimization strategies to generate densely packed substrates with diverse axonal morphologies. However, direct deformation of axonal surfaces under mechanical constraints remains less explored. We propose PhyMorphS, a mesh-based framework in which axonal morphology emerges through physics-guided growth and interactions with the local microstructural environment, without constraining cross-sections to predefined symmetric shapes. In PhyMorphS, axons, myelin sheaths, and cell bodies are represented by triangle meshes, while a mass-spring system and collision-resolution scheme guide iterative axonal growth under mechanical and packing constraints. This enables irregular, asymmetric, and non-convex cross-sections, longitudinal diameter variation, and user-defined morphological alterations such as axonal beading and myelin layer decompaction. We evaluate PhyMorphS against large-scale X-ray nano-holotomography segmentations of real 3D axons from four white matter regions with distinct fiber organizations. The synthesized axons reproduce key region-specific morphological characteristics and achieve high packing densities, while the parallelized implementation scales approximately linearly with axon count in the generation voxel. By reproducing the geometric variability observed in real WM tissue, PhyMorphS provides controlled substrates for investigating how realistic morphology influences simulated dMRI signals, testing the geometric assumptions of biophysical microstructure models, and generating diverse paired microstructure-signal datasets for training machine-learning models.

items.title: Somatic symptom burden is associated with anger internalization measured as reduced reactive aggression
items.corresponding_institution: aDepartment of Psychology, Keio University, 2-15-45 Mita, Minato-ku, Tokyo, 108-8345, Japan bJapan Society for the Promotion of Science, Kojimachi Business Cent
items.abstract: Difficulties in emotion regulation, including anger suppression, have been linked to more severe somatic symptoms in patients with chronic pain. Because this evidence comes mainly from clinical samples, it remains unclear whether such difficulties precede or follow symptom chronification. We examined whether somatic symptom burden is associated with reduced reactive aggression, as a behavioral marker of anger internalization. Forty-four healthy adults (25 females) completed the Taylor Aggression Paradigm, a competitive reaction-time task in which they selected noise intensity delivered to a fictitious opponent across three provocation conditions (low, moderate, and high). somatic symptom burden was evaluated using the Somatic Symptom Scale-8 (SSS-8) and Patient Health Questionnaire-15 (PHQ-15). Alexithymia was evaluated using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale (TAS-20). Participants with higher somatic symptom burden selected lower noise intensities overall, with significant differences at low and moderate provocation levels. Difficulty identifying feelings tended to be positively associated with somatic symptom burden, whereas alexithymia was not associated with reactive aggression. These findings suggest that inhibited retaliation, previously reported in chronic pain patients, may already be present in healthy individuals with higher somatic symptom burden, potentially aiding early identification of chronic pain risk. Difficulty distinguishing emotions from bodily sensations may also contribute to somatic symptom expression.

items.title: Computational model of developmental self-assembly of a cortical microcircuit
items.abstract: Cortical microcircuits emerge from local developmental interactions, yet large-scale computational models typically prescribe connectivity rather than explain its formation. Here we use BioDynaMo to simulate the self-assembly of ~70,000 cortical neurons from 1,200 progenitors in 3D physical space through migration, neurite growth and contact-based synapse formation. With one calibrated filling fraction per connection type, the locally formed synapses reproduce experimentally measured connectivity across 64 connection types (mean absolute error 0.0062) without prescribing individual connections. The grown spiking networks sustain stable, inhibition-dominated activity, and the same developmental rules, given different targets, generate both a canonical cortical microcircuit and a visual-cortex variant. Inverting the migration programme produces a reeler-like column whose aberrant connectivity destabilises network activity. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic link between local developmental processes and the emergence of cortical anatomy, connectivity and function.

items.title: Beyond Exploration: Heightened Recent Reward Reliance and Midfrontal Sensitivity to Outcome Differences in ADHD
items.abstract: Adaptive decision-making requires balancing the exploitation of known rewards with the exploration of alternative options, yet how attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) shapes this trade-off remains unclear. Using a restless four-armed bandit task and electroencephalography (EEG), we investigated the neural correlates of exploratory decisions and how recent rewards shape choice behavior and feedback processing in 23 adults with self-reported clinical ADHD diagnoses and 27 controls. Across 450 trials with dynamically changing payoffs, choices were classified against the highest last-observed payoff, and behavioral modeling quantified the influence of reward history on subsequent decisions. Contrary to our predictions, exploration rates, task performance, and neural differentiation between exploration and exploitation did not differ significantly between groups. However, adults with ADHD were more likely to repeat an option after high reward feedback and switch after low rewards, driven primarily by the immediately preceding outcome. At neural level, ADHD participants also showed greater midfrontal sensitivity to unsigned changes between consecutive payoffs, expressed in a feedback-evoked response spanning 280 to 568 ms and carried by slow activity below 2 Hz. Together, these findings dissociate the raw frequency of exploration from the dynamic weighting of recent outcomes in ADHD. Rather than reflecting an indiscriminate drive for novelty, behavior was characterized by heightened recent reward reliance paired with amplified slow-wave midfrontal sensitivity to outcome shifts. Crucially, this profile emerged without compromising overall performance, suggesting that, in this volatile environment, ADHD was associated with an increased weighting of recent outcomes rather than with a performance deficit.

items.title: Early visual experience redistributes cFos-tagged neurons toward the cortex while preserving presynaptic spatial stereotypy
items.abstract: The macroscale functional organization of the brain is spatially stereotyped across individuals, but whether this extends to finer spatial scales is not known. Furthermore, how experience shapes this organization across the brain remains unclear. To address this, we developed cFos promoter-driven reporter mouse lines that permanently label either the cell bodies or presynaptic terminals of neurons during defined temporal windows. Using serial two-photon tomography and voxel-wise statistics, we mapped brain-wide distributions of cFos-tagged somata or their presynaptic terminals during the first week of visual experience or its deprivation. We found that midbrain and subcortical regions show greater stereotypy for cFos-tagged neurons and their presynaptic terminals compared to cortical regions. This fine-scale spatial stereotypy remained largely preserved despite visual deprivation, which shifted the relative recruitment of cFos-tagged neurons from cortical toward the highly stereotyped midbrain and subcortical regions. Our findings identify heterogeneous, spatially constrained functional organization across the brain that is conserved across subjects yet accommodates experience-dependent reorganization of neuronal recruitment.

items.title: Geometry-Conditioned Hyperalignment for Generalizable EEG Decoding Across Datasets and Paradigms
items.corresponding_institution: ATR Brain Information Communication Research Laboratory Group, Advanced Telecommunications Research
items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) supports promising applications, but daily use remains limited by poor cross-subject and cross-dataset generalisation. That is because EEG recordings made with different electrode montages do not even share an observation space, and each subjects's leadfield projects the same neural sources onto the scalp differently. We present hTSMNet, which combines a novel geometry-conditioned hyperalignment frontend with a Riemannian symmetric positive-definite (SPD) manifold backbone that reduces the residual cross-subject distribution shift. From electrode coordinates alone, the frontend builds a linear map from any montage onto a fixed set of scalp anchors, placing every recording in one shared space. Because this map has no subjectspecific parameters, an unseen subject, dataset, or montage is aligned from its geometry alone, so transfer is zero-shot by construction. On a leave-one-dataset-out left-/right-hand motor-imagery (MI) benchmark across three datasets (172 subjects) and eight comparators, hTSMNet matches the strongest comparator at strict zero-shot, and attains the highest accuracy on every dataset once a few calibration trials for adjusting only final-layer classifier are available. We show that it orients the binary decision the same way in every dataset, so that a single linear rule learned on the source data is already correctly oriented on a held-out one. The same frozen MI-pretrained model also transfers across paradigms: with only a re-fit final-layer classifier, hTSMNet decodes mental workload and steady-state visual evoked potentials (SSVEP) well above chance, yet remains at chance on stimulus-locked event-related potentials (ERP). This dissociation follows from the architecture: covariance pooling reads oscillatory band power and is largely insensitive to the phase-locked potentials that ERP tasks depend on.
