Together, these findings establish ACE engineering as a strategy to enhance the production and antimicrobial function of human iPSC-derived neutrophils and support further preclinical development of engineered granulocyte therapies for severe drug-resistant infections.

items.title: An architectural RNA builds a reaction crucible through molecular concentration and activated enzyme selection
items.abstract: Architectural RNAs (arcRNAs) scaffold membraneless organelles (MLOs), yet how they organize functional proteins remains unclear. Nuclear stress bodies (nSBs), MLOs scaffolded by HSATIII arcRNAs, incorporate SRSFs during stress. During stress recovery, nSBs function as reaction crucibles that recruit the kinase CLK1 to accelerate SRSF rephosphorylation and normalize stress-induced splicing. Here, we identify the ASAP complex as a recruitment factor that recognizes Ser341-phosphorylated, catalytically activated CLK1. HSATIII-bound SRSFs recruit ASAP, assembling a platform for CLK1 recruitment. Biochemical reconstitution reveals that this platform enhances SRSF phosphorylation by concentrating SRSFs and CLK1 while selectively recruiting activated CLK1, establishing nSB reaction crucibles as molecular concentrators and selectors. The SRSF-ASAP-CLK1 interaction network is conserved between humans and mice, suggesting that primate-specific HSATIII arcRNAs co-opted this pre-existing network to establish reaction-crucible function in nSBs. Our findings reveal how arcRNAs organize functional proteins through quantitative enrichment and qualitative selection to build biochemically active MLOs.

items.title: Integrated exome-transcriptome analysis of a schizophrenia case with an exceptionally low polygenic risk score
items.abstract: Schizophrenia liability reflects both common polygenic variation and rarer variants of larger effect. We investigated a post-mortem schizophrenia case (SZ07) with a schizophrenia polygenic risk score below the first percentile among ancestry-matched cases, asking whether individual-level genomic and transcriptomic analyses could help identify potentially novel schizophrenia-relevant variants. We used exome analysis with multiple variant-prediction tools to generate a panel of variants and corresponding candidate genes potentially implicated in the pathological process in SZ07. The prioritised variants were then assessed using RNA sequencing of three cortical regions. Of these, only an IZUMO4 splice-acceptor variant showed direct RNA-level support. Beyond variant-specific analyses, we characterised broader transcriptomic abnormalities in the SZ07 brain. Pathway analysis of gene-level expression deviations implicated innate immune processes, calcium signalling, synaptic biology, and axon remodelling. Notably, compared with conventional single-sample biological pathway analysis, the analysis we used showed only a weak association with neuronal specificity, suggesting their reduced sensitivity to the main axis of variation related to cellular composition in bulk brain tissue gene expression data. Although the candidate genes showed no significant pathway-level convergence, the broader transcriptomic profile revealed coherent biological alterations largely compatible with the documented history of cerebrovascular disease in SZ07. These results demonstrate how the integration of exome and transcriptome data at the individual level enables the formulation and constraint of hypotheses regarding patient-specific genetic features and their molecular consequences, while highlighting important limitations related to tissue composition, comorbidity, and the choice of reference cohort.

items.title: Non-coding RNA controls long-range enhancer-promoter interactions
items.corresponding_institution: Max Planck Institute of Immunobiology and Epigenetics, Department of Genome Biology, Freiburg, Germany
items.abstract: Transcription regulation depends on interactions between enhancers and gene promoters, which often occur over large genomic distances. The molecular drivers of long-range enhancer-promoter interactions remain poorly understood. Enhancers themselves are known to be transcribed into non-coding RNAs, but the function of these transcripts is unclear. Here, we use acute genetic and chemical perturbations of transcription elongation and termination to study the role of non-coding RNA in enhancer-promoter interactions. By integrating high-resolution 3D genome mapping, transcriptomics, proteomics, biochemistry and live-cell super-resolution imaging in these perturbation contexts, we demonstrate that a strong increase in RNA molecules at enhancers disrupts their long-range interactions with gene promoters, whereas decreased RNA levels lead to stabilization of these interactions. Using separation-of-function perturbations, we show that this regulatory function of RNA is independent from the process of transcription and the proteins recruited to initiate transcription. Functionally, we show that RNA-mediated disruption of enhancer-promoter interactions is associated with reduced transcription of target genes, indicating a regulatory feedback mechanism. Together, our results uncover an additional regulatory principle of enhancer-promoter interactions mediated by non-coding RNA.

items.title: Investigating the causal and consequential role of the nuclear encoded mitochondrial genome in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
items.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is implicated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but which mitochondrial pathways are involved, and whether their involvement is a cause or a consequence of disease remains unclear. We investigated whether nuclear-encoded mitochondrial gene (NEMG) pathways are enriched for ALS genetic risk, which are dysregulated in ALS tissue, whether pathway activity defines patient subgroups that differ in survival, and whether co-expression between the nuclear and mitochondrial genomes is altered. We tested MitoCarta3.0 pathways for enrichment of ALS genetic risk using MAGMA and the largest European ALS GWAS to date (27,205 cases and 110,881 controls), using hierarchical testing across pathway tiers, and annotated the direction of gene-level effects using published TWAS and SMR results. In >1,500 bulk RNA-seq samples from post-mortem motor cortex and spinal cord (KCL Brain Bank, NYGC ALS Consortium) and iPSC-derived motor neurones (Answer ALS), we performed cell type adjusted gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), gene set variation analysis (GSVA)-based clustering with exploratory survival analysis, and nuclear-mitochondrial co-expression analysis. Of seven broad mitochondrial categories, only the mitochondrial central dogma was enriched for ALS risk after correction (Padj = 0.044). Hierarchical testing within this pathway localised the signal to translation (Padj = 0.008) and the mitoribosome (Padj = 0.014). Genetically predicted expression pointed in opposite directions for different mitoribosomal genes (lower MRPS33 and higher MRPL28 expression with increased risk), and did not agree in direction with differential expression in ALS tissue more often than expected by chance. A nominal enrichment in ROS and glutathione metabolism was largely attributable to SOD1. In tissue, mitochondrial genes were broadly more highly expressed in ALS motor cortex in both cohorts, largely as a global shift across mitochondrial genes. OXPHOS subunits and the mitoribosome were enriched beyond this shift in ALS Consortium motor cortex (both PFDR = 0.027), as were OXPHOS subunits in iPSC-derived motor neurones (PFDR = 2.4 x 10-), whereas spinal cord showed no genome-wide enrichment. GSVA based clusters were associated with diagnosis in motor cortex, and nominally with survival in lumbar spinal cord (adjusted HR 0.69, Punadj = 0.013), where cluster structure was weakest. No individual pathway was associated with survival after correction in adjusted models. In all four post-mortem tissues, nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes were more negatively co-expressed with mtDNA-encoded genes in ALS than in controls, most strongly in lumbar spinal cord, whereas iPSC-derived motor neurones showed the opposite pattern. In conclusion, inherited ALS risk shows a modest enrichment centred on mitochondrial translation, with gene specific rather than uniform directions of effect. The same pathway, alongside OXPHOS, is more highly expressed in end-stage ALS motor cortex, which may reflect a response to disease, residual differences in cell composition, or both. At the gene level, genetically predicted and observed expression changes did not agree in direction, so whether inherited risk and these tissue changes are linked remains unresolved.

items.title: RNA Small-Molecule Binding-Site Prediction by Integrating RNA Language Models and Structural Geometry
items.corresponding_institution: Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur, India
items.abstract: RNAs are emerging as promising therapeutic targets, and small-molecule binding can modulate their structure and function, creating opportunities for therapeutic development. Accurate identification of RNA small-molecule binding sites is therefore important for understanding RNA-ligand interactions and facilitating RNA-targeted drug discovery. However, the structural complexity of RNA and the limited availability of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes pose challenges for computational binding-site prediction. In this study, we propose RSMBind, a graph attention-based deep learning framework for nucleotide-level prediction of RNA-small molecule binding sites. The model integrates geometric descriptors of the local three-dimensional environment with pretrained RNA language model embeddings to capture complementary structural and sequence information. We investigate three pretrained RNA language models RNA-BERT, ERNIE-RNA and RNA-FM and assess the contributions of sequence representations and geometric features through feature-level ablation experiments. The model is developed using the TR60 and HARIBOSS datasets and evaluated on four independent benchmark datasets: RB9, TE18, TL12 and JL10. RSMBind achieves the highest MCC among the compared methods on three of the four benchmarks, with relative improvements of 17.1% on RB9, 7.2% on TL12 and 16.0% on JL10 over the best previously reported results, while achieving competitive performance on TE18. Furthermore, RSMBind retains predictive capability when using only pretrained RNA language model embeddings, highlighting their potential utility when explicit tertiary structural features are unavailable. Structural analysis indicates differences in prediction performance across RNA structural regions, with loop-associated binding sites generally being captured more effectively than those embedded within stem regions. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of selected RNA-ligand complexes provide insights into the relationship between predicted binding probabilities and dynamic ligand proximity, further highlighting the role of conformational dynamics in evaluating structure-based predictions. The source code is available at [ https://github.com/sharma-nandita/RSMBind].

items.title: scDeepSim: Deep Generative Simulation for Controlled Benchmarking of Single-Cell Methods
items.abstract: Benchmarking single-cell computational methods requires both realistic data and reliable ground truth. However, annotating real datasets is costly and, even when available, may not fully represent the diverse settings where methods are used. Simulators address this gap by generating synthetic data that has fully specified ground truth and whose structure can be tailored to challenge competing methods. Existing single-cell simulators can broadly be divided into statistical and deep generative classes. Statistical simulators offer interpretable parameters for controlling simulated data, but their modeling assumptions may not accurately represent real data. Deep generative models can learn complex expression patterns, but it remains unclear how to transparently control individual biological or technical factors without introducing unintended effects. We introduce scDeepSim, a simulator that combines a structured variational autoencoder with latent diffusion to generate synthetic single-cell expression profiles. It allows users to intervene on selected biological or technical factors at user-specified strengths, producing realistic datasets with benchmark ground truth. We demonstrate this capability by benchmarking batch correction and trajectory inference methods, showing how batch-effect strength affects batch mixing and cell-type preservation, and how trajectory geometry and noise affect pseudotime recovery. scDeepSim therefore enables researchers to vary selected biological and technical factors in realistic simulated data and assess how these changes affect the performance of single-cell analysis methods, helping understand when such methods may be appropriately applied. Code for the scDeepSim simulator and experiments is available at https://github.com/LangtianM/scDeepSim.

items.title: Leveraging state-of-the-art AI structure predictors to generate atomic resolution ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins
items.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are central to many biological processes, but their function depends on dynamic conformational ensembles rather than a single structure. Despite the impact of artificial intelligence on protein structure prediction, determining these ensembles at atomistic resolution remains challenging. Recently, we introduced bAIes, a framework that leverages the structural information encoded in AlphaFold2 distograms to generate conformational ensembles of IDPs at atomistic resolution. Here, we extend this framework to six state-of-the-art structure prediction tools (AlphaFold2, AlphaFold3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, ESMFold, and ESMFold2) and systematically compare the structural information encoded in their predicted inter-residue distance distributions. Despite differences between predictors, we show that bAIes generates ensembles with comparable accuracy against experimental NMR and SAXS data, and competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative IDP ensemble generation methods. These results demonstrate that bAIes is robust to the choice of structure predictor and that the distance distributions generated by different deep learning architectures contain valuable information about the conformational preferences of disordered proteins. More broadly, our work highlights the potential of combining AI-derived structural information with physics-based modeling to generate atomistic ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins and regions.

items.title: The Phospholipase A2 Activity of Peroxiredoxin 6 Protects Hepatocarcinoma Cells Against Ferroptosis and Mitophagy Impairment
items.abstract: Peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6) is a moonlighting protein that plays a key role in regulating redox homeostasis and lipid metabolism through its unique dual peroxidase and calcium-independent phospholipase A2 (iPLA2) activities. Here, we generated a stable HepG2 cell line harboring a D140A mutation to selectively ablate iPLA2 activity, and we compared its phenotype with that of wild-type (WT) and PRDX6-knockout (KO) cells. D140A exhibited low ROS leves, similar to WT cells, confirming that oxidative stress is due to peroxidase deficiency. In contrast, D140A cells displayed higher lipid peroxidation than WT cells, though significantly lower than that of KO cells. Furthermore, the D140A mutant mirrored the KO phenotype regarding intracellular ferrous iron accumulation, impaired lipid droplet biogenesis, and the downregulation of the key ferroptosis regulator GPX4. Mechanistically, integrated proteomic, lipidomic, and enzymatic analyses revealed that a deficiency in iPLA2 activity of PRDX6 disrupted the release of key lipid species necessary for cell structure and signaling. Consequently, organelles involved in lipid synthesis and trafficking, such as peroxisomes, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria and lipid droplet, were affected. Specifically, we found that mitochondria exhibited a reduction in cristae and a diminished capacity for mitophagy and autophagy, which ultimately makes cells much more susceptible to erastin-induced ferroptotic cell death. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that PRDX6 iPLA2 activity uniquely coordinates organelle lipid homeostasis and mitophagy to protect cancer cells from ferroptotic cell death. Consequently, the use of iPLA2 inhibitors such as MJ33, which decreased PRDX6 iPLA2 activity to a level comparable to the mutant D140A, could represent a promising therapeutic strategy for inducing ferroptotic cell death in hepatocellular carcinoma.

items.title: Genotype-Informed Drosophila Kinome Screening Prioritizes PRKX as a Candidate Vulnerability in Bladder Cancer
items.abstract: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer is molecularly heterogeneous, and the basal/squamous subtype frequently exhibits elevated EGFR expression and TP53 and RB1 alterations. Functional vulnerabilities associated with these alterations remain incompletely defined, while large-scale in vivo screening in mammalian models is experimentally demanding. Therefore, we developed a genotype-defined Drosophila melanogaster model combining Egfr overexpression, mutant p53, and Rbf suppression in Malpighian tubules. The resulting 3-hit model showed increased Malpighian tubule volume and reduced adult eclosion rate. A dominant modifier screen targeting 216 kinase genes identified 73 genes whose perturbation significantly increased the eclosion rate, and a complementary RNA interference screen identified eight kinases whose knockdown increased the eclosion rate. Among these hits, Pka-C3, a Drosophila ortholog of human PRKX, emerged as one of the strongest suppressors of the reduced adult eclosion rate in the 3-hit model. PRKX was prioritized for further study because public transcriptomic datasets showed higher PRKX expression in bladder tumors than in normal bladder tissue. PRKX knockdown reduced spheroid volume in four human bladder cancer cell lines with distinct EGFR, TP53, and RB1 profiles. Both small interfering RNAs produced significant reductions in two cell lines, whereas only one siRNA reached significance in the other two. These findings nominate PRKX as a candidate vulnerability in bladder cancer and highlight a cross-species approach that combines genotype-informed Drosophila screening with functional testing in human cancer cells to prioritize targets for further investigation.

items.title: AKAP-CaN-NFATc3 signaling drives persistent inhibitory long-term potentiation
items.corresponding_institution: University of Colorado School of Medicine
items.abstract: GABAergic inhibitory synaptic plasticity has critical roles in neuronal function, synaptic plasticity, and cognition. Activity-dependent alterations in gene expression are essential for generating long-term changes in inhibitory postsynaptic strength, yet the signaling mechanisms that drive inhibitory postsynaptic plasticity are not well understood. During an important form of inhibitory long-term potentiation (iLTP), NMDA receptor (NMDAR) activity promotes de novo synthesis of GABAA receptors (GABAARs) and the inhibitory scaffold, gephyrin, leading to persistent strengthening of inhibition. However, it remains unclear what activity-dependent signaling mechanisms control these changes in gene expression to maintain iLTP. In this study, we identify that activation of the transcription factor, nuclear-factor of activated T-cells (NFAT), and anchoring of the phosphatase, calcineurin (CaN), to A-kinase anchoring protein (AKAP79/150) are crucial in regulating long-term structural and functional GABAergic postsynaptic plasticity. Using short hairpin RNA (shRNA) to knock-down hippocampal NFAT isoform, NFATc3, we demonstrate its requirement for the synthesis of new inhibitory synaptic proteins, inhibitory synapse growth, and strengthening of synaptic currents during persistent iLTP. Additionally, using a knock-in mouse line containing a mutation in the CaN binding region of AKAP, we find that AKAP-CaN signaling lies upstream of NFATc3 activation and is required for increased inhibitory synapse clustering and synapse strengthening during iLTP via regulation of miRNA transcriptional activity and protein synthesis. Thus, we have identified an excitation-transcription coupling pathway that rapidly controls the synthesis of new inhibitory synaptic proteins and maintains persistent inhibitory synaptic plasticity, an essential process for memory formation and cognition in the brain.

items.title: Sensory context gates oxytocin effects on auditory processing in macaques
items.corresponding_institution: Laboratory of Neuro- and Psychophysiology, Department of Neurosciences, KU Leuven Medical School; Leuven, 3000, Belgium; Leuven Brain Institute, KU Leuven; Leuv
items.abstract: Oxytocin shapes social perception, yet its neural effects vary substantially across experiments and clinical trials yield inconsistent results. A key unresolved question is whether oxytocin modulates early sensory processing in primates as a function of sensory context. Using high-resolution pharmacological fMRI in two awake rhesus macaques, we compared systemic oxytocin with saline during unimodal auditory and audiovisual tasks. During unimodal auditory stimulation, oxytocin attenuated sound-evoked responses throughout auditory core, belt and associative regions for both vocal and non-vocal sounds, while distributed sound-category information remained decodable. In contrast, when the same vocalizations were presented within an audiovisual task, this attenuation disappeared and responses increased in a restricted set of auditory core and belt regions. Oxytocin also reorganized resting-state coupling among auditory, visual and prefrontal systems and changed how evoked responses covaried across runs. Together, these findings suggest that oxytocin modulates sensory response magnitude and inter-regional coordination in a context-dependent manner rather than uniformly enhancing social signals.

items.title: High spatiotemporal resolution in vivo imaging reveals preferential PACAP38 action on dural vasculature and a functional therapeutic readout
items.abstract: PACAP38-induced cephalic vasodilation is used to assess functional PACAP pathway inhibition in humans, but the vascular populations underlying this response are not fully resolved. Defining these compartments in a preclinical model could help connect clinical pharmacodynamic responses with the underlying vascular mechanisms and support further development of PACAP-targeted therapies. Using chronic cranial windows and head-mounted microscopy, we tracked meningeal vascular responses in freely moving mice. Nitroglycerin, levcromakalim, and PACAP38 each produced net vasodilation, yet the underlying responses were markedly heterogeneous and distributed differently across the vascular populations. Notably, PACAP38 evoked greater early vasodilation in dural than pial vessels, and anti-PACAP pretreatment attenuated PACAP38-induced vasodilation. These findings show that net vasodilation can conceal vessel-level response patterns and identify preferential early dural vasodilation as a spatially defined, pharmacologically modifiable feature of the systemic PACAP38 response. This phenotype provides a translational platform for mechanistic interrogation and evaluation of functional pathway inhibition by migraine-targeted therapies.

items.title: Differential effects of AMPA receptor inhibition on seizure-like events in murine and human brain slices
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology and Experimental Neurology, Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin
items.abstract: Epilepsy is a frequent neurological condition with a worldwide prevalence of 0.5-1%. Current therapies are limited by adverse effects as well as drug resistance. This highlights the need for novel, target-specific antiseizure medications with improved efficacy and fewer side effects. AMPA (-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid) receptors represent a therapeutic target as demonstrated by perampanel, an AMPA receptor antagonist used clinically as antiseizure medication. AMPA receptors typically mediate fast excitatory neurotransmission. Their properties are modulated by auxiliary proteins that can alter receptor activation, deactivation and desensitization, including converting them into slow AMPA receptors. In this study, we tested different AMPA receptor inhibitors, including perampanel, for their ability to suppress seizure-like events (SLE). SLE were recorded with extracellular electrodes in cortical brain slices from healthy mice and from epilepsy patients who underwent resective surgery. SLE were induced with 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) or a combination of 4-AP and high-potassium. We found that seizure-like events in murine tissue appeared more frequently, with higher amplitude and spike frequency, but were briefer than in human tissue. GYKI53655, NBQX and perampanel were equally effective in inhibiting SLE in murine und human brain slices. In contrast, the antagonist LY3130481, specific for the AMPA receptor auxiliary protein {gamma}-8, showed only weak efficacy in murine tissue, but blocked of SLE in human tissue almost completely. The species-specific differences we found for LY3130481 highlight the benefit of using human tissue in preclinical research and underline that auxiliary subunits remain a promising therapeutic target for the development of new antiseizure medications.

items.title: Mechanical and chemical macrophage activation differ by arm, not by amplitude
items.abstract: Mechanical cues are widely reported to polarize macrophages toward an M1-like state, but the claim rests on nuclear factor kappa B/activator protein 1 (NF-{kappa}B/AP-1) effector markers read without a common scale, and the literature does not agree on the sign of the stiffness effect. We asked a quantitative question instead: by what fraction of the chemical M1 response does mechanical perturbation move the interferon-stimulated gene factor 3 (ISGF3)-dependent interferon-stimulated gene module? Scoring ten independent studies of substrate stiffness and applied force against lipopolysaccharide (LPS) + interferon-gamma (IFN-{gamma}) anchors, processed through an identical pipeline, we find a pooled shift of -0.9% of the chemical response (95% confidence interval -6.2% to +4.5%), equivalent to zero at a {+/-}10% margin (p = 0.0019) with a minimum detectable effect of 8.8%. The result is unchanged across three independent ISG definitions. Nor is it a sensitivity failure: the most transcriptionally responsive mechanical contrast rewires thousands of genes while leaving the module inside a size-matched random distribution. Extending to ten further mechanical modalities shows mechanics is not inert toward these genes; shifts run in both directions, but no contrast supported by within-study inference exceeds 15% of the chemical anchor. Rescoring the same contrasts against an NF-{kappa}B effector module anchored on human LPS kinetics separates the two arms: across 21 modality contrasts the effector arm sits 17.7 percentage points above the interferon arm (paired p = 0.032), and in the four designs whose permutation space can reach p < 0.05 the separation is 34 points. Compression moves the effector arm +36% of the LPS anchor (p = 0.002) and the interferon arm -9% (p = 0.004). The separation is absent under static stiffness, where neither arm moves, and its sign is not fixed. A three-arm in-vivo magnetomechanical dataset assigns the effect to the rotating field rather than the internalized particle, raising the effector arm while lowering the interferon arm. Mechanically induced "M1-like" states are not the chemical M1 program rescaled. Where mechanical loading registers at all, it moves the effector arm and not the interferon arm: interferon-stimulated genes are the wrong readout for mechanical perturbation of macrophages.

items.title: Longitudinal CCR2 PET Imaging Tracks Early Inflammatory Monocyte and Macrophage Infiltration in Experimental Arthritis
items.abstract: Objective. Recruitment of C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2+) inflammatory monocytes and macrophages represent an early event in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis that cannot be tracked noninvasively with existing imaging modalities. We evaluated longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) to track and quantify CCR2 cell recruitment in experimental inflammatory arthritis. Methods. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT imaging was performed in K/BXN serum transfer arthritis (STA) mice. Imaging findings were validated using biodistribution, autoradiography, histopathology, immunofluorescence, microCT, cytokine profiling, clinical assessment, and pain-related behavioral testing. Results. Joint Ga-DOTA-ECL1i uptake increased during the acute arthritis and declined with disease resolution. Increased tracer signal localized to inflamed joints, coinciding with CCR2 monocyte and macrophage infiltration, synovial inflammation, cartilage damage, local CCL2 elevation, and mechanical allodynia. PET uptake correlated with ankle swelling, clinical disease severity, pain, and paw CCL2 levels, with peak tracer signal preceding progressive structural bone remodeling. Conclusion. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT enables noninvasive visualization and quantification of early CCR2 monocyte and macrophage recruitment, establishing CCR2 PET imaging as a mechanism-based molecular platform for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring in inflammatory arthritis.

items.title: Highly prevalent cargo genes of F plasmids harbored in pathogenic Escherichia coli
items.abstract: Analysis of prevalent orthogroups (OGs) in a collection of F plasmids from extraintestinal Escherichia coli ST131 isolates has led to the identification of two groups of previously uncharacterized cargo genes that may be widely distributed among F plasmids of pathogenic E. coli. Group 1 comprises four OGs whose encoded proteins are predicted to be involved in transport-related functions. The corresponding genes cluster with other genes associated with metabolism and are highly prevalent in extraintestinal ST131 isolates. Group 2 comprises several OGs whose encoded proteins currently have unknown functions. These OGs are present in a large proportion of F plasmids from both intestinal and extraintestinal E. coli isolates. The corresponding genes cluster within an F-plasmid region that also contains genes involved in DNA metabolism, suggesting that the proteins encoded by these newly identified OGs may likewise contribute to F-plasmid DNA biology. Characterizing the functions of these newly identified proteins may improve our understanding of the contribution of F plasmid to E. coli virulence and reveal novel targets for antimicrobial intervention, either by limiting F-plasmid dissemination among multidrug-resistant (MDR) E. coli strains or by directly targeting plasmid-carrying bacteria.

items.title: Serum extracellular vesicle proteomics reveals treatment-associated biomarkers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
items.abstract: Background Longitudinal biomarkers of treatment response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are needed. Extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched serum proteomics may provide a minimally invasive approach for monitoring systemic and tumor-associated responses to therapy. Methods Paired pre-treatment and post-treatment serum samples were analyzed from 51 patients with pancreatic cancer, including 25 treated with FOLFIRINOX and 20 treated with gemcitabine-based therapy. EVs were enriched using the Mag-Net method and profiled by data independent acquisition mass spectrometry. After batch correction and filtering, 941 proteins were retained for differential and pathway analyses. Paired linear models and gene set enrichment analyses were used to assess treatment-associated changes. Baseline protein abundance and longitudinal changes were evaluated in relation to overall survival (OS) using Cox models. Results A total of 2,089 EV-associated proteins were identified, with an average of 1,186 proteins quantified per sample. Across the cohort, 26 proteins differed between post- and pretreatment samples. Proteins that increased after treatment were primarily related to extracellular matrix organization and cell adhesion, whereas proteins that decreased after treatment were associated with actin cytoskeletal organization, coagulation, and hemostasis. Treatment-associated changes were more pronounced in the FOLFIRINOX group, in which 32 proteins were differentially expressed. FOLFIRINOX was characterized by coordinated reductions in platelet- and coagulation-associated proteins, including PF4, PF4V1, PPBP, GP5, ITGA2B, and ITGB3, accompanied by enrichment of platelet activation, coagulation, and hemostasis pathways among down-regulated processes. No individual proteins met the same significance threshold in the gemcitabine group. A composite seven-protein platelet score decreased significantly after FOLFIRINOX but not for gemcitabine, and the between-regimen difference in score change was significant. Higher pretreatment ITGB1 abundance was associated with longer OS after multiple-testing correction (HR, 0.112; BH-FDR = 0.0063). In multivariable analysis, greater treatment-associated platelet-score depletion was independently associated with shorter OS (HR per unit increase in {Delta}score, 0.56; P = 0.030). Conclusions Longitudinal serum EV-enriched proteomics identified treatment-associated biological changes in PDAC, including a coordinated platelet-related response predominantly observed after FOLFIRINOX. Baseline ITGB1 abundance and longitudinal platelet-score changes represent potentially complementary prognostic and pharmacodynamic markers. These findings are exploratory and require validation in larger, independent cohorts incorporating platelet counts, coagulation measurements, and targeted proteomic assays.

items.title: Genome-wide diversity across 130 years reveals drastic post-bottleneck genetic erosion in a recovering population of golden eagles (Aquila chrysaetos)
items.abstract: Many wild populations have experienced severe human-induced declines, but the genetic consequences of such bottlenecks are often poorly understood. In Finland, as well as in many other countries, golden eagles were heavily persecuted during the 19th-20th centuries, disappearing from southern regions and reaching their lowest population size in the 1950-1960s. Although conservation efforts facilitated demographic recovery, the long-term genomic consequences of the bottleneck remained unknown. Here, we used whole-genome sequencing data spanning 136 years to evaluate patterns of genetic diversity in 26 Finnish golden eagles before, during, and after the mid-20th century bottleneck. We found substantial loss of genetic variation, including an 82% reduction in genome-wide heterozygosity, a 42% decline in nucleotide diversity, a 67% reduction in Watterson's theta, and a substantial loss of variable sites. Analyses of the site frequency spectrum and Tajima's D confirmed historical population contraction, and runs of homozygosity analysis indicated elevated post-bottleneck inbreeding. These results indicate strong genetic erosion in Finnish golden eagles despite the census size recovery. Therefore, incorporating genomic indicators in conservation monitoring and performing regional assessments are necessary to guide management and preserve biodiversity in line with the Global Biodiversity Framework's goal of maintaining genetic variation.

items.title: Boosting Single-Cell Methods Significantly Enhances Cell-type Classification
items.abstract: Single-cell sequencing drives biological discovery by revealing key cellular processes, cell types, and cell states. Recent technological advances have accelerated atlas-scale data generation across laboratories. With the increasing amount of single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data, new challenges emerge, including effective batch correction, cell-type annotation, rare cell-type and cell-state detection, as well as biological pathway discovery. Inspired by methods for boosting weak learners such as AdaBoost, here we present a novel paradigm, scBoost, that combines single-cell analysis methods using stacked ensembles to boost task performance beyond that of individual methods. We show that scBoost pretrained on Tabula Sapiens 2.0 dataset performs significantly better than existing methods in cell-type classification on the real-world Human Fetal Heart Map and Plaque Atlas. We also demonstrate that scBoost substantially improves the performance of cell-type classification and ranks at the top of the leaderboard on the OpenProblems benchmark, a standard-in-the-field. scBoost is modular and is adaptive to new single-cell methods, which will enable it to continue to serve as a resource to the community in the future.

items.title: Sleep deprivation differentially recruits amygdala subregions in male and female mice
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neuroscience, Carleton University, Ottawa, ON, K1S 5B6, Canada
items.abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) acutely increases negative affect, and chronic insufficient sleep is associated with an increased risk of depression. Since the amygdala regulates both emotional processing and sleep, and SD dysregulates amygdalar function, amygdala functionality may link sleep loss to emotional outcomes. To better understand this, the specific sleep-impacted amygdalar nuclei need to be fully defined. To determine the impact of acute sleep loss on the relative activation of specific amygdalar regions, we screened for the neuronal activity marker c-Fos in wildtype mice that slept undisturbed, underwent 4-h SD, or 4-h SD with 2-h recovery sleep (RS). Application of whole-brain clearing and automated cell counting identified increased c-Fos expression within the cortical subplate of both male and female mice that was localized to amygdalar regions. As the amygdala comprises multiple distinct subnuclei, we parcellated and quantified c-Fos expression within each amygdalar subnucleus. Interestingly, we found that SD-induced differential c-Fos expression patterns between sexes. In male mice, SD increased c-Fos expression across several amygdalar subnuclei, which largely reversed with RS. By contrast, SD in females increased c-Fos expression only in the anterior basolateral amygdala and the intercalated amygdala, and both subnuclei remained activated even with RS. These findings highlight sex-specific spatial distribution of SD-activated amygdala cells, which may contribute to differences in emotional processing following sleep loss and offer potential anatomical targets for mitigating SD-related mood deficits.

items.title: Local goodness-of-fit measures for neural decoding
items.corresponding_institution: Howard Hughes Medical Institute, University of California, San Francisco, San Francisco, CA, USA
items.abstract: State-space models are widely used to relate neural activity to internal states that cannot be observed directly, but assessing whether a given model is appropriate for a dataset remains difficult. Current approaches, such as cross-validation, summarize model fit across an entire recording. They can reveal that a model is imperfect, but not when during the recording it fits poorly. We therefore lack tools for targeted model refinement. Here, we develop local goodness-of-fit measures that ask whether each spike is consistent with the model's prediction based on all preceding spikes. Each spike, through the tuning of the neuron that fired, points to a range of likely states, just as the prediction does. A spike that narrows a broad prediction is consistent with it; one that points to states the prediction considers unlikely is not. Because the comparison needs only the prediction and the states each spike points to, it also applies to models that decode from unsorted spike waveforms. Using simulations in which model errors are known, we show that two consistency measures, based on the overlap of high-probability regions and on predictive checks, flag such inconsistent spikes, whereas the standard Kullback-Leibler divergence also flags spikes that merely narrow a broad prediction. We then apply the measures to a hippocampal recording from a rat performing a spatial foraging task. In these data, a model assuming continuous movement is expected to fail during immobility, when the hippocampal representation can jump to distant locations, so we compare it with a model that also allows such jumps. As expected, the overlap measure flags more spikes during immobility than during movement under the continuous model, and allowing jumps removes most of the continuous model's flags. The consistency measures thus show when during a recording a state-space model fits poorly, providing tools for its targeted refinement.

items.title: Exploring subacute effects of a DMT and harmine meditation retreat on the brain's control energy landscape
items.abstract: Modeling the brain as a controllable structural network allows the estimation of the control energy (CE) required to reach functional states, where low-CE states are more accessible. Psychedelics are thought to acutely flatten the brain's CE landscape, broadening the repertoire of reachable states, but whether this reorganization persists into the subacute ``afterglow" window is largely unknown. This exploratory study uses rs-fMRI from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (N = 39; 19 verum [N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) + harmine, Ayahuasca-inspired formulation], 20 placebo) scanned before and after a three-day meditation retreat. We compute CE on a group human connectome project (HCP) structural connectome under two approaches that emphasize long and short timescale dynamics. Globally, we found no systematic shift in the distribution of CE between transitions, however mean CE increased in both groups at the long timescale approach. Surviving network effects emerge when a network's intrinsic timescale matches the stabilization regime. In the long timescale regime, the central executive network (CEN) showed an increase in post-retreat CE within the verum group that survived Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR-BH) correction. Although CE and functional connectivity are distinct, this higher CEN cost may relate to the reduced within-network connectivity previously reported subacutely after psilocybin. The default mode network (DMN) also showed a post-retreat CE increase in both groups, but neither change survived FDR correction. In the short timescale approach, the visual network (VN) showed a FDR-BH CE decrease within the verum group, consistent with reduced dynamical demand in a region acutely engaged by DMT. To examine whether changes were concentrated in less accessible states, we additionally analyzed rare brain states, defined by the top decile of information content. This analysis revealed a modest session x condition interaction in the long timescale approach. Overall, the two timescale lenses surface different network effects, that align with cortical timescale hierarchies. These findings point to network- and timescale-specific, rather than global, CE changes in the afterglow window, though effects are small and heterogeneous and require confirmation in larger samples. Characterizing whether and where psychedelic effects persist into the subacute window is relevant to psychedelic-assisted therapy, including safety, therapeutic timing, and durability of drug effects. More broadly, considering cortical timescale hierarchies may help identify network-specific CE changes that might be less apparent when networks are evaluated under a single dynamical timescale.

items.title: Maternal E-Cigarette Exposure Exacerbates Neonatal Ischemic Brain Injury Through the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 Axis
items.abstract: Background: Neonatal ischemic stroke is an important cause of mortality and long-term neurological morbidity in infants. Maternal smoking and e-cigarette exposure are recognized risk factors for adverse neonatal outcomes, but the mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility to ischemic brain injury remain unclear. This study investigated whether dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis contributes to this susceptibility. Methods: Pregnant rats were exposed to e-cigarette aerosols from embryonic day 4 to 20. Studies were conducted in male offspring on postnatal day 10. Baseline molecular changes were assessed using microRNA sequencing, quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, Western blotting, RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC) and luciferase reporter assays. Ischemic injury was evaluated following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Flow cytometry and molecular analyses were performed to characterize associated cellular changes. The effects of in vivo miR-30c-5p mimic administration, Neurod1 knockdown, and miR-30c-5p inhibition were also investigated. Results: Maternal e-cigarette exposure increased tMCAO-induced infarct size and was associated with increased apoptosis and senescence-associated changes, together with reduced expression of markers of neurogenesis and synaptic development. Under baseline conditions, microRNA profiling and molecular analyses revealed increased miR-30c-5p expression and decreased Neurod1 mRNA and protein levels in the neonatal brain. RISC and luciferase reporter assays supported an interaction between miR-30c-5p and Neurod1 mRNA. In vivo administration of a miR-30c-5p mimic reduced Neurod1 expression and increased infarct size, whereas Neurod1 knockdown independently exacerbated ischemic injury and associated cellular changes. Conversely, inhibition of miR-30c-5p restored Neurod1 expression, reduced infarct size, and ameliorated associated pathological changes. Conclusions: Maternal e-cigarette exposure is associated with baseline dysregulation of the miR-30c-5p-Neurod1 axis and increased susceptibility to neonatal ischemic brain injury in male rats. These findings suggest that this regulatory axis may contribute to the effects of prenatal e-cigarette exposure on the developing brain and may increase susceptibility to neonatal ischemic stroke.

items.title: A protocol for cortical and deep-brain calcium imaging in freely moving mice with the Mini2P system.
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, Los Angeles, CA
items.abstract: Two-photon calcium imaging has transformed our understanding of neuronal circuit function, yet conventional approaches require head fixation, limiting the study of neural activity during natural behavior. Miniaturized two-photon microscopy (Mini2P) overcomes this constraint by enabling calcium imaging in freely moving animals while preserving the optical single-cell resolution of conventional two-photon microscopy. However, its implementation requires the careful integration of multiple technically demanding procedures, presenting substantial challenges for laboratories adopting this approach. Here, we present a comprehensive, step-by-step protocol for implementing Mini2P calcium imaging in freely moving mice, emphasizing procedures that are unique to or particularly critical for successful implementation of this technique. This protocol covers system preparation and performance checks, optical alignment, field-of-view selection, baseplate installation, and strategies for maintaining imaging stability during microscope attachment and reattachment. We also address behavioral habituation, integration with behavioral tasks, imaging acquisition, quality control, and troubleshooting as a part of an integrated experimental workflow. Representative imaging data acquired through cranial windows in the primary visual and somatosensory cortices, and through a gradient-index lens in the medial prefrontal cortex, illustrate the applicability of this workflow across different brain regions and optical preparations. Designed for adaptation across brain regions and behavioral paradigms, the protocol provides practical guidance for identifying technical challenges and verifying successful implementation. By establishing clear decision points, validation criteria, and troubleshooting strategies at each stage, this workflow aims to improve reproducibility and facilitate the adoption of the Mini2P for investigating neuronal circuit dynamics during freely moving behavior.

items.title: Transcriptional and DNA Methylation Changes in the Hippocampus and Prefrontal Cortex after Fractionated Cranial Radiation in Mice
items.corresponding_institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, 1840 Old Spanish Trail, Houston, TX 77054, USA
items.abstract: Fractionated whole-brain irradiation is essential for treating brain tumors, but many long-term survivors develop cognitive decline whose molecular basis is poorly understood. We asked which cell types and gene programs change late after irradiation, how the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex compare, and whether DNA methylation changes affect the same genes or programs. Male and female mice received whole-brain irradiation (5 x 4 Gy) or anesthesia alone. Irradiated mice showed persistent deficits in executive function and spatial memory. Eleven weeks after irradiation, single-nucleus RNA sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing of pooled hippocampal (CA1-3) and prefrontal tissue showed cell-type-specific transcriptional changes in neurons of both regions. Both regions showed reduced ribosomal-protein gene expression and changes in adhesion genes, with reduced respiratory-chain genes in prefrontal neurons and bidirectional synaptic gene changes in hippocampus. Differentially methylated regions were enriched at promoters, with hypermethylation predominating in three of the four sex-by-region contrasts. Methylation and gene expression changes pointed to overlapping synaptic and signaling programs, largely through different genes.

items.title: A common neural axis links image distinctiveness and memorability
items.abstract: Stimulus-specific memorability, the tendency for people to remember and forget the same stimuli, is a powerful predictor of memory performance that is independent of the study and retrieval factors that have dominated memory research. Critically, memorability can be defined in two ways: "Hit-ability" (H-ability) and "false alarm-ability" (FA-ability), the probability of correctly recognizing studied items or falsely recognizing unstudied items, respectively. Although past work has suggested that these are dissociable facets of memorability, challenging single-factor explanations, we present neural and computational evidence that they share a common neural axis. The neural signature of high H-ability matched the signature for low FA-ability, showing that these parameters have inverse relationships with a common factor. Moreover, we show that image distinctiveness predicts the flipped relationship between H-ability and FA-ability in both behavior and neural activity, providing a unifying explanation of stimulus-specific memorability.

items.title: Rab27a modulation reverses hemorrhage-induced neutrophil dysfunction in response to secondary respiratory challenge
items.corresponding_institution: Division of Surgical Research, Department of Surgery, Rhode Island Hospital and Brown University Health, 593 Eddy Street, Providence, RI 02903, United States
items.abstract: Patients recovering from hemorrhage are susceptible to secondary respiratory infections, owing to dysregulated innate immune responses. Using a two-hit mouse model of hemorrhage followed by a secondary respiratory challenge with Staphylococcus aureus or lipopolysaccharide (LPS), we investigated the role of Rab27a in the neutrophil response to pulmonary inflammation and host defense. Hemorrhage followed by S. aureus infection increased surface CD63 expression on pulmonary neutrophils, indicating azurophilic granule release, and was accompanied by reduced neutrophil entry into the airspaces of the lung. Using HoxB8-conditional neutrophil progenitor (NP) transplantation to neutrophil chimeric mice, we observe that Rab27a-deficient neutrophils have enhanced recruitment into the extravascular pulmonary compartment compared with wild-type (WT) neutrophils. Furthermore, pharmacological intervention with Nexinhib20, a small-molecule inhibitor of Rab27a-JFC1 interactions, attenuated systemic and pulmonary inflammatory responses in the two-hit model, including a reduction in circulating myeloperoxidase (MPO) levels. Nexinhib20 also enhanced neutrophil-mediated S. aureus killing that was accompanied by increased intracellular MPO levels in neutrophils. Collectively, these findings implicate Rab27a-associated functions in the regulation of neutrophil trafficking and inflammatory responses following hemorrhage and secondary respiratory challenge, highlighting the potential of pharmacological targeting of Rab27a to attenuate inflammation without compromising antimicrobial host defense.

items.title: Hyperactivation of Mincle in exacerbated apical periodontitis in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism
items.corresponding_institution: University of Connecticut School of Dental Medicine
items.abstract: Aims: To examine the role of Mincle, a C-type lectin (Clec) pathogen recognition receptor (PRR), in exacerbated apical periodontitis (AP) in an autoinflammatory mouse model for cherubism (CBM). Methodology: Patients with immune system dysfunction have higher prevalence of AP but the mechanism remains largely unknown. We studied a knock-in (KI) mouse model carrying a Sh3bp2 mutation for CBM. We performed pulp exposure in one lower 1st molar of 5- to 6-week-old mice to introduce pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMP)-induced endodontic infection. We determined the expression levels of Clec subfamily genes by qPCR. To suppress Mincle, we generated Sh3bp2+/+Mincle+/+, Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+, and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice or injected Sh3bp2+/KI mice with a Mincle-binding DNA aptamer (AptMincle). Mice were analyzed 42 days after pulp exposure by micro-CT (mCT), qPCR and immunoblotting. Statistical analysis was performed by one-way ANOVA followed by post-hoc analysis with Tukeys test or two-way ANOVA followed by Sidak correction. p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: Expression of Clec4e (Mincle) was significantly increased in Sh3bp2 mutant mice after pulp exposure compared to WT littermates (p<0.0001). Sh3bp2+/KIMincle+/+ and Sh3bp2+/KIMincleKO/KO mice had a comparable response to pulp exposure, including the degree of bone loss and induction of inducible NOS (iNOS), IL-1b, and TNF-a. Sh3bp2+/KI mice injected with AptMincle after pulp exposure for 21 days showed significant amelioration of bone loss compared to mice with vehicle injection (p<0.0001). Conclusions: These seemingly conflicting data of suppressing Mincle by crossing with Mincle KO mice and AptMincle injection suggest that Mincle has dual functions upon PAMPs stimulation, consistent with a previous study showing that Mincle enhances tissue destruction during the inflammatory stage and is subsequently needed for inflammation resolution. Fine-tuned suppression of Mincle significantly reduces the severity of AP in Sh3bp2+/KI mice. This study suggests that patients with CBM may benefit from more frequent dental examinations and early intervention to reduce or prevent severe progressive bone loss in periapical tissues.

items.title: Surface adhesion-dependent DNA extraction bias points to an 'anvil effect' during mechanical lysis
items.abstract: DNA extraction bias is usually treated as an intrinsic property of a cell's envelope, size, or physiology rather than a feature of its physical location. Most soil bacteria live attached to surfaces, and attached cells should lyse preferentially during bead-beating if a bead striking a particle crushes the cell against it, as on an anvil, whereas a free cell must be caught between colliding beads. We tested this 'anvil effect' in sterile synthetic soil microcosms using isogenic strain pairs that differ in adhesion in two bacteria with different modes of attachment. Agrobacterium tumefaciens anchors with a unipolar polysaccharide and aggregates in an exopolysaccharide matrix, whereas Caulobacter vibrioides attaches individually by a polar holdfast. Within each strain we calculated the ratio of DNA yield from mechanical to chemical lysis, then compared adherent with non-adherent strains. In support of the anvil effect, mechanical lysis favored adherent cells in A. tumefaciens (2.0-fold) and C. vibrioides (2.6-fold). The route by which soil was transferred to the lysis tube altered the extent of bias observed, further indicating the importance of considering physical context during DNA extraction. Our synthetic soil was standardized and aggregate-free, leaving cells exposed on particle surfaces, making these results a direct test of the anvil effect. In natural soils, the aggregation, texture, and moisture may offset or amplify this effect. Surface attachment therefore biases soil DNA extraction, complicating corrections that treat extraction efficiency as a fixed, strain-specific coefficient.

items.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of the endangered northern dragonhead sap beetle, Thymogethes norvegicus (Easton, 1959)
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Biosciences, University of Oslo, Oslo, Norway
items.abstract: The northern dragonhead sap beetle (Thymogethes norvegicus) is believed to be endemic to Norway and is classified as endangered. Its life cycle is closely tied to the host plant northern dragonhead (Dracocephalum ruyschiana), itself classified as vulnerable in Norway. Here, we present a chromosome-level genome assembly of a male T. norvegicus. The assembly comprises two pseudo-haplotypes, hap1 and hap2, of 1,142 and 1,109 Mb, with 96.3% and 96.8% scaffolded into chromosomes, respectively. Hap1 contains 8 autosomes and the X chromosome, while hap2 contains 8 autosomes. Assembly quality was high, with conserved single-copy ortholog completeness scores of 96.6% and 90.7% and combined k-mer completeness of 98.1%. A total of 13,484 and 12,550 protein-coding genes were annotated in hap1 and hap2, respectively. This assembly provides a valuable genomic resource for the conservation of this endangered endemic species totally dependent on the vulnerable plant, the northern dragonhead.

items.title: Long-read analysis of complete human 5S rDNA arrays reveals a zoned organization with two-state unit methylation linked to chromatin architecture
items.abstract: Despite the fundamental importance of the 5S ribosomal DNA (rDNA) to all cellular life, the landscape of its units by position along its array has remained poorly understood. Here, recent telomere-to-telomere long-read sequencing is used to resolve 5S rDNA arrays from flank to flank and to follow the state of each unit along single molecules. The array is zoned at both the sequence and the epigenetic level. Notably, methylation is bimodal at the level of the unit, and the combination of low-methylation and high-methylation units gives rise to the overall methylation pattern of the array. Moreover, the average number of low-methylation units remains relatively constant regardless of array length. Chromatin fiber sequencing (Fiber-seq) data further show that low-methylation units are more accessible, have lower nucleosome occupancy and are more frequently footprinted at the TFIIIB-binding site, consistent with analyses of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data from cell lines. Across species, this pattern is shared among apes, whereas other species show diverse patterns. These results provide a unit-resolved view of the human 5S rDNA array and reveal a zone-specific organization of unit methylation that is associated with chromatin architecture.

items.title: Comprehensive Characterization of Somatic Mutations and Gene Expression on TP53/PTEN DKO Murine Glioblastoma Cell Lines: Insights from Whole-Exome and RNA-seq Analysis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Computer Sciences, University of Agriculture, Faisalabad
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain tumor characterized by genomic instability and transcriptional plasticity. To investigate the somatic evolution of GBM, we performed an integrated analysis using Whole-Exome Sequencing (WES) and RNA-seq on a murine glioblastoma model representing two stages: early-stage transformed neural stem cells (tNSC) and late-stage malignant GBM (mGB). The comparative analysis of mutational signatures provides evidence of a two-phase evolutionary path for tNSC and mGB. Variant calling in tNSCs revealed mutations in Pfdn2, Oip5, Trmt10a, Nabp2, Man2b1 with mGBs acquiring additional putative progression-associated genes such as Cdk4, Ubap2, Ccdc11, Errfil, and Tead2 associated with malignancy and Temozolomide (TMZ) resistance. Samples in tNSCs exhibited signatures associated with stress-(SBS4) and development-associated (SBS40) processes. In contrast, mGB samples exhibited an increase inmutation signatures, specifically associated with replication- (SBS5) and mismatch repair (MMR) processes (SBS26). Notably, SBS26 consistently ranked in the top five mutational signatures across all samples, indicating that there may have been an early, and sustained, loss of MMR. Ti/Tv ratio also revealed elevated transversions in tNSCs supporting early instability post TP53/PTEN knockout, while mGB demonstrated normal transition-to-transversion ratio. Gene ontology reveals activities in neurodevelopmental pathways in tNSCs such as neurogenesis, axon guidance, and synapse regulation while in mGB it shifts to cellular transformation and invasion, and epidermal development. Moreover, differential expression analysis showed extreme downregulation against control neural stem cells (ctrlNSCs) indicating genomic instability and then the partial restoration of expression in mGB, resembling ctrlNSCs but with a bias toward malignant upregulations. Together this suggests, early genomic instability disrupting developmental programs and blocking differentiation, and later on replication-driven mutations and cytoskeletal remodeling reprograms the tumor into a proliferative, invasive, and therapy-resistant state.

items.title: Scientific Figure Library connects visual examples with reusable plotting code
items.corresponding_institution: National Key Laboratory of Plant Molecular Genetics (NKLPMG), CAS Center for Excellence in Molecular Plant Sciences (CEMPS), Institute of Plant Physiology and E
items.abstract: Code-generating assistants can adapt plotting scripts, while researchers select visual examples and assess their relevance. Reusing those examples requires the image, implementation, and input context to remain connected. Scientific Figure Library (SFL) organizes visual examples, plotting code, input descriptions, and provenance as reusable figure assets. A user-selected local library retains working revisions and published releases, while a common provider interface makes local and externally maintained collections available through the same discovery workflow. Researchers browse candidate figures, inspect an exact preview, confirm a selection, and materialize the corresponding assets into a project for adaptation and execution. Local clients and external agents access a shared service, connecting visual selection with code-based analysis across research environments. An accompanying open resource, ScientificFigureLibrary-personal, supplies modular examples through the Open Figure Modules provider. Its organization combines previews, reusable scripts, example inputs, and licensing information, making it a concrete resource for learning and adapting scientific visualization patterns. We describe the asset model, retrieval and confirmation workflow, execution handoff, and resource organization, supported by implementation inspection and automated software checks. In a public lung single-cell case study, we reused a cell-composition template for 32 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and 28 control donors and verified the donor-level inputs and plotted proportions. SFL provides a practical connection between finding a figure and obtaining the materials needed to work with it, while preserving the identity and provenance of the selected example.

items.title: Towards a best-in-class IgE disruptor for food allergy with Claude-enabled antibody design
items.abstract: Food allergy affects an estimated 220-250 million people worldwide, for whom the constant risk of a severe reaction weighs heavily on quality of life. Allergic reactions are triggered by the cross-linking of allergen-specific IgE bound to its high-affinity receptor, Fc{epsilon}RI, on mast cells and basophils, causing degranulation, inflammation and, in severe cases, anaphylaxis. Omalizumab (Xolair), the sole FDA-approved biologic for food allergy, neutralizes circulating IgE; however, it does not effectively remove IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, where it can persist for weeks and where even a small residual amount can sustain sensitivity. Here we describe an agentic computational design campaign with Claude toward a disruptive inhibitor antibody that physically removes bound IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI. Guided by our research team, Claude pursued a biparatopic molecule that pairs a disruptor arm, which displaces IgE from Fc{epsilon}RI, with a non-competing anchor arm that holds the molecule on receptor-bound IgE. Of 91 experimentally characterized disruptor designs, 20 showed activity against receptor-bound IgE by competitive bio-layer interferometry, and in a dose-titration assay three variants removed more IgE than omalizumab at therapeutically relevant concentrations (25-400 nM). De novo designs for the anchor arm bound IgE at diverse epitopes with apparent affinities of 3.4-235 nM. These subcomponents provide the starting point for further characterization toward a best-in-class IgE disruptor.

items.title: DE-Rigor-Agent: An Agentic Workflow for Assumption-Aware Differential Expression Analysis of Bulk RNA-seq Data
items.abstract: Differential expression (DE) methods for bulk RNA-seq differ in their statistical assumptions, input data requirements, and supported study designs. Large language model (LLM) agents can automate DE analysis, but they may default to popular methods without checking whether these methods are appropriate for the data. We introduce DE-Rigor-Agent, an assumption-aware agent that organizes DE analysis into three stages: input standardization, method filtering, and method execution. Before executing any DE method, the agent uses expert-curated criteria and dataset-specific diagnostics to evaluate six commonly used methods, documents the reasons for retaining or excluding each method, and executes all retained methods. We evaluated DE-Rigor-Agent on 140 simulated datasets spanning 14 challenging scenarios involving small sample sizes, zero inflation, expression outliers, pre-normalized inputs, and confounded batch effects. Benchmarks showed that method-dataset incompatibilities could lead to inflated false discovery rates (FDRs) or reduced statistical power. Two general-purpose LLM agent baselines, including one explicitly prompted to consider statistical assumptions, selected DESeq2 or edgeR for nearly all datasets. In contrast, DE-Rigor-Agent's filtering decisions closely matched the incompatibilities introduced in the simulations and remained consistent across random seeds, with little additional computational cost. These results demonstrate that DE-Rigor-Agent provides an automated approach to assessing method suitability, making DE analysis more rigorous and transparent.

items.title: Neuropathological assessment of cerebrovascular integrity in Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy
items.abstract: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy neuropathological change (CTE-NC) is defined by perivascular deposits of phosphorylated tau, with lesions preferentially located at sulcal depths. We investigated whether CTE-NC is associated with structural changes to perivascular spaces (PVSs) or microvascular degeneration. Post-mortem middle frontal gyrus tissue from 11 CTE-NC cases and 11 age-matched controls was examined using immunohistochemistry. All CTE-NC cases exhibited pathognomonic lesions in this region. We quantified PVS width along with vessel lumen and PVS area, string vessel burden, pericyte density, and aquaporin-4 (AQP4) polarisation to the astrocytic endfoot. Total PVS width did not differ significantly between the groups in grey matter (P = 0.543) nor white matter (P = 0.468). Neither PVS area (sulcal depth, P = 0.097; gyral crest, P = 0.645) nor PVS-to-lumen area ratio (sulcal depth, P = 0.454; gyral crest, P = 0.307) differed significantly. Similarly, there were no significant differences in total microvascular length (p = 0.693), string vessel burden (p = 0.128), pericyte density (p = 0.589), or AQP4 endfoot enrichment (p = 0.538). We therefore found no evidence of large-scale PVS enlargement, lumen narrowing, capillary degeneration, pericyte loss, or altered AQP4 endfoot enrichment in CTE-NC at the locations and spatial scales investigated. Taken together, these findings suggest that the pathognomonic perivascular tau lesion is not associated with a classical small vessel degenerative phenotype in CTE-NC. However, that does not exclude more subtle molecular, functional, or ultrastructural changes at the interface between vessels, the perivascular space, and surrounding brain tissue.

items.title: Distinct input-output relationships between basal forebrain subnuclei underlie heterogeneous cholinergic modulation of the mouse cortex
items.abstract: The basal forebrain (BF) supports many behavioral functions via its brain-wide projections, which can be recruited independently and task specifically. However, the anatomical underpinnings for this functional heterogeneity are poorly understood. Here, we compared two mouse BF subnuclei, the horizontal diagonal band (HDB) and the substantial innominata (SI), in terms of their anatomical connectivity and functional recruitment. Using anterograde and retrograde tracing, we show that they target largely segregated forebrain regions, but their input comes from a partially overlapping subset of regions. However, many neurons within each region project to just one of the subnuclei, suggesting they can be recruited independently. To test this, we combined optogenetics and widefield Ca2+ imaging and showed that stimulating prefrontal cortical projections to the HDB or SI results in distinct large-scale patterns of cortical activity via a cholinergic mechanism. Our results provide an anatomical basis for the flexible, area-specific cholinergic modulation of brain function.

items.title: Striatal dopamine availability peaks in adulthood and undergoes age-dependent modulation
items.abstract: Age is a risk factor for several psychiatric disorders. An adolescent peak in striatal dopamine availability is thought to contribute to the neuropsychiatric vulnerability. However, the lifespan trajectory of striatal dopamine release capacity is undefined in most species. Here, we measured lifespan trajectories of striatal dopamine in primates and rodents and identified a delayed developmental peak in adulthood and age-dependent changes in dopamine release regulation by GABA and acetylcholine across species.

items.title: Advanced meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control linked to absorptive depth
items.corresponding_institution: University of California, San Francisco (UCSF), California, USA
items.abstract: Advanced meditation can shift conscious experience from ordinary body- and world-centered awareness toward absorption, detachment and dissociation-like states, yet the neural mechanisms that stabilize these immersive states remain unclear. We studied 18 long-term meditators during eyes-open rest and Rajyoga meditation, a practice in which practitioners reduce bodily identification while enhancing inner self-awareness. We combined multidimensional neural approach including frontal EEG spectral power, temporal non-stationarity and corticothalamic neural-field modeling, because these measures probe underlying complementary levels of the brain state transition: the strength of neural activity, its temporal stability, and the circuit level inhibition-excitation gain mechanisms. This framework is especially relevant to meditation because oscillatory, temporal organization may distinguish stable meditative states, and corticothalamic dynamics are closely linked to arousal and conscious state regulation. We correlated meditation induced neural changes with subjective ratings of absorption and dissociation. Compared with rest, meditation was associated with higher beta1, beta2 and gamma power, with no change in the slower bands (delta, theta and alpha), and with lower beta-band temporal non-stationarity, indicating a more stable expression of fast cortical dynamics. Fitting the corticothalamic model to the EEG spectra showed stronger cortical inhibitory gain and lower effective intracortical gain, placing meditation in an inhibition-dominant regime, with lower gain in the loop between excitatory and inhibitory neurons within the cortex. During meditation, these model estimates were related to subjective absorption and showed trend level links with dissociation. Together, these findings suggest that Rajyoga meditation stabilizes cortical dynamics through inhibitory gain control, linking absorption (deep and steady attention on the meditation) to dissociation-like self-detachment.

items.title: Biological aging and comorbidities are linked to HIV 1 reservoir size despite suppressive antiretroviral therapy
items.corresponding_institution: HIV Cure Research Center, Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium
items.abstract: Background The HIV reservoir persists in long-living immune cells after antiretroviral therapy initiation. Proviral DNA integrates at preferential host DNA sites, while HIV transcription continues under treatment, with potential biological consequences. Treated people with HIV remain at increased risk for premature aging and non-AIDS comorbidities compared to people without HIV. Whether HIV reservoir size and activity impact health outcomes during treatment remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 1895 people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy from the 2000HIV cohort to study associations between the reservoir and historic and prospective virologic and immunological response markers, comorbidity outcomes and biological aging scores. The reservoir was assessed by quantifying total and intact proviral HIV DNA in circulating CD4+ T cells, along with measures of HIV transcriptional activity, including cell-associated HIV RNA. Results HIV reservoir markers were highly correlating and associated with older aging scores and adverse virologic outcomes, including quantifiable and residual viremia at study entry and during follow-up. Total HIV DNA, unlike the minor fraction of intact HIV DNA, correlated with prevalent cardiovascular disease, subclinical atherosclerotic disease, liver fibrosis and incident malignancies independent of circulating inflammatory markers and lowest CD4 nadir. Total HIV RNA associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease and liver fibrosis. Conclusion The HIV reservoir associated with older aging scores and long-term health outcomes in people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy, independent of inflammation and immune suppression history. Whether reservoir-reducing interventions lower the risk of non-AIDS comorbidities should be studied in people with high reservoir markers. Funding and trial registration ViiV Healthcare; 2000HIV ClinicalTrials.gov number: NTC03994835

items.title: Tracking the conformational dynamics of single molecules in live cells; GTPase cycling in Cdc42 gradients and microclusters
items.abstract: The Rho family of GTPases play a critical role in many cellular processes by acting as molecular switches relying on conformational changes to transition between active and inactive states. The spatial distribution and kinetics of these conformational changes are complex and vary across the cell. We describe here biosensors based on environment-responsive fluorescent dyes, capable of reporting the conformational changes of individual GTPase molecules as they traffic within living cells (SPARC Cdc42 and SPARC Rac1, 'Single Particle Activation Reporter Constructs'). We use SPARC Cdc42 to determine the rates of different steps in GTPase regulation, activation/inactivation and membrane insertion, that together generate localized gradients of Cdc42 activity driving cell motility. The biosensors also revealed heterogeneously distributed clusters of Cdc42, the mechanisms of their activation, and potential roles in polarized motility.

items.title: Male-specific genome sequences for non-invasive sex identification in Nishikigoi (Cyprinus carpio)
items.abstract: Nishikigoi, ornamental cultivars of the common carp (Cyprinus carpio), are economically valuable aquaculture teleosts in which mature females command significantly higher market prices due to superior body conformation and coloration. Consequently, early and non-invasive sex identification is highly desirable for commercial breeding. Although sex determination in common carp follows an XX/XY system, sex-chromosome-specific markers and field-applicable diagnostic methods for Nishikigoi have remained limited. In this study, we conducted sequence-based bulked segregant analysis using whole-genome shotgun sequencing of female and male pools in Kohaku, a representative Nishikigoi lineage. We identified male-specific candidate contigs and successfully developed PCR-based male-specific markers. Validation across multiple Nishikigoi varieties and wild common carp demonstrated that primary primer pairs achieved high diagnostic accuracy. Comparative genomic analysis revealed that these candidate contigs mapped to the genomic region on chromosome 25B containing the male-determining gene Pangu, with the primary marker located in immediate physical proximity to the gene. To enable field diagnostics, we combined non-invasive epidermal mucus DNA extraction, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and chromatography-printed array strip (C-PAS) technology, establishing a rapid on-site detection workflow. Overall, this study provides highly reliable PCR markers associated with the sex-determination locus and establishes a non-invasive, field-applicable diagnostic platform to streamline commercial Nishikigoi breeding and sex-selected stock management.

items.title: Single-nucleus long-read RNA sequencing reveals isoform usage shifts in mouse acute kidney injury
items.corresponding_institution: Division of Nephrology, Department of Medicine, Washington University in St. Louis
items.abstract: Introduction Single-cell and single-nucleus short-read RNA sequencing has elucidated transcriptomic changes across kidney cell types at the gene expression level. However, its limited read length precludes reliable isoform identification, hindering the characterization of individual protein-coding isoforms and non-protein-coding isoforms.
