Models adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE {varepsilon}4 status. ResultsAmong 3031 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.6 [7.0] years; 1322 female [43.6%]), prodromal NSD participants had lower baseline verbal-memory performance than HC (adjusted difference, -0.20 SD; 95% CI, -0.34 to -0.07; adjusted P = .007); NSD-negative genetic carriers did not differ from HC. No other cognitive domain was lower than HC at baseline or longitudinally. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, verbal-memory trajectory differed from HC over 4 years (P = .009), whereas in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not (P = .62); the baseline difference persisted (adjusted difference, -0.28 SD; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.10; P = .003). Adjusted MCI probability increased from 10.2% to 15.1% in prodromal NSD, compared with 8.4% to 5.0% in HC and 13.4% to 17.7% in PD. The increase was greater than in HC (ratio of annual odds ratios, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.58; adjusted P = .04) but not PD (P = .62). Conclusions and RelevanceProdromal NSD was associated with modestly lower verbal memory and increasing MCI probability relative to HC, without lower performance in other cognitive domains. The baseline verbal-memory difference was robust, whereas the longitudinal trajectory finding was not reproduced in the smaller age-matched sensitivity subset. Key PointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSWhat cognitive differences characterize prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease, and how do they change over time? FindingsIn this longitudinal cohort study of 3031 participants, prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease was associated with lower verbal memory at baseline than healthy controls, while other cognitive domains were not lower. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, the verbal-memory trajectory differed from healthy controls over 4 years; in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not differ significantly. MeaningCognitive involvement in prodromal neuronal -synuclein disease may be detectable as a modest verbal-memory signal, while longitudinal changes require confirmation.

items.title: Benchmarking Structural Variant Detection in Whole-Exome Sequencing of 67 Multiple Myeloma Cell Lines
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Oncology, Dell Medical School, University of Texas at Austin
items.abstract: BackgroundAlthough the majority of structural variant (SV) workflows have been derived based on whole genome sequencing (WGS) data, they continue to be applied to whole exome sequence (WES) data for which many studies have evaluated their performance in cancer. An equally important consideration that has not been well studied is the impact of cancer context specific features among WGS-derived SV callers applied to WES data. Like personalized medicine, not all SV callers are alike and optimal for use with all cancer types and sequence data types. In addition to sequencing related data features, cancer types have embedded features withing the sequencing data that should be considered. Herein, we performed an analysis of SV heterogeneity among WGS-derived SV callers to WES data in multiple myeloma (MM), a cancer known for its genetically heterogeneous nature. Using WES data derived from a panel of 67 Multiple Myeloma (MM) cell lines, we evaluated seven WGS-derived SV detection tools (Delly, SvABA, BreakDancer, Smoove, LUMPY and Manta) for their ability to identify cytogenetically known genetic abnormalities and to characterize overall differences in the number, length, type, and runtime of SVs called among them. ResultsAmong the seven tools, Smoove and Manta both had the shortest runtime, processing files in less than 2 minutes, in contrast to tools that required more than two hours to run such as SvABA and Pindel. Smoove was the only SV caller to identify a range of SV types, while SvABA was the most restrictive, calling only breakends. All tools differed in the length of SVs called, with SvABAs unfiltered output including the shortest length of less than 10 base pairs (bps), and Delly and BreakDancers output including the longest, with SVs of less than 1,000 bps. At the chromosome level, SvABAs unfiltered output and Dellys output included 78% and 27.5% of known SVs, respectively, with the remaining tools (including SvABAs filtered output) achieved recall rates of less of less than 10%. By comparison, at the genomics coordinate level, no tool identified more than 20% of known SVs. ConclusionsAs all evaluated SV detection tools achieved poor recall rates on this comprehensive catalog of MM cell lines, this study implies SVs detected by WGS-based SV callers on WES data should be confirmed experimentally before being declared legitimate. Heterogeneity in these tools output lends support to their combined use in practice. Considering that many clinical grade sequencing panels continue to expand their repertoire of rearrangements with therapeutic implications, our results prompt the potential need for cancer type-matched workflows to evaluate the calling of such rearrangements.

items.title: Music-Synchronized Gamma Light Stimulation Strengthens Theta-Gamma Coupling in Older Adults with Cognitive Impairment: Results from a Randomized Feasibility Trial
items.abstract: Noninvasive clinical innovations for restoring gamma activity via sound and light stimulation have the potential to improve memory and cognitive abilities in Alzheimers disease. We assessed whether pairing music with theta- and gamma-band light changes memory-supporting neural dynamics, and whether those changes track cognition. In an ongoing randomized feasibility trial, 38 older adults with cognitive impairment completed eight weeks of an audiovisual intervention. The treatment group (n = 19) listened to self-selected music while viewing light stimulation that consisted of a 39-Hz gamma-band signal modulated by delta- and theta-band musical rhythms. The control group (n = 19) listened to podcasts while viewing synchronized lights without the gamma frequency (delta-band only). Before and after the 8-week intervention, participants completed a face-name association task and the Alzheimers Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive (ADAS-Cog). Individuals in the treatment group showed significant improvements on a face-name association task and the ADAS-Cog. Cluster-based permutation testing showed a larger increase in phase-amplitude coupling between acoustic theta phase and frontal EEG gamma amplitude in the treatment group compared to the control group. Across participants, increases in stimulus-driven theta to EEG-gamma phase-amplitude coupling were associated with improvements in memory. These preliminary results suggest that theta-gamma stimulation delivered through music and lights strengthens cross-frequency coupling, and may correspondingly strengthen associative memory.

items.title: Diagnostic Value in Discarded Reads: Re-evaluating Multi-Mapping cfDNA Fragmentomics and GC Bias in Early-Stage Cancer.
items.abstract: BackgroundLow-coverage plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing is an inexpensive substrate for cancer detection. Standard pipelines discard fragments with low mapping quality, which originate mostly from repetitive DNA, although pericentromeric satellite repeats are frequently hypomethylated in cancer. We asked whether the fraction of multi-mapping cfDNA fragments differs between early-stage cancer and matched healthy controls, and how it compares with conventional fragmentomic features under strict control of technical factors. MethodsWe analysed public plasma cfDNA whole-genome sequencing from 25 patients with stage I-III breast cancer and 25 healthy controls matched 1:1 for age, sex, smoking and alcohol use, each pair processed in the same library and sequencing batch, and from 8 early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cases with 8 matched controls. For every sample we computed the fraction of autosomal fragments with MAPQ < 30 and the share of these fragments located in centromeric and heterochromatic cytobands, and related them to stage, grade and copy-number deviation as proxies of tumour burden. Classifiers were evaluated by leave-one-pair-out cross-validation in breast cancer and, trained on breast cancer only, applied unchanged to HCC. Robustness to GC content and sequencing depth was tested by within-fold residualisation and by fragment-level GC weighting. Conventional fragmentomic features (fragment length, end motifs, copy number, DELFI-like profiles and window features at transcription start sites) were evaluated under four GC-handling analyses. ResultsThe multi-mapping fraction was higher in breast cancer than in matched controls (median 5.38 % vs 5.19 %; higher in 19/25 pairs; paired p = 0.0006; cross-validated AUC 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.94), in stage I (9/10 pairs), stage II (7/10) and stage III (3/5) disease and in every sequencing batch. The excess was concentrated in centromeric and heterochromatic bands, whose share of multi-mapping fragments rose from 22.0 % to 23.4 % (19/25 pairs; p = 0.004). Both signals persisted after within-fold adjustment for GC content and/or depth (AUC 0.64-0.76 for the multi-mapping fraction, 0.71-0.76 for the heterochromatic share) and under fragment-level GC weighting (18/25 pairs; p = 0.003). The multi-mapping difference was largest in stage I and decreased with stage (Spearman {rho} = -0.42, p = 0.04), and neither feature was associated with grade or copy-number deviation. In public tissue methylomes, satellites were hypomethylated in breast tumours to a similar extent as other late-replicating DNA, but the bin-level association between tumour hypomethylation and the cfDNA excess was weak and was explained by GC content. In HCC, the pre-specified endpoint, the breast-trained multi-mapping model, was not met (AUC 0.73; 5/8 pairs; sign test p = 0.36). In an exploratory analysis that was not pre-specified, the heterochromatic share was higher in 7/8 HCC pairs (p = 0.016; locked AUC 0.86, 95 % CI 0.62-1.00); across all 33 pairs, including the discovery pairs, it was higher in the cancer case in 26 (post hoc sign test p = 0.0007). In contrast, conventional fragmentomic features reached AUC 0.71 (breast) and 0.77 (HCC) only without fragment-level GC control; they tracked the per-sample coverage-GC dependence and fell to chance under each of three GC-controlled analyses, including one that preserves promoter-specific signal. ConclusionsMulti-mapping cfDNA fragments, which are routinely discarded, differed between early-stage breast cancer and batch-matched controls, largely independently of GC content and sequencing depth, with an excess in centromeric and heterochromatic DNA. The signal did not scale with stage, its biological origin is unproven, and a read-quality contribution cannot be excluded from fragment files. It is a candidate marker that requires confirmation in larger cohorts with raw reads and tumour-fraction estimates.

items.title: A multi-scale cell-type resolved map of trans-regulatory architecture in the aging human brain
authors: The Alzheimer's Disease Functional Genomics Consortium,
items.abstract: Mapping genetic effects on distal genes and regulatory programs is essential for understanding how genetic variation influences complex diseases; yet trans-QTL discovery remains limited by weak effect sizes, extensive multiple testing and poor reproducibility. Here, we introduce TransMap, a generalizable computational framework that combines multi-scale trans-QTL mapping with multi-phenotype genetic colocalization to improve the discovery and interpretation of distal regulatory variants. Beyond individual trans-eGenes, TransMap constructs local co-regulatory program phenotypes that account for background expression variation to improve the detection of weak, coordinated distal genetic effects. Across a broad range of simulation settings, TransMap achieved 9.2-36.7% higher trans-QTL discovery power than existing methods while maintaining well-controlled type I error rates. We applied TransMap to bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomic profiles from the aging human brain in the ADSP Functional Genomics Consortium (FunGen-AD), further integrating proteomic, glycoproteomic and metabolomic biomarker measurements (average N=476 donors). Genome-wide fine-mapping of TransMap single-gene and program-level QTL yielded variant annotations with 2.75-2.88x heritability enrichment across 57 complex diseases and traits (average N=307K), with complementary heritability information captured across regulatory scales. Multi-phenotype colocalization identified 49,532 trans-regulatory events supported by shared genetic signals with cis-eQTL or biomarker-QTL, including 1,825 candidate cis-trans-biomarker regulatory configurations. TransMap further revealed an asymmetric cross-cell-type regulatory architecture in which neuronal cis-regulatory signals preferentially associate with coordinated glial trans-regulatory responses, supported by co-culture experiments and spatial transcriptomics. Alzheimers disease (AD) GWAS-prioritized colocalization identified trans-regulatory associations in 115 AD-associated loci, including a KNOP1 cis-eQTL associated in trans with a microglial regulatory program containing MS4A4E, with additional support from statistical mediation analysis. TransMap provides a multi-scale, cell-type-resolved atlas of trans-regulatory variation and a generalizable framework for elucidating the regulatory architecture of complex diseases.

items.title: Computational Modeling of the Acoustic Radiation Force and Viscoelastic Displacement for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Neuromodulation
items.abstract: ObjectiveIn transcranial ultrasound neuromodulation (TUS), simulations of the harmonic pressure are often used for treatment planning. However, other mechanisms of energy transfer, such as acoustic radiation force (ARF) and the resulting tissue displacement, are reported less frequently. Furthermore, there is limited guidance on how these mechanisms should be simulated. This study evaluates the numerical convergence and accuracy of different ARF formulations and investigates the simulation of ultrasound-induced tissue displacement in the context of TUS. ApproachTwo simulations steps are used in k-Wave to first simulate the first order acoustic pressure and velocity fields. Subsequently, these fields are used to calculate the ARF using the momentum-flux density tensor, Reynolds stress force, and attenuation force formulations. The ARF is then applied as input for a second viscoelastic simulation to estimate the tissue displacement induced by the ultrasound field. Numerical accuracy and convergence are quantified as functions of the various numerical choices and hyperparameters in the solvers. Main resultsAmong the investigated formulations, the attenuation-force approach proved to be the most robust and the least susceptible to numerical errors across variable medium types and transducer geometries. Within the parameter space relevant to TUS, it is a valid approximation of the momentum flux density tensor formulation. Similar tissue displacement distributions are found across the different ARF formulations. However, the accuracy of the displacement simulation decreases with increasing pulse duration. Finally, recommendations are formulated on the ARF calculation method and on the numerical hyperparameters for ARF and displacement simulations. SignificanceThis study offers guidelines for calculating the ARF and simulating tissue displacement. The proposed framework enables a more comprehensive characterization of ultrasound-mediated energy transfer in TUS.

items.title: Investigating the potential effect of topiramate on anorexia nervosa and binge eating behaviour using drug-target Mendelian randomization
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Molecular Bioscience, The University of Queensland
items.abstract: Topiramate is an antiseizure medication used to treat epilepsy and migraine and is commonly prescribed for appetite suppression and weight loss. However, whether its pharmacological actions influence eating disorder risk remains unclear. We applied drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate potential causal effects of topiramate on the risk of anorexia nervosa (AN; 24,223 cases and 1,243,971 controls) and binge-eating behaviour (BE; 39,279 cases and 1,227,436 controls) and, exploratorily, eight other psychiatric disorders: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety disorders, alcohol use disorder, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, and schizophrenia. We used summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) to investigate genetically predicted pharmacological actions of topiramate using brain- and blood-derived cis-expression quantitative trait loci for genes encoding its molecular targets. Five genetic instruments consistent with topiramates antiepileptic action were validated: CA4 and CACNB3 expression in the brain and CA4, GRIK1, and GRIK3 expression in the blood. Robustness of the findings was assessed using SMR-multi, HEIDI, and colocalization analyses. After multiple-testing correction, genetically predicted inhibition of CA4 expression in blood was associated with decreased BE risk (OR = 0.867, 95% CI = 0.792-0.950, p = 0.002) and remained significant in SMR-multi (p = 0.0049). Colocalization provided moderate support for a shared causal variant underlying CA4 expression and BE (PPH4 = 0.58). No robust evidence was identified for AN or the eight exploratory psychiatric outcomes. Overall, our findings warrant further clinical and functional investigations into mechanisms underlying topiramate-associated appetite suppression and weight loss and their relevance to eating-disorder risk.

items.title: A Framework for Variant Filtering to Improve Diagnostic Outcomes in Genome Sequencing
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Genetics, Hadassah Medical Center, Jerusalem, Israel.	Faculty of Medicine, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Jerusalem, Israel. 	Geneyx Genomics, Is
items.abstract: Rare genetic disorders frequently remain undiagnosed despite the use of exome sequencing (ES) and genome sequencing (GS). This study aimed to enhance diagnostic yield by introducing a systematic framework: SMART filtering (Systematic, Multi-step, Automated, Rare variant prioritization Tool), designed to optimize GS analysis, with a particular emphasis on non-coding regions. We retrospectively analyzed 153 cases with previously negative ES and GS results. SMART filtering was applied as a pre-annotation filtering step, integrating conservation metrics, allele frequency thresholds, and splicing prediction scores. Then followed by phenotype-based prioritization and manual review. Application of this framework identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 4.6% of cases, strong variants of uncertain significance (VUS) in 1.3%, and additional candidate variants in 5.2% of cases. Several deep-intronic variants were confirmed by RNA studies and segregation analyses. The framework enabled efficient prioritization of non-coding and regulatory variants that were overlooked by standard analyses. In conclusion, SMART filtering offers a reproducible and scalable strategy to improve diagnostic yield in GS, particularly in cases where conventional analysis methods fall short. Integrating such frameworks into clinical genomic pipelines can enhance variant interpretability and diagnostic performance, ultimately leading to better patient care outcomes.

items.title: Pathogenic MYRF ICA Domain Variant is Aberrantly Trafficked in the RPE and Results in Isolated Nanophthalmos
items.abstract: PurposeMyelin regulatory factor is a transcription factor essential for RPE development and serves as a critical "GO" signal for eye growth. Pathogenic variants in MYRF manifest in a spectrum of clinical phenotypes ranging from isolated nanophthalmos to severe syndromic disease, in a gene dosage dependent manner. In this study, we aimed to determine the pathogenicity and molecular mechanism of a novel variant in the MYRF ICA domain, c.2083C>T (p.R695C), that leads to isolated nanophthalmos and mild retinal pigment epithelial disruption. MethodsWhole genome sequencing was performed and identified a novel MYRF variant. Pathogenecity and in silico modeling were evaluated using the Ensembl VEP tool and PyMOL. Human primary RPE and/or ARPE-19 cells were transduced with FLAG-tagged variant and wildtype MYRF or double-tagged FLAG-MYRF-MYC proteins to evaluate transcriptional activity, localization, and protein trafficking. ResultsIn silico modeling supports variant pathogenicity and altered homotrimer conformation. Functional studies in human primary RPE (hRPE) and/or ARPE-19 cells confirmed that MYRF p.R695C is cleavage deficient, mislocalized to the apical surface of polarized RPE, and demonstrated reduced synergistic transcriptional activity with co-factor SOX10 in HEK293T cells. Protein trafficking studies demonstrated that wildtype MYRF is trafficked to the apical cell surface and plasma membrane and that endogenous MYRF requires ER to Golgi trafficking pathways for proper nuclear localization and cleavage dynamics. ConclusionsTogether, these results confirm that p.R695C is pathogenic for nanophthalmos, implicate trafficking as a regulatory mechanism of MYRF in the hRPE, and support that RPE disruption as a feature of MYRF-associated nanophthalmos.

items.title: Plasma phosphorylated tau species across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases: An ONDRI study
items.corresponding_institution: L.C. Campbell Cognitive Neurology Research Unit, Hurvitz Brain Sciences Program, Sunnybrook Research Institute, Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, Toronto, ON,
items.abstract: Elevated plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species are proposed as specific biomarkers of Alzheimers disease (AD) pathology but have also been reported in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Their profile across neurodegenerative and cerebrovascular diseases, as well as their discriminatory value when combined with other plasma biomarkers, remain uncertain. We studied 551 participants (ages 40.1 to 87.1 years; 207 women), comprising 506 patients from the Ontario Neurodegenerative Disease Research Initiative (ONDRI) multi-site cohort and 45 amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) PET-negative cognitively unimpaired controls from the Brain-Eye Amyloid Memory study. Ten diagnostic groups were studied: mild cognitive impairment (MCI), AD, Parkinsons disease subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU), MCI, and dementia, frontotemporal dementia (FTD), cerebrovascular disease (CVD) subdivided into cognitively unimpaired (CU) and cognitively impaired (CI), ALS, and the control group. Baseline visit plasma measurements included p-tau217, p-tau181, A{beta}42/40, neurofilament light chain (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Cross-sectional analyses compared biomarker levels as well as p-tau217-based inference of amyloid positivity status across diagnostic groups. Receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC-AUC) analyses ascertained the discriminatory capacity of these biomarkers and ratio combinations. Within the ALS group, baseline biomarker measures were also tested for association against baseline clinical features as well as longitudinal measures of neuropsychological change. P-tau217, p-tau181, GFAP, and NfL differed across groups (all P < 0.001). Compared to controls, p-tau217 was elevated in AD and ALS, p-tau181 and GFAP only in AD, and NfL in ALS and FTD. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity was more probable in MCI, AD, ALS, and cognitively impaired CVD groups compared to controls (all P < 0.05). The p-tau217 to NfL ratio discriminated ALS from AD with an ROC-AUC of 0.92 (95% CI 0.85-0.97) compared to p-tau217 alone at 0.65 (95% CI 0.52-0.76). No ALS clinical or longitudinal association survived correction for multiple comparisons. Elevated p-tau217 and inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in ALS provide further evidence that the assay signal is not necessarily specific for AD pathology. However, the use of p-tau217 in combination with NfL provides improved discriminatory power between ALS and AD, supporting the use of plasma biomarker combinations rather than sole reliance on individual plasma biomarkers. Inferred amyloid-{beta} positivity in cognitively impaired CVD may indicate AD and/or cerebral amyloid angiopathy co-pathology. Currently available plasma biomarkers should therefore be used as diagnostic complements and interpreted within clinical context rather than as standalone molecular diagnoses.

items.title: Donepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine and progression to memantine add-on therapy in Alzheimer's disease: a nationwide cohort study emulating a target trial in the Brazilian Unified Health System
items.corresponding_institution: Health Informatics Laboratory (LabInfoS), Departamento de Ciencias Medicas Integradas, Faculdade de Ciencias Medicas, Centro Biomedico, Universidade do Estado d
items.abstract: BackgroundDonepezil, galantamine and rivastigmine are dispensed free of charge to people with mild to moderate Alzheimers disease in the Brazilian Unified Health System (SUS), but their comparative long-term effectiveness in routine care is unknown. Under the national clinical protocol, memantine is added to a cholinesterase inhibitor (ChEI) when the disease reaches the moderate stage, so memantine add-on can serve as a marker of clinical progression. MethodsNationwide new-user cohort study emulating a target trial in which adults with Alzheimers disease eligible for a ChEI would be randomly assigned to start donepezil, galantamine or rivastigmine and followed for memantine add-on. We used outpatient medication dispensing authorizations (APAC records of the Outpatient Information System, SIA/SUS) from all 27 federative units, January 2018 to December 2025. We included patients who started a single ChEI between October 2019, after memantine was first recorded nationally, and December 2025, after at least 12 months without anti-dementia dispensing. The outcome was the first memantine dispensing after the index month. Follow-up ended at add-on, recorded death, loss to follow-up (more than 3 observed months without dispensing) or end of data. Deaths were rarely recorded and were treated as censoring. One pseudonymized health card number shared by many patients was excluded, and follow-up ended earlier in the two affected states. We estimated the risk of add-on at 12 to 48 months had all patients started each drug and remained under observation, using stabilized inverse probability of treatment and censoring weights, with 95% confidence intervals (CI) from 200 bootstrap replicates. The analysis assumed no unmeasured confounding or informative censoring given the measured covariates. ResultsThe cohort included 142 758 new users (donepezil 74 165; galantamine 30 691; rivastigmine 37 902; mean age 77.3 years; 63.0% women), followed for a median of 14 months; 9 812 memantine add-on events occurred. After weighting, all standardized mean differences were below 0.05. The 24-month weighted cumulative incidence of memantine add-on was 9.7% (95% CI 9.4-10.0) with donepezil, 9.0% (8.6-9.4) with galantamine and 5.6% (5.3- 5.9) with rivastigmine. Compared with donepezil, the 24-month risk difference was -0.7 percentage points (pp) (-1.1 to -0.3) for galantamine and -4.1 pp (-4.5 to -3.7) for rivastigmine (risk ratio 0.58, 0.55-0.61). Estimates were stable across sensitivity analyses, including a composite outcome that counted unrecorded deaths and dropouts as events (24month risk difference -4.1 pp, -4.8 to -3.3) and analyses within age groups (risk ratio 0.64 below 75 years). Deaths were almost never recorded in the dispensing data (at most 0.47% of treated patients per year). ConclusionsIn routine SUS care, initiation with rivastigmine, mostly as a transdermal patch, was associated with a lower risk of memantine add-on than initiation with donepezil or galantamine. Because disease severity and death are not recorded in the dispensing data, this difference may reflect prescribing patterns or residual confounding by severity rather than slower progression; additional analyses made differential mortality a less likely explanation. It should be confirmed with linked clinical and mortality data.

items.title: Feasibility of Vibrotactile P50 Sensory-Gating Assessment Using Portable EEG
items.abstract: Sensory gating (SG), most commonly quantified using the auditory P50 event-related potential elicited by a paired "double-click" paradigm, is a well-established biomarker of early sensory inhibition that reflects the brains ability to suppress responses to repetitive sensory input. Although auditory SG paradigms have been widely used in both research and clinical settings, they impose an unavoidable auditory load and are generally limited to controlled laboratory environments, reducing their suitability for ecological monitoring and applications in which auditory resources must remain available. This study evaluated the feasibility of a portable vibrotactile sensory-gating system designed to assess inhibitory processing without engaging the auditory or visual modalities. Fifteen healthy adult participants completed both auditory and vibrotactile paired-stimulus conditions using a within-subject experimental design. Vibrotactile stimuli were delivered through transducers positioned on the volar surface of the forearm while electroencephalographic (EEG) activity was recorded using a 32-channel Emotiv EPOC Flex system. Event-related responses were extracted and analyzed using conventional sensory-gating metrics to enable direct comparison between modalities. Vibrotactile stimulation elicited time-locked P50 responses with attenuation of S2 relative to S1. Mean S2/S1 ratios were 0.521 {+/-} 0.041 for the auditory condition and 0.524 {+/-} 0.064 for the vibrotactile condition. The paired difference was 0.0029 (95% CI, -0.0221 to 0.0279), t(14) = 0.249, p = 0.807, dz = 0.064. No statistically significant difference was detected between modalities in this sample. These group-level findings support further evaluation of portable vibrotactile P50 measurement.

items.title: Regional Vulnerability to Brain Metastases Reflects Structural, Metabolic and Genetic Organization of the Healthy Brain
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurological Surgery, NYU Langone Health
items.abstract: BackgroundBrain metastases (BMs), the most common intracranial tumor, do not distribute uniformly throughout the brain, but instead preferentially localize to specific regions. Building on known associations with perfusion and the gray-white matter junction, we hypothesized that regional vulnerability to BMs also reflects the cellular and molecular organization of the healthy brain. MethodsIn a discovery cohort of 1,406 patients, we generated a voxelwise map of BM distribution and compared it with normative atlases of brain microstructure, vasculature, metabolism, cell-type composition, and gene expression. Associations were tested for replication in an independent multicenter validation cohort of 1,209 patients. ResultsIn the discovery cohort, BM frequency was higher near the gray-white matter junction and in regions with greater cerebral perfusion, glucose metabolism, and mitochondrial density. At the cellular level, BM frequency was inversely related to astrocyte and microglial transcriptional signatures. Using normative gene expression maps derived from postmortem healthy brain tissue, we identified 17 genes spatially associated with BM vulnerability and specific to metastases relative to other intracranial lesion types. These associations replicated in the validation cohort. The immune checkpoint gene LAG3 ranked among the ten genes most positively associated with metastatic vulnerability across all genes tested (r = 0.40-0.45, p < 0.001). LAG3 expression was also elevated in peritumoral brain metastasis tissue relative to control brain tissue in an independent spatial transcriptomic dataset. ConclusionsThese findings suggest that BM vulnerability reflects healthy brain organization and identify LAG-3, a clinically targetable immune checkpoint, as a candidate link between regional brain immune biology and metastatic colonization.

items.title: Quantitative evaluation of MGMT promoter methylation in FFPE and fresh frozen brain tumor samples by EpiDirect MGMT Methylation qPCR Assay compared to pyrosequencing: correlation and corresponding cutoffs
items.abstract: MGMT promoter (MGMTp) methylation is a clinically important epigenetic biomarker that guides therapeutic decision-making in patients with glioblastoma and related brain malignancies. Pyrosequencing is a widely used method for analysis of MGMTp methylation in molecular pathology laboratories which relies on chemical conversion of DNA prior to amplification by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and subsequent sequencing. The EpiDirect(R) technology represents a novel analytical approach that enables direct, quantitative assessment of DNA methylation by qPCR using native, unmodified DNA. Here we compared the EpiDirect(R) MGMT Methylation qPCR Assay to MGMTp pyrosequencing using brain tumor samples to evaluate the correlation between the two methods. We show that there is a clear correlation across two different clinical cohorts involving both formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) and fresh frozen samples and show that the EpiDirect(R) MGMT Methylation qPCR Assay is a valid alternative to pyrosequencing for quantitative assessment of MGMTp methylation in brain cancer samples.

items.title: Polygenic Prediction of Depression Liability Reveals Broad Genetic Associations Across Development, Families, and Populations
items.abstract: Polygenic prediction of depression is limited by the depth of depression phenotyping available at biobank scale as well as sample size. Here we develop a depression score combining information from depression and genetically correlated psychiatric traits using phenotype reconstruction, multi-trait genetic integration and Bayesian effect estimation. Compared with the strongest publicly available depression-only score (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium 2025, excluding 23andMe), the liability-R2 for depression in UK Biobank rose by 49.7% and within-family standardized associations with latent internalizing were up to 54% larger. Across 2,328 childhood and adolescent outcomes in the ABCD study, the association profile of the integrated score was almost identical to that of the depression-only score (r = 0.99), while being uniformly stronger. 1,494 outcomes related to mood, behavior, social functioning, hobbies and sleep were associated with the score -- 423 of them within-family. In ABCD, adolescents in the highest score decile were 3.5 times as likely as those in the lowest decile to report suicidal thoughts by age 14 (23% versus 7%) and 1.9 times as likely to report nicotine or cannabis use by age 17 (47% versus 25%). In adults, the score predicted worse general health, chronic pain, and life dissatisfaction. Associations with psychiatric symptoms were substantially stronger in girls than in boys (boys coeffiicients 0.68 times girls), particularly for girl-typical symptoms, and showed no moderation by household resources, hardship or deprivation that remained significant after correction for multiple testing. Prediction was attenuated in line with genetic distance from training data for Hispanic and African American children. Depression prediction can thus be strengthened substantially by integrating the internalizing spectrum, without detectable loss of specificity or within-family predictive ability.

items.title: Functional analysis enables reclassification of SCN1A missense variants of uncertain significance in epilepsy
items.abstract: SCN1A, the most prominent gene for epilepsy, encodes the pore-forming subunit of the voltage-gated sodium channel, NaV1.1. Loss-of-function variants reduce NaV1.1 activity in inhibitory neurons leading to hyperexcitability; they are associated with a spectrum of epilepsies, from self-limited phenotypes in genetic epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, to the prototypic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, Dravet syndrome. Thousands of SCN1A missense variants have been identified, but determining pathogenicity using ACMG criteria can be challenging. Currently, 48% of missense SCN1A variants in ClinVar are classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). We aimed to provide functional evidence to inform variant classification using a high-throughput automated patch-clamp assay. We validated our assay using 27 true pathogenic SCN1A variants and 25 true benign variants. The results show that 17/27 true pathogenic variants from patients with Dravet syndrome showed severe reductions in current density, precluding gating analysis. Of the remaining ten true pathogenic variants, seven showed an increased voltage difference between the midpoints of activation and inactivation (V0.5diff). Current density and V0.5diff were combined within a graded Bayesian framework to derive a functional log-likelihood ratio reflecting the magnitude of loss of function. We then applied our validated assay to 16 SCN1A missense variants detected in an Australian cohort: three likely pathogenic, one likely benign and 12 VUSs. These variants occurred in 31 individuals from 16 families with a broad phenotypic spectrum, including four individuals with Dravet syndrome who carried p.Ser243Phe, p.Met973Val or p.Lys1911Glu. All three variants showed loss of function: p.Ser243Phe had reduced current density, whereas p.Met973Val and p.Lys1911Glu had abnormal V0.5diff despite current density within the normal range. Of these 16 variants, ten have combined functional scores consistent with abnormal functional evidence. Combining our functional evidence with ACMG criteria, our findings changed the classification of eight of 16 variants (50%), with six of 12 VUS reclassified as likely pathogenic and two of three likely pathogenic variants upgraded to pathogenic. We show that calibrated automated patch-clamp assays can provide actionable functional data to enable the interpretation and reclassification of SCN1A variants and inform clinical care, allowing therapeutic optimisation and facilitating access to genetic therapies.

items.title: A novel patient with inherited TNF deficiency and tuberculosis
items.corresponding_institution: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center
items.abstract: Two otherwise healthy patients from Colombia, now aged 30 and 38 years, developed pulmonary tuberculosis due to inherited, complete TNF deficiency at the ages of 19 and 18 years. We report here a previously healthy Iranian patient with inherited complete TNF deficiency who was diagnosed with both pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB between 10 and 15 years of age. The homozygous TNF variant (c.673C>T) introduces a premature stop codon (TNF p.Q225*) resulting in losses of expression and function. Despite normal myeloid and lymphoid subset development, the patients primary leukocytes do not secrete detectable amounts of TNF. As in the TNF-deficient Colombian patients, the respiratory burst of GM-CSF-derived macrophages is impaired. Our findings expand the spectrum of TB phenotypes in patients with TNF deficiency and confirm that TNF is essential for immunity to M. tuberculosis in humans but apparently redundant against many other pathogens, including weakly virulent mycobacteria.

items.title: Improving Consistency in Colorectal Cancer Genetic Risk Assessment and Return of Results Through an Integrated Polygenic Risk Score
items.abstract: BackgroundPublished colorectal cancer (CRC) polygenic risk scores (PRS) may demonstrate similar population-level predictive performance but often assign substantially different risk classifications to the same individuals. Such discordance presents challenges for clinical implementation and return of results (RoR). MethodsWe developed a stable PRS for CRC (stPRS-CRC) by integrating 28 published PRS using PRSmix in the All of Us (AoU) development cohort (n=321,703). Performance was evaluated in a held-out AoU validation cohort (n=80,423) and independently validated in the Genomic Health Initiative (GHI) (n=17,545). CRC associations were assessed using logistic regression, comparing individuals in the highest PRS decile with the remaining 90%. Individual-level concordance in high-risk classification was evaluated using mean Jaccard indices. ResultsPublished CRC PRS showed substantial discordance in individual-level high-risk classification despite generally consistent associations with CRC. stPRS-CRC integrated information from multiple published PRS and demonstrated CRC associations comparable to PGS003852, the strongest-performing individual PRS. The odds ratios for stPRS-CRC were 1.94 (95% CI, 1.79-2.11) in AoU development, 2.08 (1.76-2.45) in AoU validation, and 2.08 (1.55-2.79) in GHI. Mean Jaccard indices using stPRS-CRC versus PGS003852 as anchors, each compared with the same 27 published PRS, were 0.29 versus 0.20, 0.43 versus 0.25, and 0.27 versus 0.19, respectively (all P<0.001). ConclusionsIntegrating multiple published CRC PRS significantly improved individual-level concordance in high-risk classification while maintaining population-level predictive performance. stPRS-CRC may provide a more consistent framework for clinical genetic risk assessment and ROR.

items.title: A Multicenter Retrospective Study on the Safety and Efficacy of the Surpass Evolve Flow Diverter System for the Treatment of Intracranial Aneurysms
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Surpass Evolve flow diverter system for the treatment of intracranial aneurysms across three medical centers. MethodsA retrospective review was conducted on patients with intracranial aneurysms treated with the Surpass Evolve FDS between March 2023 and May 2024 at three participating centers. Primary outcome measures included the rate of complete aneurysm occlusion (Raymond-Roy class 1) and the incidence of periprocedural major stroke and mortality. Secondary outcomes encompassed follow-up modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores, imaging assessment results, and complication rates. ResultsA total of 132 patients (132 aneurysms) were included. The median age was 60.0 years (IQR 52.5-69.0), and 80 patients (66.6%) were female. The complete occlusion rate was 73.3% (88/120). The rate of major stroke was 2.3%, with no procedure-related mortality. At follow-up, 96.9% of patients had an mRS score of 0-2. Multivariate analysis identified non-use of an intraprocedural IIb/IIIa inhibitor and the absence of a branch arising from the aneurysm as independent predictors of complete occlusion. ConclusionIn this real-world, multicenter, retrospective study, the treatment of intracranial aneurysms with the Surpass Evolve FDS was associated with a high rate of complete occlusion and a favorable safety profile. Our findings indicate that complete occlusion was independently predicted by two key factors: periprocedural avoidance of IIb/IIIa inhibitors and a favorable aneurysm morphology without incorporated branches.

items.title: The effect of carotid atherosclerosis and revascularization on cognition and dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Epidemiology, Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, the Netherlands
items.abstract: BackgroundCarotid artery atherosclerosis may accelerate cognitive decline and increase dementia risk, but evidence is fragmented and inconsistent, and benefit of revascularization on cognitive outcomes uncertain. MethodsWe systematically searched Medline, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register, and Google Scholar for articles published until 11 November 2024, reporting change in cognition or dementia incidence in relation to carotid artery intima-media thickness, plaque, stenosis, and revascularization procedures. We excluded studies that investigated people with dementia, lacked a reference group, or had post-intervention follow-up <30 days. We additionally included new data from the Rotterdam Study, and results from the recent CREST-2 trial. Two independent reviewers extracted study data. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed if data allowed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Cochrane Risk of Bias, and ROBINS-I. ResultsOf 5592 records identified, 97 studies were eligible, including 43 observational studies (N=100,326) and 54 intervention studies (N=15788, 6 randomized controlled trials). In observational studies, mostly among stroke-free individuals, intima-media thickness was associated with higher dementia risk (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase: 1.07, 95%CI 1.01-1.13; I2=24.8%; 5 studies), as was presence of 50-100% asymptomatic steno-occlusive disease (hazard ratio: 1.48, 95%CI 1.06-2.07; I2=0.0%, 3 studies). Cognitive outcomes were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis, but 11/20 observational studies reported a significant association between carotid atherosclerosis and global cognition. In non-randomized intervention studies, carotid revascularization improved global cognition (standardized mean difference: 0.73, 95%CI 0.37-1.09; I2=89.8%), but all studies were at high risk of bias, and heterogeneity was only partially explained by intervention type and study characteristics in meta-regression. Suggested benefit of stenting on cognition among Chinese patients (Standardized effect: 0.86 [0.57-1.16], 197 patients; and 1.09 [0.64-1.53], 90 patients, 2 trials) was not observed in the larger CREST-2 trial (Standardized effect: 0.03 [-0.09 to 0.15] and 0.02 [-0.09 to 0.14]), nor in post-hoc analyses of cognition in the ACAS trial and long-term dementia risk in ACST-1 (HR: 0.98 [0.75-1.28]). ConclusionsCarotid atherosclerosis is associated with increased risk of dementia. Current evidence does not support carotid revascularization for prevention of cognitive decline or dementia.

items.title: Genetic effects on serum and urine metabolites across ancestries and their links to disease
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Epidemiology and Prevention, Faculty of Medicine and Medical Center - University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany; Department of Epidemiology, Johns
items.abstract: Genome-wide association studies of the metabolome have predominantly examined European-ancestry populations using a single biofluid, constraining both the discovery of metabolite quantitative trait loci (mQTLs) and the resolution of causal variant finemapping. Here, we report a multi-ancestry genome-wide association study of 1,955 serum and urine metabolites in 4,431 European American and African American participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study. We identify 969 mQTLs for 553 metabolites, 30% unreported in studies of matched biofluid and ancestry, and replicate 91-99% of testable mQTLs in two independent cohorts. In the African American sample with balanced sample sizes, 36% of metabolites with mQTLs are serum-specific, 39% urine-specific, and 25% shared, demonstrating complementary genetic architecture. Only 23 of 632 candidate ancestry-specific mQTLs show heterogeneous effects beyond variant availability and power, yet allele frequency differences expose functional variants such as an SLC28A1 splice variant, virtually absent in Europeans, that increases urine uridine excretion, implicating impaired CNT1-mediated renal nucleoside reabsorption. Multi-ancestry finemapping improves credible set resolution, and colocalization with the Million Veteran Program phenome links the catalog to cardiometabolic, kidney and liver traits consistent with prioritized gene function. Integrating biofluids and ancestries enhances genetic discovery and mechanistic characterization of the human metabolome.

items.title: Reduced serum carboxymethyllysine is independently associated with Alzheimer's disease
items.corresponding_institution: Ningbo No.2 Hospital, Ningbo Institue of Life and Health Industry, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.abstract: INTRODUCTIONAdvanced glycation end products accumulate in Alzheimers disease (AD) brain, but the clinical significance of circulating N{varepsilon}-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML) remains uncertain. We evaluated serum CML as a complementary peripheral biomarker of AD. METHODSThis observational case-control study enrolled 101 patients with clinically diagnosed AD and 91 healthy controls. Serum CML was quantified in 191 participants. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses assessed association and discrimination. A randomly selected subcohort underwent ultrasensitive measurement of amyloid-, tau-, glial-, and neuroaxonal-related biomarkers. RESULTSSerum CML was lower in AD than controls (median 15.26 versus 23.72 ng/mL; P<0.001). In a complete-case model (n=178), each 1-ng/mL increase was associated with lower odds of AD (adjusted odds ratio 0.727, 95% confidence interval 0.656-0.804). CML alone yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.883. Five-fold cross-validation yielded AUCs of 0.727 for a clinical model and 0.911 after adding CML. In the biomarker subcohort, AD showed lower A{beta}42/A{beta}40 and higher p-tau217; exploratory CML plus p-tau217 discrimination reached an AUC of 0.966 (n=60). DISCUSSIONReduced serum CML was independently associated with clinically diagnosed AD and may reflect a systemic glycoxidative dimension complementary to canonical biomarkers. Its biological origins and clinical value require external, longitudinal, and biomarker-defined validation.

items.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Pediatrics, Peking University First Hospital
items.abstract: Reported performance of scalp electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure pre-diction is often inflated by lenient evaluation and by the vigilance-state, clock-time and admission-trend structure of monitoring data. We asked how much short-horizon warning survives a pre-specified, locked evaluation. Continuous video-EEG from 21 monitored children (1315 h) formed the development cohort. A statistical-process-control warning method, evaluated under a written protocol, detected 44% of evaluable seizures at 0.48 false alarms per hour, no better than a random predictor (51%, p = 0.86); its statistic moved three times more with vigilance state than with seizure approach. We re-designed it as a state-conditioned, directional scheme on seven global EEG features, froze it with a hash-recorded configuration and time-stamped pre-specification, and estimated its performance by nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation: 15 of 45 seizures (33%) at 0.47 false alarms per hour, above analytic (21%, p = 0.034) and permutation chance, but a predictor using only clock time, vigilance state and days since admission reproduced most of this, and the signal was confined to the last 30 min. Applied once to two validation cohorts (a second batch from the same unit and the public CHB-MIT database; 101 evaluable seizures), the frozen scheme detected 19 seizures (19%) at 0.60 false alarms per hour against 26% chance (p = 0.96); no secondary endpoint was met, and with the child as the unit of analysis no cohort was above chance. Scalp-EEG warning should be evaluated under pre-specified rules against structured chance levels; the frozen scheme and framework are offered as a reference.

items.title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
items.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) are two common forms of neurotrauma that can present with overlapping clinical features, complicating early diagnosis and management particularly in acute and mixed-trauma settings.1-3 Accurate and rapid biological differentiation remains an unmet need.4 We hypothesized that brain-derived tau (BD-tau), an ultrasensitive blood-based biomarker preferentially selective for tau protein originating from the brain, would distinguish TBI from SCI. In a multi-cohort assessment of 342 patients admitted to the neuro-intensive care unit (285 with TBI, 57 with SCI), and 22 controls, baseline serum BD-tau concentrations were markedly elevated in TBI compared with SCI, discriminating between the two populations with high accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]=0.91, 95%CI 0.87-0.96). In paired serum-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples, serum BD-tau significantly outperformed CSF BD-tau for injury-type discrimination (AUC=0.95, 95%CI 0.89-0.99 vs. 0.80, 95%CI 0.71-0.89). Baseline serum BD-tau also showed superior discrimination of TBI from SCI compared with established blood biomarkers of neurotrauma, including neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (AUC=0.82, 95%CI 0.76-0.88; vs. 0.53, 95%CI 0.43-0.63; 0.67, 95%CI 0.58-0.76; 0.71, 95%CI 0.64-0.79; all DeLong p<0.001). Longitudinally, serum BD-tau remained persistently elevated in TBI, but not SCI, for up to 144 hours post-injury, with distinct temporal trajectories between injury types. Together, these findings indicate that serum BD-tau enables rapid and minimally invasive differentiation of TBI from SCI and may support early clinical decision-making, triage, and enrollment into injury-specific therapeutic trials, highlighting the potential of circulating biomarkers to improve precision diagnostics in acute neurotrauma care.

items.title: OVM-200, a recombinant overlapping peptide vaccine, breaks immune tolerance to survivin in patients with advanced solid tumours: a multicentre, open-label, dose-expansion, phase 1 study
items.abstract: Survivin (BIRC5) is broadly overexpressed in human cancers but, as a self-antigen, is subject to immune tolerance that limits spontaneous antitumour immunity. OVM-200 is a recombinant overlapping peptide vaccine spanning full-length survivin, with cathepsin S-cleavable linker sequences inserted between adjacent peptides to enhance antigen processing and presentation. OVM-200-100 was a multicentre, open-label phase 1 study conducted at 4 UK sites. The pooled 2,000-g cohort comprised 27 patients with advanced non-small cell lung, ovarian or prostate cancer, including 24 patients from phase 1b and 3 treated at this dose in phase 1a. OVM-200 was administered subcutaneously every 2 weeks for 3 initial vaccinations, with up to 8 additional doses in patients deriving clinical benefit. The primary endpoint was safety and tolerability, secondary endpoints included survivin-specific immunogenicity, and antitumour activity by RECIST v1.1 was exploratory. OVM-200-related adverse events were exclusively grade 1-2, with no treatment-related grade [≥]3 adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, serious adverse events or deaths. A systematic literature analysis showed low spontaneous anti-survivin seroreactivity in patients with cancer. In our cohort, pretreatment tumours expressed survivin despite low baseline survivin-specific immunity. OVM-200 vaccination subsequently induced robust humoral and cellular responses, with median anti-survivin IgG titres increasing from 20 at baseline to a peak of 81,920 and median interferon-{gamma} ELISpot responses increasing from 16.7 to 504.6 spot-forming units per 10 PBMCs. Patients receiving [≥]4 vaccinations developed higher anti-survivin antibody titres and stronger T cell responses than those receiving fewer doses. Among 24 RECIST-evaluable patients, the best overall response was stable disease (SD) in 6 patients (25%). Patients with SD had significantly higher anti-survivin antibody titres than those with progressive disease (PD) (p=0.0418). OVM-200 was well tolerated and induced robust survivin-specific immunity, providing clinical evidence that it can break immune tolerance to self-antigen survivin and supporting further development. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05104515.

items.title: Excluded causal variants produce false discoveries in genetic fine-mapping
items.abstract: Statistical fine-mapping seeks to distinguish causal genetic variants from correlated variants in linkage disequilibrium (LD). Although fine-mapping algorithms perform well in simulations, they are often applied in settings that violate their assumptions. In particular, genome-wide association study (GWAS) and quantitative trait locus (QTL) workflows routinely omit variants with minor allele frequency (MAf) below 1% and most insertions and deletions (indels), excluding many causal variants before fine-mapping begins. To assess this empirically, we compared filtered and unfiltered fine-mapping at 499 All of Us loci. Twenty percent of high-confidence calls after a 1% MAf filter, and 32% when indels were also omitted, lacked support in the unfiltered analysis. Errors were particularly enriched when tested variants tagged an omitted variant, so fine-mapping misassigned its signal to a proxy variant. At RBO, omitting the frameshift that defines blood group O gave near-certain posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) to linked single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). To address this disconnect, we developed SuSiE-OUT, which enables fine-mapping in scenarios with possibly omitted causal variants. Modeling infinitesimal effects did not reliably prevent these errors, whereas imputing omitted variants or modeling them with our SuSiE-OUT method prevented most errors. Overall, we find that common analysis workflows substantially increase false discoveries in fine-mapping analyses, and we demonstrate two approaches to mitigate this challenge.

items.title: Peripheral Blood NADP(H) Redox Metabolism in Alzheimers Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Where Feasible
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Guangyuan First People's Hospital
items.abstract: BackgroundThe reduced and oxidized forms of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH/NADP{square}) connect cellular reducing power with the glutathione and thioredoxin systems. Peripheral alterations in this network may reflect systemic redox dysregulation in Alzheimers disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), but the evidence has not been quantitatively synthesized. ObjectiveTo systematically evaluate peripheral-blood NADP(H) redox metabolism and related enzymes in AD and MCI and to perform meta-analyses when the available data were sufficiently comparable. MethodsPubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 6 November 2026. Eligible observational studies compared patients with AD or MCI with cognitively unimpaired controls and reported NADPH, NADP{square}, the NADPH/NADP{square} ratio, or NADPH-related enzymes, including glutathione reductase (GR), glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD), and thioredoxin reductase (TRXR). Continuous outcomes were converted to Hedges g. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood estimation and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. ResultsOf 2,686 records identified, 1,781 remained after deduplication and 13 studies were included. No study directly reported peripheral NADPH, NADP{square}, or the NADPH/NADP{square} ratio. The pooled effect for erythrocyte GR in AD was g=-1.05 (95% CI -2.73 to 0.63; I2=95.0%; five studies); for erythrocyte GR in MCI, g=-0.15 (95% CI -8.68 to 8.38; I2=95.0%; two studies); for whole-blood/plasma GR in AD, g=-0.03 (95% CI -4.37 to 4.30; I2=97.1%; three studies); and for erythrocyte G6PD in AD, g=-0.66 (95% CI -17.36 to 16.03; I2=96.4%; two studies). Leave-one-out analyses did not materially alter the interpretation of the erythrocyte GR synthesis. ConclusionsAD and MCI may be accompanied by remodeling of peripheral NADP(H)-related enzyme networks, but the direction and magnitude of effects are inconsistent across studies. Direct measurement of NADPH, NADP{square}, and their ratio remains the most important evidence gap. Future prospective studies should standardize specimen type, pre-analytical handling, and analytical platforms and should account for disease stage, treatment exposure, and metabolic comorbidity.

items.title: Higher platelet counts are associated with migraine risk across three cohorts among more than 21,000 cases
items.abstract: ObjectiveWe assessed potential associations between migraine and complete blood cell count (CBC) data in three large population-based studies. BackgroundPlatelets are thought to be involved in migraine pathology through increased activation during an attack. Migraine attacks are often treated with NSAIDs that inhibit platelets, or triptans that target serotonin receptors, with serotonin being most highly expressed in circulation within platelet granules. However, the exact role of platelets in migraine remains unclear. MethodsThe UK BioBank (UKBB) has CBC data available from baseline blood samples and migraine diagnoses were obtained through self-report and electronic health records. CBC and migraine data from the 1999-2000, 2001-2002, and 2003-2004 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) study were obtained during single exam visits. CBCs were obtained from Framingham Heart Study (FHS) participants. Migraine history was assessed through clinical diagnostic impressions. The UKBB sample (18,919 cases (4,580 incident); 448,339 controls) was the primary discovery cohort for CBCs, with replication meta-analysis done in NHANES (1,887 cases; 7,242 controls) and FHS (395 cases (229 incident); 3,172 controls). Our primary model adjusted for age and sex, with secondary analysis adjusting for additional factors. Sex-stratified, sex-interaction and ancestry-stratified (UKBB only) analyses were also performed. ResultsMigraine was associated with platelet count (PLT) in the UKBB (OR=1.058, 95% CI [1.043,1.073], p=2.09E-14) and was replicated in the NHANES-FHS meta-analysis (OR=1.074, 95% CI [1.025,1.126], p=0.003). PLT also drove multiple significant signals of PLT-involved CBC ratios. While neutrophil counts and hemoglobin were associated with migraine in UKBB, these did not replicate in FHS-NHANES meta-analysis. ConclusionHigher platelet count is associated with an increased likelihood of migraine. Further studies with longitudinal assessments of CBCs and migraine attacks are needed to further understand the role of platelets in the onset of migraine attacks.

items.title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
items.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, non-invasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimers disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) burden using Cookie Theft picture-descriptions from two cohorts, including Hebrew- and English-speakers (IRAP, N=134; and WRAP, N=1,541). A{beta} burden was classified across lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) to standard cognitive test scores, reflecting current clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieve the highest F1 among constituent models in five of eight tasks for APOE4 status and global A{beta}. High prediction disagreement suggests complementary signals between approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperforms every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and is also significantly superior to all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional A{beta} tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and pathology, and supports development of early screening approaches.

items.title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
items.abstract: Current cancer screening efforts face the dual problems of low patient adherence and a lack of available tests for many cancers, which motivates the development of less invasive multi-cancer early detection strategies. Such strategies will likely involve the use of liquid biopsies, which can analyze biomarkers found in blood for the presence of cancer. We introduce Blackjack, a new detection approach that focuses on the fragmentation patterns of plasma-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Blackjack characterizes a persons cfDNA fragmentation sites with a position probability matrix (PPM) that encodes information about the sequence context of the sites. For classification, Blackjack computes two features that represent the similarity of an individuals PPM to those of known healthy and cancer cohorts. With these two features, Blackjack then uses logistic regression to classify a new sample as being from a healthy individual or a person with cancer. In cross-validation experiments using two external whole genome sequencing datasets, Blackjack showed high performance, achieving a minimum area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.993 and minimum sensitivity (Sn) of 91.8% (at 98% specificity). This high performance was also present for stage I (AUC 0.991, Sn 89.8%) and stage II cancers (AUC 0.993, Sn 90.2%), and across eight different cancers (minimum AUC 0.985, minimum Sn 80.0%). We demonstrate that Blackjacks accuracy is stable at low simulated sequencing depths ([~]0.24x), and that tissue of origin prediction using Blackjacks similarity measures is high (minimum 82% accuracy of the top two predicted tissues). Our findings show that cfDNA fragmentation site contexts have valuable signals for early cancer detection, and that developing diagnostics with machine learning can benefit from a focus on having a small number of informative features.

items.title: Inactivating mutations in polyadenylation factor CSTF2 disrupt intronic polyadenylation patterns and are associated with intellectual disability.
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Medical and Molecular Genetics, King's College London, London, UK
items.abstract: Alternative polyadenylation contributes extensively to transcript diversification and is particularly prominent during neuronal differentiation. CSTF2 encodes an RNA-binding subunit of the cleavage stimulation factor complex and has previously been associated with X-linked intellectual disability through a single Asp50Ala missense variant with increased RNA-binding activity. Here, we identify seven rare CSTF2 variants in ten hemizygous male probands with intellectual disability, global developmental delay and/or autism spectrum disorder, including missense, nonsense, splice-site, and frameshift variants. We functionally assessed selected variants by ectopic expression in CSTF2-depleted HEK293T cells, followed by total and 3'-end-proximal RNA sequencing. Phe19Leu, Gln543Ter and Leu555Ser markedly impaired CSTF2 function. These variants predominantly reduced the usage of strong, evolutionarily conserved intronic polyadenylation sites with prominent GU-rich sequences, while increasing the usage of downstream sites within terminal 3'UTRs. In contrast, the previously reported Asp50Ala variant produced an opposing pattern, with preferential activation of intronic polyadenylation sites, consistent with its increased RNA-binding activity. These findings data provide genetic and functional support for CSTF2 as an X-linked intellectual disability, identify inactivating CSTF2 variants as a disease mechanism, and imply that both reduced and increased CSTF2 activity can result in neurodevelopmental disorder.

items.title: Assessing the Accuracy of the NeuroBooster Array for GBA1 Variant Detection
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Clinical and Movement Neurosciences, Queen Square Institute of Neurology, University College London, London, UK
items.abstract: GBA1 variants are major Parkinsons disease risk factors, but their detection is challenging. We compared NeuroBooster Array (NBA) genotyping with reference sequencing in 3,744 individuals. NBA correctly identified 520/608 carriers (85.5%). Of 89 missed calls, 73 had no matching probe and 16 had missing calls. 25 participants had false positive calls. NBA should not be used alone for clinical decisions, but is very useful for large case control analysis.

items.title: Pooled Multiplex Amplicon Massive Parallel Sequencing for High-Throughput Confirmation of Whole-Genome Sequencing Potentially Pathogenic Variants in Patients with Parkinsonism
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Medical Genetics, University Hospital and Faculty of Medicine and Dentistry, Palacky University 779 00 Olomouc, Czech Republic
items.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. Whole-genome sequencing data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pathogenicity assessment criteria. A total of 307 variants were targeted using a custom amplicon panel comprising 290 amplicons. DNA samples were normalized, pooled into 16 mixtures, and sequenced following automated library preparation. Variant presence and sequencing quality were assessed using standard bioinformatic tools. Of the 307 selected variants, 243 were successfully confirmed. Unconfirmed variants included sequencing artifacts (18), insufficiently covered targets (5), large insertions or deletions exceeding 12 base pairs (36), and variants located within homopolymeric regions (5). Results for selected variants were concordant with Sanger sequencing, and observed variant frequencies corresponded to expected frequencies in pooled samples. This approach provides a robust, rapid, and cost-effective method for high-throughput genetic variants confirming identified by whole-genome sequencing while requiring only limited DNA input. Despite complete concordance with Sanger sequencing, larger validation studies are needed before multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing can replace routine confirmatory testing. Key PointsO_LIDesign and application of a high-throughput verification strategy for WGS variants with minimal DNA input requirements C_LIO_LIReliable and independent confirmation of WGS findings C_LIO_LIUtilization of multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing (MPS) in sample mixtures C_LIO_LIDetection of point mutations, small indels and duplications. C_LI

items.title: Tau-vulnerable medial temporal lobe connectivity drives a functional-to-synaptic cascade in Alzheimer's disease
items.corresponding_institution: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
items.abstract: Distinct tau-vulnerable and relatively spared subregions exist within the medial temporal lobe (MTL). However, it remains unclear that how functional connectivity (FC), anchored to tau-vulnerable MTL subregions, is related to tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline across the Alzheimers disease (AD) continuum. We here probe into this with resting-state fMRI data from a discovery cohort (ADNI; N = 386; cognitively normal [CN], mild cognitive impairment [MCI], and AD; 144 with 2-year follow-up) and an independent validation cohort at local hospital (N = 100; CN, subjective cognitive decline [SCD], and MCI; 25 receiving high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [HF-rTMS]). We first separated the MTL into subregions with high and low neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) burden based on histological atlases, and calculated the seed-based whole-brain FC for each subregion. Second, group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, and associations with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta})/tau pathology, synaptic biomarkers, and cognitive performance were examined. Third, serial mediation, cross-lagged, and longitudinal regression analyses were performed to investigate the proposed pathological sequence, with additional evidence from HF-rTMS intervention and autopsy-confirmed Braak staging. Our results showed that, with the development of AD, FC reductions were focused on the high-NFT MTL network, particularly involving the inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus. Baseline tau burden in high-NFT MTL regions was able to predict subsequent FC alterations. Interestingly, FC between the high-NFT MTL and global brain showed region-specific associations with synaptic biomarkers, including negative associations in the cerebellum and positive associations in the precentral gyrus. We also observed a divergent association between the FC and cognition or pathology at different AD stages, shifting from positive in the early stages to negative in advanced AD. Serial mediation analyses supported a pathway linking tau burden to cognitive impairment through altered high-NFT MTL connectivity in the precuneus and occipital regions and subsequent synaptic dysfunction. Cross-lagged and longitudinal analyses further confirmed the proposed temporal sequence. Furthermore, HF-rTMS-related cognitive improvements were partially associated with enhanced synaptic plasticity through changes in precuneus-high-NFT MTL connectivity. Collectively, these findings support a spatiotemporal framework linking the dysfunction of tau-vulnerable MTL network to synaptic impairment and cognitive decline, highlighting high-NFT MTL-based FC as a potential imaging marker tracking AD progression.

items.title: The LAMp-LC Study: Unveiling the lung microbiome in Australians with early- and late-stage lung cancer using shotgun metagenomics
items.abstract: BackgroundLung cancer remains the leading cause of cancerl71related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. MethodsWe characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n=106, healthy n=10) using shotgun metagenomics and semil71quantitative culture to evaluate microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across earlyl71 and latel71stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culturel71based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking packl71years, sex, and tumour characteristics. ResultsCumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive Neisseria subflava, Gemella sanguinis, and Rothia mucilaginosa depletion, alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. {beta} diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst diversity was significantly reduced in early-stage vs. late-stage BWs. The earlyl71stage TME demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched (Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted (Streptococcus parasanguinis, Streptococcus cristatus, R. mucilaginosa) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral {beta}l71diversity restructuring. ConclusionsThe lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiomel71based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

items.title: Genome-Wide Study of Early Disability Severity in Multiple Sclerosis
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Clinical Neuroscience, Karolinska Institutet, Solna, Sweden
items.abstract: Background and ObjectivesMultiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by demyelination and neuroaxonal injury. Genetics of MS susceptibility and long term disability is well characterized, but the genetic contribution to disability recorded earlier in the disease course is uncertain. We performed common-variant associations with the early period MS severity to identify potential causal loci, effector genes and associated pathways, and understand the relationships of early MS severity and other traits. MethodsThe primary outcome was the first age-related MS severity score (ARMSS), an age-adjusted severity measure, in 7,209 individuals of Swedish discovery cohorts and independent Italian and multi-national European replication cohorts. Replicated loci underwent conditional analysis, fine-mapping, time-to-event MS phenotype association analyses, and multi-omics-integrated gene prioritization. Using the genome-wide summary statistics, we also conducted heritability analyses, polygenic risk score association with MS susceptibility and late MS severity, gene-level analyses, cross-trait analyses, Mendelian randomization, and drug-repurposing screening. ResultsTwo suggestive loci were replicated: rs1234317 on chromosome 1 (effect allele T: beta = 0.100, SE = 0.0189, P = 1.08 x 10-7) and rs929769 on chromosome 5 (effect allele T: beta = -0.0956, SE = 0.0184, P = 1.95 x 10-7). Fine-mapping supported rs929769 strongly in chromosome 5, and rs1234317 and rs6657136 in chromosome 1 with lower confidence. The SNPs did not show a significant change in effect sizes when adjusted for heritable traits and exhibited attenuated associations with long-term MS disability progression. TNFSF4 was the top prioritized effector for rs1234317, TNFSF18 for rs6657136, and ADAMTS2 for rs929769. Early MS severity showed partial genetic overlap with MS susceptibility and late MS severity, but no significant correlation with a range of neurological, psychiatric, autoimmune, cognitive, and aging traits. Pathway analyses identified ion-channel regulation and folic acid metabolism. Mendelian randomization suggested nominal bidirectional causal associations with educational attainment. In silico drug screening nominated several candidate drugs. DiscussionThis study identifies candidate causal variants of early MS severity and their effector genes: TNFSF4, TNFSF18, and ADAMTS2. It provides insights into the genetic architecture and therapeutic measures for the early phase of MS severity.

items.title: Long-read genome sequencing resolves complex structural variants in exome-negative developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
items.corresponding_institution: Dept. of Neurology and Epileptology, Hertie Center of Neurology and Hertie Institute fuer Clinical Brain Research, University and University Hospital Tuebingen;
items.abstract: Background and ObjectivesDespite standard genetic testing, approximately two-thirds of patients with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) remain undiagnosed. Pathogenic noncoding and structural variants (SVs), that are difficult to detect or resolve using short-read sequencing, may contribute to this diagnostic gap. To evaluate the diagnostic contribution of long-read genome sequencing (lrGS), we recruited a cohort of 124 families with sporadic DEE who remained unsolved by prior ES.
